title: hooks: no check on a rewritable artifact can stop core.hooksPath drift, because the writer is the actor
description:
Left open deliberately by the round-4 fix on branch `fix/hookspath-inert-detector` (PR #1044), which named it N1 and declined to close it. Filed so the reasoning does not live only in that branch's review log.

## The gap

`core.hooksPath` drift in the shared config is written by the Claude Code agent-worktree creation path (see gqlc-7ijy, which identifies the writer). Every mitigation on PR #1044 is a *check* — `just doctor`, `check-hooks`, the tripwire hooks themselves. All of them read an artifact the drifting actor can also write.

So the detector is sound against accidental drift and against a stale config, and unsound against the actual writer, which can restore `core.hooksPath` to `.git/hooks` after any check has passed. The check tells you drift happened; it cannot make drift not happen.

## Why the obvious half-measure was rejected

The fixer considered running the tripwire under a faked environment so a hook could tell whether it was invoked by git or by the recipe. It rejected it because moving that one key breaks the tripwire's own `git config --get`, which is how it reads the value it is checking. That is not a detail of the implementation; a check that must lie about the environment to observe the environment has a circularity, not a bug.

## What would actually close it

Unclear, and that is the point of filing rather than fixing. Candidates worth evaluating before anyone writes code:

- Repair rather than detect: make the check's self-heal arm authoritative and run it at a point the writer cannot follow.
- Move the value out of the shared config — `extensions.worktreeConfig` plus a per-worktree setting changes the blast radius from "all ~20 worktrees" to one, without closing the hole.
- Fix the writer (gqlc-7ijy) so nothing drifts, and treat every check here as defence in depth rather than as the gate.
- Accept detection as the ceiling at this layer and move enforcement to CI, where the actor has no write access to the config.

The last is probably the honest answer, and if so this bead closes by writing that down in CONTRIBUTING rather than by adding a guard.

## Related

- gqlc-7ijy — identifies the drift writer
- gqlc-pyk2 — the inert detector, fixed by PR #1044
- gqlc-4thl — the drifted-config incident itself
notes:
Սեդրակ 2026-08-21: labelled class:architect, not class:warrior, deliberately. The title states
an IMPOSSIBILITY CLAIM — 'no check on a rewritable artifact can stop drift, because the writer
is the actor'. That is an argument about what is achievable, not a defect with a known fix, and
routing it to a warrior invites someone to implement a check that the bead itself says cannot
work. What is wanted first is a judgment: accept the claim and design around it (move the gate
somewhere the actor cannot rewrite), or falsify it. Related in-flight work: gqlc-4thl (PR #1044)
and gqlc-pyk2 sit in the same hooksPath family — read both before designing.
=== OBSERVATION 2026-08-22 (Ար, seat worktree gqlc-seat-ar) — a WITHIN-SESSION flap ===
Reporting this because the description frames drift as a persisted wrong value
that a check can catch late. What I saw was narrower and self-closing, which is
worse for any point-in-time detector.

At 02:2xZ two PreToolUse hook firings told me, in consecutive tool calls:
    core.hooksPath in .../gqlc-seat-ar is '/dev/null', expected '.githooks'
Roughly a minute later, three consecutive reads by me:
    git config --show-origin --get core.hooksPath
    -> file:/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/config    .githooks   (x3)
and the shared config on disk has `hooksPath = .githooks` at line 6.

WHAT I CANNOT DISTINGUISH, stated plainly rather than guessed: (a) the value
really was /dev/null and something restored it inside a minute, or (b) the
harness hook's own read is wrong or reads a different scope. I did not catch it
at /dev/null with my own command, so I am NOT claiming a measured transient. The
two accounts simply disagree and I could not reproduce either from the other.

WHY IT MATTERS EITHER WAY, and why I did not just repair and move on:
- If (a): the window is ~1 minute and closes by itself. Every mitigation on
  PR #1044 is a point-in-time read. A flap this short is missed by all of them
  almost always, and when it IS caught the value has already healed, so the
  citizen is told to run `just init` on a config that is already correct — which
  trains people to ignore the warning. That is a detector losing credibility.
- If (b): a hook is reporting a dead gate that is not dead. Same cost — the
  warning gets ignored — arriving from the opposite direction.

Both readings land on the same conclusion the description already reaches: a
check over a rewritable artifact is not the gate. This just narrows the window it
would have to hit.

write. Two writers were caught first-party this week (the harness's

better check — it is to move each load-bearing rule to a layer its writers
cannot reach, and demote everything reading .git/config to fast feedback.

following the check-pr-closes.py pattern). One predicate set, three modes:
  --message-file F [--author-email E] [--committer-email E]
      exit 1 if the message carries an offending co-authored-by line or an
      email fails the identity predicate. Used by the commit-msg hook.
  --pr-commits-json F --expected-count N
      F is the raw JSON array from `gh api repos/$R/pulls/$N/commits
      --paginate`. Checks EVERY commit's message + author/committer emails.
      FAILS if the array length != N (the endpoint caps at 250 commits;
      a mismatch means unscreened commits — fail closed, say so in the
      message). Used by CI. On failure, name each offending SHA and why.
  --body-file F
      exit 1 if the PR body carries an AI-attribution footer. Used by CI.
Predicates (put them in one place in the file, commented as the single source):
  - co-authored-by: match lines ^co-authored-by:[[:space:]] case-insensitively
    ANYWHERE in the message whose value contains "claude" or "@anthropic.com"
    (case-folded). NOTE this is deliberately WIDER than the hook's current
    trailer-block-only scan (git interpret-trailers): a prose mention in a
    commit body now also refuses. Accepted behaviour change; state it in the
    script header. Reimplementing git's trailer folding in python is the
    alternative and was rejected — divergence risk for zero real traffic.
  - identity: exact denylist test@example.invalid, fixture@example.invalid,
    root@localhost, empty; suffixes @example.com, @example.org; then shape
    (must contain @, domain must contain a dot). Same as commit-msg's
    _check_identity today, plus fixture@example.invalid (the identity that
    actually landed on PRs #1133/#1134 — commit-msg's list missed it).
  - body footer: case-insensitive "generated with" within 3 lines of end OR
    anywhere matching "generated with [claude code]" / "🤖 generated with".
    Keep the predicate dumb and enumerable; no regex cleverness.

both `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. tidy is ALREADY a required
context and ci.yml ALREADY runs on pull_request types
[opened, synchronize, reopened, edited] — the `edited` type and the
fetch-the-LIVE-body-via-API discipline exist precisely for the neighbouring
"check PR body carries Closes #N" step (bd gqlc-w4al). Follow that step's
shape exactly:

    env: GH_TOKEN, PR_NUMBER, EXPECTED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.commits }}

        --expected-count "$EXPECTED"
    (--paginate emits concatenated arrays; have the script accept either one
    array or concatenated arrays — parse with a small tolerant loader.)

    depth-1 on the synthetic merge ref, a shallow fetch cannot enumerate the

  step B "PR body carries no AI-attribution footer":

title:
git worktree add -b
origin/master sets upstream to master, so a bare push targets master
description:
CLAUDE.md's own sibling-worktree recipe is:

    git worktree add ../<repo>-<slug> -b <branch> origin/master

This sets the NEW branch's upstream to origin/master. A later bare `git push` in that worktree therefore resolves to master, not to the branch.

Measured 2026-08-19 in ../gqlc-agt0: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name '@{u}'` returned `origin/master` on branch `fix/vuln-unplaced-stdlib-assertions-covered`. The push was REFUSED, but only incidentally — push.default=simple refuses when the branch name and the upstream name differ. That is the only thing standing between this recipe and an agent pushing a feature branch's commits onto master.

Two things make it worse than it looks:
- Every agent worktree in this repo is created by that recipe, so every one of them carries the misconfiguration.
- The refusal message does not say 'your upstream is master'; it reads as an ordinary push failure, so the natural next move is to add a flag until it goes through.

Candidate fixes, in preference order:
1. Change the CLAUDE.md recipe to pass `--no-track`, or follow the add with `git branch --set-upstream-to` / an explicit first `git push -u origin HEAD`.
2. Set `push.default=current` for the repo so a bare push always targets the same-named remote branch.
3. A pre-push hook clause refusing a push whose resolved destination is master from a non-master branch.

(1) and (2) are not exclusive; (3) is the fail-closed backstop and is the only one that survives an agent typing the raw command from memory.

Verify any fix by creating a throwaway worktree with the documented recipe and asserting `@{u}` is not origin/master.
notes:
PR https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/1056 open and green (8/8 checks on 0606ad2e; live-smoke-age skipped by design). Branch fix/worktree-upstream-tracks-master, worktree ../gqlc-tfh1.

Implemented (1) + (3) + a third arm; (2) push.default=current DROPPED — repo scope means the shared .git/config, which this session was forbidden to write, and it would only mask the wrong upstream for push while git pull / @{u} / git status keep reading master.

  1. CLAUDE.md: 'git worktree add --no-track -b <branch> ../<path> origin/master' + 'git push -u origin HEAD'.
  3. .githooks/guard-push-destination, run first in pre-push: refuses a push whose RESOLVED destination is refs/heads/master|main unless the ref pushed IS that ref.
  +. just check-worktree-upstream, wired into just test: names a worktree already tracking master while it is latent (covers git pull, which the push guard cannot).

Measurements: baseline @{u} on this branch at worktree creation = origin/master; after repair + first push = origin/fix/worktree-upstream-tracks-master. Sweep of 21 sibling worktrees on 2026-08-19: 4 tracking origin/master (98ii, osuz, sxzj, tfh1).

Mutation matrix 11/11 KILLED, all LIVE + VALID. Test: .githooks/tests/worktree-upstream-test.sh, 27 cases.

Not covered: git push --no-verify; a worktree whose core.hooksPath has drifted off .githooks. Existing misconfigured worktrees: bd gqlc-q9z2 (GH #1047).

title: vuln: a grep -q consumer under pipefail conflates SIGPIPE with failure, so the platformtag self-test can refuse a fixture it matched
description:
> **Amended 2026-08-19.** Three claims in the original report were falsified by measurement while the fix was under review. They are corrected inline below; the full record of what was wrong and how each was refuted is in [the correction comment](https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/issues/1033#issuecomment-5350641756). The defect itself, and the fix, are unchanged.

`selftest_platformtag` in the `vuln` recipe pipes `go list -e "${tagflag[@]}" -f '{{.Dir}}' ./...` straight into `grep -qxF "${fixture}"`, under the `set -euo pipefail` the recipe sets at the top of its body.

`grep -q` exits as soon as it matches. The producer then takes SIGPIPE and reports 141, and under pipefail the pipeline's status is 141 even though grep MATCHED. The `if !` fires and the recipe prints 'is not in the set go list ./...' about a fixture that IS in the set, then exits 1.

Found by the Linus review of gqlc-agt0 (verdict `/tmp/lead/verdict-agt0-r1b.md` section 1). Reproduced deterministically by adding `sleep 0.2` to a stub go-list producer and changing nothing else — byte-identical error to the CI failure, with the fixture provably in the set. Unpatched flake rate measured at 1/500 idle and 1/300 under load.

This is a defect in the SHIPPING recipe, present on master, not introduced by any branch.

**Why it stays invisible here** — *corrected; the original said "two accidents: the fixture sorts last of 28, and the output fits a 64K pipe buffer". Both are false.* Sort order is not a guard at this site at all: `selftest_platformtag` issues the **tagged** listing (29 lines, fixture at 28), and the fixture is last only in the *untagged* listing, which this site never runs. Buffer-fit is neither sufficient nor necessary: a 1262-byte listing, 52x inside a 65536-byte pipe buffer, returned 141 in 20 of 20 runs when emitted a line at a time with a 20ms pause; and a 189,019-byte payload, 2.9x OVER the capacity, returned rc 0 in 60 of 60 when the match was on the last line. Size is not the variable in either direction.

What actually decides a piped site is a race — whether the producer still has a write to make when `grep` exits — and what settles it is the producer having none left once `grep` can first match. Nothing in the recipe's text settles that for `go list`, `scope` or `sort`, whose write counts follow buffering inside the producer. The real `go list` won the race in 100 of 100 runs in this checkout, which is a race won 100 times, not a guarantee.

It surfaced via gqlc-agt0's vulnguard harness because that runs the real recipe over a small throwaway tree. *Corrected:* it is not line-at-a-time emission that loses the race — the same 29-write producer without the pause returned 0 in 200 of 200 — but slowness relative to `grep`'s startup, which nothing here bounds.

**FIX:** read the listing into a variable and match with a herestring, which is what the recipe's other membership tests already do.

    listed="$(go list -e "${tagflag[@]}" -f '{{.Dir}}' ./...)" || exit 1
    if ! grep -qxF "${fixture}" <<<"${listed}"; then

*Corrected: the original called this site "the lone outlier".* There is a second site of the same shape in `selftest_tagblind`, and its polarity is worse — there a match means the guard *should* fire, so a SIGPIPE makes the `if` false and lets a regressed fixture through silently. Both are fixed together.

**ALSO:** the recipe's 'TWO HOUSE RULES' block already reasons about process-substitution statuses and about `set -e` inside command substitution. It should gain the third rule of the same family: a pipeline whose consumer can exit early conflates SIGPIPE with failure under pipefail. Because the deciding variable is not settled by anything in the recipe's text, that rule bans the shape rather than offering a test to apply to it.
notes:
2026-08-19 (Carmack, branch fix/vuln-unplaced-stdlib-assertions-covered, PR #1031): FIXED.

Correction to the FIX section above: justfile:1463 was NOT the lone piped site. selftest_tagblind's `if go list -e -f '{{.Dir}}' ./... | grep -qxF "${fixture}"` (was justfile:1363) is a second instance of the same shape, and there the polarity is worse — the match means the guard SHOULD fire, so a SIGPIPE 141 makes `if` false and the guard passes silently. Fail-open. Both sites converted to `x="$(go list ...)" || exit 1` + `grep -qxF ... <<<"${x}"`.

Third rule added to the recipe's house-rules block (now "THREE HOUSE RULES"), citing this bead.

Evidence, /tmp/probe-agt0-r2/: mktree.py replicates vulnguard's justfileFor + writeTree outside the test binary, with `--slow` inserting `sleep 0.2` into the stub's `go list ./...` emit loop (the OUTER loop — slowing go_dirs' inner one does nothing, it pipes into `sort -u`). Same generator, same sleep, only the recipe differs:
  recipe at 23d66ed5 (unpatched): 5/5 runs rc=1, "is not in the set 'go list ./...'"
  recipe with herestrings:        5/5 runs rc=0, message absent
Instrumented scratch copy printed `PROBE rc=141 shellopts=...errexit...pipefail` — SIGPIPE, with the fixture provably in the set (`grep -qxF "$F" <<<"$out"` rc=0 over the same listing).
CORRECTION 2026-08-19 (round-2 review, verified first-party by lead): the 'two accidents' account in this bead is wrong, and the error is not cosmetic.

Only ONE accident guarded master: go list fits its whole output in the pipe buffer, so it never writes again after grep matches and never takes SIGPIPE.

Sort order is NOT the second guard. selftest_platformtag issues the TAGGED listing. Measured in the worktree at cd0b37d4:
  go list -e -f '{{.Dir}}' ./...                -> 28 lines, platformtag at 28 (last)
  go list -e -tags tagblind -f '{{.Dir}}' ./... -> 29 lines, platformtag at 28 (NOT last)
The recorded '28 of 28' figure is of a command that site never issues.

selftest_tagblind is not protected by sort order in either direction: on a healthy tree its fixture is absent entirely.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the account invited the reader to check 'is my match last?' as an all-clear, and that check gives a false negative at the exact site that broke. Anyone auditing other pipelines with it would clear a broken one.

Also corrected: rule (3) summarised itself as 'every grep -q and grep -m1 in this recipe reads a herestring'. justfile:1445 is a grep -q in this recipe reading a FILE ARGUMENT — the summary was false one grep away from where it was written. The normative clause was correct; only the summary overreached. Now states that none reads a PIPE.

Carriers fixed: justfile comment, PR #1031 body, this bead. Commit cd0b37d4, comment-only, no executable line moves.
close_reason: PR #1031 merged as 359e48f8. SIGPIPE/pipefail race fixed at both sites (selftest_platformtag, selftest_tagblind) — verified on origin/master: no live pipe-into-grep -q remains, house rule 3 present. Closed #1033.

title: bd-gh-sync: the unmirrored-bead push is a read-modify-write with no lock, so concurrent runs mint duplicate GH issues that nothing can ever close
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-18. 18 of the 223 open GH issues were permanent zombies: an
open issue with NO bead pointing at it, whose title is byte-identical to a bead
that is bound to a DIFFERENT issue number. Because no bead carries the orphan's
number in external_ref, the close pass (bd-gh-sync lines 438-462, which keys on
external_ref) can never reach it. It stays open forever regardless of whether
the work lands.

THE 18 PAIRS (orphan -> canonical, bead):
  452->453 fer | 505->503 4np | 814->816 u91z | 815->818 f1yf | 817->819 65sl
  820->821 rxq9 | 875->876 t802 | 877->878 dc6k | 879->880 qv80 | 887->890 uc8f
  888->892 w1gc | 889->894 2xkf | 891->896 gyp5 | 893->898 0pb8 | 895->899 oh30
  897->900 komy | 928->930 drvx | 929->931 g3g6

EVIDENCE, counted rather than asserted:
- 16 of 18 pairs have byte-identical bodies (md5 of `gh issue view --json body`).
  The two exceptions are characterised below; neither weakens the account.
- 17 of 18 have the orphan created BEFORE the canonical, by 1-6 seconds.
- They arrive in bursts, not uniformly: 2026-07-28T03:23 (1), 2026-08-17T05:17
  (4), 07:47 (3), 08:40-41 (6), 13:40 (2).

MECHANISM THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS. .githooks/bd-gh-sync:405-426 is a
read-modify-write with no serialization:

    bd list --status all --limit 0 --json >"$_tmp/beads.json"     # READ
    ... python filter: print every bead with no external_ref ...
    bd github push $_ids                                          # WRITE

`bd github push` is what assigns external_ref. Between the READ and the WRITE
there is no lock: `grep -n 'flock|lockfile|\.lock|noclobber' .githooks/bd-gh-sync`
returns nothing. The hook fires from .githooks/pre-push:20 (and `pull` from
.claude/settings.json:29 and post-merge:11), so two concurrent agent sessions
each pushing will each snapshot the ledger before the other's push lands, each
see the same bead as unmirrored, and each mint an issue. The bead ends up
holding whichever external_ref was written last; the other number is orphaned.
The 1-6s separation and the burst clustering are what that race looks like.

NOT YET CONFIRMED: I did not reproduce the race, only showed it is unguarded and
that the artefacts match it. What would confirm it: two `bd-gh-sync push` runs
started concurrently against a scratch repo with one unmirrored bead, asserting
exactly one issue is minted. That test is also the fix's regression pin.

THE TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated because they bound the claim:
- 505/503 inverts the ordering (orphan 14s AFTER canonical) and the bodies differ
  by a trailing 'Tracked as bd `gqlc-4np`.' footer that only 505 carries. This
  pair is probably NOT the race; it looks like a hand-filed issue plus a minted
  mirror. It is included in the cleanup, not in the mechanism claim.
- 895/899 differ because 899 additionally carries a ~40-line 'AMENDMENT (PR #901
  round 7)' section. Same race shape, but the canonical was edited afterwards.

REMEDIATION ALREADY DONE (this is the manual workaround, not the fix): all 18
orphans closed as `not planned` with a comment naming the canonical, plus #892
(bead gqlc-w1gc, landed as PR #996 whose body carried no `Closes #892`). Open GH
issues went 223 -> 204. The remaining 204 are real: 198 open beads, 5
in_progress, 1 blocked.

SCOPE OF THE FIX:
1. Serialize the push pass (flock on a fixed path, or `set -o noclobber` lockdir),
   so a second concurrent run waits or exits rather than double-minting.
2. Re-read the ledger inside the lock rather than reusing the pre-lock snapshot —
   the same defect the existing comment at lines 430-433 already documents for
   the CLOSE pass ("Reusing the pre-push snapshot skips exactly the beads that
   were closed before their first push, leaving the mirror it just minted open
   forever"). That comment identifies the read-staleness hazard on one side and
   the push side has the same hazard, unfixed.
3. Add a reconciler for the orphans this has already produced and will produce
   until (1) lands: an open GH issue whose title matches a bead bound to a
   different number is a duplicate, and should be reported (not auto-closed).
4. Regression pin: the concurrent-run test described above, wired into
   .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh so `just test-hooks` reaches it.

Filed after the user asked why so many GH issues were open. The bookkeeping was
NOT the main story -- 198 of 204 are genuine open work -- but this defect is a
slow leak that adds a permanent zombie every time two sessions push at once.

title: modscope: a 'mod' submodule hides modscope callers from the sweep gate, and both readings agree so the differential stays silent
description:
Found reviewing PR #1001 (gqlc-6n9y) round 2, outside that PR's delta. Live on
master. Reproduced first-party on the real justfile against just 1.57.0 AND
1.55.1.

THE GAP. `just --dump`'s top-level keys are:

    aliases assignments doc first groups module_path modules recipes settings
    source unexports warnings

`justDump` reads only `recipes` (and within it `priors`, `dependencies[].recipe`,
`body`). A `mod` directive puts the submodule's recipes under **`modules`**, not
`recipes`. So a recipe living in a submodule is invisible to the reader.

WHY THE DIFFERENTIAL DOES NOT CATCH IT. This is the important half.
`TestParseJustfileAgreesWithJustOnThisJustfile` compares the raw-text reader
against `just --dump`. Both are blind to `modules` — the reader because it never
looks, the dump consumer because it only reads `recipes`. **Two blind readings
AGREE.** The differential's whole design assumes a disagreement surfaces a gap,
and this gap produces no disagreement.

REPRODUCER (appended to the real justfile, then restored to md5
0a50d4516460ddfcf332977a332cc85b):

    mod probe 'probe.just'
    # probe.just declares probe-caller whose body is
    #   go run ./internal/tools/modscope modules
    # with NO dependencies

    just 1.57.0 and 1.55.1: top-level recipes=29, modules=['probe']
    probe::probe-caller names modscope = True, deps = []
    --- PASS: TestEveryRecipeRunningModscopeSweepsProbesFirst
    --- PASS: TestParseJustfileAgreesWithJustOnThisJustfile

An unswept modscope caller, named by `just --dump`, passing the gate in silence.

CONTRAST, and this is what makes `mod` the dangerous one: `import 'sub.just'`
INLINES into `recipes`, so an imported caller is seen and the gate is loud. The
two directives look similar and behave oppositely here.

WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN A NOTE. The gate exists to guarantee every recipe that
runs modscope sweeps probes first. `mod` turns that guarantee off silently, in
the fail-OPEN direction, with no diagnostic anywhere.

A SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT TO FIX WITH IT. The test's "WHAT THIS DOES NOT REACH"
list does not name `mod`, and its bullet 2 says "Shapes this justfile does not
contain. It reports on these bytes" — which implies that bytes GAINING the shape
would produce a report. The probe put the shape in the bytes and got nothing. So
that bullet is false as written for this shape, independently of whether anyone
fixes the reader.

TWO ACCEPTABLE FIXES, DECIDE DELIBERATELY:
  - Read `modules` recursively and hold submodule recipes to the same gate; or
  - Refuse a justfile containing `mod` outright, so the gate fails CLOSED on a
    shape it does not model.
Either way, pin the choice with a row that RED-s if it flips. And whatever the
prose says afterwards must not claim a boundary over directives nobody enumerated
— `mod` was found by trying it, not by reading a list.

NOT MEASURED: whether `mod` is likely to appear here, and whether ciguard's
justfile reader shares the blind spot. That second question is worth asking —
see gqlc-sgot / gqlc-lisu.

Related: gqlc-6n9y (the PR that surfaced it).

title: codegen: runCorpus discards every subtest event, so a whole subtest tree can go silent unnoticed
description:
Same class as gqlc-wla6 (PR #1002), one level down, and live on master in BOTH
packages today.

`internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go:212` and
`internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go:143`:

    if event.Action == "pass" && event.Test != "" && !strings.Contains(event.Test, "/") {

The `!strings.Contains(event.Test, "/")` clause drops every SUBTEST pass event,
keeping only top-level ones. That is deliberate — the census compares top-level
test names against the `corpusTests` list, and counting subtests would break the
comparison. The gap is what the filter also buys:

**A top-level test can pass while every subtest under it stops running, and this
census cannot tell.** The name still arrives as a top-level `pass`, `corpusTests`
still matches, `ElementsMatch` is satisfied, and the non-empty guard added by
#1002 is satisfied too. Nothing here observes subtest-level silence.

This is the aggregate-emptiness shape that gqlc-wla6 was opened to close, moved
down one level: the guard proves the SET of top-level names is right and
non-empty, and says nothing about whether anything ran INSIDE them.

WHAT TO MEASURE BEFORE FIXING (do not assume the gap is reachable):
  - Do the corpus fixture's tests actually HAVE subtests? If none do, the gap is
    latent rather than live, and the bead should say which it is rather than
    asserting either.
  - Mutate: make a subtest tree vacuous (e.g. empty the table it ranges over)
    while leaving the top-level test passing, and check the census stays GREEN.
    A GREEN there is the witness; without it this is a code reading, not a
    defect.

SCREENS (these cost real rounds on #1002, do not rediscover them):
  - `go test -c` is NOT the screen here (gqlc-hreu) — the fixture compiles one
    module DOWN. Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log.
  - Assert `\[(build|setup) failed\]` absent — BOTH spellings. A fixture parse
    error prints `[setup failed]`, not `[build failed]`.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on `^[[:space:]]*--- PASS`, never `^ *--- PASS`: testify
    indents with TABs and the space-only class reported 0 where the truth was 21.

title: hooks: git rebase -i reword bypasses the AI-attribution commit-msg gate under hooksPath drift
description:
Behavioural, not prose. Found while reviewing PR #992 (gqlc-wa8c) round 3; the
branch's own prose sweep was correct and this was outside it.

`git rebase -i` with a **reword** fires `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` — two of
the four hooks — where every in-tree statement says rebase fires none. Measured
first-party in two independently written fixtures, and reproduced by the round-4
reviewer in a third:

    rebase -i REWORD (editor=true)  rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[commit-msg,pre-commit]
    rebase -i REWORD (real editor)  rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[commit-msg,pre-commit] subject="C reworded"
    rebase plain (control)          rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[]
    commit (control)                rc=0 HEADmoved=yes fired=[commit-msg,pre-commit]

rc=0 and the subject really changed, so the row is not vacuous. Exactly the four
hooks this repo ships were armed and nothing else fired.

WHY IT MATTERS: `rebase` is outside `HOOK_GATED` and
`.githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh:355` pins it warn-only. So while
`core.hooksPath` is drifted, a reword silently skips `commit-msg` — which is the
hook enforcing the no-`Co-Authored-By: Claude` rule. Agent spawns rewrite
`core.hooksPath` in the SHARED git config (see gqlc-7y7e and the hooksPath-drift
bead), so the drifted state is reachable in normal operation, not hypothetical.

The in-tree rationale for leaving rebase ungated is pre-existing and honestly
hedged. The gap is that the shape survey behind it missed the reword path.

NOT YET MEASURED, do not claim a closed enumeration: `--autosquash`, `--onto`,
`--root`, merge-preserving and conflict-resume paths were measured firing none;
other rebase shapes were not enumerated at all.
notes:
=== REPRODUCED FIRST-PARTY, THEN CLOSED BY A TRIPWIRE, 2026-08-19 (Carmack) ===

VERIFIED THE HOLE BEFORE FIXING IT, as asked. Fixture: a throwaway repo whose
.githooks/commit-msg refuses a Co-Authored-By naming claude, i.e. this repo's
gate in miniature. GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR flips pick->reword; GIT_EDITOR writes a
message carrying `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

  HEALTHY (core.hooksPath=.githooks): the gate fires, the rebase HALTS, the
    trailer is NOT on HEAD. So the gate does cover a reword when hooks are live.
  DRIFTED, no tripwire: "Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/master",
    and `git log -1 --format=%B | grep -ci claude` = 1. The trailer LANDED.
    That is this bead's claim, reproduced, with the smuggled trailer on HEAD
    rather than inferred from which hooks fired.
  DRIFTED, tripwire installed: HEAD does not move (before==after), rebase halts.

FIXED IN 43ade486. `just init` now installs .githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire into
the git common dir's hooks/ as pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push, post-checkout
and post-merge. Under drift that directory is exactly what git runs, and a
reword fires pre-commit and commit-msg -- which under drift ARE the tripwire.
So the reword path is refused rather than gated: the fix does not depend on
teaching anything about rebase shapes, which is what keeps it from inheriting
this bead's own warning that the shape enumeration is incomplete
(--autosquash, --onto, --root and the conflict-resume paths were never
enumerated). Any rebase shape that writes a commit reaches pre-commit or
commit-msg and hits the tripwire; any shape that writes no commit had no
message to smuggle.

Pinned as two rows in .githooks/tests/hooks-drift-tripwire-test.sh:
  "drifted: rebase -i reword REFUSED (bd gqlc-b1kt)"          asserts HEAD did not move
  "drifted: the reword did not smuggle an AI-attribution trailer onto HEAD"
Mutation: with the tripwire's refusal turned into `exit 0`, both go RED and the
second reports the trailer count as 1 -- so the rows witness the trailer, not
just an exit status.

in-tree PROSE and the claude-pre-bash pin still say rebase fires no hooks, and
.githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh:355 still pins `rebase` warn-only. That
statement is false as measured here and in this bead. It is a separate change to
a separate gate with its own pins, and folding it into a hooks-drift branch
would mix two arguments; it needs its own bead if one does not exist.

title: hooks: PR #946 core.hooksPath drift detector is inert in the shared repo, because .claude/settings.json runs the WORKING-TREE copy of claude-pre-bash
description:
MEASURED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, 2026-08-18. This is the repository signature defect — a branch that breaks the rule it was written to establish — in the gate built to prevent it.

PR #946 (bead gqlc-nzwa, merged 96ef5473) is titled "hooks: detect core.hooksPath drift on the first Bash call, not the next just test". It added drift detection to .githooks/claude-pre-bash. Master copy: `grep -c hooksPath` = 8.

IT DID NOT FIRE. During this session core.hooksPath drifted twice from `.githooks` to the empty default dir `/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks`, disarming .githooks/commit-msg (the AI-attribution gate) and every other hook repo-wide. I was not warned either time. The drift was found by a PR reviewer doing unrelated work, not by the detector.

ROOT CAUSE. .claude/settings.json wires the hook as a RELATIVE path: `"command": ".githooks/claude-pre-bash"`. That resolves against the WORKING TREE, not against master. The shared repo cwd is parked on branch `chore/bd-ledger-p2`, which has DIVERGED from master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/master` = false). Its copy of .githooks/claude-pre-bash predates #946: `grep -c hooksPath` = 0.

So the detector exists in master and is inert in the one place it is supposed to run. Same family as the known trap "the shared cwd is a stale ref — grepping it answers about its parked branch, not master", but with a gate rather than a grep as the victim.

THE TRIGGER IS PER-SPAWN, NOT ONE-OFF. Measured: I restored core.hooksPath to .githooks, spawned one agent, and the value had reverted to the default dir on the next read. Agent-worktree registration rewrites the local [core] section of the shared .git/config. A concurrent reviewer independently observed the same recurrence across its own session and reported it. So any repair that is a one-time `git config` is not a fix.

WHY P1. The disarmed set includes commit-msg, which is the only automated enforcement of the no-AI-attribution rule. Every commit made in the shared repo during a drift window is ungated. It is also self-concealing: the gate that would report the condition is the gate the condition disables.

ACCEPTANCE, and note a detector that exits 0 is not a gate:
1. The drift is reported on the first Bash call REGARDLESS of which branch the working tree is parked on. Demonstrate by parking the shared cwd on a pre-#946 commit, drifting core.hooksPath, and watching the warning still fire.
2. Re-verify after an agent spawn specifically, since that is the live trigger.

DESIGN NOTE, not a ruling — the fix likely cannot live only in the working-tree script, since that is precisely what goes stale. Candidates worth weighing: an absolute or git-common-dir-anchored path in settings.json; running the hook from a location that does not track the parked branch; or having the hook re-exec master version. Whoever takes this should also ask whether any OTHER .claude/settings.json hook has the same staleness exposure, because the answer bounds how much this class costs.
notes:
=== NOT CLOSED. The HARM is closed by 43ade486; the LATENCY is not. (Carmack 2026-08-19) ===

Saying explicitly which half my branch reaches, rather than leaving it to be
inferred from a merged PR.

WHAT IS CLOSED. This bead's stated severity is "every commit made in the shared
repo during a drift window is ungated", and that is gone. 43ade486 installs
.githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire into the git common dir's hooks/ -- the directory
the drift redirects core.hooksPath at -- so during a drift window a commit and a
push are REFUSED, from any branch the working tree is parked on, in every linked
worktree at once. Measured in throwaway repos: commit blocked, push blocked,
commit from a linked worktree blocked, `git rebase -i` reword blocked, healthy
state silent and unaffected. The carrier is outside the working tree, which is
the constraint this bead's own design note identifies and which no tracked file
can satisfy.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, i.e. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1 AS WRITTEN. "The drift is
reported on the first Bash call REGARDLESS of which branch the working tree is
parked on." My branch does not touch that path. .claude/settings.json is TRACKED
and wires the hook by the tree-relative path `.githooks/claude-pre-bash`, so on a
checkout parked at a pre-#946 commit BOTH files are the old ones. No edit to
either can fix a checkout parked before that edit -- that is the root cause this
bead identifies, and it is unfixable from inside the tracked tree by
construction. The remaining carriers are (a) an untracked working-tree file --
but .claude/settings.local.json is per-worktree, so it arms one worktree where
.git/hooks arms all of them, which is strictly worse; and (b) something outside
the repo, e.g. a PreToolUse hook by absolute path in ~/.claude/settings.json,
which is a machine-global edit affecting every project and is not a repo change.
I did not make that call unilaterally.

SO THE RESIDUE IS LATENCY, NOT EXPOSURE. Before: drift was silent and commits
were ungated. After: drift is silent until the next commit or push, which then
fails loudly and names `just init`. The window between the drifting write and
the report is no longer a window in which anything ungated can land. Whether
that is still worth a P1 is the lead's call; my reading is it is not, and this
bead should either be re-scoped to "report drift earlier than commit time" or
closed in favour of gqlc-7ijy's option 2 (keep agents off harness worktrees,
which removes the write instead of reporting it).

ALSO ANSWERED, since this bead asks it: "whether any OTHER .claude/settings.json
hook has the same staleness exposure". Yes, one. Round 1's table:
  PreToolUse/Bash  .githooks/claude-pre-bash            tree-relative -> stale
  SessionStart     .githooks/bd-gh-sync pull            tree-relative -> stale
  SessionStart     bd prime                             PATH lookup   -> not exposed
  PreCompact       bd prime                             PATH lookup   -> not exposed
So bd-gh-sync has the identical exposure: parked on an old branch, the session
runs that branch's sync script. That bounds the class at two, and neither is
touched by 43ade486.
2026-08-19 lead: branch fix/hookspath-inert-detector at 43ade486, NOT pushed, no PR yet. Round-1 adversarial review = REVISE (/tmp/lead/verdict-hookspath-r1.md). Design confirmed sound: carrier premise holds (git rev-parse --git-common-dir from a linked worktree returns the main .git, so one install arms all 73 registered worktrees); both drift shapes fail closed; healthy state provably silent (measured: git does NOT fall back to .git/hooks/<name> when core.hooksPath is set); gqlc-b1kt reproduces on all three arms. TWO BLOCKERS: F1 - 'git ignores the exit status of both of these' is FALSE for post-checkout (measured rc=1 on git checkout -b AND git switch; githooks(5) says the exit status BECOMES theirs). True for post-merge only. F2 - check-hooks certifies presence not function: a 3-line file (shebang + marker + exit 0) installed as all five names makes just doctor print 'ok' while a drifted commit LANDS; same for any cp-truncation between 48 and ~2900 bytes. LEAD DECISION: adopt the reviewer's 8.4 - change check-hooks arm 2 from REFUSE to SELF-HEAL (precedent: ensure-golangci, already cited in .githooks/pre-push). Reason: measured, git push --no-verify skips .githooks/pre-push wholesale, dropping just test AND just lint-new, so a refusal unrelated to your commits makes --no-verify the shortest path. Arm 1 (core.hooksPath itself) stays a hard refusal. F3 (cp -> tmp+mv atomic rename) is a hard prerequisite. Round-2 fixer in flight (agent fix-hookspath-r2, log -> /tmp/lead/impl-hookspath-r3.md).

title: factory: /tmp tmpfs exhausts inodes, and the failure looks like a broken tree rather than a full disk
description:
Hit three times on 2026-08-18 by three independent agents.

MEASURED: /tmp is a 16G tmpfs shared by every agent. At 91 registered git worktrees it reached 1048576/1048576 inodes with 4.3G bytes still free. Consequences observed:
- `git worktree add` fails "No space left on device" while `df -h` shows GB free. Two agents deviated from their brief to a sibling path under /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/ as a result.
- `just test` reports "build failed" with NO error text, on a DIFFERENT package set each run, because the build harness cannot write either. One author read this as a real test failure before diagnosing it.
- The Bash tool itself died for one agent.

THE DIAGNOSTIC, worth recording because it is not obvious: "build failed" with no error text on a VARYING package set is a full disk, not a broken tree. And `df -h` is the wrong instrument -- check `df -i`.

REMEDIATION APPLIED ONCE, MANUALLY: removed 70 stale worktrees after checking each for uncommitted state (3 were dirty and kept). Inodes 98% -> 45%. Note `git worktree remove` deletes the checkout ONLY -- commits and branch refs survive in the shared object store, so this is safe for merged branches. A scan for "commits on no remote ref" is a red herring: squash-merge plus auto-delete-branch means every merged PR head looks unpushed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED: agent worktrees are never reaped. Either a `just` recipe that prunes worktrees whose branch is merged and whose status is clean, or a convention that each agent removes its own worktree on exit. The second is unreliable -- quota walls and stall watchdogs kill agents with no warning, which is precisely how these accumulated.
notes:
SECOND AND THIRD INCIDENTS, 2026-08-19 (lead, first-party).

INCIDENT A — BYTE exhaustion, not inodes. /tmp hit 100% of BYTES. Every Bash tool call failed at ENOSPC opening its output file, BEFORE running the command — so the tool is unusable and you cannot even run df to diagnose it without retrying until a concurrent agent frees a block. Measured 12.8G across 1954 entries; 10.5G of it in 621 directories older than 12h.

COMPOSITION — this is the part that changes the bead's proposed remedy:
  93 of the 621 were registered git worktrees. Only 11 were both clean AND ancestors of master.
  528 were PLAIN directories — agent probe/scratch, not worktrees at all:
    /tmp/factory 1.5G (flat dir of logs + PR bodies), /tmp/f3uof 1.0G,
    /tmp/probe937r3 372M, then a long tail of carmack-mut-*, impl-*, author-*, linus-*.
A worktree-only reaper would have freed ~2G of the 10.5G. The bead's remedy (prune merged+clean worktrees) is necessary but NOT sufficient; the plain scratch dirs are the larger half.

INCIDENT B — inode exhaustion again, hit by the gqlc-mmej agent during a 117-run flake loop. 4 runs deviated, all at 1044255/1048576 inodes. The runs ended in the suite's own 'cannot git init' while unrelated tooling hit ENOSPC simultaneously. That agent diagnosed it correctly rather than reporting a flaky test, but only after losing time.

REMEDIATION APPLIED (lead, manual, second time): archived every .md/.txt/.log/.py/.json under old /tmp dirs to /home/antranig/gqlc-tmp-archive-2026-08-19.tar.gz — 690M of text compressed to 43M, cheap insurance — then deleted 580 dirs (all >12h old, PLAIN or clean-worktree, dirty worktrees KEPT). 75% -> 31%.

TRAP FOR THE REAPER, found the hard way: a naive walk of /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d also matches systemd-private-*, .X11-unix, .ICE-unix, .font-unix. Deleting those breaks the user's desktop session. Exclusions must be explicit and must have a test.

Also confirmed the bead's own warning first-party: 'commits on no remote ref' is a red herring. Five gqlc-h9n2-corpus-* branches (26-27 commits each, no PR, a month old) read as stranded by ancestry and proved FULLY LANDED by content — every file present on master, master's copies strictly newer. Test content, never ancestry.

title: ci: check-pr-closes exits 0 with no output when the export lacks external_ref and the PR declares its bead with 'Bead:' rather than 'Refs:'
description:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-17 on PR #951 against master f39a353a's own copy of the script and of .beads/issues.jsonl.

check-pr-closes.py:531-544 reads `ext = bead.get("external_ref") or ""`. When ext is empty it passes. PR #901 made that exit legible -- but only under `if refs is not None`, i.e. only when the PR declared its bead with a 'Refs:' opt-out line. A PR that declares its bead with a 'Bead:' line takes the same exit with refs None, so the print is skipped and the gate produces rc=0 and NO OUTPUT AT ALL.

The comment sitting on that branch (:534-538) says the silent shape 'was the one exit that read a declaration, held its number against nothing, and said so nowhere: rc=0 and no output at all, which is what a gate that never ran also looks like'. That is still exactly true of the 'Bead:' path. The fix was applied to one of the two declaration forms and the twin left live.

The same comment also asserts 'The pass is right -- there is no issue to leave open'. That justification is FALSE when the export is stale rather than the bead genuinely unmirrored. gqlc-l45j has External https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/issues/933 in the live Dolt ledger; master's committed export simply carries no external_ref key for it. So the gate passed a PR whose body says 'Closes #933' having verified nothing, on the grounds that #933 does not exist.

REPRODUCE (read-only, no CI):
  git show origin/master:.beads/issues.jsonl > /tmp/master.jsonl
  git show origin/master:.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py > /tmp/check.py
  gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/pulls/951 --jq '.body // ""' > /tmp/body.txt
  python3 /tmp/check.py /tmp/master.jsonl /tmp/body.txt fix/golangci-provisioning-429
  -> rc=0, zero bytes on stdout and stderr
PR #951's body line 1 is literally 'Bead: gqlc-l45j' and line 3 is 'Closes #933'.

SCOPE OF THE STALE-EXPORT INPUT: only 2 of 459 issue rows in master's export lack external_ref. So this is rare -- and it still hit 1 of the 6 PRs open on 2026-08-17. Rarity is not a defence; the gate is silent in exactly the case where it is wrong.

DISTINCT from the two neighbouring fail-open paths, both separately tracked:
  - :504-505 empty bead_id (no Bead: line, no slug branch) -- that is gqlc-mk7v / GH #903. Measured silent on PRs #946 and #963 the same day.
  - :527-529 bead well-formed but absent from the export -- that one PRINTS ('not in export - skipping') and is the deliberate documented deviation recorded on GH #883. Do not change it.

FIX DIRECTION (two halves, the first not optional):
  1. Legibility: move the print out from under `if refs is not None` so every no-mirror pass says so. The 'Refs:' wording names marker_n, which is None on the 'Bead:' path, so it needs a second phrasing rather than a moved line.
  2. Soundness: 'no external_ref in the export' and 'no GitHub mirror' are not the same proposition, and the comment currently asserts they are. Either stop claiming the pass is right, or distinguish the two -- e.g. treat a missing external_ref on a bead the export DOES carry as unverifiable rather than as proof of no mirror, which is the same fail-closed reasoning check-pr-closes.py's own header already argues for ('Every input this checker cannot read is a failure, not a skip').

Whoever takes this should re-measure the fleet first; the export moves.

title: claude-pre-bash: $(...) inside an unquoted heredoc bypasses the master guard
description:
git_targets() calls strip_heredocs(text) BEFORE substitution_bodies(text), so a command substitution in an UNQUOTED heredoc body is stripped away and never analysed. An unquoted heredoc does expand $(...) in its body, so the command really executes.

Measured (git 2.55.0, fresh repo on master, hook at PR #946 head + r3 commits):

  cat <<EOF > /dev/null
  $(git commit -m sneaky)
  EOF
    -> hook output EMPTY, rc=0  (SILENT ALLOW)

  positive control, same repo, same commit, no heredoc:
  echo $(git commit -m sneaky)
    -> DENY 'Direct commits to master are blocked'

So the instrument was live and the heredoc form is what evades it. Also proved
the underlying shell behaviour directly: an unquoted heredoc body ran
`touch` from a $( ) substitution; a quoted <<'EOF' body did not.

The hook comment (line 11) says heredoc bodies are stripped because 'prose
there never executes'. That is true only for a QUOTED delimiter. PR #946 r3
corrected the comment; the behaviour is unfixed.

Likely fix: extract substitution bodies before stripping heredocs, or strip
only quoted-delimiter heredocs. Needs test rows for both delimiter forms, and
care not to regress the 'heredoc body with prose+apostrophe' allow row.

Found during PR #946 round 3 while auditing universals in the file. Pre-existing;
not introduced by #946.
notes:
=== MERGED 2026-08-18 — PR #992, squash 2d0afedc, GH #960 closed COMPLETED ===

Four review rounds. CI GREEN 7/7 on d27c9c4d; round 4 was body-only (zero Go
diff). Verified at merge: Closes #960 present exactly once and #960 is the right
non-umbrella issue (0 checkbox lines); 0 AI-attribution matches; content on
master.

WHAT THE REVIEW ESTABLISHED FIRST-PARTY (re-taken in a fixture written from
scratch, 26 rows, git 2.55.0, all four hooks armed and each observed firing in
some control, every row carrying a checked effect):
  - revert x2, cherry-pick x2, am, stash push -u, stash pop, tag -a, fetch:
    rc=0, none of the four fired.
  - `git rebase -i` REWORD fires pre-commit AND commit-msg, rc=0, HEAD moved,
    subject genuinely changed. This is the finding that reopened round 3.
  - Ten other rebase shapes (plain onto diverged, --onto, --exec, squash, fixup,
    edit+--continue, conflict+--continue, --autosquash, --no-ff, --no-ff --root):
    rc=0, none of the four fired, HEAD moved.
  - Three shapes (ancestor, all-pick, -i --root) moved no HEAD and therefore
    witness nothing; the body reports rather than counts them. Good.
  - "pins it warn-only" proved LIVE by mutation, not merely present: adding
    "rebase" to HOOK_GATED turns the suite 89 passed/0 failed -> 88/1 with
    "FAIL - unset: rebase only warns (expected warn, got deny-hooks)". ast.parse
    OK, so not a parse kill.

RESIDUE FILED AS BEADS (created before this close, ids read back):
  - gqlc-b1kt — `git rebase -i` reword bypasses the AI-attribution commit-msg
    gate while core.hooksPath is drifted. BEHAVIOURAL, P1, reachable in normal
    operation because agent spawns rewrite core.hooksPath in the shared config.
  - gqlc-tr3c — claude-pre-bash:447's deny message "(commit-msg, pre-commit,
    pre-push and post-merge are all dead)" is false in exactly the fail-closed
    case round 3 disclosed. Pre-existing, identical at cbb11a7e:364.

RESIDUE NOT FILED, recorded here (all mild, none reopened the round):
  - The merged body says three times that commands "ran no hook", where all four
    in-tree carriers say "none of the four". With all 15 client-side hooks armed
    instead of four, almost every row DOES run hooks (post-index-change,
    post-commit, prepare-commit-msg, pre-rebase, post-checkout, post-rewrite);
    only `tag -a` and `fetch` genuinely ran none. Resolvable inside the
    paragraph — it defines the fixture as "exactly" those four armed two
    sentences earlier and every verb is past-tense fixture reporting — which is
    why it was ruled residue. Mechanism worth keeping: prepare-commit-msg fires
    on every rebase row while pre-commit/commit-msg fire only on reword, the
    signature of sequencer.c's run_git_commit() passing -n unless VERIFY_MSG,
    which only TODO_REWORD sets. That is why reword is singular.
  - The author's report asserted a structural body equality that re-derives
    FALSE by exactly one trailing blank line. Report-level, not a durable
    carrier.
  - Hook liveness is argued cross-row (each hook fired in some control) rather
    than per-row; `nhooks` counts files, not executability. post-index-change
    would supply a per-row witness if anyone wants one.

NO CLOSURE OVER REBASE SHAPES, by either side. Untried: --rebase-merges,
-X/--strategy, --update-refs, --fork-point, --keep-base, --signoff,
--committer-date-is-author-date, the break/drop/label/reset/merge todo verbs,
--skip, --abort, and reword reached via --autosquash with an amend!.

FIXTURE GOTCHAS worth not rediscovering: GIT_EDITOR=true may be set ambiently —
unset all four editor variables and re-supply per row, logging each invocation,
or an interactive row that silently no-ops reads as a result. Unset GIT_*_DATE
too: with fixed dates a --no-ff rewrite reproduces byte-identical commits and
reads as HEAD-unmoved. And `pick` with an unchanged parent takes the sequencer's
fast_forward_to() path and creates no commit at all, so those rows can never
witness anything — hence the --no-ff variants.

title: hooks: core.hooksPath drifted to an absolute .git/hooks in the shared config, killing every worktree's local gates
description:
Found 2026-08-17 while landing bd gqlc-l45j, by running `just test` in a fresh sibling worktree.

OBSERVED. `git config --show-origin --get core.hooksPath` read:

  file:/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/config	/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc/.git/hooks

That directory holds 14 files, all of them `.sample`, and git ignores a
`.sample`. So core.hooksPath pointed at a real directory with zero live hooks.

BLAST RADIUS. The value lives in the SHARED .git/config (extensions.worktreeConfig
is not set), so it applied to the main checkout and to all 14 sibling worktrees
at once. For as long as it stood, every agent session in this factory committed
and pushed with:
  - no pre-commit master/main branch guard
  - no pre-commit gofumpt/gci format gate
  - no pre-push `just test`
  - no pre-push `just lint-new`
  - no commit-msg AI-attribution guard (the one .githooks/commit-msg enforces
    and CLAUDE.md relies on being enforced 'at commit time')

An absolute path is the specific shape bd gqlc-5fm predicted: the recipe compares
the configured VALUE rather than testing the directory, precisely because
.git/hooks exists and an existence test would pass.

DESIGN, and why the two candidates named here were both rejected. This bead
already rules out a check at the top of .githooks/pre-commit (a dead hook does
not run). A post-checkout/post-merge assertion in .githooks/ fails for the same
reason: the drift is what stops .githooks/ being reached at all. A CI job that
"refuses a PR whose commits show no evidence of local gating" fails on the
premise -- CI cannot see local git config, and a commit records no evidence of
which hooks ran, so there is nothing for such a job to key on.

What was built instead inverts the problem. The drift points core.hooksPath at
the git common dir's hooks/ (spelled absolutely, or by being unset, which is the
same directory by default). In that state .githooks/ is dead but THAT directory
is precisely what git runs -- it just holds nothing but *.sample files, which
git ignores. So `just init` now installs .githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire there,
as pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push, post-checkout and post-merge. Healthy: git
never looks there, zero noise. Drifted: it refuses the commit or the push and
names `just init`.

Carrier: the git common dir, OUTSIDE the working tree. That is what makes it
survive an arbitrary parked branch, which is the constraint gqlc-pyk2 is about
(every TRACKED file is at the parked commit, so a tracked-only fix cannot work).
It is also shared by every linked worktree, so one `just init` anywhere arms all
~20 at once -- the same sharing that makes the drift repo-wide.

IT FAILS, LOUDLY, PROVEN. All experiments in throwaway repos; this repo's shared
config was read, never written.
  drifted to the absolute common-dir path -> commit REFUSED, HEAD unmoved
  core.hooksPath unset                    -> commit REFUSED
  drifted                                 -> push REFUSED
  drifted, from a LINKED worktree         -> commit REFUSED
  drifted, `git rebase -i` reword         -> REFUSED (closes gqlc-b1kt)
  healthy                                 -> commit lands, the repo's own hook ran
Mutation, because a green suite proves nothing: turning the refusal into
`exit 0` reddens 6 of 12 rows; deleting one installed tripwire, chmod -x'ing
one, or letting a foreign script squat the name each makes `just doctor` exit 1.
`just init` refuses to clobber a hook it did not write.

post-checkout and post-merge WARN rather than refuse, by measurement, and the
distinction is stated so the warn arm is not mistaken for the gate: git ignores
their exit status, and a non-zero post-checkout makes `git worktree add` return
1 AFTER creating the worktree -- a half-failed agent spawn that still does not
prevent the drift. The gate is the other three.

never reached, because git then runs that directory's hooks. `just check-hooks`

description:
A branch-close hook closed `gqlc-rz0l` citing SHA `3dd322dc`, annotating it "not yet
pushed". That SHA was discarded by a rebase before anything reached a remote, so the
close recorded work that never landed and the bead's true state was `in_progress`.

WITNESSED 2026-08-17 on `docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift` (PR #804), re-verified
first-party from the branch worktree:

    git cat-file -t 3dd322dc          -> commit   (the object survives locally)
    git branch -r --contains 3dd322dc -> EMPTY    (no remote ref contains it)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 3dd322dc origin/master  -> rc=1
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 3dd322dc 83de07af       -> rc=1  (branch head)

So the SHA is an ancestor of neither master nor the branch it was closed against. A
local-only commit is exactly the thing a rebase discards, and "not yet pushed" is the
hook naming that condition in the annotation while closing anyway.

## The defect

A close hook must not close a bead against a SHA no ref contains. Reachability from
some ref is the cheapest available proxy for "this work exists somewhere other than
one developer's index", and it is machine-checkable at hook time with the two commands
above. Closing on an unpushed SHA converts a rebase — an ordinary, expected operation —
into silent ledger corruption.

Suggested posture: refuse the close (or downgrade it to a note) when
`git branch -r --contains <sha>` is empty, and say which SHA and which ref set were
checked. Warning without failing is not enough; a close that already happened is the
damage.

## Scope

This is the *hook* half only. The other half — that a bead wrongly closed this way
cannot be corrected through the export, because `bdguard` refuses every reopen by
construction — is `gqlc-npyp`, which explicitly defers this defect to its own bead
("SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT worth its own bead").

The hook was not located during this investigation: `.githooks/` (`pre-push`,
`post-merge`, `bd-gh-sync`, `commit-msg`, `pre-commit`, `claude-pre-bash`) carries no
`bd close` call, so the actor is elsewhere — a `bd`-side branch-close feature or an
agent-harness hook. Identifying it is the first step of the fix.

Deliberately NOT fixed in PR #804: out of that PR's territory (a spec-fence prose and
pin change). PR #804 leaves `gqlc-rz0l` `in_progress` with a close-on-merge note.

## Orchestrator triage, 2026-08-18 at master 7ccd47c8 — HELD, not staffed

The bead says "Identifying [the actor] is the first step of the fix." I did that
step. Result: **the actor is not in this repository's tree.**

  git grep -n 'bd close' 7ccd47c8 -- .

returns only documentation and ledger data, never an executable call site:
  AGENTS.md:139                     - the quick-reference table
  CLAUDE.md:16                      - the same table
  docs/specs/codegen-stage-c6.md:816 - prose describing a close that was done
  .beads/issues.jsonl               - bead descriptions quoting themselves

No `.githooks/*` script invokes `bd close`, confirming the round-1 finding.
`.claude/settings.json` registers only `bd prime` (SessionStart);
`.claude/settings.local.json` allow-lists `bd list/show/github/config/...` and
does **not** grant or invoke `bd close`.

So the closing actor is one of:
  (a) `bd`'s own branch-close feature, i.e. upstream github.com/gastownhall/beads;
  (b) an agent-harness hook living outside this working tree.

Either way **the fix is not a gqlc code change**, which materially changes this
bead's shape from "fix the hook" to "either file upstream, or add a local
compensating guard."

### Why it is held rather than worked now

A local compensating guard would have to live in `.githooks/`, and `.githooks/`
is contested territory today: PR #946 owns `claude-pre-bash` and its suite, and
PR #901 owns `.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh`. Landing a third change
there now buys a rebase for no benefit.

### What to do when it is picked up

1. Decide (a) vs (b) by capturing the close as it happens — the annotation text
   "not yet pushed" is a literal string and should identify its emitter.
2. If (a), this is an upstream report and the gqlc-side action is at most a
   `bdguard` / `pre-push` reachability check.
3. Prefer refuse-the-close over warn: the bead's own analysis is right that a
   close that already happened is the damage.

Status left as-is; nobody is working it. The `in_progress` state is residue from
a quota-killed agent, not an active claim.

title: bdguard: a bead wrongly auto-closed against a discarded SHA cannot be reopened through the export
description:
`internal/tools/bdguard/main.go` refuses any reopen (closed at base, not closed at head) and its `.beads/allowed-drops.txt` allowlist is drops-only BY CONSTRUCTION — main.go:162 says so verbatim: "a reopen is not exempted there". There is therefore no sanctioned way to correct a bead that was closed wrongly.

WITNESSED 2026-08-17, gqlc-rz0l. A branch-close hook auto-closed it against SHA 3dd322dc. That SHA was discarded by a rebase: `git branch -r --contains 3dd322dc` is empty, and it is an ancestor of NEITHER origin/master NOR the branch head 83de07af. The work has not landed, so in_progress is the true state and master's export is wrong. Running `just bd-export-monotonic-local` on a ledger branch carrying the correction:

    bdguard: .beads/issues.jsonl regressed against d41895e5
      reopened issues (closed at base, not closed at head):
        - gqlc-rz0l (base=closed, head=in_progress)

The ledger PR (chore/bd-ledger-p3) had to carry BASE's record for that one bead rather than defeat the gate, so the export now knowingly disagrees with the live ledger, and will re-regress on every subsequent ledger PR until PR #804 merges and closes it for real.

WHY THE GATE IS RIGHT TO EXIST: it catches a stale export silently reverting other teams' ledger work, which has happened. The absolutism is the deliberate design — an allowlist that exempted reopens would let exactly the defect through. So the fix is NOT simply to add allowed-reopens.txt with the same shape.

WHAT A FIX HAS TO DISTINGUISH: a reopen that is a REVERT (an old export overwriting a newer close) from a reopen that is a CORRECTION (a close that was never earned). The distinguishing evidence in the witnessed case is that the closing SHA is contained by no ref. That is machine-checkable: if a bead's close cites a SHA, and `git cat-file -e` / `git branch -r --contains` cannot place it on any ref, the close is unearned and reopening it is a correction, not a revert. Consider requiring a reopen to carry that evidence rather than a bare id.

SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT worth its own bead if this one narrows: the close hook fired on a SHA that was never pushed and later discarded. A close hook should refuse to close against a SHA no remote ref contains.
notes:
2026-08-17: the SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT named at the end of this description is now filed as gqlc-90vt (close hook must refuse a SHA no ref contains). This bead keeps the bdguard/export half.

title: ci: the Closes gate passes vacuously when the PR body has no Bead: line and the branch carries no gqlc- slug
description:
`ci.yml:102` runs `check-pr-closes.py .beads/issues.jsonl "$bead_id"`. $bead_id is derived from a `Bead: gqlc-...` line in the PR body, falling back to a `gqlc-[a-z0-9.]+` match on the branch name. When neither yields anything, $bead_id is the empty string and the script's documented contract is 'PASS if: no bead found'.

So a PR whose body omits a Bead: line AND whose branch is named descriptively rather than by slug is never checked at all, however many Closes lines it carries and whatever numbers they name.

MEASURED LIVE on PR #845 (2026-08-17). Branch `fix/codegen-reserved-set-completeness` — no slug. Body — no `Bead:` line. Body carries three closing lines: `Closes #838`, `Closes #840`, `Closes #861`. The gate is green and has verified none of them. #838 maps to bead gqlc-fd06, which is OPEN and was deferred as separate work; #861 maps to gqlc-qx5p, OPEN; #840 has no bead mirror at all.

This is a THIRD fail-open path, distinct from the two PR #901 is fixing (its BLOCKER A: the regex knows 3 of GitHub's 9 closing keywords and only the bare #N form; its BLOCKER B: `^[ \t]*Refs:` also matches the 4-space indented-code-block spelling). Those two are about a PR that DOES name a bead. This one is about a PR that names none, and it predates #901 — it is master's behaviour today.

The compounding factor is the ledger: a bead absent from master's committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` export ALSO reads as 'no bead found'. As of 2026-08-17 the branch chore/bd-ledger-p2 was 11 commits unmerged, leaving gqlc-yb0w, gqlc-uc8f, gqlc-u039, gqlc-856f and gqlc-u91z absent from master's export and therefore ungated by this same clause.

Fix direction (NOT settled — the tradeoff is real): requiring a Bead: line on every PR would fail-close but breaks chore/ and docs-only PRs that legitimately have no bead. A narrower option is to fail-closed only when the body CONTAINS a closing keyword but no resolvable bead, since that is the case where the PR is making a claim nobody checks. Silence with no Closes line at all can stay a PASS.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description's citation, and a fleet-wide measurement.

The description cites `ci.yml:102` passing `$bead_id`. That is stale: gqlc-w4al
has since landed, and master's gate is now `ci.yml:132-145`, which fetches the
LIVE PR body from the API into a file and calls
`check-pr-closes.py .beads/issues.jsonl "${RUNNER_TEMP}/pr-body.txt" "$BRANCH"`.
Bead resolution moved INSIDE the Python script. The defect is unchanged — the
resolution order is still `Bead:` line in body, then a `gqlc-[a-z0-9.]+` match on
the branch name, then empty-string, and empty still takes the pass path.

Measured 2026-08-17 against master `dc8d10fa`'s export and master's own copy of
the script, run over all six open PRs with each PR's live body fetched from the
API:

  PR 901 [fix/closes-gate-opt-out]                  rc=0  gqlc-1ekq -> Closes #862 (ok)
  PR 804 [docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift]              rc=0  gqlc-rz0l -> Closes #715 (ok)
  PR 882 [fix/live-recipe-structural-selection]     rc=0  NO OUTPUT
  PR 881 [fix/resolver-sealed-sum-claim]            rc=0  NO OUTPUT
  PR 868 [fix/bd-gh-sync-timestamp-tiebreak]        rc=0  NO OUTPUT
  PR 845 [fix/codegen-reserved-set-completeness]    rc=0  NO OUTPUT

Four of six open PRs are not checked at all. The two that ARE checked are the
only two whose bodies carry a `Bead:` line; no branch in the fleet carries a
gqlc- slug, so the branch-name fallback fires for none of them. The four silent
passes carry seven `Closes` lines between them, all unverified — and PR #845's
`Closes #838` is an independently suspected over-claim (GH #838 = bead gqlc-fd06,
which is OPEN and deferred as separate work).

This is not a rate; it is what the fleet happens to look like today. The point is
that a silent pass and a verified pass are indistinguishable in the log, so the
green check tells a reviewer nothing about which one happened.

Reproduce without touching CI:
  git show origin/master:.beads/issues.jsonl > /tmp/master.jsonl
  git show origin/master:.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py > /tmp/check.py
  gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/pulls/<N> --jq '.body // ""' > /tmp/body.txt
  python3 /tmp/check.py /tmp/master.jsonl /tmp/body.txt "<branch>"

Fix direction is unchanged and still needs deciding: either make an unresolvable
bead a FAILURE (the script's own header already argues 'Every input this checker
cannot read is a failure, not a skip'), or require a `Bead:` line on every PR and
fail without one. The first is consistent with the doc the script already ships.

Deliberately out of scope for PR #901 — this is master's behaviour today and not
something #901 introduced.

RULING (2026-08-18, orchestrator). The description leaves the fix direction open between "make an unresolvable bead a FAILURE" and "require a Bead: line on every PR". Neither extreme. Take the narrow middle option the description itself proposes:

  FAIL when the body carries a closing keyword AND no bead resolves.
  PASS when no bead resolves and the body carries no closing keyword.

Rationale. The defect is a PR making a closing claim nobody checks. A chore/ or docs-only PR that closes nothing is making no claim, so demanding a Bead: line from it buys nothing and breaks legitimate traffic. Fail-closed exactly where a claim exists and cannot be verified; stay silent where there is no claim. This also matches the script header's own argument that "every input this checker cannot read is a failure, not a skip", scoped to inputs that actually assert something.

Two constraints on the implementation, both measured 2026-08-18 against master f39a353a:

1. Do NOT touch the :527-529 "bead not in export - skipping" path. That is the deliberate deviation recorded on GH #883 and it prints, so it is legible. It stays a PASS.

2. Use the WIDE closing-keyword matcher (GH_CLOSES, the nine GitHub keywords) rather than the narrow CLOSES, and match over prose_only() output. Reasoning to verify rather than inherit: the file's own comment at :132-140 argues GH_CLOSES may be widened freely because a hit there refuses and a miss in CLOSES also refuses, so widening cannot newly PASS a PR. The same asymmetry applies here -- the new test is in the refusing direction, so the wide matcher is the fail-closed choice. Confirm that reasoning holds for this new call site before relying on it; do not assume it transfers.

FLEET IMPACT, measured before this ruling was written, over the six PRs open on 2026-08-18 using master's own copy of the script and export:

  PR 946  fix/hookspath-drift-detection            no bead resolves, body has Closes #902  -> WOULD NEWLY FAIL
  PR 963  fix/resolver-unlabelled-edge-narrowing   no bead resolves, body has Closes #780  -> WOULD NEWLY FAIL
  PR 951  fix/golangci-provisioning-429            Bead: line present -> unaffected by this bead (it hits gqlc-63ao's path instead)
  PR 965, 966, 968                                 Bead: line present, unaffected

So this fix turns two currently-green PRs red. That is the gate working, and the remediation is one line in each body. Whoever implements it must RE-MEASURE the fleet at the time of implementation -- the set of open PRs moves -- and report which PRs the change would newly fail, so the merge can be sequenced rather than discovered.

COMPANION. gqlc-63ao is the same function, the same class, and the same file: a third silent PASS at :531-544 when the export lacks external_ref and the PR used a Bead: line rather than a Refs: line. Ship both in one PR; splitting them means two rebases over one file.
