title: config: multi-target generation — one schema, many generated packages (sqlc-style)
description:
Widen the gqlc config file from a single generation target to a list of targets, mirroring sqlc's version-2 `sql:` list. One schema file, many query directories, each producing its own Go package in its own output directory.

Wire shape (breaking change to version 1 — no v2, no users yet; user ratified 2026-07-24):

    version: 1
    graph:
      - schema: schema.gql
        schema_language: gql
        queries: internal/user/query
        query_language: opencypher
        procsig: procs.procsig.json   # optional
        gen:
          go:
            package: userdb
            out: internal/user/gen
            driver: neo4j-go-v5

Design decisions ratified with the user before any code:
- `schema` repeats per entry (sqlc-identical), not hoisted to the document root.
- `gen: go:` nesting mirrored from sqlc; `output` renamed `out` and moved under it, `driver` alongside it (the analogue of sqlc's `sql_package`).
- Top-level list key is `graph` (the analogue of sqlc's `sql`).
- version stays 1; the old flat shape simply stops loading.
- Setup failures (missing schema, empty query dir, bad procsig) fail fast, prefixed `graph[i]: `. Query-level diagnostics still accumulate across every target.
- `gqlc init` authors one target; a new `--add` flag appends one more.

Lands as a 4-branch gt stack: spec → config → pipeline → cli.
close_reason: All 4 branches merged (#374, #379, #386, #389). Acceptance criteria §12 verified end-to-end against a built binary on 2026-07-25: two-target generate produces two packages in two directories with a byte-identical second run; nested out rejected at load naming both entries; tripwire abort names the entry and the offending file and leaves target 0 byte-identical; old flat shape reports the shape change; a null entry reports graph[1], not a shifted index; init --add is wired and TTY-gated. Residual prose defects filed as gqlc-5ta and gqlc-ayq; test gap as gqlc-5yg.

title: schema/gql: support ISO GQL phrase-form node and edge type declarations (currently silently dropped)
description:
`GQL.g4` implements both ISO GQL alternatives for element type declarations:

    nodeTypeSpecification : nodeTypePattern | nodeTypePhrase    # GQL.g4:1501-1504
    edgeTypeSpecification : edgeTypePattern | edgeTypePhrase    # GQL.g4:1549-1552

`internal/schema/gql/listener.go` implements only the *pattern* branches —
`EnterNodeTypePattern` (listener.go:106) and `EnterEdgeTypePattern`
(listener.go:154). There is no `EnterNodeTypePhrase` or `EnterEdgeTypePhrase`.

A phrase-form declaration therefore parses without error, the walk collects
nothing, and `rawSchema.resolve()` (resolve.go:26) returns an **empty schema
with no error at all**.

## Repro

Valid ISO GQL that silently yields an empty schema:

    CREATE GRAPH TYPE SocialNetworkSchema AS {
      NODE Person LABEL Person { id STRING, name STRING, joined_date DATE },
      NODE Company LABEL Company { id STRING, name STRING, industry STRING },
      DIRECTED EDGE KNOWS LABELS KNOWS { since INT }
        CONNECTING (Person TO Person),
      DIRECTED EDGE WORKS_FOR LABELS WORKS_FOR { role STRING, start_year INT }
        CONNECTING (Person TO Company)
    }

with `match (p1:Person)-[r:KNOWS]->(p2:Person) ... return p1, p2, r` gives:

    internal/user/db/user.cypher: query FindPersonTest: unknown label: Person

The error blames the query file. The query is correct; the schema is the fault
and is never mentioned.

Isolated confirmation (2026-07-24):
- pattern-form `Person` + phrase-form `Company` -> `unknown label: Company`
- pattern-form nodes + `DIRECTED EDGE ... CONNECTING (p TO c)` ->
  `unknown edge: Person-[WORKS_FOR]->Company`
- converting every declaration to pattern form generates all four files
  correctly

## Why this is a contract violation, not just a gap

errors.go:5-7 states these are "Errors returned by Parse for GQL this parser
rejects: constructs outside the supported subset", and the listener *does*
loudly reject label implication (`ErrLabelImplication`), undirected edges
(`ErrUndirectedEdge`) and unsupported graph type sources
(`ErrUnsupportedSource`). Phrase form is the sole unsupported construct that is
neither supported nor rejected.

## Explicitly NOT part of this bug

All three were suspected during triage and verified legal and working:

- `CREATE GRAPH TYPE` without `PROPERTY` — `PROPERTY?` is optional
- `LABEL <name>` / `LABELS <spec>` — GQL.g4:1679-1683; `labelSet()`
  (nodetype.go:23-40) already handles both branches
- untyped properties `id STRING` — `propertyType : propertyName typed?
  propertyValueType` (GQL.g4:1701), `typed?` optional

The grammar is a faithful ISO GQL grammar and is not the problem.
design:
## 1. `EnterNodeTypePhrase` -> `rawNode`

    nodeTypePhrase       : nodeSynonym TYPE? nodeTypePhraseFiller (AS localNodeTypeAlias)?
    nodeTypePhraseFiller : nodeTypeName nodeTypeFiller? | nodeTypeFiller

Name from `nodeTypeName`, alias from `AS localNodeTypeAlias`, labels and
properties by reusing the existing `nodeContent(...)` helper (listener.go:197).
No new label or property code is needed — `labelSet()` already handles the
`LABEL` and `LABELS` branches.

## 2. `EnterEdgeTypePhrase` -> `rawEdge`

    edgeTypePhrase       : edgeKind edgeSynonym TYPE? edgeTypePhraseFiller endpointPairPhrase
    edgeTypePhraseFiller : edgeTypeName edgeTypeFiller? | edgeTypeFiller
    endpointPairPhrase   : CONNECTING endpointPair

Reuse `edgeContent(...)` (listener.go:221) for labels and properties. Map
`endpointPair` to `rawEndpoint`.

Two behaviours must match the pattern-form path:
- `endpointPairUndirected` must be rejected with `ErrUndirectedEdge`, mirroring
  `EnterEdgeTypePatternUndirected` (listener.go:150). Otherwise undirected edges
  become silently droppable again through the phrase door.
- `endpointPairPointingLeft` lists `destinationNodeTypeAlias` first; normalise to
  canonical source->target, as the pattern path already does (listener.go:177-180).

Note `edgeKind` is **mandatory** in phrase form but optional in pattern form, and
`connectorUndirected : TO | TILDE` overlaps `connectorPointingRight : TO |
RIGHT_ARROW`. `CONNECTING (a TO b)` therefore resolves as pointing-right only
because `endpointPair` lists the directed alternative first and ANTLR takes the
first match. This bead depends on that behaviour, so add a test pinning it;
gqlc-h9n.10 owns the wider ambiguity write-up.

## 3. Endpoint references are ALIAS-ONLY — resolved, see notes

    endpointPairPointingRight : LEFT_PAREN sourceNodeTypeAlias connectorPointingRight destinationNodeTypeAlias RIGHT_PAREN
    sourceNodeTypeAlias       : regularIdentifier

`CONNECTING (Person TO Person)` requires `Person` to be a declared **local
alias**; a `<node type name>` is not a valid endpoint reference. resolve.go:47-49
already populates the alias table only from `localNodeTypeAlias`, which is
correct — implement alias-only resolution and do **not** add a type-name
fallback, which would be a gqlc dialect.

The evidence and its tier are in the notes. It is INFERRED, not CITED: ISO/IEC
39075:2024 is paywalled and no public source containing the Syntax Rules for
`<endpoint pair>` could be located. Alias-only is also the conservative
direction — it rejects what the standard may reject, rather than accepting what
it may forbid — so a later citation can only widen what is accepted.

The error for the alias-less spelling must be precise: it must name that an alias
was expected and that the referenced node type declares none, not surface a bare
`ErrUnknownEndpoint`.

## 4. Empty-graph-type guard (`ErrEmptyGraphType`)

`resolve()` must reject a graph type that declares zero node types.
`ErrNoGraphType` covers "no graph type statement"; nothing covers "graph type
whose body declared no element types".

**This guard catches the total-silence case only.** A mixed schema — some
declarations in pattern form, one in phrase form — leaves `r.nodes` non-empty,
passes the guard, and still drops the phrase declaration silently (verified
2026-07-25). It is a narrow backstop, not the structural fix. The structural fix
is the branch-exhaustiveness test in gqlc-h9n.2, which this bead depends on.

Note the guard is not reachable through an empty body: `elementTypeList` requires
at least one element, so `CREATE GRAPH TYPE G AS { }` is a syntax error (verified
2026-07-25). It is reachable only via an unhandled branch — which is exactly why
the exhaustiveness test is the real remedy.

## 5. Fixtures for BOTH forms

Every existing fixture (`test/data/**`, README.md:35) uses pattern form
exclusively — that is precisely why this shipped. Add phrase-form coverage, and
prefer a paired-equivalence test: the same graph type spelled both ways must
resolve to an equal `schema.Schema`.
acceptance_criteria:
EnterNodeTypePhrase and EnterEdgeTypePhrase collect name, alias, labels and properties, reusing the existing nodeContent/edgeContent/labelSet helpers.
The alias-bearing repro schema in the description generates without error and produces a schema.Schema equal to its pattern-form equivalent.
The alias-less spelling fails with an error naming that an endpoint alias was expected and that the referenced node type declares none — not a bare ErrUnknownEndpoint.
Undirected endpoint pairs in phrase form are rejected with ErrUndirectedEdge, matching pattern-form behaviour.
Left-pointing endpoint pairs are normalised to canonical source->target.
A test pins CONNECTING (a TO b) as pointing-right, since the TO connector is grammatically ambiguous and this bead relies on ANTLR alternative order.
resolve() rejects a graph type resolving to zero node types via a new ErrEmptyGraphType sentinel, documented as catching the total-silence case only.
Fixtures cover both forms; a paired-equivalence test asserts pattern and phrase spellings of the same graph type resolve identically.
The PR restates the alias-only decision and its INFERRED evidence tier.
notes:
## RESOLVED 2026-07-25 — endpoint references are ALIAS-ONLY

Verdict: `CONNECTING (Person TO Person)` requires `Person` to be a **declared
local alias**. A `<node type name>` is NOT a valid endpoint reference. Implement
alias-only resolution; do NOT add a type-name fallback.

Evidence tier: **INFERRED, independently corroborated** — not a direct citation
of the ISO Syntax Rules. ISO/IEC 39075:2024 is paywalled and no public draft
containing the Syntax Rules for `<endpoint pair>` could be located. Flagging that
honestly so a future reader knows the strength of the claim.

**One decisive argument, two supporting:**

1. **Grammar, deliberate asymmetry (strong — this is the argument that carries
   the conclusion).** The pattern form's `sourceNodeTypeReference`
   (GQL.g4:1618-1621) accepts *either* an alias *or* an inline `nodeTypeFiller`
   (i.e. a label reference). The phrase form's `endpointPairPointingRight`
   (GQL.g4:1646-1648) accepts **only** a bare alias — no filler alternative. Had
   the standard intended endpoints in a `CONNECTING` clause to be referenceable
   by name or label, the filler alternative was right there in the adjacent rule
   and was not used.

2. **Grammar, reference positions (supporting only — weaker than first
   assessed).** `nodeTypeName` occurs at exactly two sites in GQL.g4 — 1507
   (`nodeTypePattern`) and 1515 (`nodeTypePhraseFiller`) — both *declaration*
   positions, plus its own rule at 2860. It appears in no reference position
   anywhere in the grammar.

   Demoted from "strong" on review: `sourceNodeTypeAlias : regularIdentifier`
   (GQL.g4:1669) means the grammar structurally *cannot* carry a distinct
   type-name reference in that slot — a name and an alias are the same token
   shape. So `nodeTypeName`'s absence from reference positions is what you would
   observe whether the static semantics bound type names or not. It is
   consistent with the conclusion but does not discriminate between the
   hypotheses.

3. **Independent expert corroboration (supporting).** Alex Miłowski's worked GQL
   graph-type example writes the alias explicitly and then references it:

       NODE :Person => :Thing { ... } AS Person
       DIRECTED EDGE knows {} CONNECTING (Person -> Person)

   with the note: *"In phrase version, you'll see that `AS Person` added to the
   declaration of the `Person` node type. This seems necessary as the endpoint
   pair phrase requires a local alias."*
   https://www.milowski.com/journal/entry/2024-06-26T12:00:00-07:00/

   Corroboration at the same tier, not a citation of the prose: his "seems
   necessary" shows he is reading the same grammar.

Supporting, non-decisive: Microsoft Fabric's GQL graph types reference (reviewed
by Stefan Plantikow, a GQL standard editor) uses the pattern form exclusively —
`(:Person)-[:knows { ... }]->(:Person)` — and states endpoint references resolve
by key label: *"You only need to specify the key labels ... for endpoint node
types ... The system resolves these references to the full node type
definitions."* That matches gqlc's existing pattern-form `fillerLabels`
behaviour. The page contains no `CONNECTING` example at all.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/graph/gql-graph-types

**Why acting on an inference is acceptable here.** Alias-only is the conservative
direction: it refuses a spelling the standard may also refuse. If a citation
later shows type names *are* bound, the fix widens what gqlc accepts and breaks
no existing schema. The opposite guess — inventing a type-name fallback — would
create a gqlc dialect that later has to be taken away.

## Consequence for the repro schema

The alias-less original from the user's sandbox is **not conformant** — its
`CONNECTING` clauses reference node type *names*. The conformant spelling adds
`AS <alias>`, one clause per node type:

    CREATE GRAPH TYPE SocialNetworkSchema AS {
      NODE Person LABEL Person { id STRING, name STRING, joined_date DATE } AS Person,
      NODE Company LABEL Company { id STRING, name STRING, industry STRING } AS Company,
      DIRECTED EDGE KNOWS LABELS KNOWS { since INT }
        CONNECTING (Person TO Person),
      DIRECTED EDGE WORKS_FOR LABELS WORKS_FOR { role STRING, start_year INT }
        CONNECTING (Person TO Company)
    }

An alias may share a node type's spelling (`AS Person`), so this stays readable.

Verified 2026-07-25: this spelling produces **no syntax error** from the current
grammar — it fails only with `unknown label: Person`, i.e. it parses and is then
silently dropped. So it is the correct headline repro and acceptance fixture for
this bead: it must generate successfully once phrase form is collected. The
description has been corrected to use it.

Keep the alias-less original as a second fixture asserting a *precise* error — it
must name that an alias was expected and that the referenced node type declares
none, rather than surfacing a bare `ErrUnknownEndpoint`.

## Not in scope, filed separately

Research on 2026-07-25 established that essentially all graph-type DDL is
*optional* in GQL 1.0 (Annex D feature IDs; see the
`iso-gql-annex-d-optional-features` bd memory), and that node type identity
should be the key label set rather than the complete label set (see
`gqlc-iso-node-type-identity`). Neither changes this bead: phrase form is a
*silent drop*, which is a defect regardless of whether the construct is optional.
The identity and satisfaction work is gqlc-h9n.7 and gqlc-h9n.8.
close_reason:
Landed in PR #395 (squash-merged 2026-07-26). EnterNodeTypePhrase/EnterEdgeTypePhrase now consume the phrase-form alternatives that GQL.g4 always parsed and the listener silently dropped, including the LABEL/LABELS keyword form and alias binding. Corpus resolution 32 -> 38 of 86; grammar coverage unchanged at 133/133/46 (the constructs were always reached on the parse tree — what was missing was consumption). ErrUnsupportedPhraseForm deleted with no danglers, TestSentinelReachability green. ErrUnknownEndpoint split with ErrEndpointNotAlias for a CONNECTING endpoint naming a node type rather than its alias.

Two declinations recorded in the PR body and verified by the reviewer as correct ISO readings, not gaps: no type-name fallback for CONNECTING endpoints (the grammar slot is sourceNodeTypeAlias, not the sourceNodeTypeReference the pattern form uses), and no ErrEmptyGraphType (AS { } is a parser syntax error, so the sentinel would be unreachable and unpinnable).

One re-sentinelling: phrase_form_undirected_connector.gql moves to ErrUndirectedEdge rather than resolves, because connectorUndirected: TO | TILDE means CONNECTING (a ~ b) has no canonical source->target — same reason the pattern-form ~[ ]~ is rejected.

Reviewer verified all seven claims against the tree and caught six of seven mutations thrown at new and adjacent code; the seventh escapes only in a weak reordering form the code comment does not claim to forbid.

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
Scope narrowed by team-lead ruling, 2026-07-25 (gqlc-h9n.2 phase 1).

The corpus in gqlc-h9n.2 cannot land green while phrase form is *silently dropped*: such an entry is neither `resolves` (the model is empty or short) nor `unsupported` (no sentinel exists). Rather than add a third `silentlyDropped` outcome — which would ship nothing to the user, pin the bad behaviour as expected, and give future authors an escape hatch for making the gate green — gqlc-h9n.2 adds **`ErrUnsupportedPhraseForm`** and rejects phrase form loudly.

Consequences for this bead:

1. The class-3 half (undocumented rejection) is discharged by gqlc-h9n.2, not here. By the time this bead starts, phrase form already fails with a named sentinel and the diagnostic already lands on the schema file instead of the user's query file — which is the actual user-visible fix for the complaint that started the epic.
2. This bead's scope narrows to **implementing** phrase form: `EnterNodeTypePhrase` / `EnterEdgeTypePhrase`, alias-only endpoint resolution per the RESOLVED note above, and removing the sentinel.
3. **This bead's red is a reclassification**, not a new failing test: flip the phrase-form corpus entries from `unsupported` to `resolves` and bump `wantCorpusResolving`. The corpus already asserts every element type declaration reaches the model, so the silent-drop guard is what proves the implementation actually collected them.
4. Removing `ErrUnsupportedPhraseForm` is not free: `TestSentinelReachability` sweeps bidirectionally, so its `allSentinels` entry and its `invalid/` fixture must be deleted in the same PR.

Same pattern applies to gqlc-h9n.1 (COPY OF → ErrUnsupportedSource).

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
Grammar fact that sharpens this bead's value (team-lead, 2026-07-25).

endpointPairPhrase is referenced at exactly one site in GQL.g4 — line 1558, inside
edgeTypePhrase. Nothing else in the grammar reaches it. So implementing the phrase
form is what unlocks the entire CONNECTING endpoint syntax: every endpointPair*
and connector* rule (endpointPairPhrase, endpointPair, endpointPairDirected,
endpointPairPointingRight, endpointPairPointingLeft, endpointPairUndirected,
connectorPointingRight, connectorUndirected) plus the tokens CONNECTING, TO,
TILDE, RIGHT_ARROW and LEFT_ARROW are unreachable without it.

That is roughly ten of the required-133 rules and five of the required-133 tokens
riding on this one bead, which makes it a bigger slice of ISO surface than the
'phrase form is an alternative spelling' framing suggests. Node side is much
smaller by comparison: nodeTypePhrase and nodeTypePhraseFiller only, because
nodeTypeFiller is shared with nodeTypePattern and sourceNodeTypeReference.

Also note RIGHT_ARROW ('->', connectorPointingRight) is a different token from
BRACKET_RIGHT_ARROW (']->', arcTypePointingRight). The pattern form uses the
bracketed family exclusively; the bare arrows are phrase-form only.

Until this bead lands, gqlc-h9n.2's corpus classifies all of the above as
unsupported with ErrUnsupportedPhraseForm — a sentinel added by h9n.2 purely to
convert today's silent drop into a loud rejection. This bead deletes that sentinel
and flips those entries to resolves, which is its red-green cycle.

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
Acceptance criterion is now mechanical, from the gqlc-h9n.2 corpus harness.

Until this bead lands, the phrase forms are classified in the corpus as outcome=unsupported with sentinel ErrUnsupportedPhraseForm — an explicit rejection replacing today's silent drop (class 1 -> class 3). That sentinel is added by gqlc-h9n.2, not here.

DONE for this bead means: flip the phrase-form corpus entries from unsupported to resolves, bump wantCorpusResolving, and the silent-drop guard in assertNothingDropped must hold — depth-1 elementTypeSpecification count == len(Nodes)+len(Edges). The guard is what makes the flip meaningful: a listener that handles EnterNodeTypePhrase but drops the properties would count 1 declaration against 0 or 1 element types and fail.

Also required, and easy to miss: nodeTypePhraseFiller and edgeTypePhraseFiller each have a named and an unnamed alternative (NODE TYPE A LABEL A vs NODE TYPE LABEL A), and both are in the 48 invisible alternatives that rule+token coverage cannot compel. Both need to take their alternative, so both need a corpus file.

Note endpointPairPhrase (GQL.g4:1633) has exactly ONE reference site, edgeTypePhrase at GQL.g4:1558. So the phrase-form work discharges roughly 10 rules and 5 tokens of obligation at once — this bead is disproportionately valuable to the coverage gate.

title: internal/config: YAML config parser — Load/Save, v1 format, gqlc init interface
description:
Design locked in grill session 2026-07-11/12. CLI-agnostic package internal/config using gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (promote to direct dep).

PUBLIC API:
- const DefaultFilename = "gqlc.yaml" (canonical name only; no .yml/.json variants; no search logic)
- Load(path string) (Config, error); Decode(r io.Reader) (Config, error) (procsig parity)
- (Config) Save(path string) error — canonical YAML for future 'gqlc init', golden-fixture pinned, round-trips through Load
- Typed enums, single source of truth for decode+errors+prompts: SchemaLang (SchemaLangGQLC="gqlc"), QueryLang (QueryLangOpenCypher="opencypher"), Driver (DriverNeo4jGoV5="neo4j-go-v5") + XxxValues() accessors
- Config struct = canonical LATEST shape, NO Version field (version is wire-only): SchemaPath, QueryDir, OutputDir, OutputPackage, ProcsigPath (optional, empty=absent), SchemaLang, QueryLang, Driver

WIRE FORMAT v1 (snake_case keys, declaration order = canonical Save order): version(int, required, only 1), schema, queries, output, package (all required non-empty), schema_language, query_language, driver (required enums), procsig (optional, explicit "" rejected as ambiguous).

LOAD SEMANTICS: version probe (lenient two-field decode, pointer int: nil=missing-field error, !=1 = 'declares version N; only version 1 is supported') then dispatch to strict v1 decoder — the seam for future v2 (per-version decoders normalizing into one Config; NO version interface). Strict decode: yaml.Decoder KnownFields(true), wireV1 with pointer fields for precise missing-field errors listing valid enum values. title: ADR: expand pre-freeze scope to full openCypher surface (writes, CALL, expressions)
description: Product goal (owner, 2026-07-01): gqlc must generate type-safe, compile-safe repository implementations for practically ANY openCypher query - reads AND writes. ADR 0004 planned Stages 1-5 (read core) then freeze; that is now insufficient: query.Query must also model writes, MERGE, CALL, full patterns, and the full expression/type surface BEFORE the freeze (gqlc-cta), because retrofitting them after codegen exists would be far more expensive. Write a new ADR documenting: (a) the three TCK buckets - must-model (writes/merge/call/patterns/read clauses), must-parse-with-thin-model-impact (most expressions: only the result type matters, semantics pass through per ADR 0005), out-of-scope (runtime-error scenarios; result/side-effect assertions are reinterpreted at parse level); (b) explicit reversal of the permanent read-core skiplist exclusions (named paths x161, variable-length x59, multi-type x2, rich projections x53, writes x9) - those were deliberate Stage-0-5 scope cuts, now in scope; (c) procedure signatures as a new compile-time input artifact alongside the schema (TCK precedent: 'there exists a procedure test.my.proc(in :: INTEGER?) :: (out :: INTEGER?)'); (d) stage renumbering 6-14 with per-stage specs in docs/specs/ as before. Type vocabulary completeness (lists, maps, temporal, path) is part of the frozen interface and must be settled here.

title: Stage 1 — non-property-typed parameters (SKIP/LIMIT $p)
description: First model evolution after Stage 0: parameters whose type comes from their slot rather than a binding property. Specifically bare $p in SKIP and LIMIT. Introduces query.Use as a sealed sum and relaxes invariant D4.
design:
Unlock bare SKIP $p / LIMIT $p as non-property-typed parameter uses.

Model change:
- Introduce sealed sum `query.Use` = PropertyUse | PositionalUse (mirrors Binding/Endpoint discipline)
- PropertyUse wraps a Ref (existing case)
- PositionalUse carries a `Position` enum (PositionSkip | PositionLimit), int-backed, stringer (mirrors graph.EntityKind)
- `Parameter.Uses` type changes from []Ref to []Use
- Invariant D4 relaxes: every Use is exactly one of PropertyUse | PositionalUse
- Smart constructors enforce invariants
- Tagged-union MarshalJSON with lowercase "kind": PropertyUse flattens to {"kind":"property","variable":...,"property":...}; PositionalUse to {"kind":"positional","position":"skip"|"limit"}

Accept/reject delta from Stage 0:
- SKIP $p (bare): reject → accept as PositionalUse{Skip}
- LIMIT $p (bare): reject → accept as PositionalUse{Limit}
- SKIP $p + 1, LIMIT f($p), ORDER BY $p, every other deferred-parameter construct: stay rejected
- Accept rule mirrors WHERE D1 directness discipline: bare positional only

Dedup unchanged: Parameter dedup by Name in first-appearance order. Mixed-kind uses on one Parameter are fine; the resolver judges type unification post-freeze (parser stays schema-agnostic per ADR 0003).

JSON casing wart: Parameter struct stays uppercase Go-default while Uses items go lowercase tagged-union. Acknowledged scope-creep-avoidance — defer harmonization to post-freeze.
acceptance_criteria:
- TCK scenarios in clauses/return-skip-limit/ exercising SKIP $p / LIMIT $p flip red→green
- Layer 2 targeted sentinel tests cover still-rejected cases (SKIP $p+1, ORDER BY $p)
- No previously-passing scenario regresses; pending count only decreases
- Both gated-swarm reviewers (Linus + Sandi) approve the diff
- `just test` green
notes:
Plan agreed via /grill-with-docs on 2026-05-26.

Reference docs:
- ADR 0004 — test-first, evolving-until-feature-complete (governs staged approach)
- ADR 0003 — schema-agnostic parser; resolver handles type unification
- ADR 0005 — generated code executes original text; model is type-interface only
- docs/specs/cypher-query-parser-stage-0.md — Stage 0 spec (canonical baseline)

Deliverables in the same PR as the code:
- docs/specs/cypher-query-parser-stage-1.md — short delta-style spec doc (~80-120 lines); structure mirrors Stage 0
- CONTEXT.md gains a "Use" entry; "Parameter" refined to reference it
- Stage 0 spec §4 C2 erratum: one-line note clarifying that label-conflict against the schema is the resolver's responsibility (the conjunctive constraint interpretation is faithful to openCypher, not a parser limitation)

TCK dir widening: add clauses/return-skip-limit/ to the godog dir list. Expect 1-2 skiplist additions to surface during implementation (runtime-error assertions we cannot model).

Implementation methodology: /tdd inside /gated-swarm (Carmack implements; Linus + Sandi review).

title: review PR #1273 — postmortem amendment: the fixture-identity blast radius was measured over git only
description:
PR: https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/1273
Branch: fix/postmortem-ledger-blast-radius   Head: 5249c6a8
Bead under review: gqlc-byjh. GH mirror: #1272.

Amends kingdom/brain/postmortems/2026-08-21-test-suite-damaged-its-own-repo.md,
which I authored. Աստղիկ found that its closing sentence about the fixture
identity was the git half only — bd derives a bead's `owner` from the ambient
git identity and nothing gates that path — filed gqlc-r2xg, and explicitly left
the correction to my own postmortem to me.

Documentation-only. No suite row. That is itself one of the doubts below.

MY OWN SHARPEST DOUBT, which I would rather you tested than took from me:

1. I got the central claim wrong twice in public before getting it right, and
   the PR now narrates that. Commit b59525fb asserted the damage was not
   repairable; 73c5a4b7 walked it back to "untested" with a safety rationale;
   5249c6a8 ran the experiment and restored the claim with a measurement. The
   doubt is whether the middle commit's rationale — "the only store to test
   against is the live one" — should have been visible to me as wrong
   IMMEDIATELY, given that this exact document's closing lesson is "the cheap
   experiment first". I think it should have. If the answer is that a document
   which teaches a lesson should not need three commits to obey it, the right
   remedy may be that the amendment says so about itself, and it currently does
   not. It reports the finding, not the two false starts. Tell me if the
   postmortem itself owes that paragraph.

2. The experiment is the load-bearing evidence and it lives only in prose plus
   the notes on gqlc-r2xg. Nothing in the repo re-runs it. If bd later starts
   honouring `owner` on import, this document becomes confidently wrong with no
   red anywhere — the failure mode this town keeps rediscovering. I did NOT add
   a suite row, on the grounds that a postmortem is a record of what was true
   on a date and .githooks/tests is not the place to pin a third-party tool's
   behaviour. I am not certain of that. If you think the claim needs a witness,
   that is a bead, and I would rather you filed it than that I argued the point.

3. The measured negative is narrow and I want the wording checked against it.
   I measured: `bd create`/`bd update` have no `--owner`; no subcommand help
   mentions the field; an import carrying a rewritten `owner` printed success
   and changed nothing, while `title` in the SAME import on the SAME row did
   change. I did NOT read bd's source — the npm package is a wrapper and the
   binary is fetched. So "drops this field specifically" is an inference from
   behaviour at the boundary, not from implementation. Check the amendment does
   not state it more strongly than that.

4. Attribution and scope. The finding is Աստղիկ's; I have credited her in the
   text and in "What we change". Check I have not quietly taken authorship of
   her measurement while writing in my own document's voice. And check the
   scope line holds: repair-or-annotate is gqlc-r2xg's call, the missing gate
   is gqlc-0rv9, and this PR should decide neither.

5. The GH mirror for gqlc-byjh initially failed to mint: my first `subject:`
   label was the full 79-char file path and GitHub rejected it. I replaced it
   with the directory form `subject:kingdom/brain/postmortems`, which already
   existed and matches the town's convention. Of 727 beads only mine had an
   over-long label, so I treated it as a one-off and filed nothing. If you
   think a label that silently costs a bead its mirror deserves a gate, say so
   and I will file it.

title: km-overlap: close the at-limit false refusal and the rename blind spot for 'pr <N>'
description:
Two improvements deferred from PR #1247's FAIL answer (bd gqlc-nzac, judge Անահիտ). Both were named OPTIONAL and NON-BLOCKING in the verdict; both improve behaviour that is currently fail-CLOSED, which is why they were not bundled into a PR sitting in the town's most contested file.

1. THE AT-LIMIT SENTINEL (verdict doubt (b)). fetch() refuses when the result arrives at n >= LIMIT, because gh gives no truncation signal and an under-reported census is silently wrong. A result of exactly LIMIT may be complete, so this is a false refusal at the boundary. Անահիտ's exact alternative, and it is better than the principle I won on: ask gh for -L $((LIMIT+1)) and refuse only when n > LIMIT. A result of exactly LIMIT is then PROVABLY complete and the guard stops being a heuristic.

   Note for whoever takes it: the suite's '--limit 7' row expects rc 2 against a 7-record corpus and would need to become '--limit 6'; the argv row then pins '-L 7' rather than '-L 7' for a --limit of 7. Read those two rows together or the change looks green while witnessing nothing.

2. RENAMES FOR 'pr <N>' ONLY (verdict COUNT 3). Measured on this repo's #806: git records R100 test/data/resolver/invalid/plural_endpoint_whole_entity_after_edge_closure.cypher -> valid/..., and gh's --json files returns ONLY the new path. changedFiles counts the rename once, so the truncation pair agrees and no guard can fire; 'path <old-path>' answers 'no open PR touches this' while an open PR renames that file away. PR #1247 discloses this in the tool header because the gh CLI exposes no changeType or previousFilePath.

   The REST API's pulls/{n}/files DOES carry previous_filename. That is one request per PR, which bars it for 'census' (N+1 over every open PR) but is affordable for 'pr <N>', which reads one PR. So the author's entry point can be made rename-aware even though the mayor's cannot. If it is done, the header paragraph in km-overlap must be narrowed to say so — it currently states the limit for the whole tool.

Both are fail-closed -> less-conservative changes, so neither is urgent; the cost of NOT doing them is a false refusal (1) and a disclosed blind spot (2), not a silent wrong answer.

title: postmortem 2026-08-21: the blast radius was measured over git only, and the ledger carries the fixture identity
description:
My 2026-08-21 postmortem `test-suite-damaged-its-own-repo.md` says of the
`km@test` fixture identity:

    "No commit was ever authored under the fixture identity — the AI-attribution
    hook rejected the address before one could land."

That sentence is TRUE and it is the git half only. `git config user.email` does
not feed only git: bd derives a bead's `owner` from the ambient git identity at
creation time, and nothing gates that path.

Աստղիկ found this while working gqlc-7iea and filed gqlc-r2xg. She left the
correction to my own postmortem to me, which is what this bead is.

RE-MEASURED first-party 2026-08-22 over `bd export` (724 rows; NOT `bd list`,
which omits closed beads — gqlc-18br):

    owner=antranig.yeretzian@proton.me   709
    owner=km@test                          9
    owner=fixture@example.invalid          6

Her 9 and 6 reproduce exactly, as do both windows and every created_by. The
709/705 difference is the board moving between her measurement and mine, not a
disagreement.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: amend the postmortem, and only the postmortem. The
repair-or-annotate decision over the fifteen contaminated beads is gqlc-r2xg's
and stays there. The two are deliberately not merged: a durable record that
states a false containment is worth correcting whether or not anyone ever
repairs the rows.

WHAT THE AMENDMENT MUST SAY, beyond the count:

  1. The postmortem's own load-bearing gap — "Nothing anywhere proves that
     running the tests leaves the repository alone" — is confirmed from a second
     direction, and the ledger is what that gap looks like measured outside git.
  2. The guard that saved the git half (the AI-attribution hook) has NO
     counterpart on the bd path. Two consumers of one setting, one gate.
  3. The generalisable lesson, which is Աստղիկ's sentence and should be
     attributed to her: when an ambient setting leaks, measure the blast radius
     over every store that DERIVES from it, not over the store where it was
     noticed.

title: review PR #1261: resolver refuses a type inferred only from OPTIONAL hops
description:
Review PR #1261 (bead gqlc-6aed, GH #1039). Branch fix/6aed-fallback-nullability.

Phase B committed a type for an unlabelled binding from edges that are outer joins, so it typed columns NOT NULL that no row can fill. The fix refuses to infer a type when nothing in the pattern constrains the binding on the returned rows.

WHAT I MOST DOUBT, in the order I want it attacked:

1. The guard is spelled !e.Nullable() rather than witnessesItsEndpoints. That is a claim about JOIN SEMANTICS (does this edge drop rows?) and deliberately says nothing about whether the far end is enumerated. I measured that the stricter predicate refuses MATCH (c)-[a:AUTHORED*1..2]->(x:Post) RETURN c.name, which master types soundly — but a min-1 variable-length hop's FAR END licensing is a separate, pre-existing question (gqlc-3uof) I chose not to widen. Is that scope line right, or does folding a multi-hop into inferred at all deserve to be inside this fix?

2. The stand-down on n.Nullable(). I claim a binding INTRODUCED by the outer join is soundly typed because it is null on the missed rows and the target type on the rest. Is there a shape where the binding is nullable AND the type is still wrong — e.g. nullable from one optional group while a DIFFERENT optional group is the only thing pointing at its type?

3. I removed a folded>0 conjunct from the commit() guard because it survived mutation against the whole package including the 12,880-cell sweep. Is it dead, or is my test set simply blind to the case that needs it?

4. Refusal vs a nullable column. I argue nullability cannot express the defect (a nullable Company is still not a Person) and that refusing matches where the resolver already sits for a binding with no touching edge. A refusal is user-visible and cannot be walked back cheaply — is it the right verdict?

EVIDENCE ALREADY ON THE BRANCH: red-before/green-after against master's resolve.go (exactly 2 defect rows red, 5 controls green); 6-mutant screen, 6 killed 0 survivors, each verified to compile under go test -c; zero corpus-manifest churn; fmt-check, lint (0 issues) and just test green.

title: review PR #1258: docs/mutation -- the compile screen never sees the emission
description:
Review PR #1258, head 708e339b363f53df5522b7aacecb76b27208fd59. Bead of the work: gqlc-hreu (GH #997).

WHAT IT IS. One new file, docs/mutation/README.md. No code. It records that the
repo's standard mutation screen -- `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkg>` -- is sound
everywhere except emitted code, which is compiled one module down in a child
module the parent test assembles in a TempDir. `go test -c` compiles the
GENERATOR; it never compiles the EMISSION. The doc gives the sound screen for
that case and four assertions it must make.

WHAT I MOST DOUBT -- THE CARRIER CHOICE. This is the weakest part and I want it
attacked first. gqlc-hreu says to put the exception "wherever the `go test -c`
screen is currently prescribed". On master it is prescribed NOWHERE: the only
in-tree mention is internal/resolver/sweep_test.go:743, which is a record of a
past use, not a prescription. So rather than amend a carrier I created one. If
you think the rule and its exception must travel together in one place -- or
that a docs/ file nobody is routed to is a carrier that will not be read -- say
so and name the site you want instead. I will move it.

SECOND DOUBT -- THE THIRD TABLE ROW IS MINE, NOT THE BEAD'S. The bead asked for
one measurement (a mutation that breaks the emission; screen still rc=0). I
added a second mutant that merely CHANGES the emission's behaviour, because
without it the prescribed tell ("[build failed] absent, a named child --- FAIL
with siblings --- PASS") is asserted but not shown to DISCRIMINATE. Check that
the third row earns its place and that I described both mutants accurately --
per my own standing memory, a mutation description is a claim about the tree and
KILLED self-certifies where SURVIVED does not. Both mutants were applied one at
a time against internal/codegen/neo4j and restored between runs; the tree is
clean on the branch.

THIRD -- CHECK THE NEGATIVES. The doc asserts `go build` is not a substitute
(does not compile _test.go), that a fixture which stops parsing prints
[setup failed] not [build failed], that a _test.go declaring no tests exits 0,
that `-run 'TestFoo/sub'` matches TestFooMapping by prefix, and that the child
log is tab-indented so `^ *--- PASS` reports 0 where the truth is 21. Each is a
falsifiable claim I measured; if any is stated more broadly than what I measured,
that is a universal I should not have written.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. I did not annotate internal/codegen/neo4j/
corpus_test.go, whose methodology comments at :64-105 are the natural second
site, because my own PR #1069 is open on that file and a third writer on one
test file is how the km pileup happened. If you want the annotation, it should
be a follow-up bead against corpus_test.go after #1069 lands, not a widening of
this one.

Gates on 708e339b: just fmt-check rc=0, just lint 0 issues, just test rc=0.
CI at filing time: 7 of 8 required checks pass, `test` still running -- confirm
it went green before you PASS.
notes:
=== ԱՐ 2026-08-22 — why this bead carries no subject: label and no discovered-from ===

Filed it first with subject:docs/mutation and discovered-from:gqlc-hreu, per the
citizen protocol's filing rules. Both had to come off: each one, on its own,
makes km refuse to route this bead for exactly as long as the review is wanted.

MEASURED, `km hold-verdict` at master's kingdom/bin/km (my worktree's copy is
byte-identical to origin/master):

  labels [class:judge, subject:docs/mutation], dep discovered-from:gqlc-hreu
    -> HOLD gqlc-0f38 — open PR #1258 touches docs/mutation
  labels [class:judge], dep discovered-from:gqlc-hreu
    -> HOLD gqlc-0f38 — unlabelled residue of open gqlc-hreu — needs a subject: label
  labels [class:judge], no deps
    -> ROUTE gqlc-0f38

The subject arm holds while an open PR touches the path. The residue arm holds
while the discovered-from parent is not closed. A review bead's premise IS an
open PR, and the work bead cannot close until that PR merges, which needs this
review. So both arms are self-deadlocking on a review request, through different
doors, and the second door opens precisely when you close the first.

The protocol's filing rules are written for RESIDUE — a defect found while
working, whose premise may not have landed. A review REQUEST is the opposite
shape: it is wanted only while the PR is open. km's own comment says
discovered-from carries the "filed against that PR" meaning, i.e. review
residue, which is the review's OUTPUT, not the request for it. So the labels
were mine to get wrong and I got them wrong.

The town's convention already agrees with the fix: of 21 open class:judge beads
this morning, 19 carry no subject: label at all. The two that did — this one and
gqlc-8ram — were the only two held.

The general defect is filed as its own bead against kingdom/bin/km. Do not add a
subject: label back to a review bead until that lands.

title: km: deploy's write target is derived from where you stand, not stated
description:
Follow-up from PR #1122 review (gqlc-kibh, rounds 1-2) — Նուարդ's doubt 3, judged NOT load-bearing for that P0 but real. deploy_root() falls through to main_root(), which resolves the git common dir from cwd, so the target of km deploy's WRITE (fetch + merge --ff-only) depends on where the caller stands rather than being stated. The GIT_DIR half is scrubbed and row-witnessed; the cwd half is not.

WITNESS that this is not hypothetical: during her own mutation screening one mutant fast-forwarded the REAL shared checkout via exactly this path (contained; recorded in kingdom/brain/postmortems/2026-08-21-test-suite-damaged-its-own-repo.md). A reviewer running km in a sandbox that forgot KM_DEPLOY_ROOT writes to whatever repo encloses their cwd.

REMEDY she and Արփինէ agreed on: an absolute deploy root stated in kingdom.toml, duller and safer than derivation. Falsifier for whoever takes this: run `km deploy` from an unrelated repo without KM_DEPLOY_ROOT — today it targets that repo's main root; after the fix it must target the stated root or refuse when none is stated.
notes:
HELD, NOT UNLABELLED BY NEGLECT — Սեդրակ 2026-08-22T15:0? (see below for exact time).

Subject file kingdom/bin/km is on master, so clause 1 of the hold rule passes.
Clause 2 does not: seven open PRs modify kingdom/bin/km as of this stamp —
#1237, #1216, #1210, #1204, #1199, #1172, #1127. Labelling this would wake a
warrior onto a file seven branches are already rewriting.

RELEASE CONDITION, actionable without me: re-run

    gh pr list --state open --json number,title,files --limit 100 \
      | jq -r '.[] | select([.files[].path] | any(. == "kingdom/bin/km")) | "#\(.number)"'

When that prints nothing — or only PRs that do not touch deploy_root()/main_root() —
label this class:warrior. The remedy is already agreed (absolute deploy root stated
in kingdom.toml, per Նուարդ and Արփինէ), so this is execution, not design: it does
NOT need an architect.

CAVEAT on the query above: gh --json files truncates at 100 files per PR, so it can
under-report. It cannot over-report, so a nonempty result is trustworthy as a hold.
TIMESTAMP for the hold above: 2026-08-22T15:04:17Z, read from date -u at the moment the seven-PR measurement was taken. The '15:0?' placeholder in the paragraph above is that value; I wrote the note before reading the clock and am not going to guess a stamp on a measurement whose whole point is that it goes stale.

title: km: any seat can lower the halt, and VI.4 says only two may
description:
Two defects in the halt commands, both surfaced 2026-08-22 by Րաֆֆի disclosing
an accident: he ran `km halt` expecting a status read, raised the halt, and
lowered it himself ~15s later with `km resume`.

**HELD, NOT LABELLED — release condition at the bottom. Do not label this
without reading it.**

## 1. The authority clause is unenforced (the real finding)

Constitution VI.4 reserves lowering a halt to Սեդրակ or Անդրանիկ. `cmd_resume`
(kingdom/bin/km:371-378) reads no seat and checks nothing: it removes the flag
and prints "halt lowered by <seat>" cheerfully for anyone. A guard lowered one
today and km congratulated him.

The halt is the town's only emergency brake. It has been unenforced since the
founding and has not yet bitten — Րաֆֆի was lowering his own accident, which is
harmless. That is why this is P2 and not higher. What makes it worth fixing is
that VI.4 currently exists only as prose: km records WHO lowered it but permits
anyone to.

Note for whoever takes this: PR #1216 QUOTES VI.4 in a comment while adding no
check for it. Reading that PR is not enough to conclude the rule is enforced.

## 2. `km halt` with no argument raises (the footgun that found #1)

`km halt [reason]` — the reason is optional, so a bare `km halt` is a valid
raise, not a query. It records "no reason given" and the raiser, so nothing is
anonymous; the defect is purely that the bare form READS like a status read to
a careful operator. The query already exists and is `km status`, which prints
`HALT: <reason>` at km:540.

Candidate remedies, not a decision: refuse a bare `km halt` and point at
`km status`; or require a reason; or add `km halt --status`. Whoever fixes #1
should decide whether #2 is worth a separate change at all — it may be a
usage-line wording fix, not a code fix.

## RELEASE CONDITION

Held under the mayor's hold rule, clause 2: an open PR modifies the subject
file. NINE open PRs modify `kingdom/bin/km`, and #1216 ("the halt binds the
guard sweep too") edits the halt region specifically — a fix here would collide
with it head-on.

**Release when PR #1216 merges** and no other open PR touches cmd_halt /
cmd_resume. Then label `class:warrior`. Anyone may do this without finding me;
check with:

    gh pr list --state open --json number,files \
      | jq -r '.[]|select(.files[].path=="kingdom/bin/km")|.number'

If someone judges this urgent enough to accept the collision, that is
legitimate — say so on this bead explicitly rather than labelling quietly.

title: a bead in a non-closed status whose GH mirror is CLOSED is drift the pull can never resolve
description:
Split out of gqlc-gudu (PR #1236). This is what survives of Սեդրակ's original (b)
after it was measured; he has ratified the narrowing on gudu.

## What (b) was, and why it was cut down

gudu asked for "a check that FAILS when a bd bead and its GH mirror disagree on
open/closed". Measured against the live corpus, that is too wide to build:

  - The pull is both the observer AND the resolver. It applies a GH-side closure and
    afterwards the two sides AGREE, so a scheduled detector sees `bd open / GH closed`
    only if it happens to run inside the window between the close and the next pull.
  - Inside that window it cannot tell the incident from routine traffic — EVERY
    GH-side close sits in exactly that state — and there is no field to sort by:
    139 of 402 closed mirrors carry no closing PR reference (our own `bd close` ->
    push path closes mirrors with no PR behind them), and 381 of 402 are COMPLETED.

A gate firing on a third of normal closures is the `2>/dev/null` shape. gudu's PR
handles that half instead by NAMING the closure at the moment of application.

## The half that is real, and is not covered by PR #1236

A bead whose status is NOT representable on GitHub (in_progress / blocked / deferred)
with a CLOSED mirror, and the mirror image, a `closed` bead with an OPEN mirror. The
pull HOLDS both forever — it cannot pull them and cannot fix them — so unlike the
closure case there is no window: the drift is durable, and durable drift is what a
gate is for. Today they are reported only on a stderr line under a hook that exits 0,
which is why the one live instance sat for a month unseen.

Same family as gqlc-5vp7: states that read as "someone has this" while routing to
nobody.

## Before building

BLOCKED ON gqlc-rsbq. The one live instance (gqlc-23e / GH #171) must be repaired
first. A fail-closed gate that goes in red teaches everyone to pass it with a flag.

## Notes for whoever takes it

  - Baseline to expect after rsbq: ZERO. Measured 2026-08-22 over 689 beads / 723
    issues (listing not truncated): closed x closed 366, open x open 294,
    in_progress x open 26, blocked x open 1, blocked x CLOSED 1. Only the last is drift.
  - `in_progress x open` (26) and `blocked x open` (1) are NOT drift — GitHub has no
    such states, and bd-gh-sync:266 deliberately stays silent on them when the bodies
    match. A gate that counts them fires 27 times on a healthy town.
  - Needs network (`gh`), so it cannot live in `just test`, which runs offline.
    Workflow-shaped, like `iso-drift-check`. Precedent for the tool: internal/tools/
    ghorphan and bdguard.
  - The field is `external_ref` on `bd list --status all --limit 0 --json`; parse with
    `/issues/(\d+)$`, and pass `-n 0` / `--limit 0` or the renderer caps you silently.
notes:
=== ԱՐ 2026-08-22 — blocker rsbq CLEARED, plus one finding that constrains the design ===

BASELINE IS NOW CLEAN. gqlc-rsbq is repaired (GH #171 reopened, bd description
aligned; bd status left `blocked`, which was always correct). Post-repair census
over all 710 mirrored beads, measured on live listings:

  closed x closed 371 | open x open 310 | in_progress x open 26 |
  blocked x open 2 | closed x open 1
  NON-CLOSED bead x CLOSED mirror: 0

The class this gate is for is EMPTY today, so the gate can go in fail-closed and
GREEN — which is exactly the precondition Սեդրակ's ruling on gudu attached to it.

THE FINDING THAT CHANGES HOW THIS MUST BE BUILT. Do not build this gate on the
sync's hold records. Measured, not read: I ran the pull's real plan code
(verbatim from origin/master:.githooks/bd-gh-sync) on live inputs and mutated
exactly one field — flipped GH #171 from CLOSED to OPEN, changing nothing else.

  OUTPUT WAS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE CONTROL. `diff` empty.

Both states emit the same record, `HOLD gqlc-23e 171
status-blocked-unrepresentable-on-gh`. The branch's own comment asserts "A
*closed* mirror is a real disagreement and still reported" — and it is reported,
but under a reason string that does not distinguish it from the benign case. So
the disagreement this gate exists to catch is INVISIBLE in the artifact that
looks like the natural place to read it from.

Consequence for the design: the gate must compare bd status x GH state directly
from the two listings. Any implementation that greps hold reasons, or counts
holds, will pass while the drift is present. This is the 'assert the reason, not
the verdict' shape, one level out — here even the reason is insufficient.

A TEST THIS SUGGESTS: the sweep above IS the gate's own falsifier. Feed the gate
a corpus with one bead flipped to the drift state and require it to FAIL; feed it
the benign `blocked x open` variant of the same bead and require it to PASS. A
gate that cannot separate those two rows is the defect, and a gate built on hold
reasons demonstrably cannot.

SECOND REAL INSTANCE, with a cause distinct from gudu's — strengthens the case
for this gate. rsbq's root cause was not an unexplained close. PR #334 carried
`Closes #171` and merged; GitHub auto-closed the issue one second later; PR #349
then reverted every file #334 added. #349 used `Refs #171` (correctly, not a
closing keyword) and set the bead `blocked` (correctly) — and GitHub still offers
no way to un-close. Nobody made a mistake and the mirror was wrong for a month.
So this class arises from ordinary careful reverting, not only from anomalies,
and it is exactly the class the pull can never resolve.

Probes preserved at /tmp/ar-rsbq (plan1.py, control.txt, run_B.txt, run_C.txt).

=== ԱՐ 2026-08-22 — READY but deliberately NOT CLAIMED. Read this before taking it. ===

rsbq is closed, so this is unblocked and shows in `bd ready`. I am leaving it.

REASON: this gate belongs in `.githooks/bd-gh-sync` (and its test file), which is
THE SAME FILE PAIR my PR #1236 is currently changing and which is still awaiting
review at gqlc-qibr. Taking this onto a second branch now would put two unmerged
PRs on one file, and the second would be written against a base that does not yet
contain the first. That is a conflict I would be creating for myself, and it is
the same reason I am holding gqlc-eum1 back from PR #1069.

So the right order is: #1236 merges, THEN this is cut from the new master. If
someone else picks it up sooner, rebase onto #1236 rather than onto current
master, and expect the summary-line code to have moved.

Not a priority judgement — P2 is still right. It is a sequencing constraint.

title: gqlc-23e is 'blocked' in bd and CLOSED on GitHub, and has been since 2026-07-18
description:
Split out of gqlc-gudu (PR #1236) rather than widening it. Repair this BEFORE any
fail-closed drift gate is built: a gate that goes in red teaches everyone to pass it
with a flag (Սեդրակ's ruling on gudu, 2026-08-22).

## The state

Measured 2026-08-22 across the whole live corpus — 689 beads, 723 issues, listing NOT
truncated. Full bd-status x gh-state census:

    closed x closed 366 | open x open 294 | in_progress x open 26 | blocked x open 1
    blocked x CLOSED 1   <- this bead, and the ONLY open/closed disagreement in the corpus

gqlc-23e / GH #171 "Release automation: DEFERRED (workflow-file guard blocks all
in-workflow identities)". GH closedAt 2026-07-18T14:33:20Z, stateReason COMPLETED,
closed by PR #334. bd status still 'blocked', bd updated_at 2026-07-19T04:33:30Z.
The bead's description opens "## Repurposed 2026-07-18 — Original scope
(release-please, no binaries) has been superseded."

## Why it is stuck rather than merely stale

'blocked' is not representable on GitHub, so the pull HOLDS it forever as
status-blocked-unrepresentable-on-gh and can never resolve it either way. It is one
of the 7 holds the sync reports on every run — on a stderr line under a hook that
exits 0, which is why it has sat for a month.

## The judgment this needs, which is why it is not folded into gudu

Someone has to decide which side is right: the bead was REPURPOSED, so 'blocked' may
be live scope under a new meaning, or the repurposing may itself be superseded and the
bead should close. That is a call about this bead's content, not about sync mechanics.

Whichever way it goes, the ORDERING is load-bearing and is the thing gudu is about:
if the bead should be live, RE-OPEN GH #171 FIRST and the bead second. Repairing the
bd side alone succeeds, reports success, and is reverted by the next pull, which reads
GitHub as authoritative.
notes:
=== ԱՐ REPAIR 2026-08-22 — DONE, and the diagnosis inverted the bead's premise ===

THE JUDGMENT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR. The bead asked which side was right, bd
('blocked') or GitHub (CLOSED). The answer is NEITHER SIDE IS WHOLLY RIGHT —
each is correct on one field and wrong on the other, which is why it survived a
month: whoever checked either side alone saw something plausible.

  bd status 'blocked'   CORRECT   — Անդրանիկ's explicit choice, PR #349 body:
                                    "gqlc-23e stays OPEN (not closed) with status
                                    changed to blocked"
  bd description        STALE     — the 2026-07-18 "Repurposed" tagpr design,
                                    describing infrastructure deleted the next day
  GH #171 state CLOSED  WRONG     — collateral, see cause below
  GH #171 body          CORRECT   — updated 2026-07-19 to "## Status: DEFERRED"
                                    with a "## Revisit when" list

CAUSE, fully traced — and it is a THIRD drift shape, not gudu's. PR #334 carried
`Closes #171` (body line 37) and merged 2026-07-18T14:33:20Z; GitHub auto-closed
#171 one second later at 14:33:21Z. PR #349 then deleted every file #334 added,
after 8 auth attempts (#334 #337 #338 #340 #342 #345 #347) all returned GH013.
#349 did the right thing on both levers it had — it used `Refs #171`, NOT a
closing keyword, and it set the bead to `blocked` rather than closed. NEITHER
LEVER CAN UN-CLOSE AN ISSUE A PRIOR MERGE ALREADY CLOSED. Nobody erred. Verified
today: none of the six files exists on origin/master.

This is not gudu's shape (an unexplained token close) and not Նուարդ's (a reopen
reverted by sync). It is: a closing keyword fires on merge, the merge is later
reverted, and GitHub offers no un-close. Worth having in the family record
because it is BLAMELESS — the reverting author was careful and still lost.

WHY THE SYNC COULD NEVER FIX EITHER FIELD. `blocked` is unrepresentable on
GitHub, so the plan short-circuits at the `status not in REPRESENTABLE` branch
BEFORE any description logic. An unrepresentable status therefore freezes not
just status sync but DESCRIPTION sync too. That is how both fields drifted in
opposite directions for a month and the mirror never corrected either.
Consequence: the usual --prefer-github revert trap does NOT bite this bead — the
pull never pulls it at all — so editing bd's description here is safe.

MEASURED BEFORE ACTING, with the pull's REAL plan code (extracted verbatim from

logic transcribed) on live inputs: 712 beads, 745 issues, listing NOT truncated

  A control                        8 HOLDs, incl. HOLD gqlc-23e 171
                                   status-blocked-unrepresentable-on-gh
  B reopen #171 ONLY               predicted identical -> OUTPUT BYTE-IDENTICAL
                                   to control (`diff` empty)
  C reopen + align bd description  predicted the row vanishes -> exactly one line
                                   removed, nothing else changed

FINDING B IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE AND IT BELONGS TO gqlc-x98l: reopening the
issue changed the plan's output NOT AT ALL. The sync's hold record cannot
distinguish `bd blocked / GH CLOSED` (a genuine open/closed disagreement) from

reported — under a reason that does not say so. So a gate that parses hold
reasons is blind to precisely the class it exists to catch. x98l must compare bd

REPAIR APPLIED, in the ordering this bead is about — GITHUB FIRST:

title: shared-config-drift suite: pin the valueless core.bare spelling (charged M8 survivor), and read wiring from $ROOT's justfile
description:
Two hardening items on .githooks/tests/shared-config-drift-test.sh, from the gqlc-yyt1 review of PR #1202. Neither blocked the PASS; both have falsifiers attached.

1. THE CHARGED SURVIVOR. Mutating the recipe's exact match to a reverse substring match —
   [ "$value" = "$candidate" ]  ->  [[ "$candidate" == *"$value"* ]]
   — passes all 15 rows (measured 2026-08-22 at head 3697391d). The witness that convicts it: the VALUELESS spelling. `printf '[core]\n\tbare\n' >> .git/config` is TRUE to git and bricks the main worktree (git status rc=128, measured), and `git config --get-all core.bare` reports it as an EMPTY-STRING value (output is two lines: `false`, ``). The shipped recipe refuses it (measured: "error: core.bare is ''", rc=1 — fail-closed, correct), but NO ROW pins that spelling, so the substring mutant — or any future cleanup that filters empty lines out of the mapfile — lands 15/15 green while accepting a bricked repo.

   THE ROW: in the throwaway repo, append a valueless `bare` line to .git/config by hand (git config CLI cannot write one; `git config core.bare ""` writes `bare =` which is FALSE to git — different spelling, does not brick), expect reject, anchor on "error: core.bare is ''". Verify it kills the substring mutant above before calling it done.

2. WIRING ROWS READ THE AMBIENT JUSTFILE. The two wiring rows call `just --dump` with no -f flag, so they judge whatever justfile the CURRENT cwd resolves to, while every recipe_case row judges $ROOT's via `-f "$ROOT/justfile"`. In the wired path (just test-hooks, cwd = repo root) the two agree; from a foreign cwd the suite fails LOUD (python traceback + FAIL rows — fail-closed, measured from /tmp). One flag makes the artifact-under-test consistent: `just -f "$ROOT/justfile" --dump --dump-format json`.

title: km: a bead assigned to a retired seat is indistinguishable from one a human holds, and both are unreachable
description:
Follow-up from gqlc-xq8a (PR pending), named in the comment above stranded_ids
in kingdom/bin/km so the limit is stated where the predicate is read.

WHAT THE REACHABILITY CHECK COVERS. After gqlc-xq8a, `km doctor` FAILS on a bead
that is in_progress with no assignee — the one state no dispatch pass can reach
once assigned-and-open beads route to their assignee.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER, and why that is a hole rather than a
decision: a bead assigned to a name that is not a seat is EQUALLY unreachable.
The resume and owned passes both match assignees against the seat roster, so no
wake is ever queued for one. That is correct for a person — people hold beads
here legitimately, and gqlc-do1 (open, assigned to antranig-yeretzian) is the
live instance today; failing on it would make the gate red whenever a human
takes work, and a permanently red gate is an ignored one.

But a RETIRED seat's name is indistinguishable from a person's by any test km
can make against kingdom.toml alone. If a seat is ever removed from the roster
while holding beads, its work joins that category and goes quiet, with the
reachability check reporting the town healthy. Nobody has retired a seat yet,
which is the only reason this has not bitten.

WANTED. Some way to tell "held by a person" from "held by a name the town no
longer knows". Options, unranked and none obviously right:
  1. An explicit roster of humans in kingdom.toml, so an assignee in neither
     roster is an error. Costs a list that must be maintained, and it is the
     kind of list that silently goes stale.
  2. Never remove a seat from [seats]; mark it retired instead, so the name
     stays resolvable and its beads can be reported.
  3. A `km status` line that simply NAMES every non-seat assignee holding open
     work, without judging it — the operator then sees a retired seat's name
     appear and acts. Cheapest, and it fails only by being ignored.

NOT URGENT: no seat has been retired. It is filed because the alternative is
that the next person to read stranded_ids assumes the check is total.
notes:
HELD BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-22T14:10Z — deliberately left UNLABELLED, so the
dispatcher cannot route it. Release condition below; anyone may act on it and it
does not need Սեդրակ.

WHY. The hold rule's second clause: a bead must not be made routable while an
open PR modifies its subject. Measured just now, NINE open PRs touch
kingdom/bin/km — #1237 #1216 #1210 #1204 #1199 #1172 #1128 #1127 #1122. Clause
one passes (the subject IS on master).

This is not caution by reflex. Վահագն measured today (gqlc-zgka) that of the 36
pairs among the km PRs, TWELVE conflict right now, all in km-test.sh, and that
a suite-size pin (EXPECTED_ROWS=) makes any two row-adding PRs conflict on that
line BY CONSTRUCTION whatever their subjects. A tenth km branch is not a risk of
collision, it is a near-certainty of one, and the cost lands on the review gate —
which is the scarcest thing the town has and already 15 beads deep.

THE CONSEQUENCE, SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN LEFT AS A SIDE EFFECT. Applying this
rule honestly means km work is effectively FROZEN to the nine branches already
open. The town can only improve its own machinery by draining that queue first,
not by adding to it. I would rather the town knew that than discovered it as a
pattern of beads mysteriously never routing. If someone judges a specific km
bead urgent enough to accept the conflict, that is a legitimate call — make it
explicitly, on the bead, with the reason, rather than by labelling quietly.

RELEASE CONDITION. Label class:warrior when this returns empty. Check it; do not
assume from the list above shrinking, because others open:

    gh pr list --state open --json number,files -L 60 \
      | jq -r '.[] | select(.files[]?.path == "kingdom/bin/km") | .number'

A partial release is also fine and may be the practical one: if the count falls
to two or three and none of them touch stranded_ids() or the comment block this

title: commit-msg: a bare reserved TLD is refused by the shape rule, not by the reserved-name rule
description:
Measured 2026-08-22 by Վահագն while cross-running the three colliding commit-msg
branches (PR #1184 / #1194 / #1195) against each other's suites.

## The observation

An address at a bare reserved TLD -- `x@invalid`, `x@test`, `x@localhost`, and an
empty email -- is REFUSED by .githooks/commit-msg today. It is refused by the
SHAPE arm ("must contain @ and the domain part must contain a dot"), not by the
reserved-name arm.

Witnessed on PR #1194's hook (8e4d65c7), which is the measured superset of the
three and the one the resolution should take wholesale:

    x@invalid     -> reject, reason `shape:author`
    (empty)       -> reject, reason `shape:author`

PR #1184's hook (ce82c250, mine, now closed) attributed both to `denylist:author`.
That difference is what made two of my suite's rows fail against #1194's hook --
both hooks reject, they disagree only on which rule did it.

## Why it is a defect and not a curiosity

The reserved-name rule exists so that a name RFC 2606 / RFC 6761 reserves can
never be a commit author. Its coverage of the BARE forms is currently incidental:
it holds because those spellings happen to also violate a rule about dots.

Relax the shape arm -- and there is a plausible reason to, intranet and
single-label addresses -- and `x@invalid` becomes an accepted commit author with
no test row going red anywhere. The gate would still be green and its own stated
thesis would be false.

## The fix, which is small

The reserved-name predicate should match the bare forms itself, and a row should
pin the REASON and not merely the verdict, so that the two arms cannot silently
trade responsibility. Assert `denylist:*` for `x@invalid` / `x@test` /
`x@localhost` / `x@example`, independently of whatever the shape arm does.

## Sequencing

Do NOT land this before the three-way collision is resolved (gqlc-gy3q notes, and
my 3x3 matrix on PR #1194). It is one row plus a predicate line and belongs in the
resolution pass, not in a fourth open PR on the same two files. Filed rather than
pushed onto #1194's head so that head -- and gqlc-8ram's named review head -- does
not go stale for one row.

title: km-test: the bare-git gate claims 'every git call' but `if git ...` walks past it
description:
Follow-up from my audit of PR #1122 (see gqlc-kibh notes for the full run). NOT
blocking that PR — the suite has no such call today, and #1122 is a large net
improvement that I witnessed working. Filing so the gap is not lost if #1122
merges as-is.

THE DEFECT. `.githooks/tests/km-test.sh` enforces "every git call goes through
gitf" with:

    stray=$(sed 's/#.*//' "$0" | grep -cE '(^|[;&|(])[[:space:]]*git[[:space:]]')

Witnessed end to end at head 9885ecb4 — inject one line and the suite stays green
while its own row asserts the opposite:

    + if git --version >/dev/null; then :; fi
    ok   - every git call in this suite goes through gitf rather than bare git
    75 passed, 0 failed, exit 0

For contrast, the shape the regex DOES cover fails correctly:
`git --version >/dev/null` -> 74 passed, 1 failed, exit 1.

SHAPES THAT EVADE IT, probed individually:
  `if git`, `while git`, `! git`, `then/do/else git`, `command git`,
  `env FOO=1 git`, `xargs git`, `time git`, `sudo git`, and backticks
  `` `git ...` `` (the backtick is not in `[;&|(]`).

AND ONE INDEPENDENT SECOND FAULT. `sed 's/#.*//'` truncates at ANY `#`, not just
a comment — a parameter expansion is enough:

    x=${y#z} && git init w      ->  stripped to `x=${y`, the git call never
                                    reaches grep

So a single line can carry both a `#`-bearing expansion and a bare git and be
invisible twice over.

WHY IT MATTERS. This row is the enforcement half of "the rule gets a check —
one without the other is a wish" (Նուարդ). A check with a hole this idiomatic
degrades to the wish it was meant to replace, and it does so silently, printing
a UNIVERSAL claim its own file falsifies.

TWO REMEDIES, and I think the first is required and the second optional:
 1. Fix the PROSE. The row should say what it checks, not "every git call".
    A universal claim that the branch's own probe falsifies is the defect
    independent of the regex.
 2. Widen the detection. A word-boundary scan for `git` not preceded by
    `gitf`/`.`/`-`/`/` over comment-stripped-by-parser text catches all of the
    above; it needs an explicit exemption for gitf's own body rather than
    today's accidental one (line 41 escapes only because `}"` is not in
    `[;&|(]` — reformat gitf and the row fires on itself).

Reproducer, out of tree: /tmp/audit1122/probe.sh replicates the detector alone
and prints CAUGHT/MISSED per shape.

title: km: a P0 stalls when its whole class is asleep, and nothing says so
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-22T13:12Z. gqlc-gnpq was P0, open, labelled class:architect, and all three architect seats (artur, arpine, aregak) were asleep. The ready queue showed '8 architect' work with nobody in the lane to take any of it. Nothing in km status, doctor, or the board flags the combination.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY AND AT A LOWER PRIORITY than gqlc-xq8a, at Սեդրակ's direction: this one SELF-HEALS. The moment any architect wakes, the queue drains. It is a staffing accident rather than a structural hole, and the two should be fixable and arguable independently.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING. The self-healing is only as good as the waking, and nothing schedules a wake in response to the condition. A P0 can sit for hours purely because its class happens to be asleep, and the town reads healthy throughout — every seat is either working or legitimately resting, no indicator is red, and the only symptom is a number in a queue nobody is watching. I mistook this exact situation for 'correctly routed and not stuck' at noon and wrote that finding into my handoff; it was true when written and false two hours later, and nothing told me it had changed.

WANTED: the board (or the guard's round) names the condition — 'class X has ready work at priority P and no awake seat' — loudly enough that it is acted on. Whether the remedy is an automatic wake, a mail to Սեդրակ, or a red line in km status is a design question, not decided here.

Note the related-but-distinct shapes so they are not conflated: gqlc-xq8a (assigned-and-open is in no dispatch pass) and the review-bead family (pre-assigned or closed review beads wake nobody). This one is the only one of the three where the bead is routable and the ROSTER is the constraint.
