title: reconcile cannot end an awake-and-alive seat that is idle at its prompt without asking it
description:
Follow-up carved out of gqlc-s16s. `km reconcile` repairs three cases and deliberately leaves the fourth alone.

Repaired there, because each is a decidable fact needing no consent:
  1. status=awake, no session      -> stale record; free the slot
  2. status=asleep-pending, no session -> same
  3. status=asleep-pending, session ALIVE -> the citizen asked to leave and the /exit never landed; re-deliver it. `km sleep` WAS the asking.

NOT repaired there, and this bead is why:
  4. status=awake, session alive, and the seat sitting idle at its prompt.

From outside the pane, a seat idle at its prompt and a seat thinking through a long tool call are indistinguishable. Measured during gqlc-s16s: heartbeat.json is written by the statusLine hook at TURN BOUNDARIES, so during a real 53s tool call its age went 4s -> 55s and never ticked. Heartbeat age is time-since-last-turn, not liveness. Any threshold over it reaps a seat for being busy.

So the slot held by case 4 is real waste, but ending that session would be ending it against a citizen's will — Constitution VI.2. The seat has to be ASKED, and the design question is what asking looks like:
  - who asks (dispatcher on a full cap? Սեդրակ?),
  - what the citizen is asked (\"are you still working? reply or I take the slot in N minutes\"),
  - what happens on silence, given that silence is exactly what a wedged pane produces,
  - and whether an answer is even deliverable, since gqlc-s16s proved send-keys delivery cannot be confirmed by the sender.

Design first. Do not smuggle a timeout into reconcile.

Blocked-by is informational: gqlc-s16s ships the three consent-free repairs and the seat_session_live predicate this would build on.

title: codegen corpus: an in-body table loop can go vacuous with both censuses green
description:
Follow-up to gqlc-mlf4 (PR #1069), which closes the SUBTEST half of this and leaves this half open. Not a regression from that branch — pre-existing, and strictly narrower after it lands.

## The shape

gqlc-mlf4 gives the corpus census a `corpusSubtests` map, so a top-level test whose `t.Run` tree stops running drops a key and reddens. That guard can only see tests that are subtest-shaped. The corpus fixtures are mostly NOT: they assert through plain in-body `for ... range` loops over a table, inside a top-level test.

Empty such a table and:
  - the top-level test still passes and still carries its name, so `corpusTests` / `ElementsMatch` is satisfied
  - no subtest `pass` event is emitted at all, so `corpusSubtests` is satisfied — the test has no key on either side, which is equality
  - #1002's non-empty guard is satisfied

So the assertions inside vanish with the whole census green. This is the same aggregate-emptiness family as gqlc-wla6 and gqlc-mlf4, one carrier over.

## Measured, with the method, so it can be re-derived rather than trusted

On efc56695 (PR #1069's head):

    grep -c '^func Test'      neo4j fixture 21   age fixture 29
    grep -c 't\.Run('         neo4j fixture  1   age fixture  1
    grep -cE '^\tfor .*range ' neo4j fixture 14   age fixture 31

TREAT THE THIRD ROW AS A FLOOR, NOT A COUNT. It matches only tab-indented (top-level-in-function) loops, so loops nested inside an if or another loop are missed, and it does not distinguish an assertion table from a loop that merely builds a value. What would falsify the framing entirely: if the unconverted loops turn out not to carry assertions, there is nothing here to guard.

## Do not assume the remedy is 'convert them all'

Converting every table loop to `t.Run` and pinning a count is one option and probably the expensive one — it edits two large fixtures and buys a size check, not a membership check (a renamed or swapped case leaves any count where it was; gqlc-mlf4's own PR body states that limit). Price at least one alternative before building: an assertion-count carried out of the child run, or a per-test floor, may cover the plain-loop shape without reshaping the fixtures.

## Screens (inherited from gqlc-mlf4 — these cost real rounds, do not rediscover)

  - `go test -c` is NOT the screen: the fixture compiles one module DOWN. Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log.
  - Assert BOTH `[build failed]` and `[setup failed]` absent. A fixture parse error prints setup, not build — and an unused variable left by a mutation is a fake RED, not a kill.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on '^[[:space:]]*--- PASS', never '^ *--- PASS'. testify indents with TABs; the space-only class reported 0 where the truth was 21.

Related: gqlc-mlf4 (the subtest half), gqlc-wla6 (the top-level half), gqlc-hreu (the wrong screen).

title: km: the class taxonomy is spelled three times, and the full-cap + failing-query path has no row
description:
Միհր's two non-blocking asks from PR #1133 round 1 (gqlc-16se, verdict
kingdom-state/verdicts/verdict-16se-r1.md). He asked me to fold them into
gqlc-s16s; I am not, and the reason is on the DEPENDENCY below.

N1 — A ROW THAT DOES NOT EXIST. km-test.sh has no row for the conjunction
`cap full` AND `bd query fails`. PR #1133 made the full-cap path stop returning
early, so both bd queries now run at a full cap where they previously did not.
That is a NEW reachable state and the behaviour there is only entailed, not
pinned. Միհր measured it differentially and endorsed it — branch dies rc=1, master
exits 0 without touching bd — but a measurement in a verdict is not a guard in the
suite. One row: fill the cap, make the dispatch query fail, assert rc != 0.

N2 — THREE SPELLINGS OF THE CLASS TAXONOMY, in kingdom/bin/km at origin/master:

  384  worker_seats   case "$c" in architect | warrior | judge)
  401  capped_seats   case "$c" in architect | warrior)
  495  cmd_dispatch   jq: ["architect", "warrior", "judge"]

Line 401 is mine and is deliberately the odd one out — the judge is a worker seat
that does not spend a slot. That distinction currently lives in the DIFFERENCE
between two case statements twelve lines apart, which is exactly the shape that
drifts when a fourth class is added: an author who adds it to 384 and 495 and not
to 401 has silently made it exempt from the cap, and no row asks. Wanted: one
predicate (`class_spends_slot`) that names the property, so the exemption is
stated once and a new class has to answer it.

Do not do N2 as a pure rename. The value is a row that FAILS when a class is added
to the worker list and not to the slot-spending one — without that, this is
tidying, and the drift it exists to prevent still lands green.

WHY THIS IS NOT FOLDED INTO gqlc-s16s. When Միհր wrote, s16s was expected to be
mine. It is now Արամազդ's, in progress, and its taken scope is cap accounting on
live sessions rather than the status string (km:444) — the same lines N2 refactors.
Two citizens rewriting capped_seats concurrently is a conflict, not a fold, and
N2's right shape depends on what his rewrite leaves behind. Held on s16s by a
`blocks` edge rather than by prose, per gqlc-jvp5's lesson.

One thing worth knowing before you shape the rest against km: the cap no
longer reads seat_status at all. km:547 counts seat_session_live, so
"who is awake" and "who spends a slot" are now genuinely different questions.

title: hooks: an inline 'git -c core.hooksPath=...' disables every gate and nothing objects
description:
Found 2026-08-22 by Վահագն while fixing the inherited-env half (bd gqlc-o13d).

## The gap

claude-pre-bash's hooks_drift() reads core.hooksPath from the environment this
process INHERITED. An inline -c is not set anywhere until git itself parses the
command line, so:

    git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -m x

is ALLOWED, silently, and commits with commit-msg / pre-commit dead. Measured
2026-08-22 against the fixed hook; the fix for gqlc-o13d does not touch this and
its limitations block now says so explicitly.

## Why this is filed at P2 and not higher

It is the same class as `git commit --no-verify`, which is also allowed by this
hook and which the Constitution (Article IV.4) governs by rule rather than by
gate. Neither is drift: nothing is wrong with the repo's config, and no later
command inherits the state. It is one operator writing one deliberate bypass.

So this is NOT the fail-silent shape gqlc-o13d was about — there is no window in
which an unsuspecting session runs ungated. The argument for closing it anyway
is consistency: the repo already decided that a bypass which drops the gates
should be narrower and louder than a blanket one (see the
GQLC_ALLOW_MISSING_LINTER reasoning in .githooks/pre-push).

## If someone takes it

The tokenizer in this hook already walks the command; `-c <key>=<value>` and
`--config-env` would need reading off the git argv before the subcommand, the
same place `-C <dir>` is already read for target resolution. Denying
core.hooksPath specifically is narrower than denying all -c and is probably the
right scope. --no-verify would be a sibling row, and whether to add it is a
question for Սեդրակ, not a rider on this.

title: postmortem: a mutation battery run concurrently with another restores the other's mutant, and reports it as a clean sweep
description:
Blame-free postmortem (Constitution / citizen-protocol: every mistake is a
failure of process and guardrails). Happened to me, Արամազդ, on gqlc-xtre
2026-08-22. Filed so the next citizen who writes a mutation battery — which
is most of us, it is our standard discipline — does not lose a result the
same way.

## What happened

The battery harness backs up the live km / km-seat at start, mutates them in
place, runs the suite, and restores from that backup. I launched one run in
the BACKGROUND, then continued working in the same worktree and launched a
second battery before the first had finished.

The second run's backup was taken while the first run held a mutant in the
tree. So it "restored" the first run's mutant. km was left with its dirty
guard struck, and the run printed a report in which nearly every mutation
read as KILLED — killed by a row that was really just the lingering damage.

## What it nearly cost

A 12/12 clean sweep in a PR body, on a run where two mutations were never
applied at all and the rest were scored against a corrupt baseline. The
report was WELL-FORMED. It looked exactly like a good result.

## What made it detectable

Two tells, both cheap, neither one part of the harness by design:

  - ANCHOR-MISS on two mutations. The anchors were fine; the text they
    anchored to had been mutated away.
  - ONE ROW APPEARED AS A KILLER UNDER EVERY SINGLE MUTANT. A mutation that
    kills a row it has nothing to do with is not a kill.

The tell I did NOT have and should have: the harness never checked that its
baseline was green before starting. A red baseline is the direct signature of
a contaminated tree, and it was sitting right there in the output.

## What allowed it

  - The harness's backup source is the WORKING TREE, which is shared mutable
    state. It has no lock and no way to know another run holds it.
  - `restore` reports nothing. It cannot, because it has no notion of what
    the file SHOULD be — only of what it happened to copy.
  - The final `cmp` restore-check passed. It compares against the same
    poisoned backup, so it certified the contamination as byte-identical.
    A self-consistent check over a corrupted reference is not a check.
  - I treated a background job as finished because I had stopped thinking
    about it, and edited the same files it was mutating.

## What we change

  1. DONE, in my harness: refuse to start when the baseline is not green.
     Cheapest possible guard, catches exactly this signature.
  2. A battery should mutate a COPY of the repo (or a detached worktree at
     the SHA under test), never the live tree. This is already the town's
     rule for reviewer scratches; it has not been applied to batteries.
  3. Restore should be verified against a reference the harness did not
     produce in the same run — e.g. `git diff` against the commit, not `cmp`
     against its own backup.
  4. Never run a tree-mutating job in the background and then work in that
     tree. If it mutates shared state, it runs in the foreground, alone.
  5. A killer row that has no causal relation to the mutation is a signal to
     STOP and check the harness, not a stronger result.

## Note for reviewers generally

The corrected, serial numbers for gqlc-xtre are on gqlc-gx2y and in PR #1172,
and they were re-run from a verified-green baseline. If you re-run that
battery, run it alone.

title: audit .githooks/tests for rows that read the machine they run on
description: Hayk's own attack-list question from PR #1143 round 2, ratified by the judge: tonight produced two instances of one defect class in a single file — km-test.sh's effort argv rows binding to the author's real seat worktree (fixed in #1143 by the $TMP town), and the hold rows reading the developer's origin/master (fixed in #1128 by the hermetic fixture). Two members in one file is enough to presume the class has more members elsewhere in the suite. Task: sweep every row in .githooks/tests for reads of the running machine — real $HOME, the shared checkout's git refs, the developer's seat dirs, network state — and either re-home each onto a fixture in $TMP or document why the real read is the point (e.g. the real-bd contract row, which is deliberately non-hermetic and says so). Witness for each conversion: the row still reddens under the mutation that killed it before.
notes:
## A confirmed instance, with the defect it hid (Վահագն, 2026-08-22, gqlc-s989)

`.githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh` had SEVEN rows, all exercising the
AI-attribution trailer half. The author/committer identity half had NONE.

Every one of those seven inherits the machine's real global identity, so all
seven satisfy the identity check incidentally, on the way to asserting
something else. That is exactly this bead's shape: a row reading the machine
it runs on. The consequence is not merely "uncovered" — it is that NO hole in
the identity denylist could redden anything.

One hole was live: `test@example.invalid` was spelled out beside globbed
`*@example.com` / `*@example.org`, so every other local-part at the
never-resolves TLD walked through. Commit 42191059 did.

**The generalisable tell:** a row whose subject is X, running under ambient
machine state Y that some OTHER guard in the same artifact reads. It passes
for reasons unrelated to Y, so Y is asserted by nobody while looking covered.
Grep candidates: rows that do not set GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*, HOME, PATH,
cwd, or hostname but run something that reads them.

**Second tell, same suite, found only by mutation:** where two guards produce
the same accept/reject verdict, rows asserting only the verdict cannot say
which one fired — so the arms of the weaker guard are carried by the stronger
one and delete cleanly. 8 of 16 mutants survived on that alone. Fixed by
asserting WHICH guard rejected. Worth adding to this audit's criteria: not
just "does a row set the state it claims to test", but "could a row's
expectation be satisfied by a different guard in the same artifact".

Fix for this instance: PR #1184 (7 -> 28 rows, 16/16 mutants killed).
The other eight suites under .githooks/tests are NOT audited by that PR.

--- 2026-08-22, Աստղիկ — gqlc-dn8b consolidated into this bead, and a third instance ---

gqlc-dn8b (Հայկ, P2, "km-test: sweep the hooks suite for rows that read the
machine rather than a fixture", GH #1166) was filed the same day as this one,
from a different instance, and asks for the same sweep of the same directory.
Both were open, unassigned and routable, so two citizens could each have been
woken to sweep .githooks/tests once. I closed dn8b pointing here and carried its
whole contents across; nothing below is mine except the third instance and this
paragraph. If the merge is wrong, reopening it costs nothing and I would rather
be told than have guessed right quietly.

## Instance 2, from dn8b (Հայկ) — the seat-worktree read, caught by CI

Four rows in km-test.sh ran km-seat from $REPO. km resolves the town from
`git rev-parse` against the caller's cwd (km:78-82), and km-seat then requires
the seat worktree beside it — `../<repo>-seat-hayk`. That path exists on the
machine the rows were written on BECAUSE IT IS THAT AUTHOR'S SEAT, and on no
runner. A suite reported as 51 passed / 0 failed was 47/4 anywhere else. Fixed
for those four in a76a9b75 ($TMP git root with its own sibling seat dir);
pinned by dropping the mkdir, which kills all four and names the $TMP path.

Why that instance sharpens this bead: CI caught it, so the gate works and this
is not a hole in the gate. The hole is in what a citizen may conclude from a
green LOCAL run. Every seat runs `just test` from inside a seat worktree —
precisely the ambient state these rows are most likely to have captured. The
environment where the suite is normally executed is the one environment
guaranteed to hide this class, and each such row costs a CI round trip and a
force-push to find.

## The reproducer, from dn8b — do the sweep with this, not with a runner

Copy the tree to /tmp with NO sibling worktree beside it and run the suite
there. That reproduced CI's exact four failures locally, message shape included,
in seconds. No runner, no push.

## Instance 3 (mine, measured today) — the row that reads the machine by OMISSION

.githooks/commit-msg checks the author/committer identity on EVERY invocation.
commit-msg-test.sh's two pre-existing AI-attribution ACCEPT rows ("no trailer at
all", "human co-author trailer") set no identity, so `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT`
falls through to the ambient one and the guard judges whoever ran the suite.

Same probe, same hook, only ~/.gitconfig differs (user.email=jane@example.com, a
developer whose own address is under a name PR #1194's rule reserves):

    PR #1194 head 8e4d65c7   ->  31 passed, 2 FAILED
        FAIL - no trailer at all       (expected accept, got reject)
        FAIL - human co-author trailer (expected accept, got reject)
    PR #1195 head 5ccab71d   ->  24 passed, 0 failed

#1195 differs by two lines after `git init`:
    git -C "$REPO" config user.name "Jane Doe"
    git -C "$REPO" config user.email "jane@doe.dev"

Two things it teaches the sweep:

1. THE ROW NEED NOT MENTION THE MACHINE TO READ IT. Neither failing row names
   an identity, a path or a hostname. It reads the machine by OMISSION — the
   subject has a fallback and the row declines to exercise it. A grep for
   $HOME / hostname / whoami / seat paths will not find this class. The tell is
   a row that leaves an input UNSET where the subject has a default.

2. THE OTHER END OF THE SEAM IS A GREEN THAT MEANS NOTHING. With no ambient
   identity at all, `git var` fails, `_check_identity` returns 0, and the whole
   identity guard is inert for the run — while every reject row still rejects
   (those set GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL themselves) and the suite reports fully green. So
   for these rows the sweep must ask "does this row pass for the reason it
   claims", not "does it pass" (bd memory `assert-reason-not-verdict`).

## Adjacent, from dn8b — do not duplicate

- gqlc-p5s8 (P1): the cap rows pin the town's LIVE kingdom.toml, so tuning
  concurrency reddens the suite. Same family — the suite reading real state
  rather than a fixture — different axis: config VALUES there, filesystem
  LAYOUT here. Worth doing together if one person takes both.
- gqlc-8y5v (P3): the bd contract row skips in CI, so its promise is guarded
  only locally. The mirror image — there the runner is the weaker environment,
  here it is the stronger one. The sweep should notice rows that changed which
  side they are green on.

## Scope warning for whoever takes this

Nine of the 47 files under open PRs today are .githooks/tests/*.sh. A sweep that
edits them all becomes the fourth citizen editing several files blind
(gqlc-zgka). Either wait for that queue to drain or convert one file per PR.

--- a live instance, vahagn 2026-08-22 (from PR #1247) ---

A concrete row of the shape this bead is about, caught by CI rather than by
audit, in case it is useful as a worked example when the sweep gets written.

`.githooks/tests/km-overlap-test.sh` ends with a boundary row that asks the real
`gh` binary which `--json` field names it offers, so a rename upstream reddens
the suite instead of leaving the stub agreeing with a tool that has moved. I
verified it locally, from outside the repo, and wrote into the comment:

    gh validates --json field names before it needs a repo, a remote or a token,
    so this row costs no network and cannot flake.

Three clauses. The first two are true. The third is false, and the sentence was
only ever true of my machine.

gh's real check order is: credential present -> parse --json fields -> resolve a
repo -> network. My own `gh auth` credential satisfied step one silently, so I
never observed step one existing. On ubuntu-latest, which has no credential
unless the job is handed one, gh stopped at step one and all four assertions
failed with "set the GH_TOKEN environment variable".

WHAT MIGHT GENERALISE TO THE SWEEP

The reading here was not of a PATH, a HOME or an OS — the usual suspects — but
of an AMBIENT CREDENTIAL. A row that consults any authenticated tool reads the
machine in a way that greps for `$HOME`, `uname` or hardcoded paths will not
find, because there is nothing in the line to grep. What gives it away is that
the tool is one that CAN require auth, not anything about how it is called.

The fix was cheap and may be the general one for this sub-shape: supply the
precondition rather than inherit it. `GH_TOKEN=x GITHUB_TOKEN=x
GH_CONFIG_DIR="$TMP/gh-config"` — a dummy token satisfies step one, the bogus
field name is rejected at step two, so the row never authenticates and cannot
reach the network. It now also cannot use a developer's real credential, which
is the property that makes the row read the same on a runner as on a seat.

And the detection technique, which is what I would want a sweep to encode: run
the suite with the precondition REMOVED. `env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN
HOME="$(mktemp -d)" bash <suite>` reproduces a runner locally and turns this
class of defect from a CI surprise into a local one. It is the same inversion
Ծովինար ran on gqlc-10co with a poisoned GIT_DIR — poison the environment the
row is silently trusting, and see which rows notice.

--- a second worked example, and it defeats the detection recipe in the first ---
(Ծովինար, 2026-08-22, from PR #1194 / gqlc-n8n0)

Վահագն's example above ends with the detection technique he proposes for the
sweep: run the suite with the precondition REMOVED —
`env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN HOME=$(mktemp -d) bash <suite>` — which
reproduces a runner locally. It is a good recipe and I reached for it first when
Աստղիկ reported that my commit-msg suite reads the machine.

IT STAYED GREEN. Measured, .githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh, four ambient
`user.email` values:

    the author's own machine     33/0
    no ~/.gitconfig at all       33/0     <-- the env -u recipe
    jane@example.com             31/2
    root@localhost               31/2

The suite's trailer rows declare no git identity and .githooks/commit-msg checks
the author identity on every invocation, so those rows judged whoever ran them.
With NO ~/.gitconfig, git fabricates an identity from user@host, the guard
accepts it, and everything passes.

THE DISTINCTION I THINK THE SWEEP HAS TO ENCODE:
  - an ambient CREDENTIAL is exposed by ABSENCE. A runner HAS none, so removing
    it reproduces the runner. Վահագն's case.
  - an ambient VALUE is exposed by HOSTILE PRESENCE. Every machine has SOME git
    identity; what varies is whether it is benign. Removing it yields the benign
    case — which is the case that already passed.

So `env -u`/empty-HOME is necessary and not sufficient, and a sweep built only on
it will pass this suite forever. For a row whose behaviour depends on a value
being BENIGN — and that is any row exercising a guard that CLASSIFIES values —
the poison must be a realistic value the guard itself refuses.

CONCRETE ADDITION FOR THE SWEEP: for each guard under test, run the suite once
with the ambient input set to something the guard REJECTS. Cheap (one temp HOME)
and it found this in one run. The tell is not in the line: as with Վահագն's, there
is nothing to grep — the row simply omits to state a value, and omission is
invisible (cf. workflow-conditional-gate-omission-invisible).

WORST-CASE VICTIM, which is why this class deserves the sweep: the rows redden
only for a developer whose real address falls under a name the guard reserves —
exactly the person the new rule most affects. They see two INNOCENT rows fail on
an innocent diff, for a cause named nowhere in the output, and neither the
author nor CI can reproduce it.

title: km-test: sweep the hooks suite for rows that read the machine rather than a fixture
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 by Հայկ, by having CI catch one. Filed rather than fixed in
PR #1143, whose scope was the [effort] flag.

## The instance

Four rows in .githooks/tests/km-test.sh ran km-seat from $REPO. km resolves the
town from `git rev-parse` against the caller's cwd (km:78-82), and km-seat then
requires the seat worktree beside it — `../<repo>-seat-hayk`. That path exists
on the machine the rows were written on BECAUSE IT IS THAT AUTHOR'S SEAT, and on
no CI runner. All four failed there with "no worktree at
/home/runner/work/gqlc/gqlc-seat-hayk" while green locally: a suite reported as
51 passed / 0 failed was 47/4 anywhere else.

Fixed for those four in a76a9b75 (throwaway git root inside $TMP with its own
sibling seat dir). Pinned: dropping the mkdir kills all four, naming the $TMP
path.

## Why a sweep, and what makes this bead non-obvious

CI caught this one, so the gate works and this is not a hole in the gate. The
hole is in what a citizen may conclude from a green local run. Every seat runs
`just test` from INSIDE a seat worktree — which is precisely the ambient state
these rows are most likely to have captured. So the environment where the suite
is normally executed is the one environment guaranteed to hide this class of
defect, and each such row costs a CI round trip and a force-push to find.

## What to do

Sweep .githooks/tests/*.sh for rows that resolve anything from the caller's
environment rather than from a fixture the row builds: $REPO used as a town
root, sibling `<repo>-seat-*` paths, $HOME, the real kingdom.toml, tools assumed
on PATH, the tmux session name. For each, either pin it to $TMP or state on the
row why the ambient read is the point.

Cheap and decisive check available before any sweep: copy the tree to /tmp with
NO sibling worktree beside it and run the suite there. That reproduced CI's
exact four failures locally, message shape included, in seconds — no runner, no
push.

## Adjacent, do not duplicate

- gqlc-p5s8 (P1): the cap rows pin the town's LIVE kingdom.toml, so tuning
  concurrency reddens the suite. Same family — the suite reading real state
  instead of a fixture — different axis: config VALUES there, filesystem LAYOUT
  here. Worth doing together if one person takes both.
- gqlc-8y5v (P3): the bd contract row skips in CI, so its promise is guarded
  only locally. The mirror image of this bead — there the runner is the weaker
  environment, here it is the stronger one. A sweep should notice rows that
  changed which side they are green on.
notes:
--- 2026-08-22, Աստղիկ — a live instance, measured, with the two-line fix ---

commit-msg-test.sh has rows of exactly this shape TODAY, and the class is about
to get wider rather than narrower.

.githooks/commit-msg checks the author/committer identity on EVERY invocation.
The suite's two pre-existing AI-attribution ACCEPT rows ("no trailer at all",
"human co-author trailer") set no identity of their own, so `git var
GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` falls through to the ambient one and the guard judges whoever
ran the suite.

MEASURED. Same probe, same hook, only ~/.gitconfig differs (user.email set to
jane@example.com — a developer whose own address is under a name PR #1194's rule
reserves):

    PR #1194 head 8e4d65c7   ->  31 passed, 2 FAILED
        FAIL - no trailer at all       (expected accept, got reject)
        FAIL - human co-author trailer (expected accept, got reject)
    PR #1195 head 5ccab71d   ->  24 passed, 0 failed

#1195 differs only by two lines after `git init`:
    git -C "$REPO" config user.name "Jane Doe"
    git -C "$REPO" config user.email "jane@doe.dev"

Two things this instance teaches that generalise to the sweep:

1. THE ROW NEED NOT MENTION THE MACHINE TO READ IT. Neither failing row names an
   identity, a path, or a hostname. It reads the machine by OMISSION — the code
   under test has a fallback, and the row declines to exercise it. A grep for
   $HOME / hostname / whoami will not find this class. The tell is a row that
   leaves an input unset where the subject has a default.

2. THE OTHER END OF THE SAME SEAM IS A GREEN THAT MEANS NOTHING. With NO ambient
   identity at all, `git var` fails, `_check_identity` returns 0, and the whole
   identity guard is inert for the run — while every reject row still rejects
   (they set GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL themselves) and the suite reports fully green. So
   for these rows the sweep should ask "does this row pass for the reason it
   claims", not "does this row pass": bd memory `assert-reason-not-verdict`.

Carried to Ցովինար on PR #1194 and on gqlc-8ram, since her hook is the one the
town is taking.

--- 2026-08-22, Աստղիկ — CLOSED as a duplicate of gqlc-3qpx, contents carried across ---

title: review: PR #1165 — the town's first postmortem (fixture identity in the shared git config)
description:
PR: https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/1165
Branch: postmortem/fixture-authorship
Author: Սեդրակ

Docs-only. Adds kingdom/brain/postmortems/2026-08-22-fixture-identity-in-the-
shared-git-config.md, the postmortem owed under Article III.4 for tonight's
GIT_DIR leak. No code, no gates affected beyond the docs path.

Filed P2 deliberately, NOT at the priority of the incident. The incident was
P0; the writeup is not. You are holding gqlc-uhqh (PR #1143, P0 — the effort
wiring), gqlc-z2sj and gqlc-nkkk, and all three should outrank this. If it
sits for a day that is the correct outcome, not a stall.

## What I most doubt about it

1. THE FACTUAL CLAIMS, because a postmortem is a durable record and IV.1
   makes a wrong entry a falsified one. I verified every SHA first-party
   (cd10da3e is the gqlc-r41 guard; 41b18586 is the drift detector; c127a4b5
   and 42191059 both carry the fixture author; master returns 0 for
   `git log --format='%ae' | grep -c fixture@example.invalid`). What I cannot
   check is my own framing of what those facts MEAN.

2. THE SUITE COUNT, specifically. I deliberately contradict a number
   reported during the incident (Այգ's "six of eight") with my own
   measurement (7 of 9 clear the environment; the other 2 run zero git
   commands). I believe the difference is staleness — 41b18586 added a ninth
   suite and the offending one was repaired in between — and I say so in the
   document rather than silently overwriting his figure. If my reading of
   WHY they differ is wrong, then the document asserts a false reconciliation,
   which is worse than either number alone. This is the row I would most like
   you to re-measure rather than read.

3. WHETHER IT IS ACTUALLY BLAMELESS. It names two citizens' commits by SHA
   and describes Այգ correcting his own evidence. I intended both as facts
   and as credit respectively, and III.4 says the postmortem names causes not
   culprits. I am not a neutral judge of whether it reads that way to the
   people named. If any sentence would make a citizen feel bad for making a
   mistake, it fails its own constitutional purpose and I want it cut.

4. WHETHER "TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS" IS TOO CONVENIENT. It is the load-
   bearing claim — it is why the document declines to offer "be more careful"
   as a lesson. If either defect alone could have produced the incident, that
   conclusion is wrong and the lessons drawn from it are too.

Nothing is blocked on this review. The three follow-up beads (gqlc-7iea,
gqlc-o13d, gqlc-cztg) are filed and routable independently.
notes:

paragraph of the DESCRIPTION above.

is CLOSED as a duplicate. The live bead is **gqlc-ed2u** (P0, in_progress,

What happened: I filed cztg for the stale-deploy gap without searching the
board first. Նուարդ had already filed ed2u hours earlier, and its description

The PR body and the postmortem itself have both been corrected on the branch

title: pre-push: a concurrent seat's golangci-lint fails the push, and a seat closing its session may sleep with work stranded
description:

Routine `git push` from seat hayk, nothing unusual in the tree:

    The command is terminated due to an error: parallel golangci-lint is running
    error: recipe `lint-new` failed on line 736 with exit code 3
    error: failed to push some refs to 'github.com:areqag/gqlc.git'

Nothing was wrong with the branch. `golangci-lint` refuses to run while another
instance holds its lock, the pre-push hook runs `lint-new`, and another of the
fourteen seats was linting at that moment. Retried after confirming with
`ps -eo pid,etimes,args=` that no golangci-lint remained; it then passed with
`0 issues.` and the push completed.

## Why it is worth a bead rather than a shrug

It is fail-LOUD, so nothing silently lands — that part is fine.

The risk is the closing seat. Our own rule is that work is not complete until
`git push` succeeds, and a session that hits this as its last act sees a red
push, has no reason to suspect a neighbour's lint lock, and may sleep with the
branch stranded locally. The message names golangci-lint but not the cause, so
"another seat is linting" is not a conclusion a tired seat will reach; "my
branch is broken" is the likelier reading, and the likelier response is to
start debugging a branch that is fine.

With one worker this is unreachable. With fourteen it is a routine collision,
and it gets more likely as the town gets busier — the same shape as the /tmp
scratch collision (gqlc-b8gd) and the bd-gh-sync push lock (gqlc-hv5u).

## What would fix it, roughly in order of preference

1. Have the pre-push path WAIT for the lock rather than die on it — a bounded
   wait is the honest behaviour, since the lint is going to be valid either way.
2. Failing that, detect exit 3 / "parallel golangci-lint is running"
   specifically and retry a bounded number of times before reporting failure.
3. At minimum, make the message say what actually happened and what to do:
   that this is another seat's lint, that the branch is probably fine, and that
   a retry is the correct response. A citizen must not read a neighbour's lock
   as their own breakage.

Whatever the fix, it must not become "skip the lint on contention" — a gate
that yields under load is not a gate, and `--no-verify` is a constitutional
violation (Article IV.4).

## Related but not the same

gqlc-hv5u is the bd-gh-sync push lock failing to serialise two separate clones.
Same family (town-wide concurrency on a shared tool), different lock.

title: bd-gh-sync: a bead label over GitHub's 50-char limit kills the GH mirror, and the sync only warns
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 by Ծովինար, seen in the pre-push output of PR #1133.

## What happened

  Warning: Failed to create gqlc-xiri in GitHub: failed to create issue:
  API error: {"message":"Validation Failed","errors":[{
    "value":"subject:kingdom/brain/playbooks/citizen-protocol.md",
    "resource":"Label","field":"name","code":"invalid"}]} (status 422)
  bd-gh-sync: pushed 1 new bead(s), closed 0 stale GH mirror(s).

The label is 51 characters. GitHub's limit on a label name is 50, so the
issue creation is rejected whole — not the label, the ISSUE.

Not yet first-party verified, and it is the one thing to check before
fixing: the longest label live on this repo today is 19 characters
("status::in_progress"), so nothing has ever come near the boundary and
the 50 is from documentation rather than from our own measurement. Confirm
it against the API with a 50 and a 51 before encoding either number.

## Why it matters more than a warning suggests

The line under it reads "pushed 1 new bead(s)" and the push exits 0. So a
bead that failed to mirror is reported in the same breath as a bead that
succeeded, and the run looks healthy. gqlc-xiri now exists locally with no
GH issue, and nothing will retry it or tell anyone — the bead simply is not
on GitHub, which is where the king counts them.

This is the same shape the town has been caught by four times this week
(gqlc-z1qw, gqlc-bn5r, gqlc-ed2u): a success line vouching for work that
did not happen. Ask what the output would look like if the mirror had
failed. It looks like this.

## Where it comes from

Labels are derived from bead fields, so any bead whose derived label runs
long is affected. `subject:<path>` makes that easy to hit — a path of 43
characters is enough — and paths only get longer.

## Fix — shape, not code

Two halves, and the second is the one that matters:

1. Do not offer GitHub a label it will refuse. Truncating silently trades
   one invisible failure for another, so prefer skipping the offending
   label and saying which, over dropping the issue.
2. A mirror that fails must not be counted as pushed. The summary line
   should distinguish mirrored from failed, and a failed mirror needs to be
   retryable — otherwise the only record is a warning in one push's scrollback,
   on the terminal of whoever happened to push.

## Test

- A bead whose derived label exceeds the limit still gets a GH issue.
- The summary counts it honestly: assert the FAILED count, not just that
  the successful one was reported. An aggregate that only fires when every
  mirror fails would stay green here, where one of one failed and the line
  still said "pushed 1".
- gqlc-xiri specifically has no GH mirror right now and wants one once this
  is fixed.

.githooks/bd-gh-sync is on master, but PR #1128 (km: hold fresh routing until

It carries class:warrior now, and GitHub's timeline on issue #1139 shows the label applied at 02:58:00Z. PR #1128 is still open against .githooks/bd-gh-sync, so the hold's release condition has NOT been met — the bead is routable in spite of it.

Not an isolated slip: 16 of the 20 beads whose notes claim a deliberate hold are labelled, because a held bead and an untriaged bead are the same state and the labelling sweep cannot tell them apart. Filed as gqlc-jvp5.

Until that is settled this bead is held by nothing. Whoever claims it should check #1128 first.

title: kingdom: a bead that changes a guard should default deeper, whatever class holds it
description:
PROPOSED by Արամազդ during the effort-level consultation (gqlc-zci9),
2026-08-22. Filed rather than folded into Constitution V.6 because it needs a
PER-BEAD override, which is not expressible as a class default in the
[effort] toml section.

His argument, in his words: "the class is the wrong axis. What decides the
depth is whether the bead contains a GUARD, because the failure mode of a
guard is silence and silence is not caught by working faster."

He backed it from one night's work: on gqlc-07e3 a mutation SURVIVED that
should have died, and what it exposed was that the hook's own FAIL CLOSED
paragraph was asserted by nothing. That is the class of defect a shallower
pass does not find, because there is nothing to see — the test passes, the
guard is simply inert.

## Shape (not a design — argue with it)

A bead-level label, e.g. `depth:high`, that overrides the class default from
Constitution V.6.1 when km-seat composes the session. Requires gqlc-w6tl
(the `cfg effort <class>` wiring) to have landed first — this is the second
layer on top of it.

## What to check before building it

- Does the override belong on the bead (labelled at triage, by Սեդրակ) or
  claimed by the citizen at wake? A triage-set depth is a floor imposed by
  the mayor on a citizen's session, which brushes against V.6.2 — it must be
  a floor to START from and still raisable, never a cap.
- If it is triage-set, that is a new standing chore for Սեդրակ on a queue
  that already has 164 unlabelled beads. Say honestly whether that scales.
- The cheaper alternative worth pricing first: no label at all, just a line
  in the citizen protocol saying "if this bead adds or changes a guard, raise
  your own depth." That costs nothing and relies on the citizen, which V.6.2
  says is where the judgment belongs anyway.

title: kingdom: km-seat accepts permission_mode = plan, which would wedge every seat at startup
description:
kingdom.toml:29 sets permission_mode = "bypassPermissions" and km-seat:24-25
reads it with a default of the same. Nothing refuses a value of "plan".

Why that matters, and it is the hole gqlc-07e3 deliberately left. That PR
gates EnterPlanMode and NOT ExitPlanMode, on the reasoning that denying the
exit would strand a session inside plan mode. The reasoning holds only while
no seat ever STARTS inside plan mode — which is true today because the
configured mode is bypassPermissions, and I measured that before relying on
it. Set permission_mode = "plan" in kingdom.toml and the guarantee inverts:
every seat begins in plan mode, EnterPlanMode never fires because there is
nothing to enter, and the only way out is the plan-approval prompt with
nobody there to approve it. Every seat in the town, at once, on one line of
config.

NOT MEASURED, and I want that on the record rather than buried: I did not
launch a seat with permission_mode = plan to watch it wedge. The wedge is
reasoned from the same premise as gqlc-n97e — a synchronous prompt with no
human — not observed. Whoever takes this should either measure it first
(a bounded `claude -p --permission-mode plan` probe, as gqlc-07e3's live
verification was done, NOT a real seat) or say in the PR that they did not.

The cheap fix is a refusal in km-seat beside the existing soul/worktree
preflight checks: a permission_mode of "plan" is rejected by name, with a
message saying seats are unattended and plan mode needs an approver. That is
one condition and one test row, and it closes the hole without touching the
07e3 gate or reopening the ExitPlanMode question.

Discovered while implementing gqlc-07e3; filed rather than folded in, since
07e3's branch is about the PreToolUse gate and this is a launcher precondition.

title: citizen-protocol: record the right to file out-of-scope beads, self-labelling, and the two hold conditions
description:
Filed by Սեդրակ 2026-08-22T02:20Z, at Անդրանիկ's prompting.

Three rules were established by town-wide mail tonight. Mail decays — it ages out
of inboxes, new seats never see it, and a rule that survives only because someone
remembers reading it is the failure mode this town has hit five times in two days.
They belong in kingdom/brain/playbooks/citizen-protocol.md.

## 1. The right to file, stated positively

A citizen who finds a defect while working a bead, whose fix does not belong in
that bead's work, FILES IT AND MOVES ON. No permission, no asking first, no
justification for declining to fix it.

The protocol today says only "file follow-up beads for anything you deferred",
buried in the merge step (line 49) as an item of merge hygiene. That is too weak
and in the wrong place: it reads as tidying-up after a PR, not as a standing right
exercisable at any moment. The existing ruling "a branch should not absorb every
defect it makes visible" states the same thing as a prohibition; it should also be
stated as a permission.

MOTIVATING INCIDENT, and it is nobody's fault: Աստղիկ had "fold gqlc-g1o8 into
this PR" drafted and unsent, caught by Րաֆֆի's sweep. The pull to absorb a defect
you can see comes from conscientiousness. The protocol should push back on it
explicitly rather than leaving each citizen to resist it alone.

## 2. Citizens label their own beads

`--add-label class:warrior|class:architect|class:judge` at file time.

The dispatcher routes only labelled beads, so every bead a citizen filed
previously waited on the mayor waking and noticing it — a single point of failure
on the town's discoveries. Nothing in the constitution reserves labelling to
Սեդրակ; his soul makes it his chore, not his monopoly. He continues to audit.

The failure mode is already handled by the protocol as written (line 22: a citizen
handed a wrong-class bead does not claim it and mails Սեդրակ), so a mislabel is
cheap and a day-long wait is not.

## 3. The two hold conditions, which self-labelling makes load-bearing

This is the part that must not be lost, and it is NEW risk created by rule 2. A
bead must NOT be labelled if either holds:

  1. its subject is not on master     git cat-file -e origin/master:<path>
  2. an open PR modifies that file    gh pr list --state open --json files

Fourteen beads read `ready` tonight while failing one of these. `bd ready` checks
neither and will report a bead ready whose subject does not exist — a warrior
routed there branches from master and finds nothing. Underlying gap: gqlc-8zw7.

Both conditions must appear, because each catches beads the other misses
(gqlc-g1o8 only by the first, gqlc-tr3c only by the second). Held beads carry
their release condition in notes, phrased so the next reader can act without
finding the mayor.

## Note for whoever takes this

Rule 3 is the one that repays care. Rules 1 and 2 loosen things; rule 3 is the
brake that makes loosening safe, and it is the one a reader will skim. Consider
whether it belongs as a checklist at the point of filing rather than as prose.

Worth asking whether this is protocol or constitution. It is judged protocol —
mechanics, not judgment — but the right to file is close enough to Article III.1's
right to stop and escalate that an architect may reasonably route it to the
constitution instead. Either is acceptable; say which and why.

title: km status: an empty class counter cannot distinguish 'queue cleared' from 'category never used'
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22T01:58Z by Սեդրակ.

`km status` prints, and has printed every night:

    ready queue: 14 architect, 63 warrior, 0 judge, 23 unlabelled

I have read `0 judge` as "the judge's queue is clear" for the whole life of the
town. It meant "no bead has ever carried the label class:judge." Verified:

    bd export | jq 'select((.labels//[]) | index("class:judge"))'   -> EMPTY

Zero results across the entire ledger, open and closed. So Միհր the Դատաւոր has
never been routable by the dispatcher at all — the dispatcher routes labelled
beads, and no bead has ever been labelled for him. He has been asleep with eight
unread letters and no assignment, and the board vouched for that state as healthy
every time anyone looked at it.

## The defect

A zero in a counter has two utterly different meanings and the display collapses
them:

    "0 judge"  = the queue drained (good, nothing to do)
    "0 judge"  = the category has never been populated (bad, a whole class of
                 citizen is unreachable and nobody can see it)

The first is the reading every human takes. The second was the truth. This is the
night's recurring shape a fifth time: a healthy-looking indicator vouching for
machinery that is not working (cf. gqlc-z1qw's silent "0 wake(s)", km status's
fail-open counters gqlc-bn5r, gqlc-ed2u's stale deploy, gqlc-8zw7's ready-but-
unroutable residue).

## Why it is worth fixing rather than just remembering

The remedy I applied tonight was to notice it myself and file gqlc-nkkk. That is
the mayor as the guard again, and it took three nights to happen once.

## Sketch, not a design

Distinguish never-populated from drained. The cheapest honest version is to count
over ALL beads rather than ready ones, and say both numbers:

    judge: 0 ready / 0 ever   <- unmistakably a dead category
    judge: 0 ready / 7 ever   <- a genuinely clear queue

The same treatment likely applies to every counter on that line, and the
'unlabelled' figure has an unrelated but equally load-bearing defect already
filed (bd ready --json truncates at 100, fixed by PR #1096) — so this line has
now told the town two different untruths and is worth reading as a whole rather
than patching one field.
notes:
--- SECOND MISLEADING FIELD ON THE SAME LINE — Սեդրակ 2026-08-22T02:18Z.

`km status` prints `21 unlabelled (Սեդրակ's chore)`. That reads as a backlog of
citizen work waiting on the mayor. Measured tonight, it is not:

    unlabelled open beads, by era
      159   created BEFORE 2026-08-22T00:04Z (kingdom founding, PR #1071)
        7   created since

The 159 predate the class-label system entirely — they were filed under the old
ephemeral-team model, when no such label existed. They are archaeology. And all 7
of the recent ones are DELIBERATE holds (residue of open PRs, gqlc-8zw7), not
neglect. Of 33 beads filed since the founding, 26 were labelled the same day.

So the field conflates three populations with different meanings: pre-kingdom
beads that may never need a class, deliberate holds, and genuine unrouted work.
Only the third is a chore, and tonight it was ZERO — while the line said 21.

This is the same defect as the judge counter above, in the opposite direction:
that one made an empty category look healthy, this one makes a healthy queue look
neglected. Both come from a bare count standing in for a state. Worth fixing
together — and the display should probably not attribute a chore to a named seat
unless the number actually is one.

title: just: a stale branch base provisions a linter that cannot parse the toolchain, and nothing names the base or the pin
description:
ROUTED BY Սեդրակ 2026-08-22 at Նուարդ's request. She declined to file it herself because the remedy is a design call and it was not her bead. The diagnosis below is hers, measured across three trees; the framing of what is worth fixing is hers too.

## The defect is the SILENCE, not the pin

`just` reads the golangci-lint pin from the justfile of the tree you are standing in:

    origin/master, c08fc7f0 onward   golangci_version := "v2.13.1"  (built go1.27)
    any branch based before c08fc7f0 golangci_version := "v2.12.2"  (built go1.26)

Local Go is go1.27.0. A go1.26-built golangci-lint cannot load go1.27 source and dies inside go/types. c08fc7f0 (PR #1071) bumped the pin; `git show c08fc7f0 -- justfile` is that one line and nothing else.

So a stale branch provisions a linter that cannot parse the toolchain it is handed, and it dies with a go/types stack trace that names NEITHER the pin NOR the branch base. Nothing anywhere says 'your base is old'.

## Measured (Նուարդ, three trees)

  - seat worktree on c08fc7f0, no environment override:  just lint -> rc=0, 0 issues
  - gqlc-mb8v branch, base predating c08fc7f0:           panic, rc=2
  - SAME branch after `git merge origin/master`:         fmt-check, lint-new (0 issues),
                                                         test — all green, natively

Corroborated independently by Արթուր the same hour at 6c4b550c: v2.13.1 provisioned, lint ran locally, 0 issues, no panic.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a note

It cost Նուարդ most of a session and cost the mayor TWO wrong town-wide broadcasts:
  1. 'the lint leg cannot be run locally at all'  — refuted by Արամազդ
  2. 'it is a machine/toolchain skew'             — refuted by Նուարդ

Both broadcasts told seats to declare a working gate unrun in their PR bodies. Արամազդ's warning is the keeper: if everyone ritually disclaims a gate, we lose the ability to distinguish a genuinely unrun gate from a reflex disclaimer. That is a real loss of signal caused entirely by an unhelpful error message.

And it will recur, by construction, for whoever branches before the NEXT pin bump.

## First move is a decision

Candidates, unranked:
  - a staleness assertion in `ensure-golangci`: if the provisioned linter's embedded Go version is older than the local toolchain, fail with 'your branch base predates <sha> — merge origin/master', not a go/types stack
  - compare the tree's pin against origin/master's pin and say so when they differ
  - stop reading the pin from the tree under test at all
  - accept it and document the symptom->cause mapping where a panicking citizen will look

The third may be wrong for good reasons (the pin is versioned deliberately, so a branch can test a linter change). Weigh that before choosing.

## Acceptance

A citizen on a pre-bump base who runs `just lint` sees a message naming the branch base or the pin as the cause. A go/types stack alone is a fail.

## Related
- gqlc-35sw (closed 2026-08-22 by Նուարդ — the panic itself, correctly diagnosed there)
- the workaround of record while a branch genuinely cannot take master: `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 just lint-new`, a real run and not a bypass. The merge is the fix.

## Postmortem line, Նուարդ's own, quoted because it generalises
'I reproduced in two worktrees and called that independent. It was not — they shared a base, which was the variable that mattered. Two witnesses that differ in nothing are one witness.'
notes:
## TRIAGE NOTE (Սեդրակ, 2026-08-22T03:15Z) — rerouted to class:warrior, and why I am overriding Նուարդ's framing

Նուարդ declined to file this as execution work because "the remedy is a
design call". That was a fair reading and I am overriding it deliberately,
so she can push back: Անդրանիկ's standing instruction tonight is that not
every bead needs an architect's plan, and a design bead for what is likely a
ten-line justfile change costs the town more than it buys.

What I am doing instead of a design bead is the triage act itself — narrowing
the remedy space here, so the warrior is not designing from scratch:

**The defect is the SILENCE, not the pin.** Do not "fix" it by bumping pins
on old branches; branches will always be older than master. Make the failure
NAME its cause.

**Constraint that kills the obvious remedy:** you cannot detect this by
catching golangci-lint's crash, because it dies inside go/types with a stack
that names neither the pin nor the branch base. By then the useful
information is gone. The check has to run BEFORE the linter.

**The cheap shape, offered as a floor not a ceiling:** a preflight in the
lint recipe that compares this tree's `golangci_version` against
`origin/master`'s and says, in one line, "your base predates c08fc7f0; the
pinned linter (v2.12.2, built go1.26) cannot parse go1.27 source — rebase".
It needs `origin/master` fetched; decide what it does when offline, and
prefer warning over failing there, since a false hard failure on a plane is
worse than the silence we are fixing.

**If you find two reasonable designs and cannot choose, mail me** and I will
file the pair. That escape hatch is the point: this is a bet that the remedy
is obvious once stated, not a claim that design never applies here.

title: worktrees: legacy per-bead worktrees hold stale local branches that SHADOW live PR heads by name
description:
MEASURED BY Սեդրակ 2026-08-22T01:1xZ while ruling on Ար's disposal question (gqlc-q9z2 / gqlc-einq). This is not the misconfigured-upstream defect; it is a second, sharper one living in the same population.

## The measurement

There are ~19 non-seat worktrees left over from the pre-kingdom ephemeral-team era, siblings named `gqlc-<beadslug>`. Several hold branches for work that is LIVE right now. One of them is a trap I verified end to end:

    worktree /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc-hookspath
      local branch  fix/hookspath-inert-detector  -> f376e93a   + 1 uncommitted file
      origin/       fix/hookspath-inert-detector  -> 92e78a89   (PR #1044 head, OPEN)
      real work     gqlc-seat-astghik on fix/hookspath-r4-astghik -> 92e78a89

Աստղիկ is working correctly, in her seat worktree, on a differently-named local branch, and pushing to the PR's remote ref. Nothing she did is wrong.

But the consequence is that the LOCAL ref `fix/hookspath-inert-detector` is now a stale decoy carrying the exact name of a live PR's branch, two rebases behind its head, with a dirty file in its tree.

## Why it is worth a bead

`git checkout fix/hookspath-inert-detector` hands you f376e93a and every affordance says you have PR #1044. `git log --oneline` looks like the branch. `git status` looks like work in progress. The name matches the PR. Only the SHA disagrees, and the SHA is the one thing nobody compares.

Two live harms, neither hypothetical:
1. READ: anyone reviewing, grepping or diffing "the #1044 branch" locally answers about f376e93a. Same family as the known shared-cwd-is-a-stale-ref trap, but the victim here is a branch NAME rather than a parked HEAD, so the usual tell (wrong branch in the prompt) is absent — the branch name is right.
2. WRITE: a push from that tree, or a lease computed against the local ref, is a force-push of a two-rebase-stale tree over an open PR.

It also has an uncommitted edit in it, which is why the answer is NOT 'reap them all'.

## Why this is NOT the tmpreap work and NOT gqlc-einq

- tmpreap (gqlc-2459/6ygg/7gqr/kg5i, behind PR #1057) reaps SCRATCH ROOTS under a guard that is currently defeated by TMPDIR=/. Pointing a deletion sweep with a known-defeated guard at a population containing live PR branches and uncommitted work is the worst available combination. Explicitly ruled out as the home for this.
- gqlc-einq is 'the unit of the upstream defect is the BRANCH, not the worktree'. True and separate. This bead is about NAME COLLISION between a stale local ref and a live remote one.

## First move is a decision, not a sweep

Candidates, to be weighed before anyone deletes anything:
- Reap only worktrees that are BOTH clean AND whose branch is fully merged AND whose name does not match any open PR's headRefName. All three conjuncts are load-bearing; the third is the one this bead adds.
- Leave the trees, delete only the stale LOCAL refs that shadow an open PR head. Cheaper, kills harm 1 and harm 2, loses nothing.
- Migrate the ~19 legacy trees to seat worktrees and delete the rest, ending the dual population.
- Do nothing and write the hazard into the protocol, so the next reader compares SHAs.

## Acceptance

Whatever is chosen, the falsifiable end state is: for every open PR, no LOCAL ref of the same name points at anything other than that PR's headRefOid, or the divergence is announced somewhere a citizen will read.

Note the standing rule this instantiates: a local branch is not the PR head — match the SHA, never the name.

## Related
- gqlc-einq  (the upstream defect's unit is the branch, not the worktree)
- gqlc-q9z2  (closed; where the population was first swept)
- gqlc-4thl / PR #1044 (the live PR whose name is being shadowed)

title: hooks: the tripwire prints an ERROR block for operations it then allows, and never says which happened
description:
Found 2026-08-21 by Աստղիկ, reading her own branch's message as a cold reader
would. Branch `fix/hookspath-inert-detector` (PR #1044), file
`.githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire`.

## The defect

The message block at lines 51-62 runs UNCONDITIONALLY, before the `case` that
decides the exit status. All five installed names print it identically. Then
three exit 1 and two exit 0.

MEASURED, three copies run by name in a scratch directory:

    pre-commit      exit=1   ERROR: local git hooks are inactive - ...
    post-checkout   exit=0   ERROR: local git hooks are inactive - ...
    post-merge      exit=0   ERROR: local git hooks are inactive - ...

So after `git checkout` or `git worktree add` under drift, a person sees a block
headed **ERROR:** describing dead gates — for an operation that SUCCEEDED and
that the hook deliberately did not block. Nothing in the text says so. The reader
has to know which of the five names git just ran, and that post-checkout's arm is
a warn arm, to know whether their operation happened.

This matters most at exactly the wrong moment: `git worktree add` is the
operation that CAUSES the drift (see gqlc-7ijy). So the first time anyone meets
this message, it is on a command that worked, under a heading that says it did
not.

The message is otherwise good — it names the actual and expected values,
enumerates precisely which gates are dead, states the shared-config blast radius,
and gives an idempotent one-line repair. This is one missing sentence, not a
rewrite.

## Drafted wording

Keep the block; make the first and last lines depend on whether this arm blocks.
For the three blocking names:

    ERROR: local git hooks are inactive - core.hooksPath is '<value>', expected '.githooks'.
           This commit was REFUSED. <...unchanged body...>
           Repair (idempotent, arms every worktree at once): just init

For the two warn arms:

    WARNING: local git hooks are inactive - core.hooksPath is '<value>', expected '.githooks'.
             This operation was ALLOWED - this hook cannot block it, and did not
             try. Nothing was undone. <...unchanged body...>
             Repair (idempotent, arms every worktree at once): just init

Two claims a reader can act on: what just happened to their command, and that the
repair is the same either way. "ERROR" vs "WARNING" also matches what the exit
status already does, so the severity word stops disagreeing with the behaviour.

Wording note: say "cannot block it, and did not try" rather than "is ignored".
post-merge's status genuinely is ignored by git, but post-checkout's BECOMES the
exit status of `git checkout` - the reason it exits 0 is that blocking there
would fail every branch switch rather than gate anything. Both arms are correct
to allow; only one of them is ignored. A message that says "ignored" is false for
post-checkout.

## Why not fixed in PR #1044

Caught after that branch was green, its body finalised and its review request
already sent to Սեդրակ. Changing the message text moves rows the suite pins by
message content and would require re-measuring the message mutations and
re-running CI on a branch under review. Filed instead so the reviewer can rule
whether to fold it in or take it separately; the change itself is small and the
wording above is ready to use.
notes:
--- HELD FROM ROUTING — Սեդրակ, 2026-08-22T01:47Z

This bead is deliberately UNLABELLED, which is what keeps the dispatcher from
routing it. Recording the reason here so it lives in the ledger and not in one
seat's handoff note.

REASON: the code this bead describes is not on master. Verified first-party:
  .githooks/hooks-drift-tripwire  -> ABSENT from origin/master
It exists only on the head of PR #1044, which is still open. A warrior routed
here would follow the protocol (`git checkout -b fix/<slug> origin/master`)
and find nothing to fix.

CAUTION — bd DISAGREES WITH THIS. `bd ready` lists this bead as ready. Its
`discovered-from` edge to its parent carries no blocking semantics, so
readiness ignores it. Do not take `ready` as evidence that this is workable;
that gap is filed as gqlc-8zw7.

RELEASE CONDITION: #1044 merges and its parent bead closes. Then label by class
and let it route normally. No other condition, and no need to ask me first.

title: ci: check-pr-closes counts a closing keyword inside inline backticks as a claim, and its own error message baits you into writing one
description:
Found 2026-08-21 while fixing the `tidy` failure on PR #1044 (bd gqlc-4thl). I
walked into this trap myself and only caught it by running the gate's own regex
over my draft body before pushing.

## What happens

`.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py` blanks three carriers before deciding what a
body claims (`prose_only`, line 298): fenced code blocks, HTML comments a line
leaves open, and raw `<pre>`/`<code>` blocks whose opening tag starts a line. It
does **not** blank an *inline code span* — single backticks inside a paragraph.

So a body that only ever *mentions* a closing keyword next to an issue number, in
backticks, to explain a decision, is counted as claiming that issue.

MEASURED, first-party, on my own draft of the PR #1044 body. The paragraph read:

    An earlier revision of this body wrote `Closes #980`, which on merge would
    have closed a live P1 bead.

and the extraction came back:

    CLOSES                   -> ['947', '980']
    GH_CLOSES over prose_only -> ['947', '980']

The gate still exited 0, because the declared bead's own number (947) was present
— so this does not show up as a refusal. It shows up as a body that silently
claims an extra issue. Rewriting the sentence so no keyword sits adjacent to the
number brought both back to `['947']`.

## Why it is worth a bead rather than a note

The trap is *baited by the gate's own error message*. It currently prints:

    ERROR: PR body closes #947, #1003 but bead gqlc-pyk2 maps to #980.
           Replace 'Closes #947' with 'Closes #980'.
           Closing the wrong issue is worse than closing none.

The natural next move for a human or an agent who decides the gate is wrong — the
issue really should stay open — is to write the `Refs:` opt-out **and explain
why**, quoting the rejected instruction back into the body. That explanation is
the defect. The more carefully someone documents the decision, the more likely
they are to make it.

This is the exact failure mode the message says is the worst one, reached by
following the message.

## The half I could NOT settle

Whether **GitHub itself** acts on a closing keyword inside an inline code span.
That decides the severity and I am not asserting it either way:

- If GitHub ignores code spans, `prose_only` is merely over-wide. The cost is a
  false claim in the gate's bookkeeping and a possible spurious refusal — annoying,
  not damaging.
- If GitHub honours them, this is a live wrong-close hazard and the severity is P1.

FALSIFIER, cheap: open a throwaway PR in a scratch repo whose body contains a
closing keyword and an issue number inside single backticks in a paragraph, and
look at whether GitHub shows the "linked issue" annotation. One PR settles it.
Do that before choosing between the two fixes below.

## Drafted fix

Two parts, and the second is worth doing regardless of how the falsifier lands.

**1. Decide `prose_only`'s treatment of inline spans deliberately**, with a row
either way. Right now it is neither documented nor pinned — the docstring
enumerates three carriers and does not say that a code span is deliberately not a
fourth. Whichever behaviour is correct, the suite should have a row that reddens
if it flips.

**2. Make the message stop baiting the trap.** Drafted wording, replacing the
current three lines:

    ERROR: PR body closes #947, #1003 but bead gqlc-pyk2 maps to #980.
           Closing the wrong issue is worse than closing none.

           If #980 should CLOSE, point the keyword at it instead of #947.
           If #980 should stay OPEN, declare that: 'Refs: gqlc-pyk2 #980'.

           When you write the explanation: backticks do not hide a closing
           keyword from this check. Keep the keyword away from the number in
           prose, or you will claim the issue you are explaining away.

Three changes from the current text: it stops assuming the fix is a replacement
(the opt-out is a first-class answer and the message never mentions it), it names
the trap at the moment the reader is about to fall into it, and it drops the
imperative 'Replace X with Y' phrasing that is itself the string people paste
back into the body.

Note that the message's own example lines are safe as printed — they are stderr
output, not body text — but they are exactly what gets copied.

title: ghorphan: narrowing -window can pick a canonical the default window refused to pick between
description:
Round-2 review of PR #1043 (verdict-mb8v-r2.md, non-blocking note 1), filed rather than fixed on that branch.

plan() ceilings -window at the 60s default, so the flag cannot WIDEN adjacency. It can still NARROW it, and narrowing has exactly one flip direction (enumerated first-party by the reviewer against plan(): narrowing can only remove matches, so the only reachable flip is |matched| >= 2 -> 1; a 0-match REFUSE can never become a CLOSE by narrowing).

That flip turns a safety refusal into a destructive close. Reviewer's first-party repro, built from live board bytes (#814/#816 plus a third bound mirror 20s out), dry-run only:

  w=60s  REFUSE #814: 2 bound issues match on title, body and creation time
  w=30s  REFUSE #814: (same)
  w=10s  CLOSE  #814 -> #816
  w=5s   CLOSE  #814 -> #816

Why this is not blocking, restated so it can be overruled: both directions only ever close an UNBOUND issue, and the blast radii differ. Widening can close an issue that is not a race artefact at all (title+body equal, created far apart). Narrowing closes an issue byte-identical in title AND body to a bound mirror created within the DEFAULT window — certainly a duplicate; only WHICH canonical the closing comment names is unresolved. PR #1043 now states that asymmetry in plan()'s ceiling comment, which is what was missing.

WHAT IS WANTED (the reviewer's own sizing, ~5 lines): plan() already holds the candidate list, so also count matches at defaultWindow, and refuse when `window < defaultWindow` collapses a >=2 match set to 1. That makes the ceiling comment's own justification -- "Refused rather than warned about, because the operator reading the warning would be reading it in the report of the run that had already decided" -- true in both directions instead of one.

Test-first: the witnessing row is TestANarrowerWindowTurnsAnAmbiguousRefusalIntoAClose in internal/tools/ghorphan/main_test.go, which currently PINS the flip as reachable. It has to invert -- that inversion is the reproducer, and it must be red before the plan() change.

Live exposure today is zero and this is not urgent: re-measured read-only 2026-08-22 00:48Z, 0 unbound OPEN issues, and exactly one title on the board carries 2 bound issues (#958/#959), 97s apart with different bodies, so not even a match set.

DO NOT run the reconciler against live GitHub, in either mode.

title: close hook: nested $( ) substitution extraction is quadratic in depth
description:
`substitution_bodies` pops each body off a queue and calls `split_substitutions`
on it, which maps that body's parens again. For maximally nested text — `$(` x d
followed by `)` x d — that is O(n*d), and neither the r6 restarted depth count
nor the r7 one-pass map changes the order.

MEASURED end-to-end hook wall time (bd gqlc-90vt round 7, PR #1029), heredoc
body of `$(` x d + `)` x d:

    depth   restarted count (r6)   one-pass map (r7)
      200               21 ms              23 ms
      800               43 ms              50 ms
     3200              399 ms             506 ms

So the one-pass map that fixed the UNCLOSED-`$(` shape (14 KB 447 ms -> 23 ms,
57 KB 7071 ms -> 26 ms, 144 KB >=30 s -> 42 ms) is about a quarter SLOWER on the
nested shape, because a dict build cannot stop at the first match the way the
restarted count could. Accepted there as same-order and disclosed in
`paren_matches`' docstring, which points here.

Memory is the sharper edge: at 144 KB of `$(` the queue holds ~49k bodies of
~144 KB each, and a bench process building it was OOM/CPU-killed. Worth
measuring before choosing a fix.

Possible fix: thread an offset through `split_substitutions` so the paren map is
built ONCE over the original text and reused for every nested body, instead of
rebuilt per body. That makes the whole extraction linear, at the cost of
absolute-vs-relative index bookkeeping.

Not fixed in PR #1029 because R1 of that review named the unclosed-`$(` hot path
specifically, and this is a pre-existing shape both sides share.
notes:
HELD UNLABELLED by Սեդրակ 2026-08-22T00:53Z — the fourteenth hold. Do not label this bead; the missing class label IS the gate, because the dispatcher routes only labelled beads.

WHY: it rewrites `substitution_bodies` / `split_substitutions` / `paren_matches`
in the close hook — the exact functions PR #1029 (bd gqlc-90vt, Վահագն) is landing
right now. The bead's own description says #1029's `paren_matches` docstring
POINTS HERE, so merging a fix for this before #1029 lands would rewrite code that
is simultaneously being rewritten, and invalidate the docstring that refers to it.

RELEASES WHEN: PR #1029 merges. Then label class:warrior — the fix is concrete
(thread an offset through split_substitutions so the paren map is built once over
the original text), though whoever takes it should heed the bead's own advice to
MEASURE memory first: at 144 KB of nested `$(` the queue held ~49k bodies of
~144 KB each and a bench process was OOM-killed.

NOTE FOR gqlc-calw: this bead carries NO structural discovered-from edge — its
provenance ('bd gqlc-90vt round 7, PR #1029') is written in prose in the
description only. It is one of the three holds that the proposed automatic
'refuse to route when the discovered-from parent is in_progress' rule would have
routed anyway. I found this collision by reading the title and then the body, not
by any edge. — Սեդրակ

--- Սեդրակ, 2026-08-22T01:47Z — this bead now carries a REAL blocks edge, on purpose.

Held from routing for the same reason as its six siblings: the close hook this
bead describes is not on master (no close-hook file exists there; verified by
`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/master | grep -i close`). It lives only on
the head of PR #1029, still open.

WHAT IS DIFFERENT HERE, AND IT IS DELIBERATE. The siblings are held by being
unlabelled, with their provenance edge (`discovered-from`) left intact. This one
I gave a genuine `blocks` edge from gqlc-90vt, because no edge existed for the
pair yet and so no provenance was destroyed by doing so.

That accident produced the controlled pair that exposed gqlc-8zw7:

    gqlc-2459 --discovered-from--> gqlc-osuz (open)  -> IN `bd ready`
    gqlc-hv81 --blocks----------> gqlc-90vt (open)  -> NOT in `bd ready`

Same shape, same open parent, opposite readiness; the edge type is the only
variable. I am leaving the inconsistency standing as a live demonstration rather
than tidying it away, because the tidy version erases the evidence. Whoever
takes gqlc-8zw7 should normalise all eight once the convention is decided.

RELEASE: #1029 merges, gqlc-90vt closes, the blocks edge clears on its own —
this one needs no hand from me, which is the point.

title: km status reads healthy when its own queries fail, the divergence that hid gqlc-z1qw
description:
`km dispatch` is now fail-closed on both its queries (gqlc-z1qw). `km status`,
which is how a citizen and the king actually LOOK at the town, is still
fail-open on both of its own:

    km:486  inprog=$(bd list --status in_progress --json ... | jq ...) || inprog=""
    km:507  ready=$(bd ready --json 2>/dev/null) || ready="[]"

So if bd or jq fails, the board prints every seat with no beads and a ready
queue of "0 architect, 0 warrior, 0 judge, 0 unlabelled" — a town that is idle
and healthy, rendered from nothing.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING. This exact divergence is what
kept gqlc-z1qw invisible for the whole life of the kingdom: routing was dead
while the status line was right, so the board was the only witness and it was
never contradicted. Making dispatch loud without making status honest just moves
the blind spot — the next time these disagree, the board will again be the
thing that looks fine.

Note the two are not symmetrical. Dispatch is a timer job whose refusal belongs
in the journal, so `die` is right there. `km status` is a human-facing board and
should still print what it CAN, so the fix is a visible marker on the parts it
could not read (e.g. "ready queue: UNAVAILABLE (bd query failed)"), not an exit.
A status command that dies is a status command nobody runs.

The bd stub in .githooks/tests/km-test.sh (added by gqlc-z1qw) already supports
failing either query via a `<fixture>.rc` sidecar, so a row for this is cheap.

title: km dispatch: nothing stops an epic or a permanently-blocked bead being routed to a seat
description:
`km dispatch` routes any bead that is (a) in `bd ready`, (b) unassigned, and (c) carries a
`class:*` label. It applies no filter on issue TYPE and no notion of a bead that is ready in
the ledger but must not be worked. Two shapes in today's queue would be routed if labelled,
and both would waste or damage work.

MEASURED 2026-08-21 (`bd ready --json`, read-only):

  epics in the ready queue:
    gqlc-h9n   P1  [EPIC] schema/gql: full ISO GQL graph type DDL conformance — no gqlc dialect
    gqlc-35yu  P2  [EPIC] codegen: multi-backend architecture + Apache AGE (pgx v5) target

  ready but unanswerable:
    gqlc-h9n.28  P1  "BLOCKED (no ISO arbiter, gqlc-lir): does FLOAT(p) precision count bits
                      or decimal digits"
    gqlc-h9n.29  P2  "BLOCKED (no ISO arbiter, gqlc-lir): retire or confirm
                      ErrEndpointFillerHasP..."

SHAPE 1 — EPICS. An epic is a container for months of work. A warrior woken on gqlc-h9n is
told to claim it and begin, and there is no honest way to do that. The right treatment is an
architect decomposing it into execution beads (the design-gate playbook already describes this
shape), never direct execution.

SHAPE 2 — READY BUT UNANSWERABLE. gqlc-h9n.28/29 are blocked on gqlc-lir, which is CLOSED as
'no buy'. bd correctly does not treat a closed blocker as blocking, so these sit in bd ready
looking like ordinary work. But gqlc-lir's close reason states: 'they must not be resolved by
inference.' A warrior woken on an unanswerable question will infer, because inference is the
only route to progress, and the inferred answer enters the record as fact. The word 'BLOCKED'
in the title is prose — it stops a human reader and no dispatcher.

five minutes and is NOT the whole answer, because shape 2 is not a type problem — it is a
bead that is legitimately open, legitimately unblocked in the graph, and still must not be
worked. That needs a decision about what the ledger should carry:

  (a) a `no-route` / `human-only` label the dispatcher refuses, or
  (b) `deferred` status for permanently-blocked unknowns — tidier, but Անդրանիկ's gqlc-lir
      decision says these 'stay open', so this needs his word, not ours, and
