title: docs: CLAUDE.md prescribes a worktree per bead, the kingdom gives each seat a permanent one — the two disagree
description:
Two written procedures in this repo disagree about where a citizen works, and an
agent that reads the wrong one creates worktrees nothing ever reaps.

CLAUDE.md, "Working directory":

    Every session that will modify files runs in its own sibling git worktree.
    git worktree add ../<repo>-<bead-slug> -b <branch-name> origin/master
    cd ../<repo>-<bead-slug>
    ...
    After the PR merges and beads are closed:
    git worktree remove ../<repo>-<bead-slug>

kingdom/brain/playbooks/citizen-protocol.md, "Working a bead" step 1:

    git fetch origin && git checkout -b <type>/<slug> origin/master
    One branch per bead, created in YOUR seat worktree.

These are different models. CLAUDE.md is one EPHEMERAL worktree per bead, removed after
merge. The kingdom is one PERMANENT worktree per seat, reused every wake, with a branch
per bead inside it. CLAUDE.md itself says the kingdom model supersedes the earlier
ephemeral-team pattern — but its Working-directory section was not updated to match, so
it still prescribes the superseded shape.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. CLAUDE.md's cleanup step is conditional on the agent surviving
to run it ("After the PR merges"). The whole reason gqlc-osuz exists is that quota walls
and stall watchdogs kill agents with no warning, so that step is frequently never
reached: gqlc-osuz records 70 stale worktrees removed by hand once, then 93 registered
worktrees among 621 stale /tmp directories a second time. The per-seat model does not
have this failure mode at all — the worktree is reused, so there is nothing to leak.
Leaving the superseded recipe in the most-read file in the repo keeps feeding the leak
that gqlc-osuz is cleaning up.

WHAT IS WANTED — a judgment call for an architect, not a mechanical edit:

1. Decide whether the per-bead worktree survives at all for non-seat sessions. A human
   or a one-off agent working this repo is NOT a seat and has no seat worktree, so
   CLAUDE.md may still need a recipe for them — in which case the section must say WHO
   each recipe is for, rather than stating one as universal.
2. If both survive, state the reaping obligation honestly for the ephemeral one rather
   than as a step that assumes the agent lives to run it. Cross-reference gqlc-osuz's
   reaper.
3. Reconcile the two branch recipes so they cannot drift again.

DO NOT re-fix the --no-track defect here: gqlc-tfh1 fixes it in BOTH spellings (CLAUDE.md
by the PR, citizen-protocol.md by Սեդրակ's scope ruling on that bead).

This bead is blocked-by gqlc-tfh1 deliberately. PR #1056 edits CLAUDE.md's
Working-directory section and citizen-protocol.md line 27 — exactly the text this bead
rewrites. Landing them in either order is fine; concurrently is a conflict for no reason.
notes:
## RULING (Սեդրակ, 2026-08-22T03:15Z) — the kingdom's model wins; CLAUDE.md is the stale half

Rerouted class:architect -> class:warrior. This needed a decision, not a
design, and the decision is mine to make, so here it is — which turns the
bead into a doc edit anyone can execute.

**The permanent seat worktree is correct. CLAUDE.md's per-bead worktree is
superseded.** Reasons, in order:

1. CLAUDE.md's rule predates the Թագաւորութիւն. It was written for the
   ephemeral-team pattern, where a session WAS a bead — so "one worktree per
   session" and "one worktree per bead" were the same sentence. Under the
   seat model they are different sentences, and only the first is still true.
2. A seat is defined by Constitution II.2 as a persistent identity with a
   worktree. A per-bead worktree would destroy and recreate the thing the
   constitution says persists.
3. The measured cost of the stale rule is in gqlc-qcen: ~19 orphaned
   `gqlc-<beadslug>` worktrees from the old pattern, several holding local
   branches that SHADOW live PR heads. Nothing reaps them. That is the rule
   still being followed by something.

The reason CLAUDE.md gave — two sessions sharing one HEAD and index — is
still real and still honoured; the seat worktree satisfies it. So this is a
narrowing, not a reversal, and the "why" paragraph should survive the edit.

**What to write:** CLAUDE.md's "Working directory" section says that a seat
works in its permanent seat worktree (`../gqlc-seat-<name>`) with one BRANCH
per bead, and that the per-bead-worktree instruction applies only to
non-seat sessions. Keep the shared-cwd-is-read-only rule; it is unaffected
and independently correct. Cross-reference citizen-protocol step 1 rather
than restating it, so the two cannot drift apart again.

**Do not** delete the hazard paragraph about nesting worktrees inside the
main cwd — that is measured (bd gqlc-2fi) and applies to both models.

title: bd-gh-sync: the push lock does not serialise two separate CLONES, and the comment states granularity without stating that limit
description:
The flock landed in PR #1037 keys on `--git-common-dir`, which makes every linked worktree of one clone contend on a single lock — the dominant case here, and the one the fix was for. It does NOT serialise two separate clones of the repo, which have different common dirs and therefore different lock paths.

Measured in the round-2 review (`C-V2+N1`): two separate clones both mint, `bd github push b-conc` ran 2 time(s).

The defect is the prose, not the choice. The comment states the lock's granularity ('per clone') without stating what that EXCLUDES, so a maintainer reading it concludes the push pass is serialised, full stop. Two clones on one machine is not exotic — it is what a second checkout for a long-running review is.

Fix: state the limit in the comment where the granularity is stated, and decide explicitly whether cross-clone is out of scope (it plausibly is — a cross-clone lock would need a path neither clone owns) or wants a follow-up. Wants a row pinning the limit so it cannot be quietly widened into a claim later.

title: close hook: a redirect between subcommand and flag breaks the option walk
description:
`scan_bd`'s option walk treats a redirect operator as a terminator, so a redirect placed BETWEEN the subcommand and the flags hides the flags from the scanner.

Measured (round-5 review of PR #1029, residue row R3):
- `bd close gqlc-x > /dev/null -r "Closed at <orphan>."` -> classified `allow-no-reason`, hook=allow. `is_op(">")` breaks the walk before the `-r` is seen.
- Trailing-redirect control (`bd close gqlc-x -r "..." > /dev/null`) -> DENY.

The shell accepts a redirect anywhere in a simple command; the scanner assumes it terminates the word list. Fix is to skip the redirect operator and its target and continue the walk, rather than stopping. Wants rows for a mid-command redirect at each position, and for `2>&1` / `>>` / `<` forms.

title: close hook: uppercase hex shas bypass the unpushed-sha guard
description:
`CITED_SHA_RE`/`SHA_RE` in the claude-pre-bash close arm match `[0-9a-f]` only, but git resolves uppercase hex fine.

Measured (round-5 review of PR #1029, residue row R1):
- `git cat-file -t 453E5D20` -> `commit` — git resolves it.
- `bd close gqlc-x -r "Closed at 453E5D20."` -> classified `allow-no-sha`, hook=allow.
- Lowercase control -> DENY.

So a close citing an unpushed sha in uppercase sails through the guard that exists to stop exactly that.

Fix is one character plus case-insensitive anchors: `[0-9a-fA-F]` in both regexes, and `(?i)` on the `at`/`commit` anchors. Needs a pinning row in the hook test suite in both cases, since the lowercase row alone is what let this survive six rounds.

title: ghorphan: no --repo pin, so both gh legs resolve the repository ambiently
description:
ghorphan binds an issue to a bead by BARE ISSUE NUMBER on both legs, with no repository qualifier anywhere.

- boundIssues() matches external_ref with `/issues/(\d+)$` over any URL and deliberately lets a cross-repo ref mark the local number as spoken for. That direction is safe (it can only protect an issue from being closed) and is the documented intent.
- The read leg is `gh issue list` and the write leg is `gh issue close <n>`, neither with `--repo`. Both resolve the repository ambiently from gh's own resolution order.

SO: under a non-default resolution — GH_REPO set, a different upstream remote, or the tool run from another checkout — ghorphan compares ANOTHER repository's issues against gqlc's bead ledger and closes in that repository. Every safety property the tool argues for is stated about gqlc's board.

title: ghorphan: apply()'s second bound check reads one snapshot, so it guards no ledger drift
description:
ghorphan's apply() re-checks that the orphan it is about to close is unbound, and the source comment on apply() is honest that this "catches no state plan could not".

PRECISELY: run() reads the ledger once into a `beads` slice, then calls boundIssues(beads) twice — once at main.go:240 for apply(), and once inside plan(). Two maps, one snapshot. So the second check is a self-consistency assertion over an already-read value, unreachable in production, and it protects against nothing the ledger could do between the read and the write.

MEASURED by bd gqlc-mb8v's round-1 adversarial review (PR #1043). The reviewer did not block on it; the PR body half that implied a fresh ledger read at the write boundary was corrected in round 2.

THE CONCRETE HOLE the second check does not close: two concurrent `bd github push` runs mint #100 and #101 for one bead. Run A writes external_ref=100. ghorphan snapshots the ledger here and plans CLOSE #101. Run B then writes external_ref=101 (last write wins the bead). ghorphan closes #101 — the bead's live canonical.

Reachable only while the mint race is in flight, which gqlc-mmej's lock removes. Recoverable by reopening.

WHAT IS WANTED: either apply() re-reads the ledger at the write boundary (bd list is one subprocess; the cost is one call per run, not per close), or the second check is deleted and the comment says the plan is the only decision point. What is not wanted is the current shape, where a reader sees two checks and infers two reads.

title: ci: three required checks skip when their needs: fail, and whether SKIPPED satisfies branch protection is unsettled
description:
## What is measured

`ci.yml` declares `lint`, `test` and `codegen-fence` with `needs: [actionlint, tidy]`. Branch protection on `master` requires seven contexts (`repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection`): `lint`, `test`, `tidy`, `actionlint`, `govulncheck`, `live-smoke`, `codegen-fence` — so all three dependents are required, and so are both of the jobs they depend on.

Observed on PR #1044 (2026-08-20, run 32329564664): `tidy` concluded `failure` on `check-pr-closes`, and `lint`, `test` and `codegen-fence` each concluded **`skipping`** rather than running. That is ordinary GitHub Actions `needs:` behaviour, not a defect in itself.

Swept the last 25 merged PRs for any of the five jobs ending `SKIPPED` or `CANCELLED` in their final rollup state: **none**. So if the hazard below is real, it has not been realised yet.

## What is NOT settled, and is the point of this bead

**(1) Does a required check whose latest conclusion is `skipped` satisfy branch protection?** Widely believed to, and if so a `skipped` `test` is indistinguishable from a passing `test` to the merge button. Not verified on this repo. Do not act on the belief without a measurement.

**(2) Is a state reachable where `actionlint` and `tidy` both read SUCCESS while the three dependents read SKIPPED?** This is the load-bearing question, because a merge is only at risk if the blocking parent has been cleared while the dependents stay skipped. Candidate routes, none confirmed:

- The `concurrency` block sets `cancel-in-progress: true` for non-master refs. A `gh pr edit` fires `pull_request: edited` and cancels the in-flight run; its jobs go CANCELLED and dependents go SKIPPED. Whether a subsequent `gh run rerun --failed` on that run re-runs the skipped dependents, or leaves them skipped while clearing the parent, is exactly what is unknown.
- A fresh push produces a whole new run, so the rollup's latest-per-context would come from it. That route looks safe, but "looks safe" is why this is filed rather than closed.

## How to settle it

The method is the one gqlc-9qqj uses for the adjacent `continue-on-error` question: `workflow_dispatch` against our own repo, on a throwaway branch and a throwaway PR, rather than reasoning from documentation. Two experiments:

1. Force `tidy` to fail on a scratch PR, then rerun only the failed job, and record every context's conclusion after each step.
2. Push, then immediately `gh pr edit` to cancel, then rerun-failed, and record the same.

Report the conclusions verbatim; do not paraphrase `skipped` as "passed" or "failed".

## Why this matters here

The repo's own merge protocol already defends against it: the precondition query reduces `statusCheckRollup` by `group_by(.name) | map(max_by(.startedAt))` and demands all seven read `SUCCESS`, so a SKIPPED check fails that test. This bead is about whether **GitHub's** gate is as strict as ours — i.e. whether a human clicking merge, or any tooling that trusts `mergeStateStatus`, has the same protection.

Same family as gqlc-9qqj (what `continue-on-error` does to a check run) and the general rule that a detector which exits 0 is not a gate.
notes:
2026-08-20 lead: half of this is now settled first-party by the hookspath round-3 reviewer. The mechanism is confirmed: lint, test and codegen-fence all declare 'needs: [actionlint, tidy]' in ci.yml, so a tidy failure makes all three report *skipping* rather than failing. That is dependency ordering, NOT a path filter — an earlier guess that a path filter was involved is wrong.

What remains unsettled is the part that matters: whether GitHub's branch protection treats a SKIPPED required check as SATISFYING the requirement. Observed on PR #1044 that a tidy failure produced three SKIPPED required contexts; not observed whether the PR would have been mergeable in that state. A sweep of the last 25 merged PRs found none affected, so there is no historical instance to read the answer off.

Settling it wants a deliberate probe on a throwaway branch, not a guess.

title: repair the sibling worktrees still tracking origin/master
description:
`gqlc-tfh1` (PR #1056, merged as `b8d908cd`) fixed the recipe in CLAUDE.md and
`kingdom/brain/playbooks/citizen-protocol.md`, added the `pre-push` destination
guard, and added the `just check-worktree-upstream` detector. None of those can
touch a branch that was already created the old way. This bead is that
remediation.

## State: REPAIRED 2026-08-22 (Ար)

Every branch below has had its upstream unset. Verified twice — the detector
returns 0 on each repaired worktree, and a positive control (deliberately
re-pointing a branch at `origin/master`) makes it exit 1 with its own message,
so the passing readings discriminate rather than merely pass.

## Correction: the unit is the BRANCH, not the worktree

This description previously said:

> Measured 2026-08-19, 4 of 21 sibling worktrees had `@{u}` = origin/master

and framed the whole task as a sweep over *worktrees*. **Both halves are
superseded.** Re-measured first-party 2026-08-22 over all 90 worktrees and all
197 local branches:

| branch | worktree | PR | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chore/gqlc-23e-release-pipeline-impl` | *(none)* | #334 | merged 2026-07-18 |
| `fix/govulncheck-live-tree` | *(none)* | #725 | merged 2026-08-03 |
| `fix/modscope-justdump-mod-blindness` | `gqlc-98ii` | #1030 | merged 2026-08-20 |
| `fix/resolver-phase-b-uncovered-commit` | `gqlc-sxzj` | #1032 | merged 2026-08-20 |

Four, not two — and **two of them are checked out in no worktree at all**. A
worktree sweep cannot see those, and neither can `just check-worktree-upstream`,
which inspects only the branch of the worktree it is pointed at. They are latent:
the misconfiguration arrives the moment someone checks one out. Tracked as a
follow-up, since closing it is a detector change and not remediation.

Also superseded: *"Do this as a sweep once the concurrent sessions in those
worktrees have finished."* There were no concurrent sessions. All four branches'
PRs had already merged, both worktrees were clean with no in-progress merge,
rebase or cherry-pick, and neither is a seat worktree.

## Nothing was stranded

Checked before touching anything, because a squash merge makes commit lists lie
(`--is-ancestor` reports "no" for work that landed):

- Each local tip was compared against its PR's `headRefOid` — **all four match**,
  so no local branch had drifted past what was reviewed.
- For each branch, the files it touched were diffed against its PR's merge
  commit — **no differences**, so the work is on master.

The two repo-global stashes (`WIP on chore/bd-ledger-p2`, `r6-branchfiles`)
belong to other work, are not reachable from these branches, and were left
untouched. Worktree removal would not affect them either — stashes are a
repo-global ref.

## The repair, for the next person who meets one

    git -C <worktree> branch --unset-upstream
    git -C <worktree> push -u origin HEAD    # only when ready to publish

The order is load-bearing: in a still-misconfigured worktree even
`git push -u origin HEAD` is refused, because `-u` is applied only *after* a
successful push while the guard runs before it. Both refusal messages already
print the two commands in this order.

For a branch with no worktree, `git branch --unset-upstream <branch>` works from
anywhere in the checkout.

## Earlier correction, retained

This description also used to claim that once `gqlc-tfh1` landed, "an active
session self-heals on its next run". That is false and remains false:
`just check-worktree-upstream` **refuses** (exit 1) and never repairs. What
landed is a detector, not a repair.

## Still open after this bead

The four branches above are all merged and their worktrees are finished, so the
honest end state is disposal rather than repair. That is deliberately **not**
done here: deleting another citizen's worktree is not a call to make
unilaterally. Proposed separately.

title: tmpreap: the TOCTOU window is the archive duration, not the scan duration
description:
apply() re-reads /proc BEFORE archiving, then archives (potentially minutes over 1.4 GiB), then deletes. An agent that opens a doomed directory during the archive still loses it.

main.go documents the re-read as protecting "an agent that started using a directory during it", which is true of the scan and not of the archive.

Fix: move the re-read to just before the delete loop, which closes most of the window. Note the archive is then written over a set slightly larger than what is deleted, which is the safe direction.

title: resolver: a natively-plural binding is deferred even when every candidate declares the projected property
description:
Round-1 review finding N2 on PR #1032 (bead gqlc-sxzj), re-probed unchanged in round 2. Undisclosed in the PR body.

`RETURN x.name` on the bead shape: master ACCEPTS it as NOT NULL, the sxzj branch REFUSES with `ErrAmbiguousBinding`.

Mechanism: the plural lane is entered only via the widening at `len(inferred) == 1`. So a binding whose inferred set is NATIVELY plural is deferred even when every candidate declares the projected property — which is the exact reasoning PR #1032's body uses to justify committing plural for the *widened* binding, not applied to the native case.

Fail-closed, so not a soundness hole; arguably the headline class in different clothes. Filed because PR #1032's 'newly-refused' section opens with 'Both classes below', which reads as exhaustive over the moved verdicts, and this is a third.

Source: /tmp/lead/verdict-sxzj-r2.md section 5 row N2.

title: resolver: the !attested fallback offers NOT NULL columns no row can fill
description:
Round-1 review finding N1 on PR #1032 (bead gqlc-sxzj), re-verified in round 2 and left open by scope.

The `!attested` fallback in the resolver still declares columns NOT NULL that a row cannot actually fill. Reached by one bare MATCH plus one optional hop:

    MATCH (c) OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:HAS_DESK]->(:Desk) RETURN c.smallOnly

Re-probed at review time: byte-identical ACCEPT, `c.smallOnly STRING nullable:false`, on BOTH master and the sxzj branch. So this is pre-existing behaviour that gqlc-sxzj neither introduced nor fixed.

Disclosed in PR #1032's commit body and in the PR body's 'Known residue' section. No bead existed — the fixer's own handoff says 'it deserves its own bead; I did not file one.' This is that bead.

Source: /tmp/lead/verdict-sxzj-r2.md section 5 row N1 and the Non-blocking residue section.
notes:
--- THE HUNT (vahagn, 2026-08-22) — PR #1261, branch fix/6aed-fallback-nullability

REPRODUCED FIRST-PARTY before touching anything, on valid/schemas/social_r1.gql
rather than the bead's schema, so the defect is not an artefact of one fixture:
  MATCH (c) OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[a:AUTHORED]->(x:Post) RETURN c.name
accepted on master as STRING NOT NULL. `MATCH (c)` binds every node, the
OPTIONAL hop drops none, so `c` is a Post on most rows and Post has no `name`.

ROOT CAUSE. candidateTypes folds every touching edge into `inferred` and
commit() returns the intersection, having never asked whether ANY edge is
evidence about the RETURNED rows. `attested` existed but gated only the
widening; nothing consulted the witnessing question on its own.

WHAT LIED TO ME — two over-reaches, both caught by measuring master rather than
by reasoning, both now pinned as test rows so the next person cannot repeat them:

 1. v1 used "no edge passed witnessesItsEndpoints". That refuses bindings
    INTRODUCED by the optional hop. Measured: master answers
    `MATCH (p:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[a:AUTHORED]->(c) RETURN c.title` as
    STRING nullable — correctly. Such a binding is null on the missed rows and
    the target type on the rest, so the TYPE is sound and nullability already
    carries the miss. Fixed by standing the guard down on n.Nullable().

 2. v2 kept witnessesItsEndpoints for the join question. But that predicate
    ALSO returns false for !singleHopPattern, and a minimum-1 variable-length
    hop DOES filter rows: master accepts
    `MATCH (c)-[a:AUTHORED*1..2]->(x:Post) RETURN c.name` as STRING NOT NULL and
    is right to. Fixed by spelling the guard !e.Nullable() — the join question,
    not the far-end question. What a multi-hop's far end licenses stays open as
    gqlc-3uof; deliberately not widened here.

A NEAR-MISS worth recording: after narrowing to outer joins only, my error
message still said "or a variable-length hop" — naming a case that can no longer
occur. Caught before push. When a guard narrows, its message is part of the
guard.

A GUARD I COULD NOT KILL, so I removed it: commit() also tested `folded > 0`.
Mutating it away left the ENTIRE package green including the 12,880-cell corpus
sweep — with no touching edge nothing folds, `inferred` is empty, and the round
reaches case 0 either way. Dead. commitUnlabelledRound still tests `folded`,
where blinding it does fail a row, because there the count picks between two
error messages and only one is true of a query with no touching edge.

PROOF. Red-before/green-after against master's resolve.go: exactly the 2 defect
rows red, 5 controls green. Mutation screen 6/6 killed, 0 survivors, each mutant
verified to COMPILE under `go test -c` so no kill is a compiler kill. Zero
corpus-manifest churn. fmt-check / lint (0 issues) / just test all green.
Rebased onto origin/master 24c7b852 and retested after the rebase.

title: vulnguard: the stub scan offers no decoy line, so the unplaced-stdlib header regex is uncovered
description:
`internal/tools/vulnguard`'s stub scan contains exactly ONE line matching `standard library` (`bin/go:52`, the header itself), so every relaxation of the recipe's header regex is an equivalent mutant under this fixture.

Measured by the Linus review of gqlc-agt0 (/tmp/lead/verdict-agt0-r1b.md, mutation X1): widening

    grep -m1 -E '^Govulncheck scanned the following [0-9]+ modules and the .*standard library:$'

to

    grep -m1 -E 'standard library'

leaves all eight tests in the package GREEN. LIVE=YES VALID=YES rc=0 fails=0.

Why it matters: the regex's precision is what makes the absent-header branch mean anything. The M14/M9 rows assert what the recipe does when no header is found; if the regex can match any line mentioning the standard library, "no header found" stops being a state the tests can distinguish from "wrong header found".

FIX (one line): add a decoy to the stub's `scan()` in `internal/tools/vulnguard/harness_test.go`, before the real header — e.g.

    printf 'No standard library vulnerabilities found.\n'

Then re-run X1 and confirm it flips to KILLED.

Out of scope for gqlc-agt0, whose scope is the ten named clauses of the unplaced-stdlib grading. Filed as N3 of that bead's round-1b verdict.

title: ci: no required context runs just fmt-check, so gofumpt/gci may rest on the local pre-commit hook alone
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 at origin/master 07954baf, read-only, by the orchestrator.

THE OBSERVATION. Go formatting (gofumpt + gci) has its own recipe, separate from
lint:

  justfile:677  fmt: ensure-golangci        -> {{golangci}} fmt
  justfile:681  fmt-check: ensure-golangci  -> {{golangci}} fmt --diff

`.githooks/pre-commit:42-51` calls `just fmt-check` and fails the commit on a
non-zero exit ("ERROR: unformatted Go files. Run: just fmt").

No workflow calls it. Enumerated by rendering every file under
.github/workflows/ from origin/master and grepping each for `just <recipe>`:

  ci.yml            vuln-root-residual, lint, lint-cache-check, test,
                    tidy-check, bd-export-monotonic, test-codegen-fence,
                    actionlint
  codegen-live.yml  test-codegen-live-neo4j, test-codegen-live-age
  iso-drift.yml     iso-drift-check
  vuln.yml          vuln

`fmt-check` is not among them, and `lint` runs `{{golangci}} run`
(justfile:663-664), which is a different golangci-lint subcommand from the
`{{golangci}} fmt --diff` that fmt-check runs.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD EXISTS TO SETTLE, AND WHICH I DID NOT SETTLE.
`.golangci.yml:174-177` puts gofumpt and gci under a `formatters:` block. In
golangci-lint v2 (this repo pins v2.12.2, justfile:5) `formatters:` is the
section the `fmt` subcommand applies. Whether `golangci-lint run` ALSO reports
those formatters as diagnostics decides everything here:

  - If `run` reports them, the required `lint` context covers formatting
    independently and there is no hole; fmt-check is a local convenience. Then
    this bead closes as investigated-not-a-defect and the finding is worth one
    sentence somewhere durable, because the separate recipe invites the opposite
    assumption.
  - If `run` does NOT report them, gofumpt/gci are enforced by the local
    pre-commit hook ALONE. That is the failure mode gqlc-4thl documents: when
    core.hooksPath drifts, the hook is silently absent and unformatted Go reaches
    master with all seven required contexts green. It is also this repo's
    recurring shape -- "is there a check?" is not "does it FAIL?".

HOW TO SETTLE IT. Cheap and decisive: in a throwaway worktree, introduce one
gofumpt-detectable violation (a blank line immediately after a function's
opening brace is reliable), then run `{{golangci}} run` scoped to that package
and see whether it reports. Take an rc=0 control on the pristine file first, or
the result witnesses nothing. Note the cache is per-worktree
(GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE := justfile_directory() + "/.bin/golangci-cache",
justfile:16), so a fresh worktree runs COLD and this is slower than it looks.
golangci-lint also holds a global lock -- "Error: parallel golangci-lint is
running" is a lock collision, not a lint failure; poll with `pgrep -x
golangci-lint`.

DO NOT WRITE A COUNT OR A UNIVERSAL INTO THE FIX. The enumeration above is a
result about the workflow files at 07954baf, not a property of the repo.

Related: gqlc-4thl (hooksPath drift kills the local gates; this is the second
half of its open item 2, which I recorded on that bead but did not resolve),
gqlc-7ijy (who writes the drift), gqlc-eo46 and the 'detector that exits 0 is
not a gate' family.

title: codegen: the neo4j/age corpus comment is byte-identical in two packages by hand, and nothing enforces that
notes:
Surfaced by the independent review of PR #1002 round 3 (bd gqlc-wla6). Classified
residue there: pre-existing, and nothing on that branch made it worse.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY. The comment block above corpusTests in
internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go and internal/codegen/age/corpus_test.go is
byte-identical -- 527 bytes, md5 92236145c7ec46624cbe901ff513cb50 at 15e8f9d2,
measured on both files. That identity is maintained by hand.

THE GAP. No test, no lint rule and no just recipe compares the two. A future
edit to one package's comment leaves the other saying something the author
believed they were changing everywhere. That is this repository's second most
repeated defect -- fix a class in one carrier, leave the twin live on another --
and here the twin relationship is real, deliberate, and unguarded.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE. The comment is not decoration. It is the
carrier that explains what require.NotEmpty refuses and why the list is a
declaration rather than a gate. PR #1002 spent three rounds getting its wording
true. Nothing stops round four of some future branch from correcting one copy.

DO NOT ASSUME THE FIX IS A NEW TEST. Options, not a ruling: a test in one
package that reads the sibling's source and compares the block; a shared const
or a //go:generate; or a deliberate decision that the two should be allowed to
diverge, recorded where the comment is. A test that reads a sibling package's
source bytes has its own hazard -- see the gate-reads-source-bytes note -- and
would need to render from the AST rather than grep raw bytes.

MEASURE BEFORE ACTING. Confirm the two blocks are still byte-identical at
whatever head you start from; if they have already drifted, that drift is the
more interesting finding and should be reported rather than silently repaired.

title: ciguard: justRecipe's header regex turns an unmodelled recipe spelling into a fake RED, and no carrier says so
notes:
Surfaced reviewing PR #996 round 5 (bd gqlc-sgot / gqlc-lisu). Not a defect in
what shipped; the shipped prose is conservative. This is the direction of the
limit, which no carrier currently states.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. internal/tools/ciguard/testhooks_test.go:125 builds
  header := regexp.MustCompile(`^` + regexp.QuoteMeta(name) + `[ \t]*:(.*)$`)
so a recipe header just accepts but this pattern does not match -- a
parameterised header such as `test-hooks *args:` is the obvious one -- leaves
start == -1 and fires require.GreaterOrEqualf at :135 with "has no recipe %q, so
the chain that reaches the shell suites from a required CI context is broken at
that link".

WHY IT MATTERS. That message names a broken CI chain. The actual cause would be
a recipe header spelling the reader does not model, with the chain intact. That
is the fake-RED shape this repository already screens mutations for, and the
comment block at :112-119 discusses fake RED only for `just --dump`'s parse
failures -- not for its own header pattern.

The PR body bullet (996 body 239-241) states the limit non-directionally: a
spelling just accepts and justRecipe does not model "is outside the assertions
built on it". True and deliberately non-directional, which is why this is
residue and not a blocker. But no carrier says which way it falls, and the
direction is the useful part: it is loud, not silent.

WHAT TO DO. Decide and record the direction. Options, not a ruling: widen the
header pattern to admit parameters and default values; or leave the pattern and
give the require message a second clause naming the spelling-not-modelled cause
alongside the broken-chain one; or state the direction in the comment at
:112-119 next to the existing fake-RED discussion. Whichever, the fix belongs in
the code comment or the require message -- the PR body is not a carrier CI
gates.

MEASURE FIRST, DO NOT TRUST THIS NOTE. Put an actual unmodelled spelling through
justRecipe in a scratch worktree and record rc plus the failing line, rather
than reasoning from the regex. Neither the round-5 author nor I ran one; both of
us read the pattern. The author self-reported exactly this gap.

RELATED. justRecipe "finds the recipe ... with a regex" is precise about the
header (:125, :129) and loose about the body, which is taken by indentation at
:138-148, not by a regex. Same function, smaller. Fold it in or leave it.

title: ciguard: If is read as a string, so an explicit empty if: passes require.Empty
description:
PR #996's body names this as a follow-up rather than a hole it holds open, so
this bead is that follow-up's destination.

THE GAP. In `internal/tools/ciguard`, `continue-on-error` was promoted to a
`yaml.Node` so that its PRESENCE can be distinguished from its absence, but `If`
was left a plain string. A string cannot make that distinction: an explicit
`if: ""` written on a job decodes to the empty string, which is what an ABSENT
`if` also decodes to. So an explicit empty `if:` still passes `require.Empty`.

This is the conditional-gate-omission shape — a check on `X != ""` catches
disagreement but not omission, and silence passes where it should not. The fix
is a positive declaration on both shapes, i.e. a `yaml.Node` whose kind/validity
distinguishes "absent" from "present and empty", the same way
`continue-on-error` already does.

WHAT BOUNDS THE RISK TODAY, and why this is a follow-up rather than a blocker:
`actionlint` is itself one of the seven required CI contexts, and it returned
rc=1 on every empty-decoding spelling put to it, against an rc=0 control on the
unmodified file taken before and after each row. Measured out of tree on a copy
of ci.yml. So a workflow carrying such an `if:` does not reach merge silently —
a different required context refuses it first.

DO NOT WRITE A CLOSED ENUMERATION OF SPELLINGS. That is this PR's own history:
a bullet carried a list of spellings and a sentence closing it off, and the list
was short of what had already been run. YAML decodes to empty in spellings
nobody here has typed. Any claim written under this bead is a result about ROWS
TAKEN, not about the spelling space — state it that way or state nothing.

If you re-measure: `actionlint` exits **3** with "no project was found" outside
a git repo. That is a setup error, not a lint result. `git init` the probe dir,
and take the rc=0 control on the pristine file or your rc=1 rows witness nothing.

Related: gqlc-9qqj (the check-run question the same review routed out),
gqlc-sgot / gqlc-lisu (ciguard).
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-08-18, from the PR #996 round-4 review, verified first-party on
origin/master): the yaml.Node modelling this bead asks for ALREADY EXISTS in
this same package. This is adoption of an in-package idiom, not new design.

  internal/tools/ciguard/golangci_cache_test.go:68   If  yaml.Node  `yaml:"if"`
  internal/tools/ciguard/golangci_cache_test.go:81   func present(n yaml.Node) bool { return n.Kind != 0 }
  internal/tools/ciguard/golangci_cache_test.go:453  require.Falsef(t, present(s.If), "step %q in %s carries `if: %s` ...")

So `golangci_cache_test.go` already distinguishes an ABSENT `if:` from one that
is PRESENT AND EMPTY, for exactly the reason this bead names, and already emits
the refusal. `workflow_test.go` is the file that does not -- its `If` is a plain
string (workflow_test.go:53), which is why an explicit `if: ""` passes
require.Empty there.

The fix is therefore narrow and has a working model 400 lines away: change
workflow_test.go's `If string` to `If yaml.Node`, and assert with the existing
`present()` helper rather than `require.Empty`. Check whether `present()` needs
to move or be shared between the two files.

This also sharpens the defect: the package is INCONSISTENT with itself. One file
models `if:` presence correctly and one does not, and only the correct one is
obvious to a reader who happens to open it. PR #996's closing line "Promoting
`If` to a `yaml.Node` is a follow-up" is true of the workflow_test.go types but
reads as though the modelling were novel.

--- IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-18): PR https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/1023, head 1b8e1cd7197c8306f3f9534d97f5194ef188365f

Branch fix/gqlc-ff66-ciguard-if-node. Two files touched:
internal/tools/ciguard/workflow_test.go and
internal/tools/ciguard/testhooks_test.go. (Round 1 touched only the first; see
ROUND 2 below for why that was wrong.)

WHAT CHANGED
- ciJob.If and ciSteps.If are yaml.Node.
- The job-level refusal moved into requireNoJobIf, reading present(job.If). It
  takes require.TestingT so it can be run against a job that carries an `if:`;
  ci.yml does not, so calling it over the file exercises only the passing side.
- New TestGateJobIfIsRefusedOnBeingWrittenNotOnItsValue drives it over documents
  that write the key and one that does not, with a column for what a string
  field would have read from each source.
- The step's `if:` is compared as step.If.Value against the same constant.
- recordingT/failedNow/jobIfRefusal adopted from internal/schema/gql.
- testhooks_test.go's reads of these fields moved onto present()/spell().

BEFORE/AFTER (the measurement)
Detached worktrees at origin/master (07954baf) and at the branch. Insert one line
under `  tidy:` in ci.yml, run
`go test -run '^TestPRBodyGateFailsTheJobItRunsIn$' ./internal/tools/ciguard/`.
  origin/master + `    if:`     -> ok, PASSED   <- the bug, reproduced
  origin/master + `    if: ""`  -> ok, PASSED   <- the bug, reproduced
  branch       + `    if:`     -> FAIL "job \"tidy\" carries a job-level `if:`, written as !!null"
  branch       + `    if: ""`  -> FAIL "... written as !!str"
ci.yml restored to md5 83c139ca697fa7a626869fab275230dd after each row.

MUTATION MATRIX: rows M1-M13 (round 1) plus N1-N6 (round 2), re-taken at
1b8e1cd7. Round-2 runner /tmp/factory/ff66r2_mut.py, log
/tmp/factory/ff66r2-matrix.txt, compositions /tmp/factory/ff66r2_compose.py,
session log /tmp/factory/fix-1023-r2.log. Every row anchor-checked unique, md5
before/after, unified diff printed, screened with
`go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/tools/ciguard/`, restored to pristine md5;
worktree clean at the end. Survivors: M8, N1, N2, N6. M8, N1 and N2 are proven
live rather than no-ops by composition -- M11 alone is RED and M8+M11 exits 0;
N3/N4/N5 alone are RED and N1+N3, N1+N4, N2+N5 each exit 0. A weakening accepts
what the strong form refused. They survive alone because ci.yml carries no
job-level `if:` and the gate step's condition is the correct one, so nothing in
the file parts the strong form from the weak one without a second edit. N6
survives with no composition that would kill it: recordingT/jobIfRefusal are
driven only from TestGateJobIfIsRefusedOnBeingWrittenNotOnItsValue, so nothing
inspects the text of testhooks_test.go's refusal.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD
1. The NOTES cite workflow_test.go:53 as the plain-string If. Line 53 was the
   STEP struct's field, read at line 244 by require.Equalf against a non-empty
   constant, which refused an absent and a written-empty `if:` alike. The hole
   was ciJob.If at line 66, read by require.Emptyf. The bead's DESCRIPTION
   ("written on a job") is right; the note's line number pointed at the other
   struct. Both fields were promoted anyway, so the fix is unaffected.
   (Adjudicated in the round-1 review, first-party, in the author's favour.)
2. CORRECTED IN ROUND 2 -- the sentence that stood here was wrong. It said the
   decode-error argument workflow_test.go makes for continue-on-error (a bool
   field handed a !!str) "does not run in this direction", generalising from one
   row: `if: false` arriving in a string field as "false" with no error.
   Re-measured out of tree in round 2 (/tmp/factory/ff66r2_decode) over
   documents chosen for that round, with a control in the same run showing the
   decoder reports an error when there is one (`continue-on-error: ${{ ... }}`
   into a bool -> "cannot unmarshal !!str into bool"). It runs: the !!seq and
   !!map sources put to a string field were refused -- "cannot unmarshal !!seq
   into string", "cannot unmarshal !!map into string" -- in flow form and in
   block form. The scalar sources put to the same field arrived without error,
   which is where round 1's single row came from. End-to-end: at 07954baf
   `if: []` on tidy reddens as `decode job "tidy"` (the decoder named rather
   than the bypass); at 1b8e1cd7 it reddens as `job "tidy" carries a job-level
   `if:`, written as !!seq`. So promoting ciSteps.If/ciJob.If buys more than
   uniformity on the non-scalar sources, and the PR body says so.

SELF-AUDIT: the first commit introduced two false claims in comments and the
second commit (90bbf81f) fixes them -- "a string field is told nothing about
whether the key was written" (falsified by `if: false`), and "every key present()
is asked about elsewhere in this package is absent" (never measured; M1 measures
only that nothing else parts a written-empty key from an absent one).

Everything the bead asked to verify first-party was confirmed at origin/master:
golangci_cache_test.go:68 If yaml.Node, :81 present(), :453 require.Falsef.

DO NOT CLOSE until PR #1023 merges.

ADDENDUM (same session). Two amendments to the note above:

a) "the first commit introduced two false claims" should read "the two false
   claims I found". It is not a completeness claim, and a third turned up after
   it was written: the PR body's M7 row said "all four subtests" where the
   matrix output lists the parent test plus THREE subtests -- the
   `no_if:_key_at_all` row takes the early return and never reaches the
   Contains assert. Corrected in the PR body before merge, restated there as
   the negative (which row is NOT among them) rather than as a count.
   The class recurred three times in one session, in three different carriers
   (comment, comment, PR body). Worth knowing for whoever reviews #1023.

b) The M8 explanation in the PR body now cites its measurement -- M8 alone
   leaves the whole package green -- rather than asserting "nothing in the tree
   parts them", which was the same shape unbacked.

--- ROUND 2 (2026-08-18), head 1b8e1cd7197c8306f3f9534d97f5194ef188365f

The round-1 review returned REVISE on three blockers. All three were claims
about the work rather than the work itself.

B1 -- THE SECOND READER. ciJob and ciSteps are package-level types in
`package ciguard_test`, and testhooks_test.go decodes into ciJob and asserts on
the `test` job's `if:` and on its `just test` step's. Promoting the field
therefore changed an untouched file's behaviour, and round 1's "one file
touched" said otherwise. Found in round 2 with a go/parser walk over the package
dir rather than a grep (a grep over raw bytes accepts a commented-out
occurrence), with two controls: a commented `// PROBE: var other ciJob; _ =
other.If` took `grep -cE ciJob` from 1 to 2 in that file while the walk still
reported one reader, and deleting the real `s.If` assertion removed both of its

title: codegen/conformance: sweep the AST-census tests for the aggregate-emptiness shape gqlc-wla6 closed
description:
Same-class sweep opened off the gqlc-wla6 / PR #1002 review. That PR found a
census test whose only completeness check was an aggregate one, so emptying the
source AND the expectation together went GREEN. `internal/codegen/conformance`
has tests of the same construction and none were examined.

DERIVE THE SET YOURSELF. I am deliberately not listing which tests qualify, and
not stating how many. A review-supplied count gets copied into the fix's PR body
and bead notes without being re-measured, and the counts I have supplied on this
class have been wrong repeatedly — the failure mode is always a search scoped
smaller than the claim. Walk `internal/codegen/conformance/*_test.go` with
`go/parser` and select on the SHAPE below; whatever that yields is the set.

THE SHAPE TO SELECT FOR — a test that:
  - builds a census/inventory by walking an AST or parsing a fixture, then
  - compares it against a hand-maintained expectation (a literal slice/map), and
  - has no guard that the census itself is NON-EMPTY, or whose only guard is an
    aggregate over several sources.

Both failure modes are live in this repo and are different:
  - **Aggregate emptiness**: one `require.NotZero(total)` over N sources fires
    only if ALL N are silent; drop 2 of 3 and it stays green (gqlc-…, see the
    aggregate-emptiness note). Assert PER SOURCE.
  - **Total silence expressible**: source empty AND expectation empty ⇒ the
    comparison is vacuously satisfied. Needs a non-empty guard on the census
    BEFORE the comparison.

FOR EACH CANDIDATE, the finding is a MUTATION, not a reading. Empty the source
and the expectation together and show the test still passes. A code reading is
not a defect here.

AND MUTATE THE GUARD YOU ADD. #1002's first round added a guard that was present
but not load-bearing; the row that caught it was "delete the guard ⇒ GREEN
again". Every guard added under this bead needs that third row.

SCREENS — these cost real rounds on #1002, do not rediscover them:
  - `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkg>` is the mutation screen in general, but is
    UNSOUND where a fixture compiles one module down (gqlc-hreu). Check which
    case each test is before choosing.
  - Assert `\[(build|setup) failed\]` absent — BOTH spellings. A fixture PARSE
    error prints `[setup failed]`, not `[build failed]`; a screen grepping only
    the latter misclassifies it as a real RED.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on `^[[:space:]]*--- PASS`. `^ *--- PASS` misses
    testify's TAB indentation and reported 0 where the truth was 21 — a valid
    kill reads as a fake RED.
  - A legitimate RED with ZERO sibling PASS does exist, so the build/setup
    marker is the sound discriminator; sibling count alone is not.
  - Kill-count 1 with a BLANK test name means the COMPILER killed it (fake RED).

title: ci: settle what job-level continue-on-error does to a check run, on our own repo via workflow_dispatch
description:
PR #996's body routes a finding here, so this bead is the destination of that
routing. It names no id today, so nothing in that carrier is false — but the
routing has no target until this exists.

THE OPEN QUESTION. `internal/tools/ciguard`'s `require` message says the
check-run question is "not settled here", and that is deliberate and still true
of the branch. Two sub-questions are distinct and only one has any witness:

1. Does a job with job-level `continue-on-error: true` that fails still emit a
   check run concluding `failure` (and therefore still block branch protection)?
2. What does the key do to the enclosing WORKFLOW RUN's conclusion?

WHAT IS WITNESSED, AND HOW WEAKLY. #996 settled (1) on ONE third-party
observation: `cowrie/cowrie` job 95630008478, `test (3.15t, true, true)`, whose
workflow sets `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}` at job level with
`experimental: true`; job and check run of the same id both conclude `failure`.
Job-level placement confirmed by indentation at `tox.yml@708588bc:110`.

Three limits on that witness, all of which this bead exists to remove:
  - **n=1.** The PR body states it as a general present-tense rule. It has one
    observation. The paragraph bounds the RUN axis and leaves the SAMPLE-SIZE
    axis unbounded.
  - **Not two observations.** `/actions/jobs/{id}` and `/check-runs/{id}` are
    two VIEWS of one object, not corroboration.
  - **A third-party job id is a citation that rots.** cowrie can delete logs,
    rewrite the workflow, or age the run out. This is precisely why it was kept
    out of the `require` message.

(2) is NOT witnessed at all: that workflow run also concluded `failure`, but
jobs whose `continue-on-error` resolved FALSE failed in it too, so it is fully
explained without the key and witnesses nothing at run level.

UNRECONCILED TENSION TO RESOLVE HERE. PR #996 body ~line 190 reports a scan of
160 successful runs finding NO job concluding `failure` inside them; ~line 217
asserts such jobs conclude `failure`. Both can hold if continue-on-error jobs
are rare in that sample, but nothing measured that, and the body never says so.
Whatever this bead concludes must reconcile the two or show why they are
compatible.

WHY workflow_dispatch. Live arms are dispatchable — "no Docker locally" is not a
hard limit here. A throwaway workflow on our own repo with a deliberately
failing job under job-level `continue-on-error: true` answers both questions
first-party, with a citation that cannot rot because we own it. Take the
positive control too: the same workflow with the key absent/false, or the run
witnesses nothing.

DO NOT put the result in a `require` message. The message's second clause argues
a required context is not where to settle this, and that argument stands.

title: claude-pre-bash: the deny message's '(… are all dead)' is false in exactly the fail-closed case
description:
Pre-existing prose defect in a runtime-emitted message. Found reviewing PR #992
(gqlc-wa8c) round 3. Identical string exists at cbb11a7e:364, so this is not
that branch's debt.

`.githooks/claude-pre-bash:447` emits:

    (commit-msg, pre-commit, pre-push and post-merge are all dead)

This is a four-way universal asserted at the moment of refusal. It is FALSE in
exactly the fail-closed case that PR #992's round-3 entry discloses: in the
reviewer's fixture `commit-msg` was live and fired while the message claimed it
was dead.

This is the repo's signature defect class — a universal in prose falsified by
the artifact it ships next to — and it is worse here than in a comment, because
this string is what a human sees at the moment they are being refused, and it
tells them not to bother checking a hook that is in fact running.

FIX SHAPE (do not just delete the four names): the message's job is to explain
WHY the refusal is happening. State what is pinned without quantifying over the
four hooks — the shape that survives review here states the negative and
enumerates limits without a count. Do not replace the four-name list with a
smaller list; that is the same defect with a different number.

title: Write down that go test -c is the wrong mutation screen for a testdata/*.go.txt fixture
description:
Methodology finding from PR #990 (bd gqlc-1uic), confirmed independently by both review rounds with an anchored mutation. It currently lives only in a PR body and two verdict files, none of which is a durable carrier the next author will read. It needs to land somewhere in-tree.

THE FINDING. `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkg>` is this repo's standard mutation screen, and it is UNSOUND for any mutation whose effect lands in emitted code that is compiled one module down -- i.e. anything under internal/codegen/*/testdata/*.go.txt.

Measured: making the emitted entity gate read `if linusUndefinedSymbol != nil {` leaves `go test -c ./internal/codegen/neo4j` at rc=0, while the package goes RED as `FAIL neo4jcorpus [build failed]` with ZERO child test names. `go test -c` compiles the GENERATOR; it never compiles the EMISSION. So the screen a mutation matrix relies on to distinguish a real kill from a compiler fake-RED does not see the artifact under test.

THE SOUND SCREEN, as ruled in round 1 and re-used in round 2:
  - Run the OUTER harness and read the CHILD log.
  - Assert `FAIL <childmod> [build failed]` is ABSENT.
  - Assert at least one `--- FAIL: Test...` NAMING a child test, with sibling child tests still `--- PASS`.
  - Assert `no tests to run` count is 0 (and remember `go test -run` is unanchored -- anchor `^TestX$/^sub$`).

WHY THE MATRICES BUILT ON THE BAD SCREEN SURVIVED ANYWAY, which is worth recording alongside it so nobody re-audits from scratch:
  1. SURVIVED rows are self-screening. The harness does require.NoError on the child `go test` exit status and then require.ElementsMatch(declaredTests(fixture), passed). A green package ENTAILS the child compiled and every declared test ran and passed, so a compiler kill cannot masquerade as SURVIVED.
  2. KILLED rows need the child-name tell, and it discriminates cleanly: a child compile break prints `[build failed]` with zero child names; a genuine kill prints `--- FAIL: <ChildTest>` with siblings still passing.

WHERE TO PUT IT: wherever the `go test -c` screen is currently prescribed. Whatever carrier states the rule must state this exception beside it, or the rule keeps being applied where it does not hold.

Taken because the bead had sat unclaimed since 2026-08-18 and I held the finding

rediscover.

(semantic kill).

  render_models.go emitted gate ->
    `if linusUndefinedSymbol != nil {`  go test -c rc=0 | run rc=1| 1 build-failed | 0 child names
  render_queries.go emitted pointer
    gate `!=` -> `==`                   go test -c rc=0 | run rc=1| 0 build-failed | 1 --- FAIL
                                                                    (TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull)
                                                                    + 20 --- PASS

The screen reads rc=0 on all three, so it cannot separate a broken emission from

title: codegen/neo4j: the corpus does not pin the scalar/property/temporal GetRecordValue gate
description:
Residue of PR #990 (bd gqlc-1uic, GH #975), named by both review rounds and deliberately left open there.

PR #990 pinned the entity and list arms of the emitted GetRecordValue error gate. It did NOT pin the scalar/property/temporal arm (the matrix calls it G1), and G1 is the one row in that matrix that produces NO RED at all when mutated -- the gate can be deleted and the corpus stays green.

WHY IT WAS LEFT OPEN, and this is the part to verify before acting: read off the EMITTED child sources (not inferred from the .cypher), the only carrier instantiations the corpus produces are []any, dbtype.Node and dbtype.Relationship. So that arm emits no GetRecordValue call on this corpus at all -- there is nothing to pin. Round 1 verified this claim first-party against the emitted sources and upheld it.

WHAT CLOSING IT NEEDS: a new projection in the corpus that makes the emitter instantiate the scalar/property/temporal carrier, and then a message assertion in the same shape PR #990 used for the entity arm (assert what the refusal SAYS, plus one negative assertion on what it must not say -- the fixture's old err != nil assertion was vacuous because the zero carrier makes the decode helper refuse for a neighbouring reason).

CAUTION carried from #990: the screen for this work is NOT `go test -c`. See the sibling bead on that -- for a testdata/*.go.txt fixture compiled one module down, `go test -c` stays rc=0 while the child module runs zero tests. Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log: assert `[build failed]` absent and at least one `--- FAIL: Test...` naming a child test, with siblings still `--- PASS`.

title: ciguard: the hook-suite discovery walk has six measured gaps in what it accepts and rejects
description:
Named as residues F1, F2, F3, F4, F6 and F7 by the PR #951 round-7 reviewer, each graded residue rather than blocker for that PR. They are one coherent defect class — the walk and name-rule that discover hook suites under .githooks/ — so they are filed together rather than as six stubs.

F1  THE SCAN CANNOT TELL A COMMAND FROM ITS ARGUMENT. A recipe line like `command -v just test` reads as a reference to the `test` recipe. The scan is textual, so an argument that happens to spell a recipe name counts as a call.

F2  `.githooks/.hooks.bats` IS ACCEPTED BY NOTHING. A dotfile suite in the very directory the walk owns falls outside every acceptance rule, so it could be added and silently never run.

F3  `hooks-spec.sh` IS ACCEPTED BY THE NAME RULE. The converse of F2 — the name rule is loose enough to admit a file that is not a suite. Note F2 and F3 are opposite failures of the same rule, which is the argument for fixing it rather than patching either end.

F4  HOOK SUITES OUTSIDE `.githooks/` ARE OUT OF THE WALK REACH. The walk is rooted at .githooks/, so a suite placed anywhere else is invisible to it regardless of naming.

F6  THE QUOTED-# TRUNCATION HAZARD IN THE STRIP. The comment strip treats a `#` inside quotes as the start of a comment and truncates there, so a recipe line carrying a quoted hash is read as shorter than it is.

F7  THE `cannot` ABOUT DIRECTORIES IS FALSIFIABLE BY A SYMLINK. os.ReadDir returns a DirEntry whose IsDir() is FALSE for a symlink to a directory, so a symlinked directory falls through to the name rule instead of being skipped as a directory. This one is a prose defect as well as a behavioural one: the comment states a `cannot` that a symlink falsifies. The same paragraph already discloses two adjacent holes, which is why the reviewer graded it residue — the carrier is honest about its limits, just not about this one.

ACCEPTANCE: each of the six gets a test row that reddens when the corresponding rule is reverted. F7 additionally needs its comment corrected — state the limit rather than asserting a cannot, per the standing convention against universals that the tree own artifacts falsify.

NOT THE SAME AS gqlc-sgot. That is a defect in master (a gate that greps raw justfile bytes and so accepts a commented-out dependency). The reviewer measured that they do not interact adversely: PR #951 TestTestHooksIsReachedByARecipeCIRuns is precisely what catches the comment-out spelling gqlc-sgot misses.

title: resolver: the cross-product sentinel differential is a manual procedure with no CI job
description:
Named by the PR #963 round-3 reviewer as residue R4, correctly not blocking that PR.

The resolver corpus sweep now records the refusal sentinel per cell (landed by PR #911, bead gqlc-yb0w). The stronger instrument built on top of it — the branch-vs-master cross-product differential that classifies every cell as same-verdict-same-sentinel / same-verdict-different-sentinel / different-verdict — is what actually caught the +2/-2 movement on #963 and proved the other 12518 cells did not move.

But it is run BY HAND. Nothing in CI runs it, so nothing stops a future resolver change from moving a sentinel inside a FAIL->FAIL cell with a green pipeline. That is precisely the defect class gqlc-yb0w was filed for; the sweep now RECORDS the sentinel, but only the manual differential COMPARES it across a change.

The #963 body states plainly that the procedure is manual, which is why the reviewer graded it sufficient for that PR and residue rather than blocker.

ACCEPTANCE: a CI job that fails when a cell changes sentinel without the manifest being updated in the same commit. Note the standing rule that a detector which exits 0 is not a gate — the acceptance is that it FAILS, demonstrated by deliberately changing one sentinel and watching CI go red, not merely that a job exists and prints.

Adjacent: gqlc-yb0w (closed, PR #911) landed the per-cell sentinel recording this would compare.

title: ciguard: TestTestHooksIsADependencyOfTest reads the justfile raw, so a commented-out dependency passes it
description:
Introduced by PR #901 (internal/tools/ciguard/testhooks_test.go), measured by the PR #951 round-6 author.

The test reads the justfile as raw bytes to assert that the `test` recipe depends on `test-hooks`. Because it never parses, `test: check-hooks # test-hooks` satisfies it — the dependency is commented out, the hook suites drop out of CI, and the package still reports ok. Measured, not reasoned.

This is the repository's "a comment can be a witness" class on a new surface: the gate greps raw source bytes and accepts commented-out evidence.

Fix: parse with `just --dump` (JSON) or `just --evaluate`, or at minimum strip `#` comments before the match. Note that `just --dump` prints `error:` on a parse failure, so a mutation of the justfile can fake a RED — screen for that when pinning the fix.

title: .githooks: the commit-msg:15-17 line citation is gated by nothing and is cited from three places
description:
Measured by the PR #946 round-7 reviewer, who ran the falsifier the author had not: shifting the guard from line 15 to line 20 in .githooks/commit-msg leaves ALL THREE hook suites green. Nothing detects the rot.

The same range is cited from three sites — .githooks/commit-msg's own header, .githooks/claude-pre-bash, and .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh — so the author's keep rationale was that it rots only if all three rot together. The reviewer upheld the keep for PR #946 (the file is not in that diff, the construct is named alongside the range) but ruled the citation ungated.

Two ways out: retire the line numbers across all three sites in favour of the construct name, or add an assertion that the cited range still contains the construct. The first is cheaper and matches the repository's standing preference for citing a construct a reader can grep.

title: codegen/neo4j: declaredTests parses the fixture AST, so a commented-out test is invisible to the completeness check
description:
internal/codegen/neo4j's corpus harness builds its 'declared' set by parsing testdata/corpus_test.go.txt's AST. Commenting out a whole test therefore removes it from BOTH the declared set and the passed set, so require.ElementsMatch stays green and the row silently leaves the suite.

The require.NotEmpty backstop only fires if EVERY test is commented out, so it does not bound partial silence.

This is the 'a comment can be a witness' class inverted: here a comment makes evidence DISAPPEAR from a gate rather than counting as evidence. Pre-existing, not introduced by PR #966; named as a follow-up by the round-3 reviewer.

A fix needs a declaration that does not come from the same artifact the harness parses — e.g. an explicit expected-name list, or a count derived from the fixture's raw bytes rather than its AST.
close_reason:
Merged as 07954baf (PR #1002, squash). GH #974 CLOSED/COMPLETED. Verified on origin/master: corpusTests and require.NotEmpty live in both internal/codegen/neo4j and internal/codegen/age.

WHAT LANDED. declaredTests parsed the fixture AST, so a commented-out test was
invisible to the completeness check. Replaced by an explicit corpusTests name
list in both packages, plus a require.NotEmpty guard so that emptying the
fixture and the literal together cannot produce two empty sets that silently
match. Scope was extended to age during round 1 and stayed ratified.

THREE ROUNDS, and the guard is load-bearing in both packages -- measured by an
independent reviewer, not argued: delete require.NotEmpty and the last-name edit
goes rc=0 GREEN; the one-of-many case is still not swallowed, it reds via
ElementsMatch with 20 sibling child --- PASS.

ROUND 3 CLOSED TWO PROSE BLOCKERS.
  B1: two md5 rows in the body were taken at earlier commits than the heading
      named. Fixed not by editing the two rows but by re-deriving EVERY hash in
      one scripted pass. The reviewer re-derived independently: 22 rows, 22
      MATCH, 0 stale. Round 2's heading-names-the-wrong-commit shape is gone.
  B2: 'Down to the last name ... nothing here prevents' was false about the one
      case those words exist to carve out. Rewritten to state the general case
      and name the exception, dropping 'nothing here prevents' entirely. The new
      block is byte-identical in both packages, 527 bytes.

ON MY OWN WITHHELD SUSPICION. I read 'What the edit costs the remover either way
is writing the removal down' as a possible pseudo-cleft exhaustive reading that
the preceding sentence falsifies, and deliberately kept it out of the reviewer's
brief so its finding would be independent. It found the same clause on its own
and classified it the same way: resolved by the preceding sentence in the same
paragraph. Two instruments, same finding, same classification -- residue, not a
blocker. That is the same-carrier scoping rule applied twice.

RESIDUE FILED: gqlc-vg66 (the two corpus comments are byte-identical by hand and
