title: ci: a selective tidy re-run can leave lint/test/codegen-fence 'skipped' and mergeable
description:
Witnessed while landing gqlc-w4al (PR #867), 2026-08-17.

OBSERVED. On PR #867 at head e9119f75 I removed the 'Closes #617' line. Run 32005420996 fired on the edit; its tidy job failed. Because lint, test and codegen-fence all declare 'needs: [actionlint, tidy]', GitHub marked all three SKIPPED, and a skipped check run has conclusion 'skipped', which branch protection reads as a PASS. Rollup at that moment:

  tidy    COMPLETED FAILURE   <- newest, blocks
  lint    COMPLETED SKIPPED
  test    COMPLETED SKIPPED
  codegen-fence COMPLETED SKIPPED

That state itself is safe: tidy is red and blocks the merge.

THE HOLE. gqlc-w4al made tidy re-passable at an UNCHANGED SHA (the gate now reads the live PR body over the API, so adding the Closes line back turns tidy green with no new commit). That creates a sequence that was previously unreachable:

  1. head H, body missing Closes -> run R1: actionlint ok, tidy RED, lint/test/codegen-fence SKIPPED.
     Note lint/test have now never run at H.
  2. Add the Closes line. Run R2 fires on 'edited' and would re-run everything -- CANCEL it.
  3. Re-run ONLY the tidy job of R1 ('gh run rerun <R1> --job <tidy>'). It fetches the live body, passes.
  4. Newest per context: tidy SUCCESS, actionlint SUCCESS, lint/test/codegen-fence SKIPPED (= pass).
     Mergeable green, with lint and test never having executed at H.

Before gqlc-w4al this was not reachable: the only tidy failure fixable without a push was the body gate, and the body gate could not re-evaluate at all. Every other tidy failure (tidy-check, bd-export-monotonic) needs a commit, which moves the SHA and re-runs everything.

SEVERITY. Requires deliberate action by someone with write access: cancelling a run and selectively re-running one job. It is a bypass vector, not an accidental green. Step 3 is exactly the command I ran as the stale-payload witness, so it is not hypothetical -- I ran 'gh run rerun 32004817300 --job 95312044713' and got a fresh tidy check run on the same SHA.

SHAPE OF A FIX (pick one, all have costs):
- Drop 'needs: [actionlint, tidy]' from lint/test/codegen-fence. Loses the cheap-gates-first saving that the ci.yml header comment justifies (~3.5 min of runner time on a trivial formatting miss).
- Move the PR-body gate into its own job with no dependents. Needs a new required context added to BOTH protection configs (classic branch protection and the 'protect-master' ruleset), which strands every open PR on a pending context until they are updated -- the same objection recorded in gqlc-2rli.
- Add 'if: always()' to the dependents so they run and report a real verdict even when a gate fails. Costs the runner time the needs: chain was there to save.

ACCEPTANCE. A test that reaches the state in step 4 and asserts it is not mergeable, or a workflow shape where a skipped dependent cannot be the newest verdict for a required context at a SHA where the job never ran.

RELATED. gqlc-2rli (separate-workflow shape + protection-config steps). The 'skipped reads as a pass' fact is already documented in ci.yml's trigger comment and in vuln.yml.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17, from the independent review of PR #867 (/tmp/factory/verdict-867.md).

1. A SECOND HYPOTHESIS I RELAYED IS FALSE. I had suggested to the reviewer that a
   path filter on ci.yml could produce the same skipped triple without any re-run,
   which would make this bug far wider (a routine PR-description edit would suffice).
   It does not. Measured: the 'needs:' lines are byte-identical to master, tidy
   failed at 07:21:35 and the dependents skipped at 07:21:36. The cause is only
   ever the needs: chain with a failed gate. The bead's own mechanism paragraph
   was right; my widening was wrong. Severity stays "deliberate action required".

2. THE RE-RUN SEMANTICS IN STEP 3 NEED RE-MEASURING. The reviewer found that
   attempt 2 of run 32004817300 shows lint/test/codegen-fence with NEW job ids and
   NEW 07:22:30 timestamps, while actionlint carried over unchanged at 07:12:54.
   So 'gh run rerun --job <one>' RE-CREATES the dependents and RE-EVALUATES needs:,
   rather than leaving the old skipped runs standing. In that attempt they skipped
   again only because tidy had failed. Step 4 of the sequence above therefore
   assumes something not yet demonstrated: that after a SUCCESSFUL selective tidy
   re-run, the re-created dependents are still skipped rather than executed. If
   they execute, the bypass does not exist and this bead should be closed. That
   case was NOT run end-to-end by anyone; the reviewer states its account of it is
   inference from job records, not execution.

3. THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE IS UNVERIFIED. "a skipped check run ... branch
   protection reads as a PASS" is asserted here as fact and is repeated in ci.yml's
   trigger comment and in vuln.yml. Nobody has probed it live, and the reviewer
   found ZERO recorded cases across 40 merged PRs of a required context whose
   newest run was skipped. If GitHub in fact treats skipped as unsatisfied, this
   bead is empty. Settle this BEFORE building any of the three fixes -- all three
   cost real runner time or strand every open PR on a pending context.

WHAT SURVIVES REGARDLESS. The merge-precondition rule is unaffected and is the
durable output: evaluate newest check run per context over the seven required
contexts and require SUCCESS, rejecting SKIPPED, NEUTRAL and CANCELLED. Under any
resolution of (3) that query is correct, because a dependency-skip at a SHA where
the job never ran is exactly the state a coordinator must not read as green.

## 2026-08-17 — the load-bearing premise is SETTLED, and it is TRUE

This bead rested on an unverified premise: does GitHub treat a required status
check whose conclusion is `skipped` as SATISFYING the requirement? If it did not,
this bead was empty. It does.

VENDOR-DOCUMENTED (docs.github.com, "About protected branches", read 2026-08-17):

  "Required status checks must have a `successful`, `skipped`, or `neutral`
   status before collaborators can make changes to a protected branch."

So `skipped` and `neutral` both satisfy a required context. The bead is real.

MEASURED alongside it, and worth recording because it explains why nobody has hit
this yet: across the **40 most recent merged PRs**, the only context ever
newest-and-skipped is `live-smoke-age`, which is NOT one of the seven required
contexts. Zero merged PRs have a required context skipped-newest. So the hazard
is documented but has never fired here — untested in practice, not disproven.

Query used (newest run per context, per merged PR head SHA):

  gh api "repos/areqag/gqlc/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" --jq \
    '[.check_runs[] | {n:.name,c:.conclusion,s:.started_at}] | group_by(.n)
     | map(max_by(.s)) | .[] | select(.c=="skipped") | .n'

Required contexts confirmed first-party from
`repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection`: lint, test, tidy, actionlint,
govulncheck, live-smoke, codegen-fence. `strict:false`.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY MERGE GATE, human or automated: a rollup that accepts
"not FAILURE" is wrong. SKIPPED and NEUTRAL must be rejected explicitly, because
GitHub will merge them and they represent a check that did not run.
## 2026-08-18 — BOTH QUESTIONS SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT. THE BYPASS IS NOT REACHABLE.

Q2 decides the bead, so it goes first.

### Q2 — after a SUCCESSFUL selective re-run of the gate job, are the re-created dependents still skipped? NO. THEY EXECUTE.

Instrument: throwaway branch `probe/xdd0-rerun-semantics` carrying one
push-triggered workflow (ci.yml's push trigger is `branches: [master]`, and
vuln.yml / codegen-live.yml are pull_request-or-schedule, so nothing else fired
and no PR was needed). Shape mirrors ci.yml: `preflight` stands in for
actionlint and is always green; `gate` stands in for tidy and is
`test "$ATTEMPT" != "1"`, i.e. red on attempt 1 and green on any re-run at an
UNCHANGED SHA — the same "flips verdict with no new commit" property gqlc-w4al
gave tidy by moving the body read to the API; `dependent-a` and `dependent-b`
carry `needs: [preflight, gate]` and stand in for lint / test / codegen-fence.

SHA f8301f585a747f78c242a9b15b8c8ff0a74c5fa2, run 32149913422.

Attempt 1 reproduces step 1 of the DESCRIPTION:

    gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/actions/runs/32149913422/attempts/1/jobs \
      --jq '.jobs[]|[.id,.name,.status,.conclusion,.started_at]|@tsv'
    95752916435  gate         completed  failure  2026-08-18T14:41:53Z
    95752916682  preflight    completed  success  2026-08-18T14:41:53Z
    95752961106  dependent-b  completed  skipped  2026-08-18T14:41:57Z
    95752963110  dependent-a  completed  skipped  2026-08-18T14:41:58Z

Step 3 of the DESCRIPTION, run verbatim:

    gh run rerun 32149913422 --job 95752916435

Attempt 2 — the state step 4 assumed and nobody had executed:

    gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/actions/runs/32149913422/attempts/2/jobs \
      --jq '.jobs[]|[.id,.name,.status,.conclusion,.started_at]|@tsv'
    95753853667  gate         completed  success  2026-08-18T14:44:35Z
    95753854577  preflight    completed  success  2026-08-18T14:41:53Z
    95753885061  dependent-b  completed  success  2026-08-18T14:44:42Z
    95753885089  dependent-a  completed  success  2026-08-18T14:44:42Z

`dependent-a`'s log carries `dependent-a EXECUTED on attempt 2`. `preflight` is
the carry-over the earlier reviewer described: a new job id (95753854577, was
95752916682) keeping attempt 1's 14:41:53 timestamp.

And the SHA's check-run list afterwards holds no skipped row — the skipped runs
are replaced, not left standing beside the new ones:

    gh api "repos/areqag/gqlc/commits/f8301f585a747f78c242a9b15b8c8ff0a74c5fa2/check-runs?per_page=100" \
      --jq '.check_runs[]|[.id,.name,.status,.conclusion,.started_at]|@tsv'
    95753885089  dependent-a  completed  success
    95753885061  dependent-b  completed  success
    95753854577  preflight    completed  success
    95753853667  gate         completed  success

So step 4 does not occur. A selective re-run that turns the gate green
re-creates the dependents and runs them, and a skipped dependent cannot be left
as the newest verdict for its context by that route. **The bead is empty and
should be closed as such.** Note 2 above was right to demand this measurement.

### The neighbouring route step 2 gestures at ("CANCEL it") is also closed

If a cancelled run's dependents concluded `skipped`, they would satisfy
protection (see Q1) and the bypass would exist by a route the DESCRIPTION does
not name. In ci.yml the dependents are dispatched as soon as actionlint and
tidy pass, so the reachable cancel window is one where they are in progress.
Reproduced at 4efb277b58a76ae0ee2bc11fa800dbf531904a7e, run 32150832229:
`gate` fast-green, dependents `needs: [gate]` running `sleep 180`; waited for
both to reach in_progress, then `gh run cancel 32150832229`:

    gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/actions/runs/32150832229/jobs \
      --jq '.jobs[]|[.name,.status,.conclusion]|@tsv'
    gate         completed  success
    dependent-a  completed  cancelled
    dependent-b  completed  cancelled

`cancelled`, not `skipped`. That the `cancelled` conclusion then blocks is
GitHub's documentation, not something measured here.

### Q1 — does branch protection treat a skipped required check run as satisfied? YES, and it is now measured rather than cited.

Note 3 above, and the 2026-08-17 note under it, rested on docs.github.com.
Disposable PR #1015 (closed, branch deleted) put it on an instrument. One edit:
`if: ${{ false }}` on ci.yml's `actionlint` job, which skips actionlint and,
through `needs: [actionlint, tidy]`, lint / test / codegen-fence too. tidy,
govulncheck and live-smoke were left to run. Head
b10e89bae937ff530cc5def23248a3b520a69be8:

    gh api "repos/areqag/gqlc/commits/b10e89bae937ff530cc5def23248a3b520a69be8/check-runs?per_page=100" \
      --jq '.check_runs[]|[.name,.status,.conclusion]|@tsv'
    test            completed  skipped
    lint            completed  skipped
    codegen-fence   completed  skipped
    live-smoke-age  completed  skipped
    actionlint      completed  skipped
    govulncheck     completed  success
    live-smoke      completed  success
    tidy            completed  success

    gh pr view 1015 --repo areqag/gqlc --json mergeStateStatus,mergeable
    {"mergeStateStatus":"CLEAN","mergeable":"MERGEABLE"}

lint, test and actionlint are required by the classic protection list AND by
the `protect-master` ruleset; codegen-fence by the classic list. GitHub reports
the PR CLEAN with each of their newest — and only — check runs concluded
`skipped`. The 40-merged-PR survey found no natural witness because no required
context had been skipped-newest here before; this is one.

### What this means for the prose carriers

Q1 holding means nothing in the tree is falsified. `ci.yml:18`,
`codegen-live.yml:51` ("GitHub counts a skipped check as satisfying a required
context", over `live-smoke-age`), and the require-messages in
`internal/tools/ciguard/workflow_test.go`, `testhooks_test.go` and
`golangci_cache_test.go` all say the same thing and all remain correct. No
correction PR is owed on them, and the ciguard guards that forbid a job-level
`if:` on the required jobs are guarding a real hazard.

Two imprecisions in this bead's own RELATED paragraph, corrected here rather
than left to be re-derived: `vuln.yml` does not carry the skipped-satisfies
claim — it says required checks are matched by name with no conditional
primitive, which is a different statement — and `codegen-live.yml` is a carrier
the paragraph does not name.

`gqlc-2rli` already records that the classic list and the ruleset differ (the
ruleset omits live-smoke and codegen-fence), re-verified today, so nothing new
is filed for it.

### What this does not settle

- plain `gh run rerun <id>` and `gh run rerun <id> --failed` were not run
- a dependent cancelled before it is dispatched at all: I could not reach that
  state without also leaving a non-success row on a job it `needs:`, which
  blocks for its own reason
- whether GitHub rejects `cancelled` and `timed_out` — documentation only
- both re-run measurements were on push-triggered runs; the Q1 measurement was
  on a pull_request run

### What survives, unchanged

The merge-precondition rule in the note above: evaluate the newest check run
per context over the required contexts and require SUCCESS, rejecting SKIPPED,
NEUTRAL and CANCELLED. Q1 is exactly why — GitHub will merge a skipped required
context, and PR #1015 is the demonstration.

The selective re-run in step 3 re-creates the dependents and RUNS them once the gate goes green (run 32149913422 attempt 2: both dependents success, no skipped row left at the SHA), so step 4 is not reachable by that route. Q1 was settled in the affirmative and by measurement rather than citation (PR #1015, closed): four required contexts newest-and-skipped, mergeStateStatus CLEAN. No prose carrier is falsified, so no correction PR is owed. Commands and raw output in NOTES.

title: ci: sweep-discovery-probes only recognises mktemp -d as a probe site
description:
`sweep-discovery-probes` (justfile) holds three copies of the probe names to
each other: the `*_probe` variables, the `discovery_probes` concatenation, and
the sites that create the probes. It discovers sites by grepping `just --dump`
for one idiom:

    site_re="mktemp -d ""test/data/"

So a probe directory created under test/data by anything other than
`mktemp -d` — `mkdir -p`, `install -d`, a Go helper this justfile invokes, a
test using t.TempDir with a TMPDIR pointed at test/data — is not a site to any
check in the recipe. The declared names are not held to it, the site-shape
refusal does not see it, and if its spelling is not one of the declared names
the sweep glob does not clear it either.

Not currently reachable: at the time of filing the only three probe sites in
the justfile are `mktemp -d test/data/{{ var }}.XXXXXX` (justfile:721, :832,
:1191, PR #833 head). This is a limit of the check, stated in the tree beside
`site_re`, not a live defect.

Closing it means either (a) discovering sites from the paths that actually
appear under test/data at runtime rather than from the justfile text, or
(b) moving the probe creation behind one recipe/helper that the other recipes
call, so there is one site to hold rather than a pattern to match.

title: lint: the justfile's shell is not shellchecked by any gate
description:
`just lint` runs `lint-hooks`, whose default argument is `dir=".githooks"` (justfile: `lint-hooks dir=".githooks"`, and `lint: ensure-golangci lint-hooks check-golangci-build-tags`). So every line of bash in the justfile itself — including the whole `vuln` recipe, several hundred lines of it, which is the body of a required CI context — has no static analysis behind it.

Witness: extract the `vuln` recipe body and run the repo's own `.bin/shellcheck` 0.10.0 over it. It parses and reports SC2015 (info) on `lines() { [ -n "${1}" ] && printf '%s\\n' "${1}" || true; }`. Nothing in CI does that run, so the finding has been sitting there unreported.

The fix is not simply widening `lint-hooks` to the justfile: a just recipe body is not a shell script on disk (interpolation braces, per-recipe shebangs, dedent), so it needs an extraction step first. Scope: extract each shebang recipe body, shellcheck it, fail the gate on new findings, and either clear or baseline the pre-existing SC2015.

Found while reviewing PR #846 (bd gqlc-u91z), which added ~130 lines of unlinted bash to that recipe.

title: vuln: ten assertions guarding the unplaced-stdlib grading are killed by nothing
description:
In `just vuln`, ten assertions that guard the unplaced-stdlib grading are killed
by no mutation, on either toolchain arm. Each passes on a good tree, so
neutering it changes nothing observable.

Measured first-party at `c7bee5cb` (PR #846). Each row applies ONE edit, asserts
the edit is LIVE (`diff` vs pristine, non-empty), asserts the artifact stayed
VALID (`just --summary` parses it AND the extracted 659-line recipe body passes
`bash -n`), runs `just vuln`, then restores by md5 and verifies the restore.

- M9: `expect_refusal`'s marker check `*"${marker}"*)` -> `*)` — SURVIVED rc=0.
  The clause that asserts WHICH refusal fired can be deleted; M8 and M11 are
  killed by it today, so it is live, but nothing regresses it.
- M13: delete the first `expect_refusal` call (bare 'go') — SURVIVED rc=0.
- M14: delete the second `expect_refusal` call (absent header) — SURVIVED rc=0.
- M16: the witness-quotes-the-header `case` -> `*) ;;` — SURVIVED rc=0.
- MW: the witness's two-line acceptance contract
  `[ "${accepted}" != "${witness_where}"$'\n'"${placed_header}" ]` -> `if false`
  — SURVIVED rc=0. MH and MI are killed by it, so it is live.
- M19: the per-module tally guard `if [ -n "${ungraded}" ]` -> `if false` —
  SURVIVED rc=0.
- MA: the tally's `comm -13` -> `comm -23`, so the guard mis-answers while
  looking intact — SURVIVED rc=0. Deletion is not the only shape this family
  takes; mis-direction is uncovered too.
- MG: the call site's header match
  `if ! grep -qxF -- "${graded_line}" <<<"${out}"` -> `if false` — SURVIVED
  rc=0. MF, MJ, MK and MN are killed by it, so it is live.
- ML: the same match's `grep -qxF` -> `grep -qF`, whole-line weakened to
  substring — SURVIVED rc=0. MF still dies under it, so the anchoring itself is
  not what MF turns on.
- MP: the same match's haystack `<<<"${out}"` -> `<<<"${stdlib_graded}"`, so the
  assertion compares the acceptance against itself — SURVIVED rc=0. This is the
  argument-replacement shape that produced MF one line up; here it makes the
  assertion tautological rather than opening the gate, because
  `refuse_unplaced_stdlib` is still reading the real `${out}` and its own
  refusal still fires. Substituting a name that does not exist is fail-closed
  instead: the recipe runs under `set -u`.

## Correction

The first version of this bead, and row B19 of PR #846's matrix, both said M19
"IS killed under `GOVERSION=go1.26.5-X:nodwarf5`, row B19, by the grading's own
exit". That is false, and it measures false:

    diff 846r4z-B0.log 846r4z-bl-M19.log | wc -l   ->   0

Byte-identical to the unmutated blind run. That run is red because the TREE is
blind — the grading's own refusal fires and exits long before the tally is
reached — not because the mutation was detected. Under this recipe's own
screening rule, that a kill must NAME the thing the mutation broke, B19 is not a
kill. The blind arm distinguishes M13, M14, M16, MA, MG, MW, ML and MP no
better: every one of them produces a log 0 diff lines from the blind baseline.
Of that arm's rows only M3, M17 and MF differ from it (270, 269 and 18 lines),
and only those three are kills there.

So the gap is not "killed on the other arm". It is killed by nothing, on either
arm, and that is its real size.

## Why it is still second-order

Every clause above is demonstrably load-bearing on the paths that do run, and
the two guards added for the header match cover disjoint mutants — the witness
kills MH and MI (the accepting arm dropping a line), the call-site match kills
MF, MJ, MK and MN (the arm or the call site reading the wrong string). What is
missing is the regress: nothing fails when one of them is removed.

What two of them removed together costs is measured, not asserted, and the two
pairs do not cost the same thing. Both are the M4 class: two deliberate edits,
disclosed here.

- Row MX applies MF and MG at once and is **rc=0 under
  `GOVERSION=go1.26.5-X:nodwarf5`**, with zero `error:` lines and both headers
  reading `... and the go standard library:`. That is the gate itself open —
  the blind toolchain accepted.
- Row MY applies MH and MW at once. On a release toolchain it is rc=0, with
  `graded_line` empty and `grep -qxF -- ""` matching one of the 13 blank lines
  in govulncheck's output. On the blind arm it is **rc=1, and 0 diff lines from
  the unmutated blind run** — `refuse_unplaced_stdlib` still refuses, naming the
  module and quoting the header. So MY destroys the tie between a grading and
  the scan it read while leaving the gate closed. It is the weaker of the two.

Same family as gqlc-65sl (every `selftest_*` call site in this recipe) and
gqlc-eo46 (`refuse_stale` proven to work and never proven to be called). 4 of
the 5 live `comm -13` guards in this justfile predate PR #846.
notes:
Two more survivors, found by the independent review of PR #846 at 925ca385 and
NOT in the 46-row matrix this bead was filed from. Both SURVIVE rc=0 on the
release arm and are NOT-DISTINGUISHED on the blind arm:

- R1: the accepting arm emits "${scan}" instead of "${line}".
- R9: graded_line is read from <<<"${out}".

Reproduce: /tmp/factory/lin846r5-mut.sh R1 /tmp/factory/lin846r5-edit-R1.py -> R1: rc=0.

Both belong to the already-disclosed two-edit MX class, so neither widens the
defect; they widen the survivor set. This bead makes no exhaustiveness claim and
the count above should not be read as one.

The witness's blind spot has a name and should carry it: the witness cannot see
any grading behaviour that varies with anything in the header line other than the
token, because its fabricated headers differ from a real scan only in the module
count (2 vs 43/54). That is what row R7 establishes.

Two adjacent prose nits from the same review, for whoever takes this:
docs/adr/0026:256 carries an unscoped "every invocation" where justfile:1432-1436
scopes the same claim to the recipe; docs/adr/0026:241's "...and the go standard
library: is exactly and only the unplaced rendering" is true on v1.7.0 but states
its scope 200 lines away at 439-444.

title: codegen/age: the live battery never writes an offset sidecar
description:
DEFECT: the AGE live smoke battery exercises the instant round trip but never puts an <f>Offset property in the graph, so the emitted agtypeZone is only ever live-witnessed on its absent-key branch. Neither the in-range zoned read nor the refusal added by gqlc-x5wx (PR #848) has a live witness — both are pinned only by the corpus harness, which runs the emitted helpers against hand-built props maps rather than against agtype coming back from Apache AGE.

WITNESS: run 32000835738 (codegen-live, headSha 619c7186) is green with live-smoke-age success. The scenario it drives is readScenarios' "timestamp_property_roundtrip: instant round trip + ordering" (test/data/codegen/live_age_test.go), whose oneEvent CREATE binds the instant alone. grep for "Offset" across test/data/codegen returns no write. So the live arm proves the absent-sidecar path returns the instant unchanged in UTC, and says nothing about the two paths PR #848 changed.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a live scenario whose CREATE sets both the instant property and its <f>Offset sidecar, asserting (a) an in-range offset comes back as the zone on the decoded time.Time, and (b) an out-of-range one (86400) fails the decode with an error naming the property. The second half needs the harness to admit an expected-error scenario, which readScenarios does not model today.

title: codegen/age: agtypeInstant takes any int64 as epoch-micros
description:
DEFECT: the emitted agtypeInstant (internal/codegen/age/render_models.go) reads the stored int64 and calls time.UnixMicro on it with no bound, so a property holding math.MaxInt64 decodes to a year ~294000 instant and is returned without error. Sibling of gqlc-x5wx, which bounded the <f>Offset sidecar.

WITNESS: the emitted helper is

	micros, err := agtypeInt64(raw)
	...
	return time.UnixMicro(micros).UTC(), nil

with no range test between the two. The corpus test TestAgtypeZoneRefusesAnOffsetOutsideADay (internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt) refuses math.MaxInt64 as an offset; the same value as micros is accepted by agtypeInstant.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED ON PR #848 rather than fixed there: the two are not the same shape.
1. The micros count IS the instant. Any bound on it is a calendar-range policy decision, not a well-formedness one, and there is no equivalent of "a zone no clock keeps" to key it on. The live corpus deliberately carries year 9999 and pre-epoch instants (test/data/codegen/valid/timestamp_property_roundtrip), so any candidate bound has to be argued against rows that already exist.
2. gqlc's own encode writes the micros. It is a value this encoding produced and read back, so it is not the untrusted external input the sidecar is — the sidecar is the interop affordance for graphs gqlc did not write.

Reachability is therefore lower and the fix needs a policy decision (what calendar range does this backend admit?) that belongs in its own bead, not smuggled into a bounds fix.
notes:
CORRECTION (PR #848 round 3) to 'WHY IT WAS DEFERRED' point 2. The bead stands; one clause in it does not.

WITHDRAWN, false: 'the sidecar is the interop affordance for graphs gqlc did not write.' A query whose own text names the sidecar key binds it through the emitted agtypeArgs, so a sidecar value can be one a gqlc encoding produced. Measured: one emitted package reads agtypeZone(props, "occurredAtOffset", value1) at models.go:40 and binds that same key through agtypeArgs at queries.cypher.go:51, with both helpers declared in models.go. Also refuted by the sentence's own consequence being deleted from offsetSidecar's doc and from the emitted agtypeZone doc on PR #848.

THE DEFERRAL STANDS on the rest of point 1, which is untouched and was independently judged legitimate: the micros count IS the instant, so any bound on it is a calendar-range POLICY decision rather than a well-formedness one, and there is no equivalent of 'a zone no clock keeps' to key it on. The live corpus deliberately carries year-9999 and pre-epoch instants (test/data/codegen/valid/timestamp_property_roundtrip), so any candidate bound has to be argued against rows that already exist.

What remains true in point 2 is a difference of REACHABILITY, not of provenance: gqlc's own encode writes the micros for every instant it binds, whereas it derives no sidecar parameter at all. That makes the instant path the more reachable one -- it does not make the sidecar path exclusively foreign.

title: codegen: the swept-file partition is complete but its two sides are unmeasured — moving a fixed file to inputDerivedFiles silences the sweep
description:
`internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` (PR #845, `TestEveryEmittedFixedDeclarationIsReserved`) partitions the golden corpus in two: `fixedDeclarationFiles` = `{db.go, graph.go, querier.go}`, whose exported declarations must each carry a `reservedIdentifiers` row, and `inputDerivedFiles` = `{models.go}` plus the `*.cypher.go` suffix, whose declarations follow from the batch and owe nothing. Every golden must fall in one side or the other, so an emitted file nobody classified fails.

THE HOLE IS THE SIDE A NAME IS PUT ON. Membership in `inputDerivedFiles` is asserted, never measured. Moving a fixed file to that side silences the sweep for it and passes the completeness check, because the file is still classified.

WITNESS (first-party, detached worktree at `c4642404`, `go vet ./internal/codegen/` printing BUILD OK before the test ran):

    fixedDeclarationFiles = {"db.go": true, "querier.go": true}
    inputDerivedFiles     = {"models.go": true, "graph.go": true}

    test exit=0 · kill-count(top-level FAIL)=0 · ok github.com/areqag/gqlc/internal/codegen 35.216s

`graph.go` is the Apache AGE-only file: `SessionInit`, `EnsureGraph`, `DropGraph`. All three lose their obligation and the package stays green. This is the same fail-silent family as the aggregate `swept` counter #845 replaced — one edit narrower.

FIX DIRECTION: derive the side rather than declaring it. The property that separates them is measurable in the corpus already: a fixed file's exported names are the emitter's own, so the set it declares is drawn from a fixed vocabulary across every fixture of a target, while an input-derived file's names track the fixture. `graph.go` declares the same three names in all 45 AGE goldens; `models.go` declares `Person` in one fixture and `Movie` in another. A file classified input-derived whose exported names never vary across the fixtures of a target is misclassified, and that is a check, not a claim.

RELATED (nit N2, independent review of #832): there are now three hand-maintained emitted-file lists, two of them of opposite polarity — `conformance_test.go:638` `connectionSurface` (exclusion, `{db.go, graph.go}`), `prepare_test.go` `fixedDeclarationFiles` (inclusion) and `inputDerivedFiles` (exclusion). A derivation would retire two of the three.

ACCEPTANCE: the witness above turns a NAMED test red, with `go vet` clean before the test runs so the kill is not the compiler.

PROVENANCE: found and measured while fixing blocker 1 of the independent review of PR #845, 2026-08-17. The blocker's own prescribed fix (count per basename) does not kill the mutation that motivated it; pinning the file set to the corpus does, and this is what that pinning still cannot see.

The bead's stated FIX DIRECTION is falsified in its naive form and was NOT implemented as written. Symmetrically, directory.cypher.go and people.cypher.go have exactly one fixture each, so "never varies" is trivially true of them and the rule would red-flag AllPersonIds/PersonNameById, which are genuinely input-derived.

Margins are wide on both sides (83/83 and 45/45 vs 62/83 and 5/71), so the discriminator is not near a boundary.

title: check-pr-closes forces a Closes on any PR whose branch or body names a bead, including PRs that only change its status
description:
`.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py` derives the bead a PR is about from a
`Bead:` line in the body, falling back to the branch name, and then requires
the body to carry `Closes #N` for that bead's GitHub mirror. The gate has no
way to say "this PR touches the bead but does not resolve it".

## Witness

PR #609 reopened bead `gqlc-4np` (GH issue #503). Its branch happened not to
contain the id, so the gate stayed silent. Had the branch been named after the
bead — the repo's own convention — the gate would have demanded `Closes #503`
on a PR whose whole purpose was that #503 should be open, and merging it would
have closed the issue it had just reopened.

Choosing a branch name that dodges the id is not a control: it is invisible,
unenforced, and it also disables the gate for PRs that genuinely should close
their issue.

## Why it was left out of gqlc-w4al

gqlc-w4al fixed re-evaluation (`edited` in ci.yml's `pull_request` types) and
the frozen-payload read (the body is now fetched from the API). Both make the
gate harder to get past. This one pulls the other way: any opt-out marker is
by construction a one-line bypass, and now that the gate re-evaluates on every
body edit, an opt-out can be added to a body at any point up to merge. What
the marker should be, and what stops it being used to wave a PR through, is a
design decision that deserves its own review rather than a fold-in.

## Shape of a fix

Needs to decide, at minimum:
- the marker's spelling and where it may appear (e.g. `Bead: gqlc-x (refs)` vs
  a separate `Refs:` line vs a label);
- whether an opt-out PR must still say something checkable — e.g. that the
  bead is not `in_progress`/`closed` in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, or that the PR
  demonstrably does not close it — so the marker is not simply "trust me";
- whether a label is better than body text, since labels are events
  (`pull_request: labeled/unlabeled`) and are attributable.

## Acceptance

- A PR that changes a bead's status without resolving it can name that bead
  and merge without `Closes #N`, and does so via a declared marker rather than
  by avoiding the id in the branch name.
- The marker cannot be used to skip the gate on a PR that does resolve its
  bead without that being visible in the diff or the check's output.
- `.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh` gains a row per new verdict.
notes:

title: codegen/neo4j: no live scenario decodes a nested list, so the depth-suffixed decoder arms have never met a real Bolt server
description:
PR #822 (`0a139b74`, bd gqlc-ye6g) changed the emitted decoder for nested list
columns: `walkListElemBody`'s `inner`/`innerAcc` and `walkListElemPlan`'s `elem`
are now suffixed by nesting depth via `elemLocal`. The review of that PR recorded
"the emitted decoders were never exercised against a real Bolt server" as an
unverified gap, attributing it to Docker being down on the review box.

Docker is not the binding constraint. I dispatched the live workflow on a branch
carrying that emitter (run 32001875182, `gh workflow run codegen-live`) and both
jobs went green with a REAL execution — 47.3s wall, zero `(cached)` lines, zero
`no tests to run` lines. It still witnesses nothing about this change.

WITNESS — the live battery has no nested-list shape in it:

    grep -rn 'list_list_int|schema_list_property_widths|schema_list_any_property' \
      test/data/codegen/*.go
    -> no matches

    grep -rn '\[\]\[\]' test/data/codegen/live_test.go
    -> no matches

`TestLiveSmoke` (test/data/codegen/live_test.go:267) iterates `readScenarios`
(:235-248) plus `edgeUnionScenarios` (:257). The full scenario list is:

    one_col_one_param_one, many_col_many, entity_node_projected_one,
    entity_edge_projected_one, mixed_read_write_batch,
    timestamp_property_roundtrip, edge_union_undeclared_relationship_type

None projects a `LIST<LIST<...>>`. The goldens that DO contain `innerAcc` /
`inner1` — `list_list_int`, `schema_list_property_widths`,
`schema_list_any_property` under test/data/codegen/valid/ — are driven by the
conformance golden sweep and by `just test-codegen-fence`, which COMPILE and
LINT them against the real driver but never execute them against a server.

So the depth-suffix change is covered on three axes (golden text, compilation
against the real neo4j driver, and the corpus driver-stub battery
`TestEmittedDecodersRunOnDriverValues`) and on zero live ones. Nothing has ever
handed a real Bolt `[]any` of `[]any` to `decode...` and read the result back.

This is distinct from gqlc-df3d, which is about the `-run` allowlist mechanism
preventing a NEW live test from being selected. Here the test does not exist at
all; adding one would also have to clear df3d's allowlist to actually run.

ACCEPTANCE: a `readScenarios` entry that seeds a nested list property (depth >= 2,
so the emitted decoder declares `inner1`/`innerAcc1`), reads it back through a
generated method, and asserts the round-tripped value; selected by the live
recipes' `-run` regex; witnessed executing in a `codegen-live` run with no
`no tests to run` line and no `(cached)`. Reverting `elemLocal` to `return name`
should redden it.

title: spec fence: a driver binding written without map[string]any{ is unswept
description:
The binding sweep's anchor is the literal `map[string]any{` — the opening brace is part of the anchor. A spec that states a binding as a bare code span, with no literal around it, is not read at all.

Witness (measured 2026-08-17 on PR #804, head dbeabc3a, and still live): inserting into docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md §5.3 the bullet

    - The driver binding is `"minAge": minAge` inside the map literal.

leaves TestSpecParamsMapBindsGeneratorOwnedValue PASS. That line documents the capture vector gqlc-lhs3 removed from the emitter, in the section gqlc-rz0l exists to correct, and the fence says nothing.

The symmetric signature escape was closed on that branch by anchoring a second scanner on a backtick before the context parameter (ADR 0029 decision 10). The same move was declined for bindings after measurement: the swept documents hold 130+ bare `"key": value` code spans across 21 files, essentially all JSON model shapes with no relation to a driver binding, so a brace-less recogniser would fire on prose across the corpus. See ADR 0029 decision 10.

Closing this needs something narrower than a bare key/value recogniser — e.g. grading only spans whose key matches a parameter name the surrounding section declares, or requiring specs to print bindings only inside the literal and fencing that requirement.

title: codegen/neo4j: the decoder probe stops at two levels of list nesting
description:
`decoderProbeWidths` in `internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go` derives, for each scalar the type table admits, that scalar plus `LIST<scalar>` plus `LIST<LIST<scalar>>`. Two levels is the first depth that reaches `writeSliceNarrow`'s recursive arm at all: `nested0`, `acc0`, `elem1`, `i1` and `v1` enter the swept set there and are absent at one level.

But no finite depth closes this, because the emitted names are depth-indexed (`internal/codegen/neo4j/render_models.go:327-359`):

    item := fmt.Sprintf("elem%d", depth)
    idx  := fmt.Sprintf("i%d", depth)
    inner := fmt.Sprintf("nested%d", depth)
    acc   := fmt.Sprintf("acc%d", depth)
    ... fmt.Fprintf(b, "%sv%d, ok := ...", body, depth)

So a schema declaring a three-deep list emits `elem2`, `i2`, `nested1`, `acc1` and `v2` — five identifiers the sweep has never seen, and a property named after any of them would collide undetected. Depth 4 adds five more. Extending the probe to depth 3 only moves the boundary.

The fix is different in kind from widening the probe: pin the *family* rather than the set. Either derive the guard from the format strings (no emitted local may be `fmt.Sprintf`-derived from a property name), or assert that the depth-indexed families are closed — that for every name in the swept set of the form `<stem><n>`, no property may be named `<stem><m>` for any m.

Filed from gqlc-320w, which reaches depth 2 and states the limit in the `decoderProbeWidths` doc comment rather than hiding it.

title: codegen/neo4j: TestTypeMapProperty leaves ANY VALUE and the bare LIST unswept
description:
`internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go`'s `TestTypeMapProperty` enumerates 29 of the 31 `graph.PropertyType` constants: 21 representable widths plus the 8 unrepresentable ones. `graph.TypeAnyPropertyValue` and `graph.TypeList` are named nowhere in that file, so the two arms of `typeMap.Property` that answer `any` and `[]any` have no unit row behind them.

Found while doing gqlc-320w, which built a walk (`propertyArmNames` in `internal/codegen/neo4j/decoder_test.go`) that reads the case expressions of `typeMap.Property` off types.go. That walk already gives `TestTypeMapProperty` the derivation it needs: hold its case table to naming every constant the switch has an arm for, rather than to a hand list.

Measured 2026-08-17 on fix/neo4j-decoder-probe-derives-coverage:
  grep -o 'graph.Type[A-Za-z0-9]*' internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go | sort -u | wc -l  -> 29
  the same over internal/graph/propertytype.go                                             -> 31

Not a defect in emitted code — both arms are exercised end to end by the decoder probe added in gqlc-320w and by the golden corpus. It is a hole in the unit-level table test.

title: resolver: Phase B commits an unlabelled binding to one type through a far end that does not cover
description:
On test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql:

  MATCH (p:Person)-[q:WORKS_AT]->(c)
  OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[h:HAS_DESK]->(d:Desk)
  MATCH (c)<-[w:WORKS_AT]-(x)
  RETURN x.personOnly

accepts {"type":"STRING","nullable":false}. The Employee&Person -[WORKS_AT]-> Company&Large row matches with h/d null, so c is Company&Large, the only WORKS_AT into it comes from Employee&Person, and that x has no personOnly. A NOT NULL column that is null.

candidateTypes computes c = {Company,Company&Large} INTERSECT {Company} = {Company} with covered=false, because the HAS_DESK hop is OPTIONAL and witnessesItsEndpoints refuses it. inferUnlabelled then writes resolved[c]=Company anyway and merely withholds the resolvedCovers mark. The covering lane gates what OTHER bindings learn from c; it does not stop c itself being committed to a strict subset of the attainable types, and x is then inferred singularly from that wrong c and projected directly.

So the resolver has two different notions in one map: 'the type' and 'the types a row can have'. The narrowing respects the difference; the projection path does not.

Same soundness class as gqlc-3uof but a different mechanism — 3uof was endpointLabels under-enumerating, this is Phase B committing on an admittedly-incomplete intersection. Closely related to the unlabelled-binding axis in gqlc-pv0u / gqlc-h6h7, and to gqlc-856f / gqlc-edze (ResolvedType is not a sealed sum), since the honest answer here is probably a plural node type rather than a refusal.

Witness for any fix: the query above must not offer x.personOnly as NOT NULL. The one-token twin with the OPTIONAL made mandatory must stay accepted — every returned row then really does have a HAS_DESK out of c, HAS_DESK is declared from the bare Company only, and the chain is sound.
notes:

title: resolver: a refusal-sentinel change inside a FAIL->FAIL cell is invisible to the corpus sweep, so a worse diagnostic can land green
description:
The strongest evidence for PR #806 (merged `aade7a40`, bead gqlc-0tft) was a corpus sweep: 310 queries x 28 schemas = 8680 cells, branch vs base, reporting 8 FAIL->PASS, 2616 PASS->PASS with every golden byte-identical, and zero accept->refuse / accept->different-answer. That is a strong result and it is why #806 was sound to land.

It has a hole, and the hole is a whole quadrant. The sweep compares VERDICTS (accept/refuse) and golden BYTES. It does not compare error strings. So of the 8680 cells, the **6056 that were FAIL before and FAIL after are compared on nothing but the fact of failing.** A change that swaps which sentinel a refusal returns — or degrades a precise diagnostic into a generic one — moves no cell between quadrants, changes no golden byte, and is therefore invisible.

This is not hypothetical. The reviewer found one by hand while spot-checking: a refusal that changed from `ErrAmbiguousLabel` to `ErrUnknownEdge`. That instance is an IMPROVEMENT, so nothing is broken today. But it was found by hand, and the reviewer stated plainly it 'cannot bound the rest' — nobody knows how many of the 6056 changed sentinel, or in which direction.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND #806: this is the sweep methodology the resolver work keeps using to prove a narrowing change is safe. Every future use inherits the same blind spot, and diagnostic quality is exactly what a narrowing change is most likely to perturb — narrowing changes which check fires first.

Same family as gqlc-fd06, gqlc-x5dq, gqlc-320w: a guard that is structural on one axis and blind on another, so it defends the shapes it was written alongside.

FIX: have the corpus sweep record the sentinel (or the full error string) per refusing cell and diff that too, so a FAIL->FAIL cell whose sentinel changed is reported as a third category rather than folded into 'no change'. Then the sweep's own output states which of the three it is: same verdict same sentinel, same verdict different sentinel, different verdict.

ACCEPTANCE: deliberately change one refusal's sentinel in the resolver, run the sweep, and confirm it REPORTS the change rather than printing an all-clear. Today it does not — that is the defect.

Do the before/after drill in both directions, and watch for the fake RED: a sweep that errors out because the harness cannot parse a changed message is not the same as one that detects the change.

PROVENANCE: the 'Not verified' section of the independent Linus review of PR #806, 2026-08-17, /tmp/factory/verdict-806.md. Filed rather than folded in; #806 had zero correctness blockers and this is a gap in the verification method, not in the shipped behaviour.

title: codegen: reservedIdentifiers is a hand-maintained list — a new emitter-fixed exported name is not reserved and the collision gate fails open
description:
PR #832 (merged as `5718a935`, bead gqlc-e6mh) added `reservedIdentifiers` in `internal/codegen/prepare.go:49` — 12 rows, 9 `scopePackage` + 3 `scopeMethod` — so a schema element named `Queries`/`DBTX`/`ErrNoRows`/... is refused instead of emitting a non-compiling package.

The set is CORRECT today. An independent `go/parser` sweep over all 153 golden target trees found exported package-level fixed decls == exactly the 9 `scopePackage` rows and exported `*Queries` methods == exactly the 3 `scopeMethod` rows. There is no under-broad hole at this commit.

THE DEFECT IS THE MAINTENANCE PROPERTY, NOT THE CURRENT CONTENTS. The list is hand-maintained and nothing holds it against the emitters. A future backend or emitter change that introduces a new exported package-level fixed declaration WITHOUT adding a `reservedIdentifiers` row leaves the gate green, and the collision it was built to refuse silently returns.

WITNESS (independent reviewer on #832, reproduced first-party): appending `type Config = any` to every golden's `db.go` leaves the whole suite green. `Config` is now an emitter-fixed exported package-level name that no reserved row covers, so a schema entity named `Config` would once again emit a package that does not compile — exit 0, broken Go, which is exactly the gqlc-e6mh defect.

This is the fail-open shape this repo keeps getting bitten by: the gate keeps compiling, keeps passing its own tests, and stops covering the thing that was just added. Compare gqlc-x5dq (offset-sidecar gate keyed on the carrier text) and gqlc-eo46 — same family.

FIX (reviewer estimated ~6 lines): derive the obligation instead of listing it. `db.go`/`graph.go`/`querier.go` hold exactly the emitter-fixed declarations, and `conformance_test.go:638` already names a file set (`connectionSurface = map[string]bool{"db.go": true, "graph.go": true}`) — note `querier.go` is NOT in that map today, so the fix must establish its own file set rather than reuse that one. Walk those files' ASTs across the golden targets, collect exported package-level decls and exported `*Queries` methods, and assert set equality against `reservedIdentifiers`. Then adding an emitter-fixed name without a reserved row goes RED naming the missing identifier.

ACCEPTANCE: appending `type Config = any` to the goldens' `db.go` (the witness above) turns a NAMED test red. Mutate it to confirm it is not a fake RED — the tree must still compile when the assertion fires, so the kill must carry a real test name, not a blank one.

PROVENANCE: nit N1, independent Linus review of PR #832, 2026-08-17. Filed rather than folded in, per this repo's preference for a well-filed follow-up over a rushed fold-in.

title: vuln gate: ADR 0026 overclaims the build-tags check, and a leaked discovery probe wedges four gates
description:
Two findings from the independent adversarial review of PR #813, raised after it
had already squash-merged as 7dfcf04e. Fixed in PR #833.

## 1. ADR 0026 claims a coverage the recipe denies

docs/adr/0026:118-119 said `check-golangci-build-tags` holds `.golangci.yml`'s
`run.build-tags` and the tree to each other "in both directions". justfile:172,
from the same change, says it compares in ONE direction "because the other one
cannot report anything".

The recipe is right. An undeclared term in the tree is refused by the derivation
— `classify` returns `classUnknown`, the caller errors naming the file — so it
never survives to reach a comparison in the recipe. Flip the recipe's `comm` and
the remaining direction is empty by construction, which is why it injects a
stale term of its own on every run.

"still holds" was false as well: the recipe was new on that branch.

This is the two-halves defect (bd gqlc-eo46) expressed in prose, in the artefact
someone reads right before deleting `return classUnknown`.

## 2. `goDirs` asserted a universal the same branch falsifies

main.go said a Go module with no directory holding a Go file "is not a thing".
The branch creates exactly that three times per run — the discovery probes are a
go.mod and nothing else.

Measured: plant test/data/{vuln,fence,xtest}probe.LEAKED and

    check-golangci-build-tags  rc=1      check-codegen-external-tests  rc=1
    test-codegen-fence         rc=1      vuln                          rc=1

all four blaming "the walk broken rather than the module empty" — a misdiagnosis
of the repo's own artefact. .gitignore already anticipated the leak.

Fixed in two parts: the refusal stays but states the negative it can support and
names the leaked probe as the first cause with its remedy; and a shared
`[private] sweep-discovery-probes` dependency clears residue before any of the
four recipes calls modscope. Shared and covering all three names because the
recipe that breaks is not the one that leaked — test-codegen-fence depends on
check-codegen-external-tests, so a leftover fenceprobe takes out the dependency
first. A per-recipe, per-name sweep was tried and measured still wedging the
pair.

## Rejected during the fix

Extending the probe traps to INT/TERM/HUP. A trap on INT runs the handler and
RESUMES, so Ctrl-C would delete the live probe and let the recipe continue
asserting things about it. Bash was measured running the EXIT trap on SIGTERM
regardless. Traps stay EXIT; the sweep covers SIGKILL, which no trap can.
notes:
ROUND 2 (2026-08-17). The independent review of PR #833 at 880a825f returned
REVISE with three blockers, all of them defects the FIX introduced rather than
ones it failed to fix. It confirmed the two originals are genuinely closed and
that the headline gqlc-s3lt empty-walk claim is a real RED (four named FAILs,
tree still compiles, so not a fake RED).

1. The sweep recipe was inserted between check-golangci-build-tags and its
   45-line doc block, so `just --dump` showed that recipe's doc as None and the
   build-tags prose as documentation for a three-line rm -rf. Moved below, blank
   lines restored; verified by diffing the whole recipe->doc map against master.

2. The sweep glob was a FOURTH hand-maintained copy of the probe names, held to
   nothing. Renaming the fenceprobe mktemp literal left `just test-codegen-fence`
   green with the sweep no longer covering it — this bead's own defect class
   (gqlc-oxne), and refused by the standing rule in the comment block the sweep
   had been parked under. Names now come from one variable block; .gitignore,
   which cannot read them, is held by a `git check-ignore` witness inside the
   sweep that reddens on a rename. The lookup counts its own calls (gqlc-eo46:
   a working guard invoked zero times passes as quietly as a broken one).
   Seven mutation rows KILLED, each naming the right cause.

3. The ADR paragraph added to fix the "both directions" contradiction introduced
   a universal of its own: "a term the key does not declare is refused by the
   derivation". False — classify checks four vocabularies in order and the key
   decides only the classCustom arm. Witnessed on a scratch root: hurd, linux,
   go1.24 and unix all exit 0 undeclared; only zzmystery is refused.

Fixed in 2f75d284 (ADR) and d17b81c5 (justfile + main.go comment nits).

Reported honestly, not fixed: two mutation rows SURVIVE — deleting the
invocation counter itself (a second-order guard; guarding it starts a regress)
and silencing the sweep's firing-case echo (observability, not a gate).

title: vuln/modscope: 'A Go module with no such directory is not a thing' is falsified by its own harness
description:
MERGED WITH THIS DEFECT KNOWN. PR #813 (7dfcf04e) landed on master while this was an open Linus blocker — auto-merge fired on green CI ahead of the review verdict. Filing so it is not lost.

THE UNIVERSAL, both on origin/master:
  internal/tools/modscope/main.go:284 — '// is not a thing, and the postcondition this walk feeds — every directory'
  internal/tools/modscope/main.go:324 — '"file. A Go module with no such directory is not a thing, so this is the walk "+'

WHY IT IS FALSE: the branch that wrote it creates exactly that shape THREE TIMES PER RUN. Its own probe harness does mktemp -d plus a lone go.mod, producing a Go module whose directory holds no Go file. The code asserts the shape cannot exist while the test suite manufactures it on every invocation. This is the repo's recurring 'a branch breaks its own rule' pattern, and the standing rule is that a cannot/never/every in prose which the branch's own rows falsify is a blocker: state the negative and enumerate the limits instead.

SECOND, OPERATIONAL DEFECT IN THE SAME AREA: a probe module that leaks — left behind by a killed or interrupted run — wedges 'just lint' across FOUR gates, because the stray go.mod is discovered as a module. That is a self-inflicted outage with no cleanup guarantee. The probe modules need to be created somewhere the walk does not reach, or removed under a defer/trap that survives a kill.

WITNESS: adversarial review of PR #813, blocker 2. Re-verified first-party against origin/master after the merge with:
  git grep -n 'is not a thing' origin/master -- internal/tools/modscope/

FIX: replace the universal at :284 and :324 with the measured negative and its limits, and make the probe modules unable to leak into the walk. Note the :324 text is an ERROR MESSAGE a user can see, not just a comment — so this is user-facing prose asserting something the tool's own tests contradict.
notes:
WORKTREE /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc-c7o7, branch fix/modscope-empty-module-universal, HEAD ff31a0e5 (round-4 review fixes were made in a separate detached worktree /tmp/fix920r4 and pushed to the same branch; the gqlc-c7o7 checkout is behind origin until it pulls).

PREMISE STALE: the universal at main.go:284 and :324 was already replaced on
master by PR #833 (aa52da4f), which landed after this bead was filed. Verified
first-party at dc8d10fa: git grep 'is not a thing' -- internal/tools/modscope/
returns nothing. Duplicate of the closed gqlc-4xto (GH #834).

RESIDUE FOUND AND FIXED HERE: the four sweep-discovery-probes dependency edges
were hand-maintained and held to nothing. Measured: dropping the edge from
check-golangci-build-tags left the recipe green and silent on a clean tree, and
rc=1 with modscope's empty-walk refusal once a probe was planted.
internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go now derives the edges off the justfile.

LIMIT FILED: gqlc-wkio — the caller carrier is the package path, so an
invocation that never spells it is unswept. Witnessed: rewriting one site as
./intern"al"/tools/modscope and dropping that recipe's edge leaves the test green.

LIMIT FILED: gqlc-6n9y (round 4) -- the caller carrier is also the recipe
header, and justHeader takes the first colon on the line, so a parameter default
spelling := is read as an assignment and the recipe is not read at all.
Witnessed: vuln x="a:=b": leaves just --dump at rc=0 with vuln intact and the
live test passing; the same edge dropped with a readable header fails rc=1.
Pinned open by the want:nil row in TestParseJustfileReadsWhatJustReads.

Fixed by PR #920, merged to master as bfe958e5 (GH #830 closed). Four rounds of adversarial review.

WHAT LANDED: the universal at internal/tools/modscope/main.go:284 and :324 is replaced by the measured negative plus its limits, and internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go now holds every justfile recipe that runs modscope to sweeping its probes first — the operational half of the bead (probe modules leaking into the walk and wedging 'just lint' across four gates).

REVIEW EVIDENCE (round 4, independently measured by the reviewer, not taken from the author):
- G14 load-bearing: overlay mutation adding a quote-refusal to justHeader produces EXACTLY TWO failures, and with G14's row deleted the live test still FAILs alone. justfile:622 is 'lint: ensure-golangci lint-hooks check-golangci-build-tags' at this head.
- G15 load-bearing: quote-aware colon mutation gives exactly one failure; with its row deleted the package is ok — SURVIVES.
- No replacement universal: 'uniquely|sole|alone|the only' screened across the whole tree, all four commit bodies and the PR body.

title: vuln: ADR 0026 says the register is compared 'in both directions', justfile:172 says ONE
description:
MERGED WITH THIS DEFECT KNOWN. PR #813 (7dfcf04e) landed on master while this was an open Linus blocker — auto-merge fired on green CI ahead of the review verdict. Filing so it is not lost.

THE CONTRADICTION, both on origin/master, shipped in the same commit:
  docs/adr/0026-govulncheck-cannot-see-in-package-tests.md:119 — 'other in both directions.'
  justfile:172 — '# This recipe therefore compares in ONE direction, because the other one cannot'

One of these is false and they ship together. ADR 0026:83 and :196 and :259 also say 'in both directions', so the ADR is self-consistent and the justfile is the odd one out — which makes it likely the ADR is the stale side, but that must be MEASURED, not assumed.

SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME PASSAGE: ADR 0026:118-119 uses the word 'still', which presupposes a prior state the recipe was already doing this in. The recipe is NEW on that branch. There is no earlier state for it to still be doing anything in, so 'still' is false independently of the direction question.

WITNESS: adversarial review of PR #813, blocker 1. Re-verified first-party against origin/master after the merge with:
  git grep -n 'both directions' origin/master -- docs/adr/0026-govulncheck-cannot-see-in-package-tests.md
  git grep -n 'ONE direction' origin/master -- justfile

FIX: establish by experiment which direction the recipe actually compares — delete a package from the register and confirm the gate fails, then add one and confirm it fails — then make the ADR and the justfile agree with what was measured. Drop 'still'.

title: vuln: every selftest CALL in the vuln recipe is deletable with the gate green
description:
The same two-halves defect gqlc-eo46 documents for `refuse_stale`, measured in
the `vuln` recipe. It is not one instance — it is every `selftest_*` invocation
in that recipe, and it predates the branch that added the newest one.

## Reproduction (lead, first-party, at 620cea66 / PR #813)

Each row deletes ONE line from the justfile and runs `just vuln`:

    delete the `selftest_platformtag` call      rc=0   SURVIVED
    delete the `selftest_tagblind` call         rc=0   SURVIVED

The BODY of each selftest is well witnessed — mutate the assertion inside
`selftest_platformtag` (`*",windows,"*` -> `*",zzneverwindows,"*`) and the gate
goes rc=1 immediately; same for `selftest_tagblind`'s derived-tag assertion. So
both halves of gqlc-eo46's pattern are present here too: the guard works, and
nothing proves it runs.

`selftest_tagblind` predates `fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence`, so this is a
standing class the branch extends by one instance rather than one it introduces.
That is why it is filed rather than fixed there.

## Why it does not close in-script

Same regress gqlc-eo46 names: any counter or assertion wrapped around the call
site is itself a line someone can delete, and the recursion does not terminate
inside the script. The close is the same out-of-band move eo46 proposes — run
the recipe against a fixture tree in which the selftest's precondition is
violated, and assert rc=1 with the term named.

Doing it once for the whole family is probably cheaper than doing it per
selftest: a single harness that, for each `selftest_*` function, deletes its
call site, runs the recipe, and requires rc!=0.

## Scope note

Not a defect in what the gates measure — every selftest passes on the real tree
today, and the properties they assert are independently checked elsewhere in the
recipe. The defect is that their continued presence is unenforced.

title: ci: justfile recipe bodies are outside shellcheck coverage, and lint-hooks:130 is a real ERROR
description:
`just lint` runs shellcheck over the `.githooks` tree only. The justfile's own
recipe bodies — which are `#!/usr/bin/env bash` scripts with `set -euo pipefail`,
several of them 60+ lines and carrying the repo's gate logic — are outside that
coverage entirely.

This is not hypothetical. Two findings this week were plain shell bugs that
shellcheck-class analysis is built to catch:

- `fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence` shipped a collision guard that matched
  newline-delimited `sort -u` scalars with the space-delimited
  `case " ${a} ${b} " in *" ${x} "*)` idiom. It could not fire, and it shipped
  in the commit whose job was to close the finding that the clause it guards had
  no coverage. Found by review, three rounds in.
- The same file uses that idiom correctly seven other times, on genuine arrays
  where `${arr[*]}` joins on a space. Scalar-vs-array is exactly the distinction
  a linter tracks and a reader does not.

Measured while reviewing that branch: shellcheck over the five recipe bodies the
branch owns reports 0 error and 0 warning at enforced severity, so enrolling
them is not a wall of pre-existing noise.

One real pre-existing hit does exist, on master:

    justfile:130  (inside `lint-hooks`)  — shellcheck ERROR

That one needs fixing or an explicit inline disable before the gate can be
turned on, and it is the argument for turning it on rather than against.

## Shape of the work

Extract each recipe body (just already knows them; `just --dump` or a small
reader like the one in `internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go` can enumerate
them), write each to a temp file with its shebang, and run shellcheck at the
same severity `lint-hooks` uses. Gate must FAIL on a finding, not warn — a
detector that exits 0 is not a gate.
notes:
## Measurement from the fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence review (PR #813, 2026-08-17)

That branch adds ~795 lines to the justfile. Shellcheck was pointed at the four
shebang recipe bodies it owns, by hand, with just interpolation ({{x}}) replaced
by a placeholder first:

    check-golangci-build-tags     --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings
    test-codegen-fence            --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings
    check-codegen-external-tests  --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings
    vuln                          --severity=warning  rc=0, 0 findings

So turning this bead's gate on would NOT have blocked that branch. At info
severity there are three findings, all judged intentional:

  - SC2015 x2, both the same helper `lines() { [ -n "${1}" ] && printf ... || true; }`
    where the `|| true` is the point (the function must always succeed).
  - SC2086 x1, `go list -deps ... ./... ${xtest}` — deliberate word-splitting of
    a newline-separated list into separate arguments.

This bead's headline finding is independently reproduced: extracting `lint-hooks`
and running shellcheck over it gives SC1073/SC1124/SC1072/SC1085 at ERROR, all
from the `# shellcheck only supports shell; ...` comment sitting BETWEEN case
items (justfile:130 on master). Shellcheck parses any comment beginning
`# shellcheck` as a directive, and directives are only valid before a complete
command. The fix is to reword the comment so it does not start with the word
`shellcheck`, which is a one-line change that should land with the gate.

No prose on that branch claims the recipes are linted; verified by grep over its
diff of justfile, docs/ and .github/.

title: ci: check-golangci-build-tags proves refuse_stale works and never proves it is called
description:
`check-golangci-build-tags` carries a 60-line witness proving `refuse_stale`'s
BODY refuses a stale entry, and nothing at all proving that body is APPLIED to
the real sets. The application is one line:

    justfile:302   refuse_stale "${derived}" "${configured}" || exit 1

Delete it and a genuinely stale entry passes in silence.

## Reproduction (lead, first-party, at 620cea66)

Inject a real stale entry — `- zzstalereal` in `.golangci.yml` run.build-tags,
constraining no file in the tree — then run `just check-golangci-build-tags`:

    A  pristine justfile + stale entry      rc=1  names zzstalereal, 5 stderr lines
    B  justfile:302 deleted + same entry    rc=0  no stderr
    C  pristine justfile + clean config     rc=0  no stderr

B is byte-identical in observable behaviour to C. The gate reports "clean" on a
tree it never checked.

## Why the branch's own idiom does NOT close it

620cea66 introduced a positive control for exactly this class: look up every
term the two sets contain and refuse if the lookup cannot find them. That works
for `uses_term` because the control can positively exercise the predicate. It
does not transfer here — any counter or assertion added around line 302 is
itself deletable, and the regress does not terminate inside the script. The
reviewer's "closable with `control`'s own idiom" is optimistic; measured, it is
not.

The close is out-of-band: a test that runs the recipe against a fixture tree
with a known-stale tag injected and asserts rc=1 and that the term is named.
That is the same move `feat/age-dialect-gap-admission` made for its justfile
recipes (a Go test that parses the artefact and asserts properties of it), so
there is a worked precedent in-tree.

## Related residue on the same branch

- Deleting the whole `control` loop survives (`control=0` -> `1`). Same
  last-line-of-the-script shape, disclosed by the implementer as NB-2.
- Both are "the outermost assertion is unguarded", NOT the vacuous-pass class
  that gqlc-s3lt covered — that one is closed and stays closed.
notes:
PR #833 round 3 widens the surface this bead describes, and does not close it.

sweep-discovery-probes now carries nine refusals (empty aggregate, empty probe
value, no *_probe declared, odd-shaped site, no site at all, site variable off
the *_probe convention, declared-vs-swept in both directions, per-name coverage
asking BOTH `git check-ignore -q` and `-v` with the source pinned to .gitignore,
lookup-membership, uncovered-control, post-sweep verify). Every one has this
bead's shape: the refusal is deletable and nothing inside the script observes
that it is gone.

Measured at a5f07491 (PR head), mutation harness /tmp/r3-mut-833.py, 42 rows,
28 KILLED / 14 SURVIVED, per-row preconditions 'just --summary rc=0' AND the
rendered recipe body passing 'bash -n', md5 restore verified on justfile and
.gitignore per row. The guard-isolation rows -- each refusal deleted ON ITS OWN
with its own defect still applied, so only the deleted guard could have spoken:

  membership refusal deleted, no other defect       rc=0 SURVIVED
  zzuncoveredprobe control mkdir deleted, no defect rc=0 SURVIVED
  final verify loop deleted whole, no defect        rc=0 SURVIVED

    to .git/info/exclude                            rc=0 SURVIVED
  lookup `-q` hide check deleted + negated

  site-shape refusal deleted + dotless site         rc=0 SURVIVED
  literal-site refusal deleted + literal site       rc=0 SURVIVED
  declared-vs-swept refusal deleted + its defect    rc=0 SURVIVED
  per-name coverage refusal deleted + its drift     rc=0 SURVIVED

Some refusals overlap, so deleting one is sometimes caught by another (deleting
the empty-aggregate refusal still trips the empty-value one; deleting the
swept-not-declared accumulation still trips the coverage refusal unless
.gitignore is also given a rule for the extra name). Nothing in the recipe makes
that so -- it is incidental, and the rows above are the ones where it does not
hold.

The recipe states this limit in the tree beside the lookup-membership refusal
rather than only in the PR body. The close is unchanged and still out-of-band: a

title: resolver: an inline endpoint's type is read as a satisfying set, emitting NOT NULL on a nullable column (master too)
description:
MATCH (:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(c) RETURN c.smallOnly emits {"type":"STRING","nullable":false} on BOTH origin/master (f4fb1a19) and branch feat/resolver-narrow-plural-endpoints. The row may match a Company that is not Company&Large, so smallOnly can be absent -- a NOT NULL column that is null.

Root cause is shared with the branch's F1/F2 findings: endpointLabels' InlineEndpoint arm (internal/resolver/resolve.go, ~:617-640) returns the exact SPELLED key rather than the set of declared types satisfying it, so callers reading it as a complete statement about the pattern's ends under-approximate.

Found by adversarial review of that branch on 2026-08-16 (verdict /tmp/lead/verdict-0tft2.md, NB2). Recorded as PRE-EXISTING and therefore out of scope for that branch, which only had to stop ANSWERING where master refused.

The reviewer's assessment: fixing this is probably the same change that fixes F2 (gating candidateTypes at resolve.go:975, or restructuring so the superset/subset distinction is carried in the type rather than a comment convention). So check whether F2's fix already closed this before doing separate work -- it may be closeable for free, or already closed.

Related: gqlc-pv0u, gqlc-qlr2 (filed from round 1 of the same review).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #857, squash-merged to master as 26971c2ec3922d3b3210b26bbdbb7e7aa107d159 on 2026-08-17. endpointLabels' InlineEndpoint arm now returns satisfyingNodeTypes rather than the spelled label key, so the inline and var spellings of a pattern agree. title: codegen spec fence: the census has a per-document floor of one graded site
description:
The spec fence's census reconciles per (document, method-name), so a document keeps its census entry as long as ONE graded site survives. A one-part invisible edit therefore passes green.

Reproduction (found by adversarial review of branch docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift, 2026-08-16): move docs/specs/codegen-stage-c4.md:404 -- the WriteQuerier member -- out of the anchor. The suite stays GREEN, exit 0. Deleting the whole document's entry is caught; losing all but one site is not. The binding half has the same floor: c1.md:1339 map[string]any{"id": arg} -> mapOf{...} is GREEN.

Confirmed by the reviewer to fall OUTSIDE all five existing deferrals (gqlc-vu7z, gqlc-jfwo, gqlc-173n and the two others cited in that review).

Why it was documented rather than closed on that branch -- three closures were tried and each measured to lose:
- per-(document, method-name) census: does NOT close it. C4 grades RemovePerson at :363, :404 and :840, so the NAME survives :404 leaving.
- per-site COUNT: closes it, but is exactly the shape specfence_test.go:82-85 argues against (a bare '9 != 10' with no name in the failure).
- per-site VERBATIM census: closes it, but makes the test file a copy of the documents -- red on every honest edit to an example, which is how a census gets bulk-updated without being read.

So closing this likely needs a different mechanism, not a wider census. Note the related growth-direction gap gqlc-jfwo needs candidate roots from an independent source (the repo's own markdown); the same independent-source idea may close both.

Filed at lead level because the implementing agent was instructed not to write .beads while sibling agents were live.

title: resolver: closeEdge reads an inline endpoint's spelled key, not its satisfying set
description:
endpointLabels' InlineEndpoint arm (internal/resolver/resolve.go) returns the exact key the query spells, not the set of declared node types satisfying those labels. edgeCandidates is therefore a SUBSET of the keys a matching row can carry, and closeEdge commits an edge type on that subset.

Reproduction (test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql: Person / Person&Employee, Company / Company&Large, WORKS_AT declared Person->Company and Person&Employee->Company&Large):

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(:Company) RETURN r
    -> ResolvedEdge{Person -[WORKS_AT]-> Company}

Both declarations match the pattern, so r is genuinely plural and the answer names one of two. The var spelling MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN r closes over the full cross-product and is refused, so the two spellings of one pattern disagree.

This predates gqlc-0tft and is unchanged by it: identical on f4fb1a19 and on the branch. gqlc-0tft's NarrowPluralEndpoints stops reading the under-approximation via endpointKeysCoverEveryMatch, which contains the node-type half; this bead is the edge-type half that remains.

Fix is to make the InlineEndpoint arm return satisfyingNodeTypes(ls, sch). That widens closeEdge's candidate sets, so queries that resolve today become ambiguous refusals -- the ADR 0006 forbidden direction -- and it needs its own decision about whether a spelled label set should key exactly or satisfy. Not a drive-by.

The stale citation in endpointLabels' doc comment (it pointed at the CLOSED gqlc-h9n.23, which is about multi-label edge types) is repointed here.
