title: spike: AGE temporal + parameter mechanics against a live container
description:
Research-only spike against a live apache/age container (scratch code in /tmp or the nested test module on a throwaway branch — nothing ships). Three questions, each answered with reproducible evidence (exact SQL/cypher run + observed output), recorded in this bead via bd update --notes/--design:

1. TEMPORAL REALITY. src/include/utils/agtype.h shows agtype has no temporal value types (enum: NULL/STRING/NUMERIC/INTEGER/FLOAT/BOOL/VERTEX/EDGE/PATH/ARRAY/OBJECT — verified 2026-07-31). User is skeptical; verify empirically: what happens storing timestamp-ish values, does any casting or function surface exist (Postgres-type interop at the SQL boundary, any toTimestamp-style functions), and validate the fallback encoding table — timestamp=epoch-micros integer, date=ISO string, duration=ISO-8601 string, zoned=offset-preserving string — including ORDERING: WHERE n.ts > param must compare correctly under each encoding.
2. PARAMETER MECHANICS. AGE cypher() third-argument params require the prepared-statement dance; the upstream Go driver instead does fmt.Sprintf interpolation (disqualifying, injection vector). Validate the mechanism generated pgx code will use: cypher() third arg via pgx extended-protocol prepared statements vs the age_prepare_cypher two-step. Pick one; string interpolation of user args is banned unconditionally.
3. AGTYPE TEXT CORPUS. Capture exact result-text forms for scalars, vertex, edge, path, arrays, maps, nulls (including the ::vertex-style suffixes) to drive decode-helper TDD in the emission beads.

Output: a confirmed-or-amended encoding table + the chosen param mechanism + the text corpus. If AGE turns out to handle temporals natively, the encoding table shrinks accordingly and the epic design note gets amended. No production code in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: All three questions answered with reproducible commands + captured output in the bead; encoding table confirmed or amended per finding; one param mechanism selected with evidence it binds server-side; corpus covers every agtype shape the emission beads decode.
notes:
# SPIKE RESULTS (gqlc-35yu.5) — empirical, live container, 2026-07-31

## Environment (reproducible)

    Image:  apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb
            (= docker.io/apache/age:latest as of 2026-07-31)
    Server: PostgreSQL 18.1 (Debian 18.1-1.pgdg13+2)
    AGE:    extversion 1.7.0
    Client: github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.10.0, go1.26.5

    docker run -d --name age-spike -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=spike -e POSTGRES_USER=postgres \
      -e POSTGRES_DB=spikedb -p 5455:5432 \
      apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb

Every psql run below is a single session prefixed by:
    LOAD 'age';
    SET search_path = ag_catalog, "$user", public;

=====================================================================
# *** BLOCKER: contradicts a LOCKED epic decision — NOT re-decided ***
=====================================================================

Epic gqlc-35yu locked design states:

  "all emitted SQL fully qualifies ag_catalog.cypher / ag_catalog.agtype
   so search_path is never a session dependency."

EMPIRICALLY FALSE. Full qualification is necessary but NOT sufficient.
AGE's Cypher->SQL transform emits bare OPERATOR references (=, >, +, @>).
PostgreSQL resolves operators through search_path, and AGE does not emit
the OPERATOR(ag_catalog.=) form. So ag_catalog must be on the session
search_path for essentially every non-trivial query.

Evidence — search_path deliberately WITHOUT ag_catalog, every identifier
fully qualified:

    SET search_path = "$user", public;
    SHOW search_path;   -->  "$user", public

    -- (1) literal RETURN
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ RETURN 1 $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
     v
    ---
     1                                                     <-- OK

    -- (2) MATCH + property projection
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P) RETURN n.name $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
     "alice"
     "bob"                                                 <-- OK

    -- (3) ORDER BY
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P) RETURN n.name ORDER BY n.name $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
     "alice"
     "bob"                                                 <-- OK

    -- (4) WHERE with '='
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P) WHERE n.name = 'alice' RETURN n.age $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  cannot cast agtype string to type boolean      <-- FAIL

    -- (5) WHERE with '>'
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P) WHERE n.age > 35 RETURN n.name $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  cannot cast agtype integer to type boolean     <-- FAIL

    -- (6) inline property-map match (uses the @> operator)
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P {name:'alice'}) RETURN n.age $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  operator does not exist: ag_catalog.agtype @> ag_catalog.agtype   <-- FAIL

    -- (7) arithmetic
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike', $$ RETURN 1 + 1 $$) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  operator does not exist: ag_catalog.agtype + ag_catalog.agtype    <-- FAIL

Adding ag_catalog back fixes all four, same statements verbatim:

    SET search_path = ag_catalog, "$user", public;
    ... WHERE n.name = 'alice' ...   -->  30
    ... WHERE n.age > 35 ...         -->  "bob"
    ... RETURN 1 + 1 ...             -->  2

Consequence (for the owner to decide — NOT decided here): SessionInit /
pgxpool AfterConnect must do BOTH `LOAD 'age'` AND
`SET search_path = ag_catalog, ...`. search_path becomes genuine per-session
state the generated code depends on — relevant to pgbouncer transaction
pooling / DISCARD ALL, and to any user who re-SETs it. Full qualification of
cypher()/agtype is still worth keeping, but it does not remove the dependency.

All working results elsewhere in this note were obtained with ag_catalog on
the search_path.
=====================================================================
# Q1. TEMPORAL REALITY — prior CONFIRMED; encoding table AMENDED (2 of 4 fail)
=====================================================================

## 1a. No temporal types, no temporal casts, no temporal functions

Complete cast catalogue to/from agtype in AGE 1.7.0:

    SELECT castsource::regtype AS src, casttarget::regtype AS tgt, castcontext AS ctx
    FROM pg_cast WHERE castsource='ag_catalog.agtype'::regtype
                    OR casttarget='ag_catalog.agtype'::regtype ORDER BY 1,2;

           src          |        tgt         | ctx
    --------------------+--------------------+-----
     boolean            | ag_catalog.agtype  | e
     bigint             | ag_catalog.agtype  | e
     integer            | ag_catalog.agtype  | e
     double precision   | ag_catalog.agtype  | e
     ag_catalog.graphid | ag_catalog.agtype  | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | boolean            | i
     ag_catalog.agtype  | bigint             | a
     ag_catalog.agtype  | smallint           | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | integer            | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | text               | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | json               | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | double precision   | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | integer[]          | e
     ag_catalog.agtype  | ag_catalog.graphid | i
     ag_catalog.agtype[]| ag_catalog.agtype  | e
    (15 rows)

  -> NO timestamp / timestamptz / date / time / interval in either direction.
     Also: there is no text -> agtype cast (only agtype -> text).

Direct attempts:

    SELECT now()::timestamptz::agtype;
    ERROR:  cannot cast type timestamp with time zone to agtype

    SELECT '"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"'::agtype::timestamptz;
    ERROR:  cannot cast type agtype to timestamp with time zone

    SELECT '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'::agtype;          -- bare, unquoted
    ERROR:  invalid input syntax for type agtype
    DETAIL:  Token "-01" is invalid.

Cypher-level function surface — the only temporal-ish name that exists:

    SELECT * FROM cypher('spike', $$ RETURN timestamp() $$) AS (v agtype);
     1785541437366                    <-- plain INTEGER agtype, epoch MILLIS

    RETURN datetime()                 --> ERROR: function datetime does not exist
    RETURN date()                     --> ERROR: function date does not exist
    RETURN localdatetime()            --> ERROR: function localdatetime does not exist
    RETURN duration({days:1})         --> ERROR: function duration does not exist
    RETURN toTimestamp('2024-01-01')  --> ERROR: function toTimestamp does not exist
    RETURN datetime('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z') --> ERROR: function datetime does not exist

    SELECT proname FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace
    WHERE n.nspname='ag_catalog'
      AND proname ~* 'time|date|dur|epoch|local|zone|instant';
     age_timestamp        <-- the ONLY hit out of 348 ag_catalog functions

    \df ag_catalog.age_timestamp
     ag_catalog | age_timestamp | ag_catalog.agtype | (no args) | func

VERDICT: the prior HOLDS. AGE 1.7.0 has no native temporal value type, no
temporal casts, no temporal constructors. AGE's own "timestamp" notion is an
integer epoch-millis. The encoding table is required; it does not shrink.

## 1b. One usable SQL-boundary bridge (not a temporal type)

`agtype -> text` UNWRAPS string scalars, so Postgres-type interop is one hop:

    SELECT ('"hello"'::agtype)::text AS as_text, length(('"hello"'::agtype)::text) AS len;
     as_text | len
    ---------+-----
     hello   |   5                       <-- quotes stripped

    SELECT ('"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"'::agtype)::text::timestamptz;
          timestamptz
    ------------------------
     2024-01-01 00:00:00+00               <-- works, via text

    SELECT ('"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"'::agtype)::json;
     "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"

CAVEAT — ::text does NOT work on entities:

    SELECT (v)::text FROM cypher('corpus', $$ MATCH (n:Person {name:'Carol'}) RETURN n $$) AS (v agtype);
    ERROR:  agtype_value_to_text: unsupported argument agtype 6

So ::text is a scalar/array/map-only bridge; decode helpers cannot lean on it
for vertex/edge/path.

## 1c. agtype string comparison follows the DATABASE COLLATION, not byte order

This governs whether any string encoding sorts correctly.

    SELECT datcollate, datlocprovider FROM pg_database WHERE datname=current_database();
     en_US.UTF-8 | c

    RETURN 'Z' < 'a'                          -->  false   (agtype)
    SELECT 'Z' < 'a';                         -->  f       (SQL, DB collation)
    SELECT 'Z' COLLATE "C" < 'a' COLLATE "C"; -->  t       (byte order disagrees)

  -> agtype string ordering == DB collation ordering. For the digits+hyphen
     alphabet used by ISO dates all collations agree, so the date encoding is
     safe; but ANY string encoding is in principle collation-sensitive. That is
     a portability caveat for a fixed encoding table.

# Q2. PARAMETER MECHANICS — SELECTED: cypher() 3rd arg via pgx extended protocol
=====================================================================

## 2a. AGE hard-rejects every non-parameter third argument

    SELECT * FROM cypher('spike', $$ ... $name ... $$, $$ {"name":"alice"} $$) AS (v agtype);
    ERROR:  third argument of cypher function must be a parameter at character 85

    SELECT * FROM cypher('spike', $$ ... $$, ('{"name":"alice"}')::agtype) AS (v agtype);
    ERROR:  third argument of cypher function must be a parameter at character 85

    SELECT * FROM cypher('spike', $$ ... $$, (SELECT '{"name":"alice"}'::agtype)) AS (v agtype);
    ERROR:  third argument of cypher function must be a parameter at character 84

  -> Only a raw $n placeholder is accepted. This is a STRUCTURAL guarantee:
     AGE physically cannot be handed an interpolated parameter map.

## 2b. pgx QueryExecMode matrix

Statement used verbatim for all five modes:

    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike',
      $$ MATCH (n:P) WHERE n.name = $name RETURN n.age $$, $1) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)
    arg: `{"name": "alice"}` (Go string)

    CacheStatement (pgx default) OK  -> "30"
    CacheDescribe                OK  -> "30"
    DescribeExec                 OK  -> "30"
    Exec                         OK  -> "30"
    SimpleProtocol               ERR: ERROR: third argument of cypher function
                                      must be a parameter (SQLSTATE 22023)

SimpleProtocol is the ONLY pgx mode that interpolates client-side, and it is the
ONLY one AGE rejects. The server log shows exactly why — pgx had already spliced
the value into the statement text:

    LOG:  statement: SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('spike',
          $$ MATCH (n:P) WHERE n.name = $name RETURN n.age $$,  '{"name": "alice"}' )
          AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)
    ERROR: third argument of cypher function must be a parameter

  => The unsafe path FAILS CLOSED. Generated code cannot accidentally ship
     interpolation through pgx without an immediate hard error.

## 2c. Alternative REJECTED on evidence: age_prepare_cypher

    \df ag_catalog.age_prepare_cypher
     ag_catalog | age_prepare_cypher | boolean | cstring, cstring | func
       (args are (graph_name, query_string))

It does work:

    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.age_prepare_cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P) WHERE n.name = $name RETURN n.age $$);
     t
    PREPARE pc(ag_catalog.agtype) AS SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher(NULL, NULL, $1) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype);
    EXECUTE pc('{"name":"alice"}');   --> 30
    EXECUTE pc('{"name":"bob"}');     --> 41

But it couples through per-session global state consumed at PLAN time:

    -- prepare a DIFFERENT cypher query, then re-run the OLD prepared stmt:
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.age_prepare_cypher('spike', $$ MATCH (n:P) RETURN n.name $$);
    EXECUTE pc('{"name":"alice"}');   --> 30      (still the OLD query text)

The cypher text is latched into the plan when the PREPARE is parsed. The binding
between age_prepare_cypher and the following PREPARE is invisible,
connection-global, and order-dependent. Under pgx statement caching, Parse
happens once at an unpredictable moment (cache miss, fresh pooled conn, cache
eviction), so the required "prime the session global, THEN Parse" ordering
cannot be guaranteed by generated code. And without a preceding prepare:

    ERROR:  session info requires cypher(NULL, NULL) to be passed

## 2d. *** SELECTED: direct cypher('<graph>', $$...$$, $1) ***

Single self-contained statement, no session coupling beyond LOAD + search_path,
works in all four extended-protocol pgx modes, and the interpolating mode is
rejected by the server.

# Q3. AGTYPE TEXT CORPUS
=====================================================================

Captured with `psql -A -t` (raw bytes) and cross-checked byte-for-byte against
what pgx v5 receives (Go %q of the scanned []byte) — IDENTICAL (see C11).

Corpus graph:

    SELECT create_graph('corpus');
    SELECT * FROM cypher('corpus', $$
      CREATE (a:Person {name:'Alice', age:30, score:9.5, active:true, nick:null})
            -[r:KNOWS {since:2019, weight:0.5}]->
             (b:Person {name:'Bob', age:41, tags:['x','y'], meta:{k:'v', n:[1,2]}})
      CREATE (b)-[:KNOWS {since:2021}]->(c:Person {name:'Carol'})
    $$) AS (v agtype);

## C1. SCALARS

    RETURN null                     -> (SQL NULL — see C8, NOT the text "null")
    RETURN true                     -> true
    RETURN false                    -> false
    RETURN 42                       -> 42
    RETURN -42                      -> -42
    RETURN 9223372036854775807      -> 9223372036854775807
    RETURN -9223372036854775808     -> -9223372036854775808
    RETURN 1.5                      -> 1.5
    RETURN -0.0                     -> -0.0
    RETURN 1.0                      -> 1.0
    RETURN 1e100                    -> 1e+100
    RETURN 0.1 + 0.2                -> 0.30000000000000004      (17 sig digits)
    RETURN toFloat(1)/3             -> 0.3333333333333333
    RETURN toFloat('1.5')           -> 1.5

  NUMERIC is a distinct type with a SUFFIX form (distinct from FLOAT):
    SELECT '1.5::numeric'::agtype;  -> 1.5::numeric

  NON-JSON literals that are valid agtype (decoder MUST handle these):
    SELECT 'NaN'::agtype;           -> NaN
    SELECT 'Infinity'::agtype;      -> Infinity
    SELECT '-Infinity'::agtype;     -> -Infinity
    SELECT '{"n": NaN}'::agtype;    -> {"n": NaN}
  (`RETURN 1.0/0.0` raises `ERROR: division by zero`, so these arrive via stored
   data / agtype_in, not via Cypher arithmetic.)

  STRINGS — JSON-escaped, double-quoted:
    RETURN 'plain'                  -> "plain"
    RETURN 'has "quote"'            -> "has \"quote\""
    RETURN 'back\\slash'            -> "back\\slash"
    RETURN 'tab\there'              -> "tab\there"
    RETURN 'new\nline'              -> "new\nline"
    RETURN 'unicode: e' cafe' ...'  -> raw UTF-8 passed through, NOT \u-escaped
    RETURN ''                       -> ""

## C2. ARRAYS   (separator is ", " — comma AND space)

    RETURN []                       -> []
    RETURN [1,2,3]                  -> [1, 2, 3]
    RETURN ['a','b']                -> ["a", "b"]
    RETURN [1,'a',true,null,1.5]    -> [1, "a", true, null, 1.5]
    RETURN [[1,2],[3]]              -> [[1, 2], [3]]
    RETURN [{a:1},{b:[2]}]          -> [{"a": 1}, {"b": [2]}]
    SELECT '[1.5::numeric, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity]'::agtype;
                                    -> [1.5::numeric, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity]

  NOTE: `null` INSIDE a container is the literal text `null` (contrast C8).

## C3. MAPS   (`"key": value`, separator ", ")

    RETURN {}                       -> {}
    RETURN {a:1}                    -> {"a": 1}
    RETURN {z:1, a:2, m:3}          -> {"a": 2, "m": 3, "z": 1}
    RETURN {s:'x', n:null, b:false, f:1.5, arr:[1], nested:{k:'v'}}
          -> {"b": false, "f": 1.5, "s": "x", "arr": [1], "nested": {"k": "v"}}
    RETURN {`key with space`: 1, `q"uote`: 2}
          -> {"q\"uote": 2, "key with space": 1}
    SELECT '{"a": 1.5::numeric, "b": NaN}'::agtype;
          -> {"a": 1.5::numeric, "b": NaN}

  *** KEY ORDER IS jsonb-STYLE: by key LENGTH first, then lexicographically. ***
  (b,f,s = len 1; arr = len 3; nested = len 6.) Input order is NOT preserved.
  Decoders must be order-independent; GOLDEN TESTS MUST EXPECT THIS ORDER.
  Note also that `n:null` vanished from that map entirely — see C8(c).

## C4. VERTEX — `{...}::vertex`, keys id, label, properties (length order)

    MATCH (n:Person {name:'Alice'}) RETURN n
    {"id": 844424930131969, "label": "Person", "properties": {"age": 30, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex

    MATCH (n:Person {name:'Bob'}) RETURN n
    {"id": 844424930131970, "label": "Person", "properties": {"age": 41, "meta": {"k": "v", "n": [1, 2]}, "name": "Bob", "tags": ["x", "y"]}}::vertex

    MATCH (n:Person {name:'Carol'}) RETURN n
    {"id": 844424930131971, "label": "Person", "properties": {"name": "Carol"}}::vertex

  id is a graphid: (label_id << 48) | sequence. 844424930131969 = (3<<48)|1.

## C5. EDGE — `{...}::edge`, keys id, label, end_id, start_id, properties

    MATCH ()-[r:KNOWS]->() RETURN r
    {"id": 1125899906842625, "label": "KNOWS", "end_id": 844424930131970, "start_id": 844424930131969, "properties": {"since": 2019, "weight": 0.5}}::edge
    {"id": 1125899906842626, "label": "KNOWS", "end_id": 844424930131971, "start_id": 844424930131970, "properties": {"since": 2021}}::edge

  NOTE: end_id comes BEFORE start_id (length order again: 6 < 8).

## C6. PATH — `[...]::path`, alternating vertex/edge, EACH keeping its own suffix

    MATCH p=(:Person {name:'Alice'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person) RETURN p
    [{"id": 844424930131969, "label": "Person", "properties": {"age": 30, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex, {"id": 1125899906842625, "label": "KNOWS", "end_id": 844424930131970, "start_id": 844424930131969, "properties": {"since": 2019, "weight": 0.5}}::edge, {"id": 844424930131970, "label": "Person", "properties": {"age": 41, "meta": {"k": "v", "n": [1, 2]}, "name": "Bob", "tags": ["x", "y"]}}::vertex]::path

    -- variable-length, 2 hops (`[:KNOWS*1..2]` returns both the 1-hop and this):
    [ ...Alice::vertex, ...KNOWS(2019)::edge, ...Bob::vertex, {"id": 1125899906842626, "label": "KNOWS", "end_id": 844424930131971, "start_id": 844424930131970, "properties": {"since": 2021}}::edge, {"id": 844424930131971, "label": "Person", "properties": {"name": "Carol"}}::vertex]::path

## C7. ENTITIES NESTED IN CONTAINERS — suffixes occur at ARBITRARY DEPTH

    RETURN [n]        -> [{"id": ..., "label": "Person", "properties": {...}}::vertex]
    RETURN {node:n}   -> {"node": {"id": ..., "label": "Person", "properties": {...}}::vertex}
    RETURN collect(n) -> [<...>::vertex, <...>::vertex, <...>::vertex]

  *** A decoder CANNOT just strip a trailing suffix. `::vertex` / `::edge` /
      `::path` / `::numeric` are VALUE-LEVEL type annotations that can appear at
      any nesting depth. ***

## C8. NULL SEMANTICS — three distinct cases

  (a) Top-level Cypher null, a null property, and a MISSING property all become
      SQL NULL — not the text "null":

    MATCH (n:Person {name:'Alice'}) RETURN n.name, n.nick, n.missing, n.age
      name   |    nick    |  missing   | age
    ---------+------------+------------+-----
     "Alice" | <SQL NULL> | <SQL NULL> | 30

    SELECT (v IS NULL) FROM cypher('corpus', $$ ... RETURN n.nick $$) AS (v agtype);
     t                                        <-- genuinely SQL NULL

    From Go: Scan into *string leaves the pointer nil with err=<nil>.

  (b) null INSIDE an array/map is the literal text `null` (see C2/C3).

  (c) *** NULL PROPERTIES ARE DROPPED, NOT STORED ***

    CREATE (n:NullProp {a:1, b:null}) RETURN n
    {"id": 1407374883553281, "label": "NullProp", "properties": {"a": 1}}::vertex
                                                                 ^^^ "b" is GONE

    MATCH (n:NullProp) SET n.a = null RETURN n
    {"id": 1407374883553281, "label": "NullProp", "properties": {}}::vertex
                                                                 ^^ key REMOVED

    Matters for bead .9 (entity columns): a nullable field's key will be ABSENT
    from the properties map — never present-with-null.

## C9. AGGREGATES / MISC

    MATCH (n:Person) RETURN count(*)          -> 3
    MATCH (n:Person) RETURN avg(n.age)        -> 35.5
    MATCH (n:Person) RETURN collect(n.name)   -> ["Alice", "Bob", "Carol"]
    MATCH (n:Person {name:'Alice'}) RETURN id(n), label(n)
                                              -> 844424930131969 | "Person"

    Empty match          -> ZERO ROWS (not a null row)
    Write without RETURN -> ZERO ROWS, but the AS(...) list still needs exactly
                            one agtype column, e.g. `AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)`.

## C10. AGE 1.7.0 LIMITATION worth recording

    SELECT * FROM cypher('corpus', $$ CREATE (x:A:B {n:1}) $$) AS (v agtype);
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near ":"

  Multi-label vertices are NOT supported. Vertex text always carries exactly one
  scalar `"label"`, never a list. Relevant to schema admission (phase Z/A) if
  gqlc's GQL/Cypher schema surface permits multiple labels.

## C11. pgx byte-for-byte cross-check

Scanned as []byte through pgx v5 and printed with Go %q — identical to psql -A:

  vertex      "{\"id\": 844424930131969, \"label\": \"Person\", \"properties\": {\"age\": 30, \"name\": \"Alice\", \"score\": 9.5, \"active\": true}}::vertex"
  edge        "{\"id\": 1125899906842625, \"label\": \"KNOWS\", \"end_id\": 844424930131970, \"start_id\": 844424930131969, \"properties\": {\"since\": 2019, \"weight\": 0.5}}::edge"
  path        "[{...}::vertex, {...}::edge, {...}::vertex]::path"
  array-mixed "[1, \"a\", true, null, 1.5]"
  map-nested  "{\"b\": false, \"f\": 1.5, \"s\": \"x\", \"arr\": [1], \"nested\": {\"k\": \"v\"}}"
  string-esc  "\"has \\\"q\\\" and \\\\ and \\t\""
  float       "0.30000000000000004"
  int64max    "9223372036854775807"

=====================================================================
# SUMMARY FOR DOWNSTREAM BEADS
=====================================================================

.7 (scalar reads):
  - param: ONE Go `string` holding an agtype/JSON object, bound to $1 of
    cypher('<graph>', $$...$$, $1). Never []byte, never map[string]any.
  - agtype arrives as TEXT (format=0); its OID is DB-specific (16461 here) and
    must never be hard-coded. Scan into *string / *[]byte and parse.
  - decoder must handle NaN / Infinity / -Infinity / `X::numeric` (all non-JSON),
    plus SQL NULL vs the literal `null`.

.9 (entity columns):
  - `::vertex` / `::edge` / `::path` are value-level annotations at ANY depth.
  - jsonb key order (length, then lexicographic) — bake into goldens.
  - absent key, not null value, for unset properties.
  - single label only in AGE 1.7.0.

.11 (temporals):
  - timestamp = epoch-micros int64            (CONFIRMED)
  - date      = ISO string, years 1..9999     (CONFIRMED)
  - duration  = total-micros int64            (AMENDED — ISO-8601 string SORTS WRONG)
  - zoned     = <f> int64 + <f>Offset int64   (AMENDED — offset string SORTS WRONG
                                               and mis-compares equal instants)
  - calendar durations (months/years): generate-time error.
  - time-of-day: NOT covered by this spike — still open.

ALL BEADS:
  - the epic's "search_path is never a session dependency" claim is FALSE;
    ag_catalog MUST be on the search_path. Flagged for the owner; not re-decided.

Scratch code (nothing shipped): /tmp/age-spike (SQL probes) and
/tmp/age-spike/gospike + /tmp/age-spike/gospike/corpusrun (pgx programs).
No files under internal/ were touched; worktree gqlc-35yu5-age-spike is clean.

Encoding table amended (duration, zoned -> int64); param mechanism selected (direct cypher() 3rd arg via pgx extended protocol) with server-log proof of server-side binding; agtype corpus captured. Reversed the epic's search_path decision (owner-approved). Outcomes recorded on the epic and on .6/.7/.11.

title: codegen live tests: shared scenario battery + per-backend adapters (v5/v6 arms)
description:
Refactor test/data/codegen/live_test.go from per-arm inlined copies into a shared scenario battery. Enabler: every backend generates from the same fixture inputs, so generated method sets are signature-identical across backends — scenario bodies are written ONCE against a test-local structural interface. A per-backend adapter owns: container start, connect + handle construction, seed(cypher), and the isolation strategy (neo4j: serialized DETACH-wipe; AGE later: unique graph per scenario, parallel). Scenario coverage keeps the existing battery: ErrNoRows on empty graph, single-row read, ErrMultipleResults on duplicates, exec write + re-read.

This bead lands the v5/v6 arms only; the AGE arm is a later bead. Seed cypher must stay in the openCypher dialect intersection (CREATE/MATCH basics) — fine for smoke scenarios. Preserve failure-pointing (the current file inlines bodies for exactly this reason) via t.Helper + per-scenario named subtests + require messages. Update golden import paths for the per-target subtree relocation. Stays in the nested module behind the codegen_live tag; digest-pinned image and GQLC_SKIP_LIVE behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Each scenario body exists exactly once; v5 and v6 arms both run the full battery green under -tags codegen_live; a deliberately broken assertion reports the scenario name and assertion line, not a wrapper; adding a backend arm requires only an adapter.
notes:
=== CONSTRAINT: "shared scenario battery" cannot be a plain Go interface ===
Measured on the .3 branch, not assumed.

The bead says scenario bodies are written once "against a test-local
structural interface". The method SIGNATURES are textually identical
across arms:

  PeopleByAgeAndLocale(ctx context.Context, arg PeopleByAgeAndLocaleParams) ([]PeopleByAgeAndLocaleRow, error)

but Params/Row are package-local named types, and each target emits its
own package (golden/neo4j-go-v5 vs golden/neo4j-go-v6). So
v5.PeopleByAgeAndLocaleParams != v6.PeopleByAgeAndLocaleParams and no
single non-generic interface can be satisfied by both handles.

Same problem for the error assertions, and worse: ErrNoRows and
ErrMultipleResults are per-package `errors.New` values, so
errors.Is(v6err, v5.ErrNoRows) is FALSE. A scenario body cannot name one
sentinel and have it hold for both arms.

Implication for the adapter seam: the adapter must narrow the generated
surface to types the TEST owns — plain scenario-local structs/args and
the arm's own sentinel values exposed as methods (errNoRows() error,
errMultipleResults() error) — not merely own container/connect/seed/
isolation. That narrowing is the mechanism that makes one scenario body
serve N backends; it is not incidental glue.

Generics were considered and are the wrong tool here: a type parameter
can carry P and R through the call, but a scenario body must CONSTRUCT a
P and READ FIELDS off an R, which needs per-arm code regardless. The
adapter pays that cost once per fixture per arm, explicitly.

Consequence for the AGE arm (.8): adding a backend stays "write one
adapter", but the adapter is ~15 lines of field mapping per fixture, not
zero. Acceptance criterion "adding a backend arm requires only an
adapter" is still met.

title: codegen tests: single-fixture layout with per-target golden subtrees
description:
Restructure test/data/codegen so each fixture holds its inputs exactly once: manifest.json gains targets (list of registry wire keys; omitted = all registered targets); golden/ gains one subtree per target key; the _v6 twin fixtures (verbatim input copies per codegen_test.go:36 doc) are deleted. The suite iterates fixtures x declared targets, constructing each generator via the registry (from the registry bead). A registered target enrolled in a fixture with a missing golden subtree is a RED test — this is the forcing function that means a new backend cannot register without entering the golden + compile gates.

Invalid fixtures split the same way: core (backend-independent) errors run under all targets; backend-specific errors (e.g. the unrepresentable_width family) declare their target list.

TestGoldenBuild needs no changes — it compiles the whole nested module, so per-target subtrees are swept automatically; it remains the fully generic compile gate.
acceptance_criteria: _v6 twin fixture dirs gone; every input file exists once per fixture; golden contents byte-identical to pre-migration modulo relocation (diff the trees to prove it); suite has no per-target switch; deliberately deleting one golden subtree turns the suite red; TestGoldenBuild still compiles everything.
notes:
ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT surfaced by the .2 adversarial review (Linus, finding 5) — fold into this bead's restructuring:

The codegen conformance suite (internal/codegen/neo4j/neo4j_test.go) now imports internal/cli/backends to construct generators through the registry. That import direction means the suite lives inside the neo4j package while iterating over ALL registered targets. Once AGE registers (bead .6), this suite will construct AGE generators from the neo4j package's test directory.

The suite therefore needs a new home as part of this bead's "suite iterates fixtures x declared targets" work — a backend-neutral package (e.g. internal/codegen/conformance or a test/ package) that imports every backend via the registry, rather than living under one backend's directory. Doing this here is cheap because the suite is being restructured anyway; deferring it to .6 makes AGE's bead carry a neo4j refactor.

This is an implementation constraint, not a change to the acceptance criteria.

=== ENROLLMENT MODEL — OWNER DECISION 2026-08-01 (amends the locked "omitted = all registered" clause) ===
The locked rule read: manifest targets omitted = all registered targets; registering a backend auto-enrolls it into every fixture, and a missing golden subtree is red.

Taken literally at migration time that obliges a v6 golden subtree for all 67 fixtures that currently carry a v5 golden only (~258 new generated files, ~12k lines differing from v5 by import path and DriverWithContext -> Driver), and obliges ~289 AGE subtrees the moment AGE registers at .6.

OWNER CHOSE: explicit enrollment, coverage unchanged. Every fixture declares its targets:
  - the 8 _v6 twins collapse into their base fixture with targets ["neo4j-go-v5","neo4j-go-v6"]
  - the remaining 67 carry targets ["neo4j-go-v5"]
  - ZERO new golden files. Migration is pure relocation; existing golden bytes must not change.

CONSEQUENCE: targets is a REQUIRED manifest field. Omission is a loud fixture-authoring error, not a default. A silent "omitted = all registered" default would be a trap once AGE registers — a new fixture authored without targets would enroll every backend and go red for reasons unrelated to the fixture.

CONSEQUENCE: the "registering a backend auto-enrolls it" forcing function does not survive this choice. Backend enrollment becomes an explicit, per-bead act: .6-.11 add "apache-age-pgx-v5" to fixture target lists as AGE capability lands. Each of those beads owns the goldens for the fixtures it enrolls.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-01 (adversarial review, Linus) — unrepresentable_width is NOT backend-independent ===
An earlier implementation note claimed all 24 invalid fixtures behave identically under
every target, so labelling the unrepresentable_width_* family "neo4j-specific" was
documentary only, and suggested enrolling them everywhere at .6. THAT IS WRONG.

codegen.TypeMap (internal/codegen/typemap.go) is a PER-BACKEND interface. The set of
widths for which Property returns ok=false is owned by the backend, and the eight-width
list lives in internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go. AGE runs on postgres and can plausibly
carry DECIMAL faithfully, so it may not raise ErrUnrepresentableWidth at all.

The fixtures' declared targets in the .3 commit are correct as written
(["neo4j-go-v5","neo4j-go-v6"]). Do NOT enrol unrepresentable_width_{decimal,float16,
int128,uint256} into apache-age-pgx-v5 at .6 without first checking what AGE's TypeMap
actually rejects; the ones AGE also rejects get enrolled, the rest stay neo4j-only.
close_reason: Merged as PR #642. Fixtures are keyed by input, goldens by target; manifest.targets is required with no default. 289 goldens relocated byte-identical, zero new. Suite moved to internal/codegen/conformance, resolving via codegen.Registry. Two -update blast-radius bugs found and fixed in review.

title: codegen: runtime Registry + config parity test + pipeline wiring (no init())
description:
Add codegen.Registry + Entry{Key string, New func(pkg string) Generator} with NO package-level state and NO init() registration (explicit user requirement — init-based registration is a hack). The CLI composition root (internal/cli) constructs the registry explicitly, listing the neo4j package entries (neo4j-go-v5, neo4j-go-v6); pipeline.Run takes the registry and resolves the config wire key through it, replacing the hardcoded switch at internal/cli/pipeline/pipeline.go:221. Also replace the test-side generatorFor switch (internal/codegen/codegen_test.go:49) with registry lookup so the conformance suite constructs generators exactly the way production does.

Config posture: internal/config keeps its closed Driver enum, UnmarshalYAML validation, and parse-time error messages. Drift between the two lists is killed by a parity test asserting registry keys == config.DriverValues() (chosen over making the registry the single vocabulary source, which would ripple the loader signature through every call site).
acceptance_criteria: Registry constructed only at the composition root; grep proves no init() registration and no package-level registry var; pipeline driver switch deleted; test generatorFor switch deleted; parity test red if a registry key or enum const is added without its twin; adding a backend = one Entry + one enum const.
close_reason: Merged via PR #640 (squash 44e-series on master). Registry + parity test + pipeline wiring landed; generatorFor switch deleted; no init(), no package-level state.

title: codegen: split core from the neo4j backend (internal/codegen/neo4j)
description:
Pure refactor, no behavior change. Move the neo4j-specific emission layer — render_*.go, driverTarget (driver.go), and the neo4j-shaped column-decode strategy mapping in prepare.go — into internal/codegen/neo4j, which implements codegen.Generator end-to-end. internal/codegen keeps Input/File/Generator/errors and phases Z/A/B (schema admission + entity naming, batch admission, name derivation), with the Go-type mapping parametrized so a second backend supplies its own table.

Why: the core currently hardcodes neo4j — prepare.go strategy enums are named after neo4j.GetRecordValue / dbtype.Node shapes; render templates inline the neo4j API; only driverTarget abstracts v5/v6 import paths. Epic gqlc-35yu locks shared-core + full-Generators as the seam.

Notes: the exact split line is discovered during the refactor — this bead pins intent and gate, not a file list. No internal-API freeze applies (bd memory no-internal-api-freeze); refactor freely. Sibling worktree + stacked branch; TDD posture here means the gate below is red until the split is complete.
acceptance_criteria: Existing golden trees byte-identical (this IS the gate — any golden diff fails the bead); go test ./... green; core files emit no neo4j import strings or API names; internal/codegen/neo4j implements codegen.Generator; consumers (pipeline, tests) compile against the new layout.
close_reason: Merged in PR #638. Linus review PASS (no blocking findings); three nits fixed in a follow-up commit. Goldens byte-identical — no golden-update path run. Deferred narrow-width list-element fixture tracked as gqlc-hhd0.

title: [EPIC] codegen: multi-backend architecture + Apache AGE (pgx v5) target
description:
Why: internal/codegen emits only neo4j-go-driver v5/v6, and neo4j specifics live in the shared core (prepare.go decode strategies are named after neo4j.GetRecordValue/dbtype shapes; render templates inline neo4j API). Goal: refactor so each backend is its own sub-package implementing the Generator seam, then add Apache AGE (Postgres extension, github.com/apache/age) as a second backend family.

Locked design (grill session 2026-07-31):
- Seam: internal/codegen keeps Input/File/Generator/errors + phases Z/A/B (admission, naming) with the Go-type mapping parametrized per backend; internal/codegen/neo4j and internal/codegen/age each implement Generator end-to-end and own their render layer. No fine-grained render-plugin interface — AGE emission differs too radically for holes shaped by n=1 backend.
- AGE runtime: generated code imports github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 only (major-only import paths; consumer go.mod picks the minor, like neo4j today). DBTX interface satisfied by pool/conn/tx + WithTx(pgx.Tx). gqlc emits its own agtype decode helpers. The apache/age Go driver is disqualified for generated code: its parameter path is fmt.Sprintf interpolation into Cypher text (injection vector), it drags lib/pq + the ANTLR runtime into consumer builds, and it has been dormant since 2024 (verified from drivers/golang source 2026-07-31).
- Registry: codegen.Registry + Entry{Key, New}, constructed explicitly at the CLI composition root — no init() registration, no package-level state. Keyed by config wire strings. Config keeps its closed Driver enum and parse-time errors; a parity test asserts registry keys == config.DriverValues(). New wire key: apache-age-pgx-v5 (const DriverApacheAgePgxV5).
- Graph lifecycle: New(db DBTX, graph string) — graph name is a runtime arg (AGE analogue of neo4j database selection). EnsureGraph/DropGraph are methods on the generated Queries handle (join the reserved-identifier sweep; excluded from the Querier interfaces); package-level SessionInit matching pgxpool AfterConnect runs LOAD age; all emitted SQL fully qualifies ag_catalog.cypher / ag_catalog.agtype so search_path is never a session dependency. This makes parallel acceptance tests trivial: unique graph per test + EnsureGraph + Cleanup DropGraph, one shared container.
- Type gaps: agtype has NO native temporal types (verified against src/include/utils/agtype.h enum: NULL/STRING/NUMERIC/INTEGER/FLOAT/BOOL/VERTEX/EDGE/PATH/ARRAY/OBJECT). Spike bead validates real temporal + parameter behavior against a live container FIRST; agreed fallback is faithful per-type encodings (timestamp=epoch-micros integer, date=ISO string, duration=ISO-8601 string, zoned=offset-preserving string) with the Go surface identical across backends; generate-time error reserved for types with no faithful encoding.
- Tests: fixtures restructure to one dir + per-target golden subtrees with a manifest targets list (omitted = all registered); the suite iterates fixtures x registry, so registering a backend auto-enrolls it and a missing golden subtree is a red test. TestGoldenBuild stays the fully generic compile gate (compiles the whole nested module). Live tests: shared scenario battery against a test-local structural interface + per-backend adapters (generated method sets are signature-identical across backends); AGE arm uses unique-graph-per-scenario parallel isolation; joins the codegen_live nightly job; AGE image digest-pinned (gqlc-9u5 precedent). PR CI wall-time untouched.
- Process: every implementation bead follows TDD (failing golden/fixture/live test first), one sibling worktree + stacked branch per bead, PR per bead.

Child DAG: core-split -> registry -> fixture-migration -> live-refactor; spike independent (parallel); C0 needs registry+fixtures; scalar-reads needs spike+C0; live-arm+CI needs live-refactor+scalar-reads; entity-columns and write-path need scalar-reads+live-arm; temporals need write-path+live-arm. Dialect-gap posture is unblocked backlog.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads closed; gqlc generate with gen.go.driver apache-age-pgx-v5 produces a package that compiles (generic golden build gate) and passes the shared live scenario battery against a live AGE container.
notes:
=== SPIKE gqlc-35yu.5 OUTCOME (2026-07-31) — TWO LOCKED DECISIONS AMENDED ===
Owner-approved amendments. Full evidence (818 lines) in gqlc-35yu.5.
AGE image pinned for all downstream work:
  apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb
  (PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0)

1. SEARCH_PATH — the locked claim is FALSE, decision reversed.
   Locked text said: "all emitted SQL fully qualifies ag_catalog.cypher /
   ag_catalog.agtype so search_path is never a session dependency."
   Empirically: full qualification is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. AGE's own
   Cypher->SQL transform emits BARE OPERATORS (=, >, +, @>) and does not emit
   the OPERATOR(ag_catalog.=) form, so Postgres resolves them through
   search_path. With ag_catalog off the path and every identifier qualified:
   RETURN 1, bare MATCH and ORDER BY succeed, but
     WHERE n.name = 'alice'      -> ERROR: cannot cast agtype string to boolean
     MATCH (n:P {name:'alice'})  -> ERROR: operator does not exist: agtype @> agtype
     RETURN 1+1                  -> same, for +
   gqlc CANNOT fix this by emitting better SQL: the operators come from AGE's
   transform, not from us.
   AMENDED DECISION (owner, 2026-07-31): ag_catalog MUST be on the session
   search_path, and SessionInit is the enforcement point. SessionInit runs
   LOAD 'age', then SET search_path = ag_catalog + the caller's, then a CANARY
   that exercises an operator (RETURN 1 = 1) and returns an error if it fails.
   Rationale for the canary: SessionInit is the pgxpool AfterConnect hook, so
   returning an error there keeps the connection OUT of the pool — the failure
   surfaces at connection establishment (at startup for a pinging/pre-warming
   consumer) rather than when the first WHERE clause runs. This matters because
   AGE's failure mode is PARTIAL: simple queries succeed while operator queries
   fail, so a misconfigured deployment otherwise looks healthy until first use.
   Costs one round trip per new pool connection; pool conns are long-lived.
   New(db, graph) is UNCHANGED — verification lives in SessionInit, so the
   constructor still does no I/O and still returns no error.

2. TEMPORAL ENCODING TABLE — 2 of 4 amended (spike mandate covered this).
   Failed encodings round-trip correctly but SORT WRONG, which breaks
   WHERE n.ts > $param. Ordering, not round-tripping, is the real gate.
     timestamp/instant | epoch-MICROS int64                    | CONFIRMED
     date              | ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, zero-padded  | CONFIRMED
     duration          | total-MICROS int64                    | AMENDED
     zoned datetime    | TWO int64 props: <f> epoch-micros     | AMENDED
                       |   plus <f>Offset offset-seconds       |
     calendar duration | no faithful encoding (months/years    | generate-time
                       |   are not a fixed micro count)        |   error
   duration as ISO-8601 string sorted P1D, PT10H, PT1H, PT2H, PT90M — and
   WHERE v > 'PT2H' returned only PT90M (1.5h): one false positive, two false
   negatives. zoned as offset-preserving string returned an 07:00Z row for
   WHERE v > '...08:00+00:00'. A map {t,o} also sorts wrong (jsonb key order)
   and would force gqlc to rewrite user ORDER BY; the FLAT SIDECAR keeps the
   sort key as the property itself, so user ORDER BY passes through untouched.
   date stays a string by owner decision (2026-07-31) despite agtype string
   comparison using DB COLLATION rather than byte order — ISO dates are
   fixed-width digits and hyphens, and readability in the stored graph wins.
   No temporal casts exist in AGE (full pg_cast table captured in the spike);
   the only temporal function is timestamp(), returning epoch-MILLIS.

3. PARAMETER MECHANISM — selected: direct cypher('<graph>', $$...$$, $1) over
   the pgx extended protocol. age_prepare_cypher REJECTED: it latches query
   text into the plan via connection-global state at Parse time, which pgx
   statement caching schedules unpredictably. Server-log evidence: parse/bind/
   execute are separate phases and the logged statement text ends in the
   literal $1 at every phase, with the payload appearing only under
   DETAIL: Parameters. A Cypher-injection canary table survived intact.
   Note: pgx SimpleProtocol — the only interpolating mode — is the one mode
   AGE rejects outright, so the unsafe path fails closed.

=== AMENDMENT 3 (owner, 2026-08-01) — FIXTURE ENROLLMENT IS EXPLICIT, NOT AUTOMATIC ===
Locked text said: "fixtures restructure to one dir + per-target golden subtrees with
a manifest targets list (omitted = all registered); the suite iterates fixtures x
registry, so registering a backend auto-enrolls it and a missing golden subtree is a
red test."

The auto-enroll half is SUPERSEDED. Taken literally at migration time it obliges a v6
golden subtree for the 67 fixtures that carry a v5 golden only (~258 new files, ~12k
lines differing by import path and DriverWithContext -> Driver), and ~289 AGE subtrees
the moment AGE registers at .6 — which would also put master red from .6 through .11,
violating the "each branch independently mergeable" rule in AGENTS.md.

AMENDED DECISION: targets is a REQUIRED manifest field; there is no "omitted = all
registered" default. Enrollment is an explicit, per-bead act.
  - .3 migrates with coverage unchanged: the 8 _v6 twins collapse into their base
    fixture with targets ["neo4j-go-v5","neo4j-go-v6"]; the other 67 carry
    targets ["neo4j-go-v5"]. ZERO new golden files — pure relocation.
  - .6-.11 each add "apache-age-pgx-v5" to the target lists of the fixtures that
    bead's capability covers, and own those goldens.
What survives: a target enrolled in a fixture with a missing golden subtree is still a
RED test, and TestGoldenBuild still compiles every subtree. The gate is intact; only
the enrollment trigger changed from implicit to explicit.
SEQUENCING PLAN (2026-08-01), after .3 merged as PR #642. Remaining chain is near-serial: .6 -> .7 -> .8 (also needs .4) -> {.9 ∥ .10} -> .11 -> .12. title: bd pull re-derives in_progress from started_at, silently reverting a deliberate 'open'
description:
`bd update <id> --status open` does not stick for any bead that was ever
claimed. The next `bd-gh-sync pull` re-derives `in_progress` from the bead's
non-nil `started_at`, and the next `chore(bd)` export PR then silently
reverts master.

## Evidence

`gqlc-4np` was deliberately set to `open` last session, pending an ADR call,
and committed to master that way. It came back as `in_progress`.

It is not coming from GitHub: `GH#503` is OPEN with zero assignees, and
GitHub has no in-progress state to map from. It is bd reconstructing the
status locally from `started_at = 2026-07-28T09:55:09Z`.

Proof it was the pull and not a human: `gqlc-4np.updated_at` is
`2026-07-31T00:05:31Z`, byte-identical to the epoch embedded in the ghost
bead id the SAME pull minted (`gqlc-1785456331014`). The hook reported
"Pulled 2 issues (1 created, 1 updated)" -- this is the updated one.

## Why it cannot be worked around

`bd update` exposes no flag to clear `started_at`. `--defer` and `--due` both
take an empty string to clear; `started_at` has no equivalent. So `open` is
not a reachable steady state for a previously-claimed bead.

Worked around for now by using `blocked`, which carries the same intent
("not being worked, waiting on a decision") and sits outside the
re-derivation path. Whether `blocked` also gets re-derived is untested --
the next pull will tell.

## Review implication

Diff every `chore(bd)` export record by record, parsing the +/- JSON lines
and printing `id | status`. This revert is one line out of 234 and is
invisible in a diffstat. Cf. memory `patch-check-does-not-detect-reverts`.

Memory: `bd-pull-rederives-in-progress-from-started-at`.

## Correction 2026-07-31: `blocked` is NOT a workaround

The original text above proposed `blocked` as a status that carries the same
intent and sits outside the re-derivation path. That was asserted without
testing and it is **false**. Measured, both arms, deterministic:

    bd update gqlc-4np --status blocked ; .githooks/bd-gh-sync pull  -> in_progress
    bd update gqlc-4np --status open    ; .githooks/bd-gh-sync pull  -> in_progress

The re-derivation overrides *any* non-closed status. For a bead that was ever
claimed, `in_progress` is the only reachable steady state short of closing it.

PR #612's body and commit message carry the same wrong claim; this bead is the
correction of record.

Caught only because `just init` re-activated the local hooks, so `post-merge`
started firing the pull again and the revert reappeared within one merge. It
had been latent while `core.hooksPath` was pointing at an empty directory.
notes:
=== SAME CLASS, DIFFERENT TRIGGER: a git-side revert of the JSONL rolls the DB
back silently. Observed 2026-08-01 while merging gqlc-35yu.7's ledger PR. ===

This bead is about `bd pull` re-deriving status. I hit the mirror image of it
through a plain git operation, with no bd sync command involved.

Sequence, all of it routine ledger hygiene:
  1. bd update gqlc-35yu.8 --status in_progress   -> DB: in_progress. Correct.
     (an auto-export wrote AND staged .beads/issues.jsonl)
  2. git checkout master  -> refused: local changes to .beads/issues.jsonl
  3. I inspected the staged diff, saw the ONLY delta was
     gqlc-35yu.8 open -> in_progress, i.e. state already in the DB, and
     discarded it with `git restore --staged --worktree .beads/issues.jsonl`
     on the reasoning that the Dolt DB is authoritative and the JSONL is a
     passive export, so the file could be regenerated.
  4. merged the PR, pulled master, re-ran `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`
  5. The export wrote status "open". `bd show` confirmed the DB itself had
     reverted to OPEN -- while still carrying `Started: 2026-08-01`.

So the export is NOT passive in the direction the docs imply: reverting the
working-tree file propagated back into the DB. started_at survived and status
did not, which is the same torn state this bead already describes, reached
without `bd pull`.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the reasoning in step 3 is correct given a
genuinely passive export, and it is exactly what anyone will do when git blocks
a branch switch on this file -- which happens on EVERY bead, because closing a
bead and starting the next one both dirty it. The failure is silent: no
warning, and the next `bd export` cheerfully writes the reverted value into the
committed ledger, so the wrong state can reach master looking freshly exported.
I only caught it because I diffed the regenerated file against what I expected.

WORKAROUND until fixed: after any git operation that reverts, stashes or checks
out .beads/issues.jsonl, re-assert status with `bd update` and verify with
`bd show` before exporting. Do not trust an export taken straight after a
working-tree revert.

Worth deciding as part of the fix whether the JSONL should be import-on-change
at all. If it is meant to be an export, the DB should ignore it; if it is meant
to be bidirectional, `git restore` is an unguarded write path into the DB and
the guard (internal/tools/bdguard) does not cover this direction.
=== INVESTIGATED 2026-08-01 (branch fix/bd-gh-sync-state-fidelity): the stated
mechanism does NOT reproduce on bd 1.0.4, and the opposite one does ===

This bead says the pull re-derives in_progress from a non-nil started_at, and
the 2026-07-31 correction escalates that to "the re-derivation overrides ANY
non-closed status ... in_progress is the only reachable steady state". Both
claims fail against measurement.

DISCONFIRMING EVIDENCE 1 -- the live corpus. Four beads currently sit with
started_at set and a non-in_progress, non-closed status, some for weeks:
  gqlc-do1    open    started 2026-07-12
  gqlc-h9n.33 open    started 2026-07-28
  gqlc-h9n.1  blocked started 2026-07-28
  gqlc-23e    blocked started 2026-07-02
If any non-closed status were overridden, none of these could persist. The
correction claim that `blocked` is also re-derived is contradicted twice over
by gqlc-h9n.1 and gqlc-23e.

DISCONFIRMING EVIDENCE 2 -- isolated scratch DB (/tmp, `bd init`, no GitHub,
no shared state). Create bead, --claim (-> in_progress, started_at set),
`bd update --status open` -> open WITH started_at retained. Export, then
import that file back: status stays open. No re-derivation.

WHAT DOES REPRODUCE, deterministically, is the reverse direction -- and it is
gqlc-63y third repro, not this one:
  DB set to in_progress; issues.jsonl on disk says open; then
    bd list            -> in_progress survives (auto-sync does NOT import)
    bd hooks run post-merge -> status becomes OPEN, started_at retained
So the clobber is the JSONL replay inside `bd hooks run post-merge`, it goes
in_progress -> open, and it produces the torn open+started_at pair. The two
beads are NOT mutually contradictory observations of one bug; 63y direction is
real and this bead direction is not reproducible. Treat this as the stale one.

Corollary: open+started_at is a NORMAL bd-producible state (see evidence 2),
not the signature of a torn write, so it cannot be used as a detector.

MANAGER FORK (remove the re-derivation vs gate it, teaching the sync to record
what it last wrote): declined as posed, because it presumes a re-derivation
that does not exist here. It would also be unreachable from this script -- any
such logic lives inside the bd binary, and `.githooks/bd-gh-sync` cannot gate
it. Nothing is removed, so nothing is lost: the "started but never updated"
signal the fork worried about is still carried by started_at itself.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD, which serves this bead intent without guessing at a
cause: a postcondition. After the scoped pull, bd list is re-read and any bead
that was HELD OUT of the pull but whose status moved anyway is reported by
name with the exact `bd update <id> --status <old>` needed to re-assert it.
That is agnostic about which component moved it, so it catches the JSONL
replay above even though this script never invokes it. Pinned by tests in
both arms (moved -> warns; unchanged -> silent).

NOT FIXED, and out of reach of this branch: `bd hooks run post-merge` still
replays the JSONL over newer DB state. Note it is currently UNREACHABLE in
this repo -- core.hooksPath is .githooks, and nothing in .githooks, the
justfile or .claude/settings.json chains to .beads/hooks/ or runs `bd hooks
run`, so the beads-managed hooks are inert. That is why the postcondition
warns rather than blocks. If those hooks are ever re-activated, the underlying
replay needs its own bead against bd itself.
MANAGER CORRECTION: this bead's stated mechanism does not reproduce. I verified the refutation myself.

The bead claims `bd pull` re-derives `in_progress` from a non-nil `started_at`, so `--status open` cannot stick for a previously-claimed bead. If that were true, no bead could sit in open-with-started_at for any length of time. Four do, and two have for over a month:

  gqlc-h9n.1    blocked  started=2026-07-28  updated=2026-07-28
  gqlc-h9n.33   open     started=2026-07-28  updated=2026-07-28
  gqlc-do1      open     started=2026-07-12  updated=2026-07-14
  gqlc-23e      blocked  started=2026-07-02  updated=2026-07-19

gqlc-do1 has been open with started_at set since 12 July and gqlc-23e blocked since 2 July, across many pulls. The implementer independently reproduced the negative in an isolated scratch DB: claim, then --status open, leaves it open with started_at retained, and re-importing that export re-derives nothing.

Note also that the bead's own Correction says `blocked` sits outside the re-derivation path and is a usable workaround; two of the four above are blocked, but two are plain `open`, so `open` is not special either.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS, and it is the opposite direction. `bd hooks run post-merge` replays the JSONL over newer DB state, reverting in_progress -> open while KEEPING started_at. That is deterministic and was reproduced. So the status damage is real; the arrow was drawn backwards, and the bead named started_at re-derivation for what is actually stale-export replay.

HOW THE ORIGINAL EVIDENCE MISLED. The bead's strongest-looking argument was that gqlc-4np.updated_at is byte-identical to the epoch embedded in the ghost bead id minted by the same pull (gqlc-1785456331014). That correctly proves the same pull touched both. It does not prove WHY the status moved — identical timestamps establish co-occurrence, not mechanism. The ghost-minting is gqlc-onji; the status move is replay. One pull, two effects, and the shared timestamp says nothing about which caused which.

I RESTATED THIS BAD DIAGNOSIS TO THE IMPLEMENTER as settled fact when I added jwuw to their scope, including the "no flag to clear started_at" framing that follows from it. They checked instead of believing me, and were right to. Recording that here rather than quietly dropping it: the bead was filed from a real symptom and a plausible story, and the story was wrong.

gqlc-63y and gqlc-jwuw were flagged as mutually contradictory. That is resolved: 63y's direction is the real one.

DISPOSITION: not fixed as filed, because there is nothing to fix at the stated site. The implementer added a POSTCONDITION instead — held beads must return unchanged from a pull, warning by name with the re-assert command. That is the right shape for a bead whose mechanism was misidentified: it pins the observable property the bead actually cared about without encoding the wrong cause. Whether that fully retires this bead is for the review round to say.
close_reason: Closed

title: gqlc-fex has two GH mirrors (#597/#598) plus a sync-created ghost bead — cleanup needs an owner decision
description:
Bead `gqlc-fex` acquired two GitHub mirrors, and the pull sync then manufactured
a second bead for one of them.

## Timeline (2026-07-30, all UTC)

- 00:49:40  GH #597 created — short body ending "Bead: gqlc-fex".
- 00:52:02  GH #598 created — same title, long body (TDD plan, acceptance
            criteria). `gqlc-fex.external_ref` points here, orphaning #597.
- 00:53:41  PR #599 merged carrying `Closes #597` → #597 closed at 00:53:42.
- 00:53:43  Bead `gqlc-1785373131289-1-b6686b0c` closed — a ghost bead the
            GH→bd pull created for #597, whose description is #597's body,
            which itself reads "Bead: gqlc-fex".
- 00:59:30  #598 closed separately.

## Current state

Both GH issues are closed and both beads are closed, so nothing is incorrectly
open — the residue is cosmetic but misleading:

- Two GH issues describe one bug, neither marked as a duplicate of the other.
- The ghost bead is now in `.beads/issues.jsonl` (landed by #609, deliberately,
  because the export must mirror the Dolt DB rather than be hand-edited).
- PR #599's `Closes #597` did not match `gqlc-fex`'s mirror (#598). The
  check-pr-closes gate did not catch it: `gqlc-fex` was not yet in the
  committed export, so the gate took its "unknown bead — PASS (don't block on
  stale export)" branch. That escape hatch is load-bearing for same-day beads
  and is worth re-examining.

## Likely cause

The `--prefer-github` amendment ordering recorded in memory
`bd-gh-sync-reverts-descriptions`: the description was amended and a second
issue was opened instead of editing the first. This is plausibly downstream of
`gqlc-63y` — the divergence guard that would have flagged the amendment never
ran.

## Decision needed

1. Delete the ghost bead from the Dolt DB, or keep it as an inert record?
   Deletion is destructive and propagates, so it needs an owner call.
2. Mark #597 or #598 as a duplicate on GitHub so the pair reads correctly.
3. Decide whether the gate's unknown-bead PASS should stay, given it is what
   let the wrong `Closes` number through.
close_reason: Ghost bead deleted and the drop declared (PR #611). #597 closed as DUPLICATE of #598; gqlc-fex intact on #598. Deletion is not permanently durable — the pull re-mints a ghost for any touched orphan issue; durable options filed as a P1 follow-up.

title: check-pr-closes gate does not re-evaluate on body edits — unre-triggerable, and bypassable after opening
description:
The `check-pr-closes` gate in `ci.yml` (tidy job) reads the PR body from the
workflow event payload:

    PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}

and `ci.yml` declares `on: pull_request:` with no `types:`, which defaults to
`[opened, synchronize, reopened]` — `edited` is not included.

Two consequences, found while fixing PR #600 on 2026-07-30.

## 1. A correct fix cannot re-trigger the gate

Adding the missing `Closes #N` to the body fires no event, so the check stays
red. A re-run does not help either: a re-run replays the original event
payload, so the gate re-reads the stale body. The only ways out are pushing a
commit or closing/reopening the PR. Neither is discoverable from the failure
message, which just says "Add 'Closes #598' to the PR body".

## 2. The gate is bypassable after the fact

A PR can carry `Closes #N` at open time, pass the gate, then have the line
edited out of the body. No `edited` event, no re-evaluation, and the PR merges
green with the GH issue left open — the exact failure the gate exists to
prevent.

## 3. The gate assumes any PR naming a bead is closing it

The bead id is taken from the branch name when the body has no `Bead:` line,
and the gate then demands a `Closes #N`. That is wrong for a PR that changes a
bead's status without resolving it. PR #609 reopened `gqlc-4np`; had the branch
been named after the bead, the gate would have demanded `Closes #503` and
closing that issue would have been precisely the wrong outcome. Working around
it by choosing a branch name that avoids the id is not a control.

## Fix direction

Add `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]`, or have the step fetch
the body from the API at run time rather than trusting the payload. The API
read also fixes consequence 2, since a re-run would then see current state.
Separately, give the gate a way to express "this PR touches the bead but does
not resolve it" so item 3 does not depend on branch naming.

## Acceptance

- Editing a PR body to add the missing `Closes #N` turns the check green with
  no push and no close/reopen.
- Removing `Closes #N` from a previously-passing PR body turns the check red.
- A status-change PR can name its bead without being forced to close it.
notes:
PR #867 https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/867 — head e9119f75, branch fix/pr-closes-gate-reevaluates, worktree /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc-w4al. AWAITING MERGE (orchestrator holds merge authority; do not merge from this session).

LIVE WITNESS of the acceptance property, run on PR #867 itself, head unchanged at e9119f75 throughout (no push, no reopen):
 1. baseline: all 8 required contexts green, mergeStateStatus CLEAN.
 2. 07:21:00Z removed the 'Closes #617' line -> run 32005420996 created 07:21:03Z, same SHA.
 3. its tidy (job 95313776365) FAILED: "ERROR: PR body is missing 'Closes #617'".
 4. with the line still absent, re-ran the PRE-EDIT run's tidy ('gh run rerun 32004817300 --job 95312044713') -> job 95313989391, run_attempt 2, FAILED, same message. Attempt 1 of that same job had PASSED on the frozen payload. This is the half 'edited' alone would not cover.
 5. mergeStateStatus BLOCKED; both tidy check runs on the SHA were failure.
 6. 07:22:56Z restored the body -> run 32005559232 created 07:22:57Z; tidy (job 95314195022) SUCCESS, '[check-pr-closes] gqlc-w4al -> Closes #617 (ok)'.
Acceptance property HOLDS: a body that loses its Closes line is not mergeable green, and a body edit alone both breaks and repairs the verdict.

CERTIFIED at e9119f75 (head), detached worktree: fmt-check, tidy-check, actionlint, test, lint all exit 0. Docker down locally so test-codegen-live* not run.

RESIDUE: gqlc-1ekq (consequence 3, gate assumes bead-naming == closing), gqlc-2rli (full-re-run cost / separate-workflow shape), gqlc-xdd0 (NEW: selective tidy re-run can leave lint/test/codegen-fence 'skipped' = pass at a SHA where they never ran; this change is what makes tidy re-passable at an unchanged SHA).
MEMORY: bd remember workflow-closing-issue-refs-index-lags-body-edit.
close_reason: Merged as c575ae8b (PR #867). GH #617 closed by the Closes line. Both halves shipped: ci.yml gains types:[...,edited] and the check-pr-closes step fetches the body from the API at run time; tidy gains pull-requests: read. Consequence 3 (a status-change PR forced to Closes its bead) is NOT closed here — deferred to gqlc-1ekq / GH #862, named in both the PR body and the commit message. Independent review PASS, zero blockers, verdict at /tmp/factory/verdict-867.md.

title: schema/gql: which endpoint's rejection wins when both edge endpoints are defective is unpinned
description:
A mutation sweep over `internal/schema/gql/listener.go` (81 cases, 73 caught) left one
survivor that is a genuine coverage gap rather than a defensive tripwire.

## The survivor

`EnterEdgeTypePattern` reads its two endpoints in written source-then-destination
order, short-circuiting on the first failure (listener.go:353-365):

```go
if r := directed.EdgeTypePatternPointingRight(); r != nil {
        src, refErr = sourceRef(r.SourceNodeTypeReference())
        if refErr == nil {
                dst, refErr = destRef(r.DestinationNodeTypeReference())
        }
        filler = r.ArcTypePointingRight().EdgeTypeFiller()
}
```

Swapping the two so the destination is read first — keeping the short-circuit
intact, so this changes only *which* rejection is reported when both ends are
defective — leaves the entire suite green.

## Why nothing sees it

`sourceRef`/`destRef` return only what `fillerLabels` returns, which is one of two
sentinels: `ErrEndpointFillerHasProperties` and `ErrEndpointFillerImpliesLabels`.
Every existing fixture has a defect on exactly one end, or the same defect on both:

- `invalid/endpoint_filler_properties.gql` — destination only, HasProperties
- `corpus/18.3-edge-type/endpoint_key_label_set.gql` — source only, ImpliesLabels
- `TestEndpointFillerRejectsProperties`' "both sides carry properties" case — both
  ends, but the *same* sentinel, so the order cannot be observed

With one end defective the short-circuit reports that end whichever way round the
reads go. With both ends carrying the *same* sentinel the answer is that sentinel
either way. The order is only observable when the two ends carry *different*
sentinels, and no file does. The "both sides" case above is the near miss: it was
written for this construct and stops one sentinel short.

## The behaviour, confirmed by probe

The source's rejection wins, and it wins *by role, not by written position*:

| written                                              | reported          |
|------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `(:Person => :Employee) -[:E]-> (:Post { x :: INT })` | ImpliesLabels (source) |
| `(:Person { x :: INT }) -[:E]-> (:Post => :Article)`  | HasProperties (source) |
| `(:Post { x :: INT }) <-[:E]- (:Person => :Employee)` | ImpliesLabels (source) |

The last row is the one worth pinning. In a left-pointing arc the grammar reports
the *rightmost written* endpoint as the source, so "source first" and "leftmost
first" disagree, and the code follows the role. That is the right answer — the
reported end is the same end regardless of which direction the author wrote the
arc in, so the diagnostic does not move when the edge is respelled — but nothing
says so and nothing would notice it changing.

This is the same class as the check ordering in `EnterEdgeTypePhrase` and
`EnterEdgeTypePattern`, where the mismatch sentinel deliberately fires before the
directed-only bail so the message names the author's actual mistake. That ordering
carries a comment arguing for it and tests that go red when it is swapped
(sweep cases 43 and 44, both caught). This one has neither.

## Proposed fix

Test-only; no product change. Extend the endpoint-filler coverage with the
mixed-sentinel pairing on both arc spellings, asserting the source's sentinel is
the one reported and the other is *not* — a bare `ErrorIs` on the winner would
still pass if both were somehow reported. Add the sentence about role-vs-position
to `sourceRef`/`destRef` or to the pattern collector.

## Provenance

Sweep script `/tmp/gqllist_sweep.py`, results `/tmp/gqllist_sweep.json`, case 56.
The other seven survivors were each instrumented with a logging probe and run
against the whole suite; all seven are defensive tripwires or equivalent mutants
and are correct as written:

- `SyntaxError`'s `tok.GetText() != ""` — 0 hits on an empty-text token, 4 on a
  non-Token offending symbol, so the `ok` half is load-bearing and the text half
  cannot fire
- `SyntaxError`'s `return` after the token branch — masked by `fail()` idempotence
- `walk`'s pre-walk `l.err != nil` bail — taken 6 times, but removal is invisible
  because `fail()` is first-wins; it guards against a panic on an unreliable tree
- `unsupportedSource`'s `src == nil` arm and its sentinel — 0 hits, error recovery only
- `unsupportedSource`'s trailing `return ErrUnsupportedSource` — 0 hits, unreachable
  by construction: `graphTypeSource` has exactly three alternatives (GQL.g4:347-350)
  and the guard tests for the third, so it is the documented forward-compat arm
- `nestedDepth` starting at `ctx` rather than its parent — 0 hits; no caller passes
  a `nestedGraphTypeSpecification` context, so it is an equivalent mutant
close_reason: Closed

title: schema/gql: nothing reaches fillerLabels' trailing nil bail; ({ }) is the only spelling that does
description:
`fillerLabels`' trailing bail (internal/schema/gql/edgetype.go:125-127) was reached
by no test:

    if impliedLabels == nil {
        return nil, nil
    }

Neutralising it — `impliedLabels == nil && false` — leaves the whole suite green:

    go build ./...            ok
    go test ./internal/...    ok

It is not dead. Falling through calls `impliedLabels.LabelSetPhrase()` on a nil
interface, so any input taking this path would panic rather than fail a test.

THE ONE SPELLING THAT REACHES IT is `({ })`, an endpoint filler that is an empty
property block and nothing else. The path is narrow, which is why it was missed:

  - `f == nil` (`()`, no filler at all) returns from the guard at :96, not here.
    endpoint_no_filler.gql covers that.
  - `({ x :: INT })` is rejected at :112 as ErrEndpointFillerHasProperties before
    reaching this line. invalid/endpoint_filler_properties.gql covers that.
  - `(:Person { })` — the label-bearing sibling — leaves impliedLabels non-nil and
    returns at :128. corpus 18.3-edge-type/endpoint_empty_property_block.gql
    covers that, and it is the near miss: it was written for this construct and
    stops one label short of this line.

So only an EMPTY block with NO label lands here. Confirmed by probe:
`(:Person) -[:AUTHORED]-> ({ })` parses and rejects with ErrUnknownEndpoint,
which is endpoint_no_filler.gql's outcome reached through the other arm.

FOUND BY the 21-case mutation sweep of edgetype.go + nodetype.go (2026-07-28),
which caught 18. The two other survivors are inert by grammar and are recorded in
bd memory rather than filed:

  edgetype.go:106  `spec != nil` — nodeTypePropertyTypes has exactly one
                   mandatory child, propertyTypesSpecification (GQL.g4:1542-1544)
  nodetype.go:44   `spec == nil` — all three labelSetPhrase alternatives yield a
                   LabelName or a labelSetSpecification (GQL.g4:1679-1682)

THE FIX is a corpus entry, not an invalid/ fixture. The reading of a label-less
endpoint is open — endpoint_no_filler.gql records both, and gqlc-h9n.35 holds the
question — so if it is ever settled the "any node type" way, `()` and `({ })` flip
to resolves together and the entry moves with it. An invalid/ fixture would
survive that commit as an orphan.

SECOND FINDING, forced by the first. Adding the corpus entry turned
TestCorpusResolvingCarriers red, and the failure is a real one rather than
bookkeeping: `nodeTypeImpliedContent#2` was filed in declinedCarriers under
ErrUnnamedNodeType, and the register requires every carrier of a name to reject
with the group's sentinel. The new file carries it and rejects with
ErrUnknownEndpoint.

Both are true, and neither is a misfiling. The alternative is a filler that is a
property block and nothing else; declared as a node type it has no key label set
(ErrUnnamedNodeType), and used as an endpoint it references the type with the
empty key label set, which ADR 0018 makes undeclarable (ErrUnknownEndpoint). One
missing identity, reported from the two sides it can be seen from.

The register's own doctrine has an escape for a name carried by two families —
file it under the class — but that was written for ADR 0019's five value-type
families, which have ErrUnsupportedType. These two have no class, and inventing
one to satisfy a test register would be backwards.

So: a `declinedAlso` map keyed by name, one row, guarded four ways so it cannot
become a laundering channel. Each guard verified by breaking it:

  row deleted                     -> carrier unaccounted (the original failure)
  row for an unregistered name    -> "accounts for nothing"
  row repeating the group sentinel-> rejected
  row naming an unexercised error -> carrier unaccounted

It is a map rather than a field on declinedName so the fifty-odd existing
two-field positional literals stay untouched, and so a second row has to be
argued rather than appended.
close_reason: Closed

title: resolver: ErrOutOfR0Scope has 18 emitters and 5 fixtures — path and unwind bindings rejected untested
description:
An audit of every ErrOutOfR0Scope emitter, prompted by gqlc-bef item 4. The
sentinel has eighteen emitters and five negative fixtures, and the five map 1:1
onto the five proven sites — so thirteen emitters are unproven, and the sentinel
reads as fully covered anyway.

Method: swap ErrOutOfR0Scope for a different sentinel at one site at a time and
run the suite. CAUGHT means some fixture reaches that site; SURVIVED means none
does.

    CAUGHT     scope.go:701   refProjectionType property on var-length edge
    CAUGHT     scope.go:933   PropertyUseWitness property on var-length edge
    CAUGHT     resolve.go:464 untyped edge
    CAUGHT     resolve.go:791 list-of-nodes projection
    CAUGHT     resolve.go:793 list-of-edges projection

    SURVIVED   scope.go:622   wildcard-expanded name resolves to nothing
    SURVIVED   scope.go:642   unknown projection variant
    SURVIVED   scope.go:680   refProjectionType out-of-scope ref
    SURVIVED   scope.go:930   PropertyUseWitness out-of-scope ref
    SURVIVED   scope.go:983   WitnessUse unknown ExprUse position
    SURVIVED   scope.go:986   WitnessUse unknown Use variant
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:24  empty branches
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:133 empty parts
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:200 unsupported binding kind
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:394 no branch scope tables
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:406 Use Branch index out of range
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:453 PropertyUse Part index out of range
    SURVIVED   resolve.go:917 unknown Effect variant

TestSentinelReachability (resolver_test.go:499) asserts every canonical sentinel
has at least one negative fixture. It passes here while 13 of 18 emitters are
untested, because it is per-sentinel, not per-emitter.

## The one that was a real gap, and why the obvious fixture does not pin it

resolve.go:200 is the default arm of the Binding type switch. Five binding kinds
exist (query.go: node, edge, call, path, unwind); the resolver handles three and
rejects path and unwind as out of R0 scope. Both are ordinary Cypher —
`MATCH p = ...` and `UNWIND ... AS x` — and the parser emits them, verified
directly. Neither had a fixture.

Writing the obvious ones does not help:

    MATCH p = (a:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person) RETURN p
    UNWIND [1, 2, 3] AS x RETURN x

Both pass, and both are useless. Delete the rejection arm and they *still* fail
with ErrOutOfR0Scope, because p / x are then unbound and the projection walk
raises the same sentinel from scope.go:680. Measured: the sentinel-swap mutation
is caught, but dropping the arm outright survives. The guard and its own
downstream fallthrough collide on one sentinel, so errors.Is cannot separate
them.

The fix is in the fixture. Exercise the rejection without naming the rejected
binding, so that removing the guard makes the query *succeed* rather than fail
identically:

    MATCH p = (a:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person) RETURN a
    MATCH (a:Person) UNWIND [1, 2, 3] AS x RETURN a

Both mutations are then caught by exactly these two fixtures.

This also explains scope.go:680's SURVIVED above: with :200 intact, nothing
reaches :680, and with :200 relaxed, :680 covers for it. They mask each other
through the sentinel, across two files. See bd memory
sweep-negative-fixture-must-not-name-rejected-binding.

## The other twelve

Ten are defensive tripwires on closed sums or resolver-internal invariants, and
should not be re-filed:

  scope.go:642, :983, :986 and resolve.go:917  default arms of closed type
        switches / a position enum. Unreachable without adding a variant.
  scope.go:622  the comment says it outright — a name in scopeOrder that
        resolves to nothing is a resolver-side bug.
  resolve.go:24, :133  empty branches / empty parts; the parser never emits an
        empty query.
