title: codegen: the §3 shadow doc describes one gate; the parameter side has two
notes:
Residue R-B from the Linus review of PR #937 (merged as 3d0bcdc9, GH #741).

docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md's §3 row at :222 justifies why the
tagged //gqlc:unreachable sites stay unreached with "the shadow rests on the two
arm lists being equal". That is an accurate description of the COLUMN side.

For the PARAMETER side it is incomplete. The reviewer's MU-L17 deleted Phase A's
parameter gate `if !ok { return }` (leaving the assertion as `prop, _ := ...`)
and measured: the mutation was KILLED by the conformance suite, but
TestSentinelTaxonomy/TestUnreachedBranchesAreUnreached PASSED. prepare.go:821
stayed unreached because the width check `tm.Property(prop.Type)` is a SECOND
shadow that catches the zero-value `prop` first. Only when MU-L18 bypassed BOTH
parameter gates did the fence go RED naming `param-type-invariant`.

So: the parameter shadow is two gates deep (type assertion + width check), and
the doc names one. Nothing in the doc is FALSE — the reviewer graded it "a doc
nuance, not a false claim", which is why it was residue and not a blocker.

Scope: amend the §3 justification so the parameter row states both gates, or
scope :222's sentence to the column side. Prefer wording that quantifies
nothing if a count would rot.

Do not re-derive from this note alone — verify at the then-current head that
both gates still exist and that MU-L17 still reproduces (single-gate deletion
must leave TestUnreachedBranchesAreUnreached green). If a later change collapsed
the two gates into one, the doc became correct and this bead closes as obsolete.

title: docs/adr/0025: the account of what the two Scalar pins redden under-counts, and one pin is unobservable in a whole-package run
description:
Non-blocking residue from PR #956 (bead gqlc-0otp), found by the round-1 Linus review. All four items are the same class: the merged text's account of its own pins is imprecise. None is a false universal; each under-claims rather than over-claims, which is the safe direction, so this was correctly graded non-blocking.

1. 'reddens both, at the subtest for the text that lost it' under-counts. Deleting the 'any' arm reddens Property/any, Property/[]any AND Scalar/any — three subtests, not one. The same under-report appears in the PR body's table.

2. Under the delete-'map[string]any' mutation, a whole-package run never reaches the closure pin at all: decodeFunc panics and the test binary dies. 'Reddens both' is only observable when the two are run separately. Worth stating, because a future reader reproducing the claim the obvious way will not see what the sentence promises.

3. 'only mention of agtypeMap outside its own declaration' — each golden also carries its doc comment.

4. The PR body says agtypeString 'is reached only through carrier == "string"'. True of decodeFunc's routing, which is the scope the sentence is about, but emitted helper bodies call agtypeString directly at render_models.go:519, :547 and :621. The PR page is a durable carrier, so the imprecision persists; not worth a CI-cancelling body edit on a merged PR, but worth recording here.

Also noted and NOT filed as a defect: types.go:204 still carries the unqualified 'unservedColumn refuses... so no emitted code reaches them'. Pre-existing and not false — the reviewer verified tm.Scalar has exactly two non-test callers (prepare.go:811, :1100), every route to them is refused by a named arm of unservedColumn, and the ScalarNull list path returns 'any' without calling tm.Scalar at all.

Acceptance: correct items 1-3 in the tree. Item 4 can only be fixed on the PR page or left recorded here.

title: query: the *ast.FuncType skip guard in sealedsum_test.go is not load-bearing
description:
Residue from PR #940 (bead gqlc-1vkb), filed by the round-3 Linus review.

internal/query/sealedsum_test.go's AST walk carries a skip arm for *ast.FuncType. Deleting that arm leaves the whole suite green: no fixture in internal/query declares a func-typed field or a func literal whose parameter list would reach the arm, so the guard classifies nothing on this corpus.

Two readings, both worth resolving:
 (a) the arm is dead and should go, or
 (b) it guards a shape that WILL appear and needs a fixture that fails without it.

Decide which, and if (b), add the fixture so the arm is measured. Note the measurement trap recorded on gqlc-1vkb: parseQueryPackage does os.ReadDir(".") + parser.ParseFile on real disk paths, so 'go test -overlay' does NOT reach it and a mutation row against this file reads as a vacuous PASS. Mutate on disk in a throwaway worktree with a positive control.
close_reason: Duplicate of gqlc-5ckc, which is the same finding filed 4 minutes earlier (22:28:32Z vs 22:32:24Z) from PR #940's round-3 residue. I created this one after searching the corpus with 'bd list --json', which silently caps at 50 rows while 55 beads exist — the original was outside the window and read as absent. gqlc-5ckc now carries this bead's full description (the two readings, and the parseQueryPackage/-overlay measurement trap). Work the finding on gqlc-5ckc.

title: query: the *ast.FuncType skip guard in sealedsum_test.go is not load-bearing
description:
Residue from PR #940 (bead gqlc-1vkb), filed by the round-3 Linus review.

internal/query/sealedsum_test.go's AST walk carries a skip arm for *ast.FuncType. Deleting that arm leaves the whole suite green: no fixture in internal/query declares a func-typed field or a func literal whose parameter list would reach the arm, so the guard classifies nothing on this corpus.

Two readings, both worth resolving:
 (a) the arm is dead and should go, or
 (b) it guards a shape that WILL appear and needs a fixture that fails without it.

Decide which, and if (b), add the fixture so the arm is measured. Note the measurement trap recorded on gqlc-1vkb: parseQueryPackage does os.ReadDir(".") + parser.ParseFile on real disk paths, so 'go test -overlay' does NOT reach it and a mutation row against this file reads as a vacuous PASS. Mutate on disk in a throwaway worktree with a positive control.
notes:
Found by Linus review of PR #940 round 3 (head 96b33b72), finding F2, non-blocking.

internal/query/sealedsum_test.go:543 has 'if _, isMethod := field.Type.(*ast.FuncType); !isMethod { continue }'. Mutation MX1 deletes the guard outright and NOTHING goes red — field.Names is empty for every non-method interface field, so the loop already skips them.

The guard's comment describes it accurately; it simply is not doing work. Inverting it (MX1b, !isMethod -> isMethod) IS killed by table_covers_every_interface_with_its_own_marker, so the surrounding walk is genuinely pinned — only this arm is redundant.

Decide: delete it, or keep it and say it is belt-and-braces rather than implying it is what makes the walk correct. Note PR #940's body cites this guard as what makes a claim 'checkable', which is weaker than it reads.

title: codegen/age: the testdata/ sweep exclusion is justified as 'the generator's OUTPUT', which it is not
description:
Found during PR #913 round-3 review (Linus nit N8), measured not guessed.

The age type sweep excludes testdata/ with the justification that 'that tree is the generator's OUTPUT'. It is not. testdata/ holds 4 .gql generator INPUTS plus a hand-written driver template. The generator's actual output goes to a t.TempDir().

The exclusion itself is SAFE — the reviewer measured 0 .go files and 0 typeMap occurrences under testdata/ — so this is not a live hole. Only the stated reason is false.

This is the repository's signature defect class: a justification in prose that the tree falsifies. It matters because the next person to widen or narrow the exclusion will reason from the false premise. If testdata/ ever grows a .go file, 'it's output, so it can't carry a type' is the sentence that will let it through unswept.

Fix: state the true reason (no .go files, and the tree is fixture input the sweep has no claim over) instead of the false one.

title: codegen/age: returnedGoType reads first.X and drops first.Y, so a concatenated literal return type is unswept
description:
Found during PR #913 round-3 review (Linus nit N9), measured not guessed.

internal/codegen/age's type sweep resolves a function's returned Go type via returnedGoType, which reads only first.X of the return expression and never reads first.Y. So a return whose RHS is a concatenation of literals is invisible to the sweep:

    return "[]" + "decimal.Decimal", true

is count-preserving (md5 7fac379e) and the sweep PASSES with 23 subtests. A carrier introduced this way would be unswept.

Not a blocker on #913 because (a) the package is still RED elsewhere for that mutation, and (b) the operative disclosure sitting beside the claim is true. But the prose there says 'the AST cannot close it', which is false as stated — the AST can close it; this walk does not.

Two fixes are possible: read the full binary expression when the RHS is a concatenation of literals, or narrow the prose to say what the walk actually does. Prefer the former; the latter alone leaves the hole.

title: codegen: paramFieldName preserves ALL-CAPS, so an ALL-CAPS edge label mangles to an ALL-CAPS or run-together Go type name
description:
Found while reviewing PR #932 (bd gqlc-2sb8). Not in that PR's territory — filed, not fixed.

internal/codegen/names.go:42 — paramFieldName splits the raw name on '_', capitalises the first rune of each non-ALL-CAPS segment, and passes ALL-CAPS segments through unchanged (the isAllCaps branch, names.go:66).

internal/codegen/prepare.go:488 — the derived name for an edge type routes its label through that same paramFieldName, then checks exportedGoIdent (^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$, names.go:35).

Both of those checks pass on ALL-CAPS input, so the Go type name a Neo4j-idiomatic edge label derives is:

- LINKED -> LINKED (a Go type named LINKED)
- ACTED_IN -> ACTEDIN (segments run together, no word boundary left)

Both are valid exported Go identifiers, so nothing refuses them and no test row pins them. Neo4j's own convention is SCREAMING_SNAKE relationship types, so this is the shape a real schema is most likely to hit.

Undecided and part of the work: whether the right answer is Linked / ActedIn (title-case every segment when the whole label is ALL-CAPS), or to keep the pass-through and pin it as intended. paramFieldName's ALL-CAPS branch exists for parameter names ($ID, $URL), where preserving the caps is the point — an edge label is a second caller with a different convention, so a fix has to not regress the parameter case.

title: resolver: validated.go's ResolvedType doc points at gqlc-edze as an open question
description:
internal/resolver/validated.go:106 ends ResolvedType's doc comment with:

    Whether the codegen boundary should normalise them away instead of
    refusing them is gqlc-edze's question.

gqlc-edze answered it (PR #937): the default arms over resolver.ResolvedType refuse, permanently, and their rows stay in §2 of docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md. Normalising pointer forms to value forms at Prepare's boundary closes nothing, since an embedder is neither a value form nor a pointer form and arrives at the default either way; §5.1 step 5 of the taxonomy now records the posture.

So the line points a reader at a closed bead for an answer that is written down. Replace it with the posture and a pointer to the taxonomy's §5.1 step 5.

Left out of #937 on territory: internal/resolver was another team's live surface in that wave.

title: bdguard: the reopen recency condition is a shape check, not an anti-forgery control
description:
`.beads/allowed-reopens.txt` grants an exemption when the head record's
`updated_at` is strictly later than base's (plus the sha-citation condition and
the reachability veto). Base is read with `git show <ref>:.beads/issues.jsonl`,
so a PR's tree cannot restate it — but HEAD's `updated_at` is just a field in a
file the PR author is editing.

So the recency condition separates the two shapes it was built for — a stale
export copied forward before a close (updated_at at or behind base's) from a
correction written after it (ahead) — and it does that mechanically. What it
does not do is resist a hand-written timestamp: an author who edits
`.beads/issues.jsonl` to bump one bead's `updated_at` past base's, and adds the
matching `<bead-id> <closing-sha>` line, is granted.

That is not obviously wrong. The declaration file is deliberately read at the
PR head so the exemption lands in the diff a reviewer already reads, exactly as
`.beads/allowed-drops.txt` does; the human declaration is the authority and the
machine conditions bound what can be declared. The cost of the forgery is that
it is two visible edits rather than none.

Worth deciding explicitly rather than leaving implicit:

- Whether the export's `updated_at` for a declared id should be cross-checked
  against the bd DB (`refs/dolt/data`) rather than trusted from the file.
- Or whether to state in `allowed-reopens.txt`'s header that the recency
  condition is a shape check, not an anti-forgery control, so nobody later
  reads it as the latter.

Discovered while landing bd gqlc-npyp (PR for GH #922).

title: spec fence: ADR 0029 and specfence_test.go each carry a claim their own measurements falsify
description:
Residue from the round-7 review of PR #804 (merged as e7735736). The reviewer
declined to block on these: the normative spec text is correct, the code is
correct, and round 6 had already graded the same class in the same file as a
nit. Blocking round 7 on comment prose would have manufactured an eighth round.
They are still wrong, and they are the kind of wrong that misleads the next
reader about WHY a design choice was made.

1. `docs/adr/0029-the-codegen-spec-fence.md:245`

   "Neither direction can be closed by a better fence rule, because the
   line-opening test is reached only by a run of three or more."

   The reason attaches to direction B, not direction A. Measured: the option-2
   fence fix DOES close direction A -- probing the real `scanBareSigs` shows
   the line-opening triple go from 0 sigs to 1, with 82 corpus documents and
   17 of 18 rows still green.

   The CONCLUSION survives, for a different reason: under that fix, a
   line-opening triple *inside* a fenced block becomes a fresh divergence,
   because cmark renders it literal. That is exactly what
   `internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go:1460-1462` already says
   correctly. So the fix is to give ADR 0029 the reason the test file already
   has, not to change the conclusion.

2. `internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go:1843`

   "A tab-indented run is never a fence to cmark-gfm."

   False. Inside a list item the ticks ARE consumed and it IS a fence -- which
   is the construct the immediately preceding sentence itself names. Behaviour
   is correct either way; the sentence is not.

   This is the house no-universals defect: a `never` that the surrounding prose
   falsifies two lines up.

3. Smaller, same file family:
   - `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md:763` -- "on every spelling measured" is
     ambiguous between "every spelling we measured" and "every spelling there
     is".
   - `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md:1446` -- "Two divergences are measured"
     reads closed, but it is a floor: a third is pinned at :1094.
   - `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md:41` -- one 30-column line the rewrap
     commit missed.

ACCEPTANCE. Each sentence is true of the tree, and item 2 states the negative
(what a tab-indented run IS a fence for) rather than asserting a universal.
Item 1 should name direction B explicitly rather than saying "neither
direction". No new universal introduced by the fix.

title: codegen/neo4j: the corpus edge type carries a subset of the widths, so BYTES / TIMESTAMP element carriers and the third nesting depth run on dbtype.Node alone
description:
Measured on gqlc-2sb8 at 92ebb9a7 (branch feat/neo4j-corpus-edge-type).

The Edgy edge type added there declares rank (INT32), ranks (LIST<INT32>), matrix (LIST<LIST<INT64>>), payload (ANY VALUE), loose (LIST), depths (LIST<FLOAT32>) and weight (FLOAT32). Between them those reach the emitter's narrowing-scalar, nullable-narrowing-scalar, walked-list, nested-walk, walked-nullable-list, unwalked-[]any and shapeless arms over dbtype.Relationship.

Three things the node types exercise are not on the edge:

- LIST<BYTES>, whose elements the driver hands back as []byte and which isSliceType excludes from the walk;
- LIST<TIMESTAMP>, whose element carrier is time.Time and which moves renderModels' 'time' import gate;
- the third nesting depth (LIST<LIST<LIST<...>>>), which is where writeSliceNarrow's accumulator locals first nest one inside another.

The emitter code for those arms is shared between the two entity kinds — writeEntityFieldDecode branches on e.Kind only for the carrier type and the argument name — so a defect specific to the edge kind in one of them is what stays unmeasured, not the arm itself. That is why this is P3 and not P2.

Not blocking gqlc-2sb8.
notes:
2026-08-17, PR #932 review round 2 — this bead's own inventory was incomplete, in the same way the PR's prose was.

Re-derived from the emission for testdata/corpus_schema.gql (Generate at 471e3891, models.go). The per-property arms are eight, not seven: writeEntityFieldDecode (render_models.go:214) branches nullable/non-nullable x {walked slice, narrow-convert, plain assign} = six, and writeShapelessFieldDecode (render_models.go:264) carries two more. The 'nested-walk' this description lists is not one of them — it is writeSliceNarrow recursing, inside the walked-slice arm.

Edgy's seven properties land on SIX of those eight:
  depths  -> nullable walked slice
  weight  -> nullable narrow-convert
  loose   -> nullable plain assign (out.Loose = &s; []any is excluded from isSliceType)
  matrix  -> non-nullable walked slice
  ranks   -> non-nullable walked slice  (same arm as matrix)
  rank    -> non-nullable narrow-convert
  payload -> non-nullable shapeless

So the mapping is neither onto nor one-to-one. Two arms run off dbtype.Node only and never off the Relationship in this fixture, in addition to the three widths already listed here:

  - non-nullable plain assign: out.Loose = value1 in decodeBin (loose :: LIST NOT NULL), also decodeScalar's active and id. Edgy has no non-nullable property whose carrier already equals its emitted Go type.
  - nullable shapeless: out.Maybe = &v in decodeAnything (maybe :: ANY VALUE). Edgy has no nullable ANY VALUE.

Both are now named in the corpus_schema.gql header comment and in PR #932's body. Whoever picks this bead up should treat it as five items, not three.

title: bdguard: the git boundary (run, showAtRef, gitRefContaining) has no automated test
description:
internal/tools/bdguard/main_test.go states at the top that it targets check() directly, with no git shellout, and that the git boundary of run() is exercised only by an end-to-end incident replay recorded in a PR body. The stated reason is that earlier attempts to stage a real repo per test occasionally landed git calls in the outer worktree despite GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES.

gqlc-npyp added a third shellout, gitRefContaining, behind the same boundary. It is injected into check() as a func value, so its CALLERS are covered by fakes, but the function itself — cat-file -e, for-each-ref --contains, merge-base --is-ancestor, and the decision to collapse every failure into "" — is verified only by hand. Same standing as showAtRef, which has been in that position since the tool landed.

What a test would have to do: build a scratch repo outside the worktree (t.TempDir plus GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE set explicitly rather than relying on cwd, which is what previously leaked), commit twice, delete the branch, and assert that a referenced sha names a ref and an orphaned one returns "". Also worth pinning: a sha the repo does not have at all returns "" rather than erroring out of the run.

Not blocking: the veto direction means a wrong "" grants no exemption on its own — the other two conditions still have to hold — and a wrong non-empty answer only refuses a declaration, which is loud.

title: bdguard: the reachability veto is inert in CI because the checkout is depth-1
description:
gqlc-npyp's reopened-arm exemption has three conditions. The third — no ref in this checkout contains the declared closing sha — is a veto: it can refuse a declaration, never grant one. It is inert in CI.

.github/workflows/ci.yml uses `actions/checkout@v4` with the default fetch-depth of 1, then `git fetch --depth=1 origin \$BASE_SHA` before `just bd-export-monotonic`. In that clone `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` fails for anything outside the fetched pack, so gitRefContaining returns "" and the veto says nothing. The two conditions that do the work in CI are the base close_reason citation and the updated_at ordering, both of which are answerable from the two files alone; the veto only bites under `just bd-export-monotonic-local`, where the dev worktree has full history and remote-tracking refs.

Making it bite in CI needs a workflow change (fetch-depth: 0, or a targeted fetch of the declared shas), which is outside gqlc-npyp's territory — ci.yml was owned elsewhere in that wave. Weigh it against the reason the job fetches depth-1 in the first place: the comment there says cost is deliberately O(1) in history size. A targeted `git fetch origin <declared-sha>` per entry in .beads/allowed-reopens.txt is O(entries) and keeps that property; a blanket fetch-depth: 0 does not.

Note the veto is weak even with full history: gqlc squash-merges and deletes the branch, so an EARNED close's cited branch sha is orphaned as surely as an unearned one's. It bites on the narrower case where the branch is still pushed and its remote-tracking ref exists.

title: liverecipes: subtract's empty-taken path is asserted in prose but pinned by no row
description:
PR #882 round 3 rewrote the vacuity-guard comment in internal/liverecipes/split.go
to say that Read builds Local by removing CI from the justfile's live invocations,
'which makes an empty CI the state where every live invocation sits in Local rather
than one where there are none'.

That is true — subtract(all, nil) leaves the 'remaining' map empty, so no element is
skipped and every invocation accumulates into 'left' — but no row exercises it.

TestSubtractLeavesLocalRecipesOnlyCIDoesNotReach (split_internal_test.go:207) calls
subtract with a PARTIAL taken and a FULL taken, never an EMPTY one. So a short-circuit
like 'if len(taken) == 0 { return nil }' would survive the suite while falsifying the
sentence the comment now makes.

Remedy: one assertion, subtract(all, nil) returns all of them.

Not fixed in #882: adding it after CI had gone green would have cost a full re-run of
seven required contexts at round 3, for a clause with no realistic mutation. Filed
instead so the claim is tracked rather than assumed.

title: query: internal/query's sealed sums restate the marker-closes-the-sum universal
description:
`gqlc-856f` corrected the "unexported marker seals the sum" universal in
`internal/resolver/validated.go` and in `AGENTS.md`. Its widened sweep — keyed on
the claim (`exhaustive`, `cannot implement`, `same package`, `every case`,
`smuggle`, `no other type`) rather than on `Resolved*` names — found the same
universal restated about `internal/query`'s own sums, which no earlier sweep
could reach because none of them names a `Resolved*` type.

Sites, all on `origin/master` at `dc8d10fa`:

- `internal/query/query.go:289` (`Binding`), `:698` (`PathMember`), `:1174`
  (`Endpoint`), `:1253` (`Projection`), `:1542` (`Use`), `:2017` (`Effect`) —
  each says "It is a closed sum of A, B, C — **no other type can implement it**
  — so a X is exactly one of the N."
- `internal/query/type.go:12-13` — "sealed sum via the private `isType()` marker
  — **no foreign package can add a variant**, so switching on a Type is
  exhaustive across the parser+resolver boundary."
- `internal/query/query_test.go:379` and `:477` — "The sealed interfaces close
  the sums: **only the four/five package-defined variants satisfy them**, so a
  binding/endpoint is always exactly one known shape." This one says *satisfy*,
  which is the half that is false; the other two say *implement*.

## Compile witness (measured, not asserted)

In a detached worktree, appended to `internal/query/query_test.go`, which is
`package query_test`:

    type qwEmbedBinding struct{ query.NodeBinding }
    var _ query.Binding = qwEmbedBinding{}
    var _ query.Binding = &query.NodeBinding{}
    type qwEmbedType struct{ query.TypeBool }
    var _ query.Type = qwEmbedType{}

    $ go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/query/
    rc=0

Go promotes an embedded type's unexported methods, and a pointer's method set
contains its value methods, so both constructions obtain the marker from any
package in the module. Neither matches a `case query.NodeBinding:` arm, so every
type switch over these interfaces reaches its default or leaves the switch on
them. The marker seals *declaration* — a from-scratch foreign variant is a
compile error — not *inhabitation*.

## What is NOT established here

Whether any of those switches has a default documented as dead on this
reasoning, or a `//gqlc:unreachable` tag resting on it, the way
`internal/codegen` did for `resolver.ResolvedType` (`gqlc-h4ug`). That is the
part worth measuring before deciding whether this is prose-only. The
`internal/query` dispatch sites were not audited by `gqlc-856f`; only the 31
`resolver.ResolvedType` sites were.

## Why filed rather than fixed

`internal/query/**` is outside `gqlc-856f`'s acceptance criterion, which is
`resolver.ResolvedType`. Branch `fix/resolver-sealed-sum-claim` stayed inside
`internal/resolver` and `AGENTS.md`.

## Suggested shape

Use the phrasing `internal/resolver/sealedsum_test.go:126-128` and
`AGENTS.md:105-113` now use: a method of that name in another package does not
satisfy the interface, so the variants are the whole set of types that *declare*
the marker; the set that *satisfies* it is unbounded. If a dispatch audit finds
a switch relying on totality, that is a separate defect from the prose.

Added TestQuerySumsAreNotClosed/table_covers_every_marker-sealed_interface: sealedInterfaces() reads every interface in the package sources naming an unexported method of its own (off the existing parseQueryPackage AST walk) and requires that iface->markers map to equal the table's. ## Round 3 (PR #940, ff74d98f -> 96b33b72) — reviewer's single blocker closed

BLOCKER B1-r2: typing.go's commonType doc, rewritten in round 2 to close r1's B2,
replaced one false claim with another: "two entries with equal String therefore
agree on everything the model carries ... including the pointer and embedding
forms". Independently reproduced with `go test -overlay` against the REAL
applyListOp and unwindElementType (list-op ctx built with exactly one child
expression, i.e. the index path):

  query.TypeList / struct{query.TypeList} / *query.TypeList all String() == "list<int>"
  all three promote Element() == int
  applyListOp:       value -> int  | embedder -> unknown | pointer -> unknown
  unwindElementType: value -> int  | embedder -> unknown | pointer -> unknown
  type switch:       value -> case query.TypeList; other two -> DEFAULT
  commonType([embedder, value]) -> embedder -> applyListOp -> unknown
  commonType([value, embedder]) -> value    -> applyListOp -> int

i.e. an all-equal-String slice's list-op result depends on its ORDER. The two
forms the sentence named by hand were exactly the two that disagree.

Chose close (a) (scope to the wire name + name the assertions) over (b) (delete
the clause): the comment exists to justify comparing String rather than the
concrete type, so (b) leaves the measured hazard documented nowhere at the
function that creates it, and a bare "String is the canonical wire name" still
implies sufficiency by omission where sufficiency is measurably false.

Named the assertions with "such as", NOT as a list: a module-wide grep finds a
THIRD site that discriminates on the concrete TypeList,
internal/resolver/resolve.go:1283 (resolveType). A two-item list would have been
the same defect class again.

Kept "(see query.Type's doc comment)": self-refuting only while the citing
sentence asserted agreement; with the polarity flipped, type.go:17-26 ("reaches
its default on them") corroborates it.

NIT N1-r2 also closed: sealedInterfaces' limit said embedded methods "stay on the
embedded interface's own entry", false for an anonymous interface literal. Now
states what the walk skips.

MEASUREMENT NOTE worth keeping: `go test -overlay` is a BUILD overlay. It does
NOT reach sealedsum_test.go's parseQueryPackage, which does os.ReadDir(".") +
parser.ParseFile on real disk paths. My first MC reproduction PASSed vacuously
because the walk never saw the mutated file. Redone on disk in a throwaway

"Ranking":["isRanking"]) proving the walk was live.

title: docs: AGENTS.md states the testify rule with no exception, but govulncheck forces bare testing.T in two packages
description:
AGENTS.md's Tests section says "Use testify ... Not bare testing.T" with no exception.

Two packages must break it to stay inside govulncheck's call graph:

- internal/tools/modscope/main_test.go — pre-existing, in-package, imports no testify.
- internal/liverecipes/split_internal_test.go — added by gqlc-df3d (PR #882).

The forcing constraint is the vuln gate itself. At 771b7447 (before the split) `just vuln` is rc=1 naming internal/liverecipes: an in-package test that imports third-party code makes govulncheck discard the in-package test variant together with everything only it imports (bd gqlc-m5rc). The gate's own message prescribes the remedy that was applied — move the exported-surface tests to an external test package, keep in-package only the ones that need unexported state.

So the deviation is forced, not a style choice, and the drift is AGENTS.md's: the rule is stated as a universal while the tree has two standing exceptions.

Fix: record the exception in AGENTS.md's Tests section, naming the govulncheck constraint and the shape that satisfies both (external test package by default; bare testing.T in-package where unexported state is needed).

Found by the adversarial review of PR #882 (NIT 3). Ruled residue, not a change to that branch: AGENTS.md is outside its territory and the deviation there is correct as shipped.

title: codegen/age: propertyWidths says it is taken from the property table; it is written out by hand
codegen spec fence: a parameter list inside a code block is not read
description:
The spec fence's signature sweep reads a parameter list out of an inline code
span: the anchor is a run of backticks immediately before `ctx context.Context`,
and the matching run of the same length ends the list. A **code block** carries
no such span, so a parameter list written on its own line inside one is not read
at all.

Three spellings, each measured first-party on `docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift`
(inserted into `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` §5.3, immediately before the
`` **`<return>`** `` bullet — the section `gqlc-rz0l` exists to correct — then
`go test -run '^TestSpecMethodArgIsGeneratorOwned$|^TestSpecParamsMapBindsGeneratorOwnedValue$|^TestSpecBareSigScannerDetectsDrift$' ./internal/codegen/conformance/`,
compile-screened with `go test -c -o /dev/null`, reverted clean):

1. a ```` ``` ````-fenced block with no info string whose body is the bare line
   `ctx context.Context, minAge int64` — **green**;
2. the same block opened as ```` ```go ```` — **green**;
3. a four-space-indented block with the same body — **green**.

The control, the identical list inside a one-backtick span on a prose line, is
red (`TestSpecMethodArgIsGeneratorOwned`, "documented method argument is not
generator-owned"). So the capture vector `gqlc-lhs3` removed can be restated in
a spec, in the most normative-looking place a spec has, and the fence says
nothing.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

The fence scans raw markdown bytes with one anchor per shape. Reading a code
block means block-level markdown parsing — tracking fence open/close state and
indentation across the whole document, before any anchor runs — and then
deciding what a multi-line block body even *is* for a scanner that grades one
parameter list at a time. A body is not a signature; it is lines, and collapsing
them into one string to grade produces a "parameter list" no reader wrote.

The cheap version is worse than the gap: dropping the block rule and letting a
fence's own ```` ``` ```` delimiter open a span makes the whole block body one
graded list, so a block holding several lines grades collapsed text and a block
opened with an info string still escapes — coverage that depends on whether an
author typed `go` after the fence.

Pinned rather than left implicit: `TestSpecBareSigScannerDetectsDrift` carries
ALLOW rows for the fenced and the indented spelling, so the skip is a written
expectation and a scanner change that starts reading blocks is red on the pin.

## Scope

The **parenthesis-less** spelling only. The paren anchor needs no code span, so
`scanSpecSigs` reads a code block like any other text: a fenced or indented
block holding
`func (q *Queries) PersonByAge(ctx context.Context, minAge int64) error` is
**red** (`TestSpecMethodArgIsGeneratorOwned`), measured the same way. What a
block hides is a list with the parentheses taken off it.

This is also the code-block half only. A code span written *inside* a fenced block is
read like any other span (there is a REJECT row for it), and the run rule means
`` ``ctx context.Context, minAge int64`` `` is read too — that half is closed on
this branch. What is left is a list with no span around it, which is the same
surface as a list written into running prose (`gqlc-offa`, `gqlc-e143`).

Related: `gqlc-offa` (a binding stated with no `map[string]any` literal around
it), `gqlc-e143` (prose beside an intact graded span), `gqlc-x2sg` (an exhibit's
exemption taken by a claim spelled the same way), `gqlc-0rjn` (one graded site
per listed document is the floor).

title: codegen: the //gqlc:unreachable fence is a passing check, never proven to fail
description:
`just test-codegen-fence` exits 0 and prints "0 issues.", and CI has a required
`codegen-fence` context that is green. Nobody has shown it goes RED.

The three live tags it fences are `internal/codegen/prepare.go:724`
(`param-type-invariant`), `:741` (`row-field-alias`) and `:898`
(`column-type-invariant`). Each is documented dead-by-named-shadow in
`docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md` §3.

## Why this is worth a row

A detector that exits 0 is not a gate. The fence's whole value is the claim
"if a branch tagged //gqlc:unreachable is ever executed, this fails". That
claim is currently unmeasured. The failure mode is fail-silent: if the fence
stopped instrumenting those sites — a tag typo, a moved build tag, a changed
coverage path — it would keep printing "0 issues." and keep the required
context green, and the shadow argument in §3 would be resting on nothing.

## Why it was not done on gqlc-856f / PR #881

Pre-existing machinery that branch does not touch, and the independent reviewer
of #881 explicitly flagged it as separate work rather than something #881 owed.
Widening #881 to certify it would have crossed into `internal/codegen`, held by
other open PRs.

## Acceptance

A mutation row that makes one tagged branch reachable — or removes the tag while
leaving the branch dead — and shows `just test-codegen-fence` exits NON-ZERO,
naming the site it reports. Restore verified by checksum. If the fence turns out
not to fail on that mutation, that is the finding, and this bead becomes the fix.

title: resolver: the corpus sweep resolves every cell under regR7, so the registry axis of CALL diagnostics is uncovered
description:
TestCorpusSweepManifest (gqlc-yb0w, PR for #841) crosses 310 fixture queries against 38 fixture schemas, and every one of the 11780 cells is resolved as New(sch, WithRegistry(regR7)). WithRegistry is the resolver's only Option (internal/resolver/resolver.go:48), so the schema axis and the query axis are swept and the registry axis is a constant.

ErrCallArgAssignability and the R7 YIELD column typing arms read the registry. A change to one of those diagnostics that only manifests under a registry other than regR7 — a different signature set, a missing procedure, a different param token — moves no cell in the sweep.

FIX candidates: add a second registry to the cross product (regR7 plus an empty or narrowed registry) and key manifest cells on (query, schema, registry); or bound the claim explicitly and leave the registry axis to the targeted R7 fixtures.

Cost note: the sweep runs 11780 cells in ~0.15s, so a second registry roughly doubles a cheap test and doubles the manifest, which is already 1.4MB.

PROVENANCE: self-review of the gqlc-yb0w branch.

title: resolver: the corpus sweep's accept column digests the marshalled model, so a field no MarshalJSON emits is outside it
description:
TestCorpusSweepManifest (gqlc-yb0w, PR for #841) records an accepting cell as a digest of json.Marshal(ValidatedQuery). Every ResolvedType in internal/resolver/validated.go writes its own MarshalJSON emitting an explicit anonymous struct, so the digest reaches exactly the fields those methods list. A field added to a ResolvedType struct but not to its MarshalJSON is invisible to the sweep's accept column.

This is the SAME bound the existing test/data/resolver/valid/*.validated.golden.json files already carry — TestValid marshals through the same methods — so the sweep is not weaker than what shipped, but it is not stronger on this axis either, and the bead it came from (gqlc-yb0w) is about a quadrant compared on too little.

Same family as gqlc-yb0w itself: a guard structural on one axis (which cells) and bounded on another (what a cell's value records).

FIX candidates: a reflect-based census asserting every exported field of every ResolvedType appears in that type's MarshalJSON output for at least one corpus cell; or fold the check into the existing sealed-sum work (PR #881 holds validated.go and sealedsum_test.go, so this must sequence after it).

PROVENANCE: self-review of the gqlc-yb0w branch, filed rather than fixed because validated.go is held by PR #881.

title: check-pr-closes: a PR that names no bead anywhere is never checked
description:
Found while implementing gqlc-1ekq (PR for bd gqlc-1ekq).

gqlc-1ekq's premise is that dodging the bead id in the branch name is "not a
control: it is invisible, unenforced". Its fix gives the declared alternative
(`Refs: <bead> #<issue>`), so an author who WANTS to say "touches, does not
resolve" now has a checkable way to. It does not remove the undeclared path:
a PR whose body has no Bead:/Refs: line and whose branch carries no id exits
at "No bead on this PR -> pass" having read nothing.

That path cannot be closed from the body alone; closing it means requiring
every PR to declare a bead (or an explicit "no bead"), which is a policy
change with a cost on trivial PRs, and would want the same treatment gqlc-1ekq
got: its own review.

ACCEPTANCE. Decide whether an undeclared PR is a refusal. If it is, the
refusal has to name both escapes (a `Bead:` line and a `Refs:` line) and there
has to be a declared spelling for "this PR is about no bead", with a row each.

title: check-pr-closes: a Bead: line naming a mirror-less bead still overrides a branch that names a mirrored one
description:
Found while implementing gqlc-1ekq (PR for bd gqlc-1ekq).

A body declaration outranks the branch name unconditionally, and that
precedence is deliberate and pinned ("a Bead line in the body overrides the
branch name"). The consequence is that on branch `fix/gqlc-<mirrored>-thing`,
a body line `Bead: gqlc-<some-bead-with-no-external_ref>` resolves to the
mirror-less bead, takes the "no GH mirror -> pass" exit, and the mirrored bead
the branch names is never examined. One line, no diff, nothing in the log.

The new `Refs:` opt-out from gqlc-1ekq does NOT have this hole: it refuses
when the branch names a different bead ("an opt-out naming a bead the branch
does not is refused"). `Bead:` was left alone because tightening it the same
way would newly refuse PRs that legitimately retarget, and because the escape
predates that branch.

ACCEPTANCE. Decide whether a `Bead:` line that disagrees with a bead id in the
branch name is a refusal, a warning annotation, or stays a silent pass; if it
becomes anything louder, a row per verdict in
.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh.

---

## AMENDMENT (PR #901 round 7): the wider variant, which the description above does not cover

The description is written around the *mirror-less bead* variant. There is an
easier and stronger one, reproduced first-party on `master` as well as on the
PR branch, so it is pre-existing rather than PR #901's regression:

    Bead: gqlc-<any well-formed id the export does not carry>

That takes `check-pr-closes.py`'s not-in-export exit (`bead not in export -
skipping`, rc=0). It disables the gate on **any** branch, in one line, and
needs no knowledge of a real bead id — where the mirror-less variant needs one
that exists and has an empty `external_ref`.

That door is held open deliberately: this repo's `.beads/issues.jsonl` trails
the ledger by whole sessions, so a bead created today is legitimately absent,
and PR #901 pins the behaviour with a row (*a bead the export does not carry
does not block the PR*). The rationale is sound. What was missing is that the
consequence was not written down anywhere durable.

**And it can be written invisibly.** `BEAD_IN_BODY` is read over the raw body,
not over `prose_only()`'s, so unlike the `Refs:` marker it is still matched
inside fenced code blocks, HTML comments and `<pre>`/`<code>` blocks. So:

    <!--
    Bead: gqlc-notinexport
    -->

is a gate bypass that no human reading the rendered PR body can see. The only
trace is the one log line in the check run. That asymmetry is deliberate and
argued in the `BEAD_IN_BODY` comment — for a *mirrored* bead a `Bead:` line
ends in a demand for `Closes #N`, so widening where it is read is fail-closed —
but the not-in-export skip is the one exit where the widening is a pass, which
is exactly this issue.

**ACCEPTANCE, extended.** Whatever this issue decides, it has to decide it for
the wider variant and for three carriers, not for the mirror-less variant in
prose alone.
notes:
WIDER THAN THE TITLE RECORDS (independent review of PR #901, confirmed first-party).

This bead is written around the mirror-less-bead variant: a 'Bead:' line naming a bead with no GitHub mirror overrides a branch that names a mirrored one, so the gate demands nothing.

The easier and stronger variant is 'Bead: gqlc-<any well-formed id the export does not carry>'. It takes the not-in-export skip (check-pr-closes.py, the 'bead not in export - skipping' exit), disables the gate on ANY branch in one line, and needs no knowledge of a real bead id. Reproduced identically on master, so it is pre-existing and not PR #901's regression.

PR #901 pins that door open DELIBERATELY (gqlc-zzz5's 'well-formedness, not presence' deviation, plus the row 'a bead the export does not carry does not block the PR'): this repo's export trails the ledger by whole sessions, so a bead created today is legitimately absent. The rationale is sound; what was missing was the consequence being named anywhere. PR #901's body now names it under 'where it is weakest', and check-pr-closes.py's BEAD_IN_BODY comment cites this bead.

WHERE THE 'Bead:' LINE CAN BE WRITTEN (added round 3 of PR #901, measured against GitHub's own renderer via POST /markdown, mode gfm).

BEAD_IN_BODY is read over the raw body, not over prose_only()'s. PR #901 round 3 makes the 'Refs:' opt-out blind to three carriers GitHub does not render as prose - fenced code blocks (CommonMark's rule, not a toggle), HTML comments, and <pre> blocks. 'Bead:' is deliberately NOT given the same treatment, so all three still reach it. So both variants above can be written where no human reading the rendered PR body can see them:

  <!--
  Bead: gqlc-notinexport
  -->

is a one-line gate bypass that is invisible in the rendered body. Same rc=0 'bead not in export - skipping' exit; the only trace is that one log line in the check run.

That asymmetry is deliberate and argued in the BEAD_IN_BODY comment: for a MIRRORED bead a 'Bead:' line ends in the demand for 'Closes #N', so widening where it is read is fail-closed, and narrowing it would newly refuse PRs. The not-in-export skip is the one exit where the widening is a pass, which is exactly this bead.

Whatever this bead decides, it now has to decide it for three carriers rather than for prose alone.

STILL NOT IN ANY PUSHED ARTEFACT AT THE TIME OF WRITING: .beads/issues.jsonl at origin/master 0c214d20 carries this record with no 'notes' key at all, and GH #899's body is the narrow description only. These notes live in the local ledger until a sync moves them. PR #901's body states that rather than claiming the mirror records it.

title: check-pr-closes: a bolded **Bead:** label is not read as a declaration
description:
Found while implementing gqlc-1ekq / gqlc-zzz5 (PR for bd gqlc-1ekq).

BEAD_IN_BODY is `(?i)Bead:\s*(\S*gqlc-\S*)`. The markdown-bolded spelling used
by this repo's own ADRs — `**Bead:** gqlc-h9n.22`, see docs/adr/0022 line 5 —
puts `**` between the colon and the id, so `\s*` does not reach the token and
the line matches nothing at all. The PR then falls back to the branch name, or
to no bead.

PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by that PR: master's regex `(?i)Bead:\s*(gqlc-\S+)`
misses the same spelling. gqlc-zzz5 closed the backticked and trailing-dot
spellings by widening the captured VALUE; this one is about decoration around
the KEYWORD, which is a different position in the pattern.

Direction matters: unlike gqlc-zzz5's spellings, recognising this one newly
DEMANDS a Closes on PRs that today are unchecked, so it is a widening of the
gate and wants its own review rather than a fold-in.

ACCEPTANCE. `**Bead:** gqlc-x` and `**Refs:** gqlc-x #N` resolve as
declarations. A row per spelling in .githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh.

title: decoder_reachability_test.go: the nonReservedWords count is 47, stated as 46
description:
Found by the independent review of PR #847 (/tmp/factory/verdict-847-r2.md) and
recorded as a report-only nit; the PR merged as 11a652ad.

A comment in internal/codegen/conformance/decoder_reachability_test.go states
that GQL.g4's nonReservedWords rule has 46 entries. Counted first-party by the
reviewer, it has 47.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING despite being one digit. The count is not decorative -- it
is offered as the evidence that the list was read rather than skimmed, in support
of the claim that nonReservedWords is the only keyword route into
regularIdentifier. That surrounding claim was verified independently and is
CORRECT: the reviewer walked labelName -> identifier -> regularIdentifier (exactly
2 alternatives) and closed the ANTLR lexer-ordering trap by finding
REGULAR_IDENTIFIER at GQL.g4:3591, after BOOLEAN_LITERAL (:3111) and NULL_KW
(:3411), so the keyword tokens win. So the membership claim stands and only the
arithmetic is wrong -- which is the worst shape for it, because a future reader
who recounts will find the mismatch and distrust a conclusion that is sound.

FIX. Correct the number, or drop it and state the property without a count. If the
count is kept it should be derived, not transcribed -- a hand-copied number in a
comment goes stale the first time the grammar gains a keyword.

ACCEPTANCE. The comment's count matches a count taken from GQL.g4 at the same
commit, or carries no count at all. Pick this up in whatever branch next touches
that file rather than opening one for a digit.

title: codegen/age: the width walk is silent on an unannotated width with a computed value
description:
`declaredPropertyTypes` / `declaresAWidth` (internal/codegen/age/sidecar_test.go)
derive the sweep's domain from `internal/graph`'s declaration by reading the
`PropertyType` annotation off the AST. PR #848 round 2 widened that walk. What
it now does and does not see, measured first-party at 20264ffd (screen is
`go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/age/`, rc=0 on every row below,
`-run '^TestTheDecodeAndTheGateReadTheSameSidecarKeys$'` anchored, 0
`no tests to run`):

ADMITTED to the domain
- `TypeFoo PropertyType = "FOO"` (const)
- `var TypeFoo PropertyType = "FOO"`

REFUSED by name (the walk fails loudly)
- `TypeFoo = "FOO"` (untyped const)
- `TypeFoo = PropertyType("FOO")`
- `TypeFoo = PropertyType("F" + "OO")` — only the call's Fun is read, so the
  argument's shape does not matter
- `var TypeFoo PropertyType` (annotated, no value)
- `var TypeFoo PropertyType = ListOf(TypeInt, false)`
- `var TypeFoo PropertyType = "F" + "OO"`

SILENT — the residue this bead is for
- `TypeFoo = "F" + "OO"` (untyped const, computed value): test rc=0, no FAILs,
  domain comes back 31 while internal/graph declares 32.
- `var TypeFoo = ListOf(TypeInt, false)` (unannotated var, computed value):
  same, test rc=0, no FAILs.

NOT LEGAL GO, so not a residue
- `const TypeFoo = ListOf(TypeInt, false)` — `ListOf(TypeInt, false) (value of
  string type PropertyType) is not constant`.

So the gap is exactly one shape: a declaration carrying no `PropertyType`
annotation whose value is neither a string literal nor a `PropertyType(...)`
conversion. `declaresAWidth` returns false for it, `declaredPropertyTypes`
skips it, and the domain comes back one width short with the sweep still
reporting agreement.

The four anchors in `declaredPropertyTypes` catch a walk that reached nothing
or stopped part way through. They do not catch a 32nd width the walk cannot
read.

Also unrecognised, not measured because there is nothing in internal/graph to
measure it against: a declaration bearing neither mark `declaresAWidth` reads
(a name prefixed `Type`, or a spec sharing a block with the annotated widths).

Close condition: either the walk stops keying on spelling — type-check
internal/graph with `go/types` and read the constants' computed values, which
sees every spelling — or a guard asserts the domain's size against a count
derived some other way, so a silently-dropped width is named. Whichever is
chosen, mutate it with the two SILENT rows above and show a named
`--- FAIL:`.

Screen note: `go build ./...` is rc=0 on a broken `sidecar_test.go`, and
`go vet ./internal/codegen/age/...` is nondeterministic in this repo (677
pre-existing `unreachable code` findings from generated ANTLR, surfacing or
not with build-cache state at the same SHA). Use
`go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/age/`.

title: resolver: describeColumnType panics on a nil list element, the in-package twin of edze's prepare.go fault
description:
Found while auditing `internal/resolver`'s `ResolvedType` type switches for
`gqlc-856f`. Recorded here rather than fixed because the nil posture belongs to
`gqlc-edze`, which `gqlc-856f` was explicitly scoped out of deciding.

`describeColumnType` (`internal/resolver/resolve.go:363`) has a default arm
that returns `t.String()`. That refuses gracefully for a pointer or embedded
form — which is why `gqlc-856f`'s audit passed it — but its `ResolvedList` arm
recurses on `v.Element`, and a nil `Element` is a nil interface, which matches
no arm and reaches `t.String()` on nil.

Measured at 52f8662 via `go test -overlay` (no file added to the tree):

    describeColumnType(ResolvedList{Element: nil})
      -> PANIC: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

`resolvedTypeEqual` is safe on the same input — its `a == nil || b == nil`
guard catches the recursion — and returns false:

    resolvedTypeEqual(ResolvedList{Element: nil}, ResolvedList{Element: ResolvedNode{}}) = false

The two compose into the fault path: `compareBranchColumns`
(`resolve.go:~2050`) calls `describeColumnType` only for columns
`resolvedTypeEqual` reported unequal, so a nil-element list on one branch and a
populated list on the other reaches the panic while building the mismatch
message.

## Reachability: latent, not live

No originator was found. All three `ResolvedList{...}` constructions in
non-test code assign a non-nil `Element`:

- `scope.go:1004` — `ResolvedEdge` or `ResolvedEdgeUnion`
- `resolve.go:1294` — the result of `resolveType`
- `resolve.go:1458` — the result of `unify`

`unify` will *propagate* a nil: `unify(ResolvedUnknown{}, nil)` returns
`(nil, true)`, so `ResolvedList{Element: nil}` is constructible at
`resolve.go:1458` from an already-nil element. That is propagation, not
origination. `describeColumnType` is unexported and reached only through the
resolver's own pipeline, so this is not reachable by an out-of-package caller
the way `internal/codegen`'s sites are.

## Relationship to gqlc-edze

`gqlc-edze` already owns `resolver.ResolvedList{Element: nil}` faulting at
`internal/codegen/prepare.go:1050`, plus the eight typed-nil pointer forms.
This is the same question one package earlier. If `edze` chooses normalisation
at the boundary, this site may be covered for free; if it chooses refusal, this
default arm needs a nil check of its own. Fold into `edze` if it is being taken
whole.

## Acceptance

Either `describeColumnType`'s default distinguishes a nil interface from a type
it does not recognise, or `edze` records that the resolver's own pipeline
cannot originate a nil element and this stays latent by argument rather than by
accident. A regression pin either way.

title: docs: five prose restatements of ResolvedType as a sealed sum survive gqlc-856f
description:
`gqlc-856f` corrected the claim at its source (`internal/resolver/validated.go`)
and `gqlc-h4ug` had already corrected it in
`docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md` (rows at lines 138 and 222 now state
the unbounded-inhabitant reading accurately). The prose restatements below are
what is left. Each describes `ResolvedType` as sealed/closed:

- `docs/specs/resolver-stage-r0.md:245` — "`ResolvedType` is the sealed sum the
  columns and parameters carry." §3.4's opening sentence.
- `docs/specs/resolver-stage-r5.md:963` — "the sealed sum" in the type-equality
  paragraph.
- `docs/adr/0010-codegen-typed-repositories-from-validatedquery.md:16` — "sealed
  `ResolvedType` sum".
- `docs/specs/codegen-prepare-commits.md:385` — describes a fence row using "a
  test-file-local stub `ResolvedType` implementation that satisfies the sealed
  interface via `isResolvedType()`". The construction described only works
  in-package; from outside, embedding is what obtains the marker.

## A different sum, same reasoning — worth a separate decision

`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c5.md:739` says of the **synthesised edge-union
interface in generated code** (not `resolver.ResolvedType`):

    Consumers type-switch on the interface at the call site; the sealed
    sum guarantees exhaustive coverage under `gochecksumtype`.

Two things to check rather than assume: (1) the same
embedding/pointer argument applies to any Go interface sealed by an
unexported marker, including the generated one, so "guarantees exhaustive
coverage" is the same overclaim one layer down; (2) `gochecksumtype` is not in
`.golangci.yml`'s enabled linters, so whatever it would guarantee is not
currently run. Neither is verified here — this bead records them as questions.

## Why filed rather than fixed

`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c5.md` is held by open PR #804
(`docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift`). The other four files are unheld, but they are
prose restatements rather than type switches, so they fall outside
`gqlc-856f`'s acceptance criterion, and splitting them across territories
mid-flight buys nothing.

## Acceptance

Each of the four `ResolvedType` restatements either drops "sealed" or says what
the marker does and does not cover, pointing at
`internal/resolver/validated.go`'s corrected comment rather than repeating the
argument. The c5 question is answered either way and recorded.
notes:
gochecksumtype item upgraded from question to VERIFIED FINDING (measured on bf5fe17a, .golangci.yml at that SHA).

Item (2) of the "different sum, same reasoning" section is now measured, not
suspected: `grep -n gochecksumtype .golangci.yml` returns no match. The file sets
`linters: default: none` with an explicit `enable:` list, so only listed linters
run and gochecksumtype is not among them. What IS enabled is `exhaustive`
(.golangci.yml:39) with `default-signifies-exhaustive: true` (:82-83) — which
covers enum constants, not marker-sealed interfaces, and which a `default:` arm
silences anyway.

So codegen-stage-c5.md:739 cites a gate that does not run, about a sum that is
not sealed. Both halves of that sentence are wrong, not just the "sealed" half.

Item (1) — whether the embedding/pointer argument carries to the SYNTHESISED
edge-union interface in generated code — remains UNVERIFIED. I did not measure
it; it needs a probe constructing an embedder of a generated candidate type.
Recording that gap rather than implying it was checked.

Deferral still correct: codegen-stage-c5.md remains held by open PR #804.
Three more carriers, from gqlc-856f's WIDENED sweep (keyed on the claim —
exhaustive / cannot implement / same package / every case / smuggle / no other
type — rather than on Resolved* names, which is what the first sweep keyed on
and why none of these were reachable):

- `.golangci.yml:92` calls `ResolvedType` one of "the closed sums". Peripheral:
  the operative reason at that line is "either/or type, no concrete type to
  return". A fourth carrier all the same. NOT edited on the 856f branch —
  `.golangci.yml` is off that branch's territory.
- `docs/specs/resolver-stage-r2.md:513-516` — "The dispatch is exhaustive over
  the sealed `Use` sum (three variants, all covered). A parser-side additive
  `Use` variant later would be a compile error at the switch default." Note this
  is about `query.Use`, not `resolver.ResolvedType`; the sum itself is now on
  gqlc-1vkb, this line is the spec restatement.
- `docs/adr/0008-query-model-surface-resolver-api.md:235` — "sealing is
  unaffected (the unexported method still closes the sum)". Historical ADR
  record; decide whether ADRs get corrected or annotated.
- `internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go:83` — the third-party
  `neo4j.ResultWithContext` "carries unexported methods and so cannot be
  implemented outside it", given as the reason the driver package is stubbed.
  Mildest of the four: the DECLARE half is true and is the operative reason for
  the stub. Listed for completeness, not asserted as a defect.

Item (1) of the c5.md question is now VERIFIED rather than open: the same
embedding/pointer argument does apply to any Go interface sealed by an
unexported marker. Measured first-party at bf5fe17a in a detached worktree,
appended to `internal/resolver/sealedsum_test.go` (`package resolver_test`):

    var _ resolver.ResolvedType = embedNode{}
    var _ resolver.ResolvedType = &resolver.ResolvedNode{}
    $ go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/resolver/   -> rc=0

and the contrast, a from-scratch out-of-package declaration in the same file:

    type probeNinth struct{}
    func (probeNinth) String() string { return "probe9" }
    func (probeNinth) isResolvedType() {}
    var _ resolver.ResolvedType = probeNinth{}
    $ go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/resolver/   -> rc=1
      probeNinth does not implement resolver.ResolvedType
      (unexported method isResolvedType)

So "the sealed sum guarantees exhaustive coverage under gochecksumtype" at
`codegen-stage-c5.md:739` is the same overclaim one layer down, for the
generated edge-union interface, and the generated interface has the same hole.
Item (2) — gochecksumtype not being an enabled linter — is unchanged and still
unverified here.

Two sites this sweep CLEARED, so do not file them again: `internal/codegen/errors.go:185-198`
and `internal/codegen/conformance/assembled_input_test.go:517` already state the
correction explicitly ("a seal that is not one ... stops another package writing
an implementation from scratch and stops nothing else, because Go promotes an
embedded type's unexported methods").

AGENTS.md:105-108 was a fifth carrier and is NOT on this bead — gqlc-856f fixed
it in place on branch fix/resolver-sealed-sum-claim (PR #881).

title: codegen/age: unservedColumn's fall-through comment restates the sealed-sum claim gqlc-856f corrected
description:
`internal/codegen/age/errors.go:423-425`, at the end of `unservedColumn`,
justifies its fall-through with:

    // ResolvedType is a sealed interface, so the switch above is its
    // whole membership; a variant added to the resolver lands here and is
    // dropped rather than emitted through an arm chosen for some other
    // shape.

Both halves are wrong in the way `gqlc-856f` corrected at the source
(`internal/resolver/validated.go`). `ResolvedType`'s unexported marker is not
a seal: a pointer form of any variant satisfies it (value receivers, and a
pointer's method set contains its value methods), and a struct embedding a
variant satisfies it from any package (Go promotes an embedded type's
unexported methods). So the switch above is NOT its whole membership, and the
type reaching the fall-through today is not "a variant added to the resolver"
but a pointer or embedded form of one of the existing eight.

**The behaviour is correct** — the fall-through returns
`"projects " + t.String()`, a non-empty reason, so an unrecognised type is
refused rather than served. Only the comment is wrong. It is the last live
restatement of the claim in Go source after `gqlc-856f`.

## Second, smaller finding in the same file

`internal/codegen/age/errors.go:251`, in `unservedReason`:

    _, union := col.Type.(resolver.ResolvedEdgeUnion)

For `*resolver.ResolvedEdgeUnion` or a struct embedding it, `unservedColumn`
returns a non-empty reason (via the fall-through above) but this assertion
yields `false`, so the `edgeUnion` flag is false for what is in substance an
edge-union column. That flag drives the ranking `unservedReason` documents at
lines 240-248 ("an edge-union column outranks an unserved parameter"). No
panic; the reason text is still produced, only the ranking degrades.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed

`internal/codegen/age/errors.go` is held by open PR #848
(`fix/age-offset-sidecar-hardening`). `gqlc-856f`'s acceptance criterion asks
for a verdict or a filed follow-up per audited site, not a cross-territory
edit.

## Acceptance

The comment says what the seal does and does not cover, and names the
construction that actually reaches the fall-through. Decide whether the
`edgeUnion` ranking flag at :251 should recognise the non-value forms or
whether the degradation is acceptable, and record which.

title: codegen: three hand-maintained emitted-file lists, two polarities, one of them unheld
description:
Three hand-maintained lists of emitted-file basenames now live in the tree, two of them of opposite polarity:

- `internal/codegen/conformance/conformance_test.go:638` `connectionSurface` — exclusion, `{db.go, graph.go}`
- `internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` `fixedDeclarationFiles` — inclusion, `{db.go, graph.go, querier.go}`
- `internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` `inputDerivedFiles` — exclusion, `{models.go}`

PR #845 held the two `prepare_test.go` lists to the corpus in three ways: every emitted basename must be classified, every entry must match a golden, and a basename whose exported names every emitting fixture declares must be on the fixed side. `connectionSurface` is held by nothing of the sort. A reader also has to keep two polarities straight to answer "which files does the sweep read".

This was carried as a RELATED note inside gqlc-qx5p, whose acceptance PR #845 meets; splitting it out so it does not close with that bead.

FIX DIRECTION: derive `connectionSurface` from the same corpus measurement, or state in one place which list is authoritative and have the others reference it.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a basename to any one of the three lists that no golden emits, or dropping one that every golden emits, turns a NAMED test red for all three lists.
notes: Split out of gqlc-qx5p's RELATED note by PR #845 round 4 so it does not close with that bead. #845 holds the two prepare_test.go lists to the corpus three ways (every emitted basename classified; every entry matched by a golden; a basename whose exported names every emitting fixture declares must be on the fixed side). connectionSurface at conformance/conformance_test.go:638 is held by none of those. Note that conformance belongs to PRs #804/#847 right now — do not edit it from a codegen-side branch without checking for a collision first.

title: codegen: the .cypher.go suffix arm still admits a file only one fixture emits
description:
`internal/codegen/prepare_test.go` (`TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet`, PR #845) now measures which side of the emitted-file partition a basename sits on: a basename more than one fixture emits, and an exported name every one of those fixtures declares, is a name that does not follow from the batch, so its file must be in `fixedDeclarationFiles`. That closes the `helpers.cypher.go` escape — a new emitted file ending `.cypher.go` written into every golden — because `Helper` then reaches 83/83 fixtures and the guard names the file.

THE RESIDUAL HOLE IS THE ONE-FIXTURE BASENAME. The measurement needs two fixtures to have any evidence at all, so a basename exactly one fixture emits is skipped. Today those are `directory.cypher.go` and `people.cypher.go`, both from the `multi_source_files` fixture, both genuinely input-derived (`AllPersonIds`, `PersonNameById`). Measured out-of-tree over the 642 committed goldens:

    db.go               fixtures=83  New/WithTx/Queries at 83/83     -> fixed, measured
    graph.go            fixtures=45  SessionInit/EnsureGraph/DropGraph at 45/45 -> fixed, measured
    querier.go          fixtures=83  Querier/ReadQuerier/WriteQuerier at 83/83  -> fixed, measured
    models.go           fixtures=83  top name Person 62/83           -> no full name, correctly skipped
    queries.cypher.go   fixtures=71  top name GetAction 5/71         -> no full name, correctly skipped
    directory.cypher.go fixtures=1   AllPersonIds 1/1                -> SKIPPED, n<2
    people.cypher.go    fixtures=1   PersonNameById 1/1              -> SKIPPED, n<2

So an emitter that grew a fourth fixed file ending `.cypher.go` AND enrolled exactly one fixture for it would still leave the sweep silently. The suffix arm names no file, which is what makes it the only arm with this width; the two map arms are pinned name by name.

FIX DIRECTION: either enumerate the query-source stems the corpus carries (a fourth hand-maintained list, which cuts against gqlc-qx5p's RELATED note), or read the per-source query file names from the fixtures' own query source files rather than from a suffix, so the arm admits exactly the files the batch's sources justify.

ACCEPTANCE: a fourth emitted file ending `.cypher.go`, written into the golden targets of exactly one fixture with a declaration no `reservedIdentifiers` row holds, turns a NAMED test red, with `go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/codegen/` clean before the test runs.

PROVENANCE: measured while fixing blocker 1 of the round-3 independent review of PR #845, 2026-08-17. The reviewer's F1b row (a `helpers.cypher.go` in every golden) is closed by that PR; this is what the same escape hatch still admits at n=1.
notes:
Filed from PR #845 round 4 as the residue of gqlc-qx5p's fix. The measurement that closes qx5p needs n>=2 fixtures emitting a basename before it has evidence, so a one-fixture basename is skipped. Reviewer row F1b (helpers.cypher.go written into every golden) IS killed at head d2acfd54: 'every one of the 83 fixtures emitting helpers.cypher.go declares [Helper], so those names do not follow from the batch, but helpers.cypher.go is classified out of fixedDeclarationFiles and this sweep never reads it'. The n=1 variant is what remains. Stated in TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet's doc comment, which names this bead.
ROUND 6 CAVEAT the description omits: "exactly one fixture" means one fixture DIRECTORY across every target, because goldenFixture (internal/codegen/prepare_test.go) keys on the fixture directory basename and drops the target. directory.cypher.go and people.cypher.go each sit under one fixture directory (multi_source_files) but exist as two files, one per target. Counterfactual measured first-party over the 642 goldens: keying on fixture@target instead puts both at n=2 with an everywhere-name apiece (AllPersonIds, PersonNameById), at which point the sweep demands they enter fixedDeclarationFiles and the test goes RED. So target-qualifying that key — which reads like a correctness improvement — is not a safe standalone edit; it has to land with whatever closes this bead. Both facts are now stated in the tree, at goldenFixture's doc comment and in TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet's.

The hole itself was reproduced independently by the round-5 review: helpers.cypher.go written into the golden dirs of exactly one fixture leaves TestFixedDeclarationSweepEqualsTheReservedSet entirely absent from the FAIL lines.

title: codegen spec fence: an exhibit's exemption is taken by a claim spelled the same way
description:
The spec fence exempts a small written set of parenthesis-less parameter lists as EXHIBITS -- shapes a document quotes to show what the fence catches, rather than claims about the emitted surface. The census (`specBareListExhibits`, internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go) names each exempted list verbatim, per document, and exempts it once: a second list spelled the same way in the same document is graded.

What is still open: the exemption is claimed by the FIRST list matching that text, and the fence cannot tell an exhibit from a claim spelled identically. So replacing an exhibit IN PLACE with a sentence asserting that shape is what the emitter prints keeps the census satisfied and leaves the claim ungraded.

Reproduction (measured first-party 2026-08-17 on docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift, vet-screened, reverted clean). In docs/adr/0029-the-codegen-spec-fence.md Decision 10, replace

    Measured: a bullet reading ``the parameter list is `ctx
    context.Context, minAge int64` `` inserted into C1 5.3 -- ...
    left both sweeps green.

with

    The emitted parameter list is `ctx context.Context, minAge int64` at one
    query parameter.

-> `go test ./internal/codegen/conformance/` exits 0. The document now states the capture vector gqlc-lhs3 removed as a fact about the emitter, and the fence says nothing.

Scope: this is what is LEFT of the earlier, much wider hole. Before this branch's round-4 change the census named DOCUMENTS, so every parenthesis-less list anywhere in a listed document was ungraded -- appending `ctx context.Context, minAge int64` to that ADR was green with nothing removed. That is now red; only the replace-an-exhibit-in-place spelling survives.

Why it was not closed here: distinguishing an exhibit from a claim needs something in the document the fence can read -- a marker on the line, or a section the exemption is scoped to. Both put fence syntax into prose that a reader sees, which is a design call rather than a fix, and neither was measured. A per-site verbatim census over ALL graded sites is separately argued against in gqlc-0rjn (it makes the test a copy of the documents); the census here is bounded to the three lists the fence declines to grade, which have to be written down somewhere to be declined at all.

Related: gqlc-0rjn (per-document floor of one graded site), gqlc-e143 (prose beside an intact graded span), gqlc-jfwo (roots the censuses never name).
notes: Filed from PR #804 round-4. Branch docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift, head 840a74c6. The wide hole (any parenthesis-less list anywhere in a listed document went ungraded) is CLOSED there; this bead is the residue: the exemption is claimed by the first list matching the census text, so replacing an exhibit IN PLACE with a claim spelled the same way keeps the census satisfied and leaves the claim ungraded. Witnessed green 2026-08-17, vet-screened, reverted clean. Stated as a negative in four places: specfence_test.go header (floor of five), specBareListExhibits' own comment, ADR 0029 decision 10 + consequences, and c1.md 5.7's open list.

title: ci: which live arm a live test belongs in is asserted nowhere
description:
internal/liverecipes asserts that the union of the live recipes' -run allowlists equals the set of top-level tests the codegen module declares (bd gqlc-df3d). It does not assert WHICH half a test belongs in.

Which containers a live test needs is a property of its body — it calls into the neo4j driver, or into the AGE dialect — and is declared nowhere the reader can see. So the following stays green:

- moving TestAGESessionInit out of test-codegen-live-age's -run and into test-codegen-live-neo4j's, where it runs against a neo4j container and either fails for the wrong reason or passes vacuously;
- dropping a test from the half that has the container it needs while the other half still claims it.

Both are union-preserving, and the union is all this guard reads.

Closing it needs a declared property per test that the recipes can be checked against — a naming convention the reader enforces, a per-test tag, or a registry the tests themselves write to. Filed as residue from gqlc-df3d; not a regression of it.

title: codegen: the fixed-declaration sweep records a method whatever its receiver, so a non-*Queries method would be forced into reservedIdentifiers and over-refuse queries
description:
`TestEveryEmittedFixedDeclarationIsReserved` (`internal/codegen/prepare_test.go`, PR #845) walks the emitter-fixed golden files and requires a `reservedIdentifiers` row for every exported declaration it finds. Its `*ast.FuncDecl` arm records the name whatever the receiver is.

That is right for the corpus as it stands — probed independently on #845: the three fixed files declare exactly the twelve reserved names, and no method in them has a receiver other than `*Queries`. It is wrong in principle for a method the emitter might add on some other receiver. Such a name occupies no package block and collides with nothing, but the sweep would demand a row for it, and `internal/codegen/prepare.go:570` refuses a *query* on membership in `reservedIdentifiers` alone — at either scope. So satisfying the sweep would refuse a query name that generates fine.

WITNESS (mutation M13, independent review of #845, reproduced first-party at `660fe68a`): appending `func (h qHelper) Validate() bool { return true }` to every golden `db.go` turns `TestEveryEmittedFixedDeclarationIsReserved` red demanding a reserved row for `Validate`. `go vet` clean before the test ran.

Today the limit is stated in the test's doc comment and nothing enforces it. Two ways out, and the second is cheap:

  1. Record a method only when its receiver is `*Queries`, and assert separately that no other receiver appears in those files — so a new receiver type is a decision someone makes rather than a row someone adds.
  2. Leave the sweep as it is and add the receiver assertion alone: the sweep's demand is then correct because the antecedent is fenced.

ACCEPTANCE: the M13 witness above no longer demands a `reservedIdentifiers` row for a method on a non-`*Queries` receiver, and a golden carrying such a method still fails some NAMED test rather than passing silently.

PROVENANCE: nit N1, independent review of PR #845, 2026-08-17. Not reachable at that commit — zero such methods exist in the corpus.
notes: REVIEW FINDING (PR #845 round 6, 2026-08-17): this bead's description claims golden `db.go` has no non-`*Queries` receiver. Measured false — 108 of 153 golden files carry one. Fix option 1 as written is therefore unimplementable; whoever picks this up must re-derive the fix direction before starting.

title: a PR body edit now re-runs the whole of ci.yml for a one-line check
description:
gqlc-w4al added `edited` to `ci.yml`'s `pull_request` types so the
check-PR-body gate re-evaluates when a body changes. `ci.yml` carries five
jobs (lint, test, tidy, codegen-fence, actionlint), so every body edit now
costs a full pipeline run — about 3.5 min of wall time on recent runs — for a
step that reads one file and one API response.

## Why it was accepted rather than optimised

The cheap version is a job-level `if:` skipping the expensive jobs on
`edited`, and it is a bypass rather than an optimisation. Every job in a
triggered workflow emits a check run; a skipped job's conclusion is `skipped`;
branch protection reads `skipped` as a pass; and the newest check run for a
context is the one it reads. So a red `lint` on the head SHA would be erased
by anyone editing the PR description. vuln.yml carries the same reasoning in
its header for govulncheck.

The correct shape is a separate workflow holding just this check, triggered on
`[opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]`, with its own concurrency group.
That was not done here because the new job id would have to be added to
master's required status checks, and a required context that does not yet
exist on the PRs already open reports as "Expected — waiting for status to be
reported" and blocks every one of them until it is re-triggered. Doing that
mid-flight would have stranded other work.

## Mitigation already in place

The concurrency group is `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with
cancel-in-progress off master, so an edit that lands alongside a push collapses
into a single run rather than doubling. The pathological case is an edit
arriving mid-run, which cancels the run in progress and restarts it.

## Shape of a fix

- Add `.github/workflows/pr-body.yml` with one job running
  `.github/scripts/check-pr-closes.py`, on the four PR activity types.
- Drop the step from `ci.yml`'s tidy job and drop `edited` from its types.
- Add the new job id to both master's classic branch protection contexts and
  the `protect-master` ruleset's required_status_checks. Both exist and their
  lists currently differ (the ruleset omits live-smoke and codegen-fence).
- Do it at a quiet moment, and re-trigger every open PR afterwards.
- `internal/tools/ciguard` asserts the step lives in the `tidy` job because
  `tidy` is a required context; those assertions move with the step.

## Acceptance

- A PR body edit runs one job, not five.
- The new job is a required status check in both the ruleset and the classic
  protection, verified by reading them back after the change.
- No PR is left with a permanently pending required context.

title: spec fence: docFiles' docRoots existence guard is unwitnessed
description:
internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go, docFiles(): require.NoErrorf(t, err, "docRoots entry %q does not exist", root) is structurally unable to fail on a clean tree, and no witness stands in for it.

Witness (independent review of PR #804 at dbeabc3a, mutation m15): replacing that require with `continue` leaves the whole package green — SURVIVED, screened for compile breaks by go vet.

ADR 0029 decision 7 draws the line between witnessed plumbing and unwitnessed assertions and enumerates six lines in the first category. This is a seventh line of exactly that shape and is outside the enumeration, so it is neither witnessed nor declared.
