Blast radius is small: if a censused root vanished, the censuses still redden by the lost direction (measured — probe D3 moved README.md off disk and both fence tests reddened). Only a root no census names (README.md, CONTEXT.md today) would go silent.

Fix is either a witness in the same shape as TestSpecSweepsCarryUnreadableSites (docFiles taking its roots as a parameter) or an eighth item in decision 7's enumeration.

title: resolver: an unsatisfiable endpoint refuses as ErrUnknownEdge inline and ErrUnknownLabel as a var
description:
On test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql, the same endpoint written two ways refuses two different ways:

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(:Company:Desk) RETURN p
    -> unknown edge: Employee&Person-[WORKS_AT]->Company&Desk, Person-[WORKS_AT]->Company&Desk

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(z:Company:Desk) RETURN p
    -> unknown label: no node type satisfies Company&Desk; declared types carrying these labels: Company, Company&Large, Desk

No declared node type carries both Company and Desk, so the honest diagnosis is the var spelling's: the LABEL SET is unsatisfiable, and there was never an edge to look for. The inline spelling reports a missing edge and invites the author to go declare one.

The cause is ordering. A var endpoint goes through resolveNodeLabels at Phase A1, which refuses an unsatisfiable label set before edges are closed. An inline endpoint has no binding and is only ever read by endpointLabels at edge-closure time, where the empty satisfying set falls through to the spelled key and closeEdge refuses the probe set.

gqlc-3uof's branch pins the CURRENT wording (TestInlineEndpointCommitsOnTheTypesSatisfyingIt/a_conjunction_no_type_satisfies asserts the whole message) because the fallback is what makes the refusal name Company&Desk at all rather than nothing. Any fix here should move that row, not delete it.

Fix is likely a satisfiability check over inline endpoint label sets at Phase A1, before CloseEdges runs. That also makes TestInlineEndpointsAgreeWithTheirVarSpelling assertable on the error message rather than on verdict class alone — today it compares err.Error() and passes only because these unsatisfiable spellings are not among its rows.
notes: Pre-existing; unchanged by fix/resolver-inline-endpoint-satisfying-set, which deliberately preserves it so describeTriedEdges still names the labels the author wrote.

title: resolver conformance: invalidFixtureContains is opt-in and no new fixture opts in, so a refusal's message text is unpinned
description:
`invalidFixtureContains` is the manifest field that pins the TEXT of a refusal, as opposed to its sentinel. It is conditional — a fixture that omits the field is simply not message-checked — and the independent review of PR #806 measured that **0 of the 18 fixtures that PR added opt in**.

This is the 'conditional gate omission is invisible' shape this repo has been bitten by before: `if entry.X != ""` catches DISAGREEMENT but not ABSENCE. A fixture that says nothing about the message passes the message check by saying nothing. Silence should not read the same as agreement.

WHY THIS IS P3 AND NOT HIGHER — the review deliberately downgraded it from a blocker, and the reasons are worth preserving so nobody re-escalates it without cause:
  - the shape is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by #806;
  - `invalidFixtures` and the schema mapping are both totality-checked, so a fixture cannot silently drop out of the run entirely;
  - eight dedicated tests already assert messages via `ErrorIs` + `Require().Equal`, so the most important messages are pinned outside the manifest mechanism.

So the exposure is: a refusal's wording can degrade for the 18 new fixtures without any test noticing, while the sentinel and the verdict stay pinned. Related to gqlc-yb0w, which is the same blind spot at corpus scale — there the sweep cannot see a sentinel change inside a FAIL->FAIL cell; here the manifest cannot see a message change at all.

FIX: make the declaration positive on both shapes rather than conditional on one. Either require every invalid fixture to carry `invalidFixtureContains`, or require it to carry an explicit opt-out that says why the message is not worth pinning. Absence must be a decision someone wrote down, not a default.

ACCEPTANCE: add an invalid fixture with no `invalidFixtureContains` and no opt-out, and confirm a NAMED test goes red saying which fixture failed to declare. Today it passes.

PROVENANCE: nit N3, independent Linus review of PR #806, 2026-08-17, /tmp/factory/verdict-806.md.

title: resolver: comments in resolve.go and scope.go narrate the review's history and defend rejected alternatives
description:
PR #806 (merged as `aade7a40`, bead gqlc-0tft) added 408 comment lines to 228 code lines in `internal/resolver/resolve.go` and `internal/resolver/scope.go`. An independent review measured the banned-shape rate with the same grep on both sides: 1.2% across the two files' 679 pre-existing comment lines vs 7.4% across the 408 added — six times the files' own rate.

AGENTS.md: comments explain WHY, never WHAT; no narration of changes; no justifying a design by contrasting a rejected alternative (that belongs in an ADR, which a comment may cite but must not restate).

VERIFIED VERBATIM ON MASTER (I read each, they are not paraphrases):

  resolve.go:888  '...filed as gqlc-pv0u rather than narrowed here.'
  resolve.go:891  'Package-level rather than closures inside orientationDisagreement because...'
  resolve.go:1347 'This is a STRICTER question than qualifiedDemoter's, and deliberately not the'
  resolve.go:1418 'The OPTIONAL arm is deliberately blunter than DemoteNullability's... but that
                   is a further widening, and it is filed rather than taken here.'
  scope.go:90     '...the alternative is an eleventh branchState lane, and no fixture pays
                   the precision.'

'deliberately not the' is an AGENTS.md ban-list phrase verbatim.

A NOTE ON ONE UNVERIFIED COUNT: the review reported 'nine `changes no answer and no test can pin it` blocks, ~60 lines, freezing one instant of the test suite into source.' I could not reproduce nine — `git grep -c "changes no answer" origin/master -- internal/resolver/` returns 2 in resolve.go and 1 in scope.go. Either the phrasing varies across the blocks or the count is wrong. Whoever takes this should establish the real number first rather than inheriting nine. The underlying concern is sound regardless: a comment asserting that no test pins something is a claim about the suite at one instant, and it rots silently.

PRECEDENT that this is a real class here and not taste: master already carries `c1558e9e` — 'codegen/age: the sweep's comments state the rule, not the review's history (#829)', the same cleanup applied to a different package.

WHY THIS IS A FOLLOW-UP AND NOT A REVERT: the review returned ZERO correctness blockers. Independent corroboration ran 310 queries x 28 schemas = 8680 cells, branch vs base: 8 FAIL->PASS, 2616 PASS->PASS with all goldens byte-identical, and **zero accept->refuse, zero accept->different-answer**. No pre-existing .golden.json was modified. B1 questions no line of behaviour.

FIX: rewrite each comment to state the contract the code must honour. Where the rationale is genuinely load-bearing, move it to an ADR and cite the ADR from the comment.

ACCEPTANCE: the two files' banned-shape rate is no higher than their pre-#806 baseline of 1.2%, measured with the same grep on both sides.

PROVENANCE: blocker B1, independent Linus review of PR #806, 2026-08-17, /tmp/factory/verdict-806.md.

title: bd-gh-sync: neither side's sync timestamp is a description-edit time, so the prefix tiebreak has a residue in each direction
description:
gqlc-6mx3 added an edit-time tiebreak to the append-only eligibility rule in .githooks/bd-gh-sync: where the GH body properly extends the bead description, the bead is pulled only when gh.updatedAt is later than bd.updated_at by more than a 60s skew margin. Both inputs are proxies, measured first-party on 2026-08-17 in throwaway workspaces under /tmp:

* bd.updated_at moves on writes that are not description edits. It does not move on every write either. Moved: 'bd update' with -d, --title, -p, -s, --notes, --append-notes, --design, --acceptance, -a, --external-ref, -t, --set-metadata, and 'bd note', 'bd assign', 'bd priority', 'bd close', 'bd reopen'. Did not move, all exiting 0 with the write visible in 'bd show': 'bd tag <id> <label>', 'bd label add', 'bd label remove', 'bd update --add-label/--remove-label/--set-labels', 'bd set-state <id> <dim>=<value>' (a label write), 'bd comment' and 'bd link'. The earlier note here said "any write" and cited 'bd tag add', which is not the CLI shape and exits 1; the corrected shape was re-measured and is in the unmoved list.
* gh.updatedAt bumps on a comment, not only a body edit. 'gh issue list --repo areqag/gqlc --state all --limit 200 --json number,updatedAt,comments': 17 of 17 commented issues have updatedAt within 2s of their newest comment's createdAt (#818 +0s, #770 +1s, #760 +1s, #756 +0s, #755 +0s, #745 +0s).

Consequences, both pinned only as prose in the script header today:
1. OVER-HOLD (fail-closed, visible): a legitimate GitHub append followed by one of the bd-side writes that does move updated_at is held, and the notice reprints on every merge until one side is edited again. Recoverable by hand.
2. FAIL-OPEN (silent): a trailing block cut in bd, followed by a comment on the GH issue, makes GitHub the later side and the cut block is written back over the bead. This is the gqlc-6mx3 defect surviving in a narrower shape.

This script manufactures the comment in (2) itself. .githooks/bd-gh-sync:896 runs 'gh issue close <n> --comment "Auto-close: bead <id> closed locally."' for every bead closed locally whose mirror is still open, which moves gh.updatedAt. So a bd-side trailing cut on a bead that is then closed locally is self-triggering: the push path comments, and the next pull sees GitHub as the later side. Driven through the shipped selection on 2026-08-17, the cell (bd closed, GH closed, body extends, gh later) returns ALLOW. The waiting-on is not an external actor.

Closing (2) needs an input neither bulk listing carries. Candidates not investigated: GitHub's REST issue payload does not expose a body-edit time in 'gh issue list --json' (the field list has no lastEditedAt; checked 2026-08-17), so it would need the GraphQL userContentEdits connection or a per-issue call, which costs one request per bead; or bd's own Dolt history for the description column, which is local and free but says nothing about GitHub. A third, cheaper than either: have the push path stop moving gh.updatedAt on its own close, or record the ids it commented on so the next pull discounts them. Decide which before widening the rule.

No fixture covers (2) today because the suite would have to assert the current wrong answer.

title: codegen/prepare: three 'X rather than Y' comments restate rejected alternatives, and scopeName's if/else mislabels a third scope
description:
Two small residues from PR #832 (`5718a935`, bead gqlc-e6mh), in `internal/codegen/prepare.go` and its test.

(1) THREE COMMENTS JUSTIFY THE DESIGN BY CONTRAST. AGENTS.md forbids a comment that defends a choice by naming what was rejected — that belongs in an ADR, which a comment may cite but must not restate. Three comments added by #832 are in the "X rather than Y" shape. Locate them with:

    git grep -n 'rather than' origin/master -- internal/codegen/prepare.go internal/codegen/prepare_test.go

and judge each: keep the sentence if it states a non-obvious CONSTRAINT a reader cannot derive from the code, delete it if it is only defending the choice. Note that at least one of these ('a cost this test locks in rather than hides', prepare_test.go:548/:578) is doing real work — it is the only place the AGE-only over-breadth of DBTX/SessionInit is admitted, and gqlc-xv62 tracks moving that admission into the spec. Do not delete it until the spec carries it, or the information is lost.

(2) `scopeName` WOULD MISLABEL A THIRD SCOPE. The `identifierScope` enum (`prepare.go:23-30`) has two members, `scopePackage` (iota, the zero value) and `scopeMethod`. `scopeName` renders them with an if/else rather than a switch with a default, so adding a third member silently renders it as whichever branch the else covers — a wrong diagnostic string, not a compile error.

This is fail-open in the diagnostic rather than in the gate, so it is genuinely minor: the refusal still fires, only its wording is wrong. Filing it because the same fail-quiet-on-extension shape is the substance of gqlc-fd06, and closing both together is cheaper than twice.

FIX: switch on the scope with a default that panics or returns an explicit unknown-scope string naming the value. The zero value must remain `scopePackage` — #832 relies on that for fail-closed behaviour, since an unset scope reads as the stricter package scope.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a third `identifierScope` member without teaching `scopeName` about it is caught — by a compile error, a panic in test, or a named failing assertion. Not by a silently wrong string.

PROVENANCE: nits N4 and N5, independent Linus review of PR #832, 2026-08-17. Both non-blocking; the review returned PASS with zero blockers.

title: codegen spec: sentinel taxonomy omits that two reserved identifiers are AGE-only, so the table overstates the refusal
description:
`docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md:144` describes the C1 exported-identifier reserved set landed by PR #832 (`5718a935`, bead gqlc-e6mh) without the backend caveat the tests now spell out.

MEASURED (independent reviewer, #832, first-party): emitting a package per (name x backend) for `(:N { name :: STRING NOT NULL })` plus one `:one` query, at a commit with no gate, then `go build` in `test/data/codegen`'s module, partitions the 12 reserved rows three ways:

  - fail on BOTH backends (7):  Queries, New, Querier, ReadQuerier, WriteQuerier, ErrNoRows, ErrMultipleResults
  - fail on apache-age-pgx-v5 ONLY (2):  DBTX, SessionInit  -- these COMPILE CLEAN on neo4j-go-v5
  - compile on both (3):  WithTx, EnsureGraph, DropGraph  (method scope, no package-level clash)

So for `DBTX` and `SessionInit` the gate is OVER-BROAD on neo4j: it refuses a schema that would have generated a perfectly good package. That is a deliberate, defensible choice — a false refusal is the safe direction, and the alternative is a backend-conditional reserved set — but it must be STATED, not silently implied.

Corroboration that the neo4j goldens really do not carry these names: `grep -rl 'DBTX\|SessionInit' test/data/codegen/valid/*/golden/neo4j-go-v*/` returns 0 files.

The code side already says this plainly. `internal/codegen/prepare_test.go:548` and `:578` call it "a false refusal on that target... a cost this test locks in rather than hides", and PR #832's body repeats it under "Where this is weakest". Only the SPEC is silent, so a reader of the taxonomy alone would conclude all 12 names collide on every target.

FIX: give the taxonomy row the same three-way partition, and say in the negative which target each name actually collides on. Per AGENTS.md, state the limit and enumerate it rather than asserting a universal the corpus falsifies.

ACCEPTANCE: a reader of `codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md` alone can say, for each of the 12 reserved identifiers, which backends it would actually break and which it is refused on defensively.

PROVENANCE: nit N2, independent Linus review of PR #832, 2026-08-17.
notes: MET by PR #845 head d2acfd54; close on merge, `Closes #840` is in the PR body. §6 of docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md now lists all twelve rows with Scope, Declared by and Breaks on, and the closing paragraph gives the three-way partition in the negative. Round 4 corrected two errors in that paragraph the round-3 review caught: (1) it claimed the three method-scope rows 'collide with nothing on any target', which is true only on the entity axis — a query method is emitted on *Queries with its name verbatim, so a query named WithTx redeclares the WithTx every target's db.go carries; (2) the over-broad count on a neo4j-only batch is FOUR (DBTX, SessionInit, EnsureGraph, DropGraph), not five — WithTx is load-bearing on every target. The table is fenced in both directions by TestSentinelTaxonomy/TestReservedSetSectionMatchesTheReservedRows against reservedIdentifiers and the corpus-measured columns. The READY PATCH referenced above is superseded and should not be applied.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #845 (merged d41895e5). GH #840 closed.

title: elemLocal doc comment justifies its design by contrasting a rejected axis — AGENTS.md forbids that in a comment
description:
`internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:704-709` (on master, landed in PR #822 / `0a139b74`) carries a second paragraph on `elemLocal`'s doc comment that is an 'the axis is A, not B' contrast:

    // The axis is depth, not the column position the row assembly's own
    // accumulator numbers on: sibling list columns each open their own loop
    // at the row assembly's indent, so their locals sit in disjoint blocks,
    // while a nested list's loop is emitted inside the enclosing one's body
    // and shares it. The outermost depth is unsuffixed, so a single-level
    // list column emits the loop spec §5.5 spells out.

AGENTS.md forbids both shapes present here:
  1. It documents the CALLER's naming scheme (the row assembly's accumulator
     numbering), not this function's contract. A reader of `elemLocal` does not
     need to know how a different function numbers a different variable.
  2. It justifies the chosen design by contrasting a rejected alternative. That
     belongs in an ADR, which a comment may cite but must not restate.

The FIRST paragraph (:698-703) is fine and should stay: it states the non-obvious
constraint — that under a fixed name the inner declaration shadows the enclosing
one and the emitted package stops compiling at nesting depth three. That is a WHY
a reader cannot derive from the two-line body.

Surfaced as an unfiled nit by the independent reviewer on PR #822 (linus-ye6g);
filed rather than folded in, per this repo's preference for a well-filed follow-up.

FIX: delete the second paragraph. If the depth-vs-column-position distinction is
load-bearing for a future reader, it belongs in the C5 spec section that describes
the row assembly, next to the accumulator numbering it is contrasting against.

ACCEPTANCE: `elemLocal`'s comment explains only why the depth suffix exists; no
sentence in it describes what the row assembly does or what naming axis was
rejected.

title: codegen spec C3 §? claims list loops use 'for i, elem := range value' — false at depth>=1 and for bare-element arms
description:
`docs/codegen-stage-c3.md:1250` (on master, verified at origin/master) states as a bolded invariant:

    - **List loops use `for i, elem := range value`** — the emitted
      loop variable pair is idiomatic; ...

Both halves of that variable pair are falsified by the emitter that landed in PR #822 (`0a139b74`).

WITNESS (first-party, `git show origin/master:internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go`):

    :682 func walkListElemPlan(..., depth int) {
    :685   indexVar := "i"
    :686   if carriesElemBare(e) {
    :687     indexVar = "_"
    :688   }
    :690   iterVar := elemLocal("elem", depth)
    :691   fmt.Fprintf(b, "%sfor %s, %s := range %s {\n", indent, indexVar, iterVar, srcVar)

and `elemLocal` (:710) returns `name + strconv.Itoa(depth)` for depth != 0.

So the emitted loop header is:
  - depth 0, element asserted:  `for i, elem := range value`   <- the only case the spec describes
  - depth 0, bare element:      `for _, elem := range value`
  - depth 1:                    `for i, elem1 := range inner1`
  - depth 2:                    `for i, elem2 := range inner2`

This is pre-existing spec drift, not a regression introduced by #822 — the depth suffix is what #822 added, and the spec bullet was never updated. It was surfaced as an unfiled nit by the independent reviewer on #822 (linus-ye6g) and is filed here rather than folded in.

FIX: state the negative and enumerate the limits per AGENTS.md — the loop header is `for <index>, elem<depth> := range <src>`, where <index> is `i` when the body's fail message names it and `_` otherwise, and where the depth suffix is empty at the outermost level. Do not restate a universal the emitter does not honour.

ACCEPTANCE: the C3 bullet describes all four emitted shapes above, and a reader can predict the loop header for a depth-2 nested list column from the spec alone.

title: codegen/age: ADR 0028 says the five refusals are 'not yet' verified by CI — a dispatched run witnessed them
description:
docs/adr/0028-age-refuses-on-the-query-text-only-with-a-witness.md:442-447 currently reads:

  '**The first run of TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine.** The AGE live
   half is nightly-and-manual (codegen-live.yml, job live-smoke-age, skipped on
   pull requests), so these five refusals ship verified by a hand-run spike and
   not yet by CI.'

The parenthetical is still TRUE — live-smoke-age is skipped on pull_request. But 'not yet by CI' is now FALSE, and the passage's whole point is provenance.

WITNESS (verified first-party, not taken from the author's report):
  gh run view 31996378339 --json workflowName,event,headBranch,status,conclusion
    -> wf=codegen-live event=workflow_dispatch branch=feat/age-dialect-gap-admission
       status=completed conclusion=success
  gh run view 31996378339 --json jobs -> live-smoke: success / live-smoke-age: success

The recipe in that log names the test as a WHOLE -run alternative:
  cd test/data/codegen && go test -count=1 -tags codegen_live -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit|TestAGERefusesRelationshipTypeAlternation|TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine' -skip 'TestLiveSmoke/neo4j' ./...
ending 'ok github.com/areqag/gqlc/test/data/codegen 11.499s', with ZERO 'no tests to run' lines in the log. Both functions are declared (test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go:89 and :196).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT TO CARRY INTO THE FIX: the recipe has no -v, so there is no per-test PASS line. That the two witnesses executed is an INFERENCE from (regex names them as whole alternatives) + (both declared) + (no '[no tests to run]' marker) + (ok). It is sound, but the ADR must state it as an inference, not as an observed pass — this repo has been bitten by go test -run's unanchored regex printing PASS over nothing.

FIX: replace 'not yet by CI' with what actually happened, citing run 31996378339 and the branch it ran on, and keep the true part about pull_request skipping. Consider whether the wider claim in gqlc-osf1's orbit needs the same correction.

The broader capability this surfaced: codegen-live is workflow_dispatch-able, so 'Docker is not running locally' is not a hard limit on witnessing live behaviour. Worth stating once in the ADR so the next author reaches for it.

title: codegen/neo4j: the nested-list arm's fixed 'ok' depends on 'inner' being depth-suffixed
description:
Found by the adversarial review of gqlc-ye6g (PR #822, merged 0a139b74).

`walkListElemBody`'s ColumnList arm emits, at render_queries.go:809:

    fmt.Fprintf(b, "%s%s, ok := %s.([]any)\n", indent, inner, iterVar)

`inner` is now `elemLocal("inner", depth+1)` and so is a fresh identifier at
every depth. `ok` is not — it is a fixed name, as are `v`, `node` and `rel` in
the leaf arms above it.

That is legal today, and the reason is worth writing down because nothing in
the tree says it: Go's `:=` needs only ONE new variable on the left, and
`inner_d` supplies it. Each nested level is also its own block, so the inner
`ok` shadows rather than redeclares.

The dependency runs the wrong way round from how the code reads. The fix
gqlc-ye6g landed is described as being about shadowing at depth; but if
`inner` ever went back to a fixed name while the arms stayed in one block,
the failure would not be the shadowing this bead's comment describes — it
would be `no new variables on left side of :=`, the exact error shape ibg5
produced. The suffix on `inner` is load-bearing for two separate reasons and
the comment names only one.

Proposal: one sentence at the ColumnList arm recording that `ok` is
deliberately unsuffixed and what makes that safe. No emission change.

title: githooks: bd-gh-sync's held-bead ids skip the charset gate the rest of the script relies on
description:
Found in adversarial review of fix/bd-gh-sync-pull-witness (PR #825), fixed at
the rendering layer there, not at the source.

The pull path has three python payloads. Two of them (pull selection, push
selection) take ids that have been past the shell charset gate

    case "$_bid" in "" | -* | *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) ... refuse

The third — the postcondition that compares the two `bd list` snapshots — does
not: its ids come straight off `bd list`, because the beads it is about are
precisely the ones no batch touched, so nothing filtered them.

PR #825 closed the two observable consequences (a space rendering one bead as
two names in the summary, a newline splitting a moved.txt record so one bead is
counted as two) by escaping at the point of rendering: `one_line()` in the
postcondition plus an awk join that cuts the record tag by field. Four
assertions pin it.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: the asymmetry itself. Any future reader of that snapshot —
a new field, a new record type, a new summary arm — starts from unvalidated
bytes again and has to rediscover it. The two selections and the postcondition
should agree on what an id may contain, either by gating the postcondition's
ids too or by stating in one place that it deliberately does not and why.

Related: gqlc-p5gh (the same file's `_run_batch` stdin), gqlc-tvv7 (the census
that guards these assertions).

title: githooks: bd-gh-sync-test's empty-last-line arms are unexercised, so their loss is silent
description:
Commit 0c13ddcb (branch fix/bd-gh-sync-pull-witness, merged as PR #825) added
`[ -z "$_ll" ] ||` to the assertion arm for `an exemption set that could not be
written stops the held-bead check`, and the commit message says every other arm
of that shape already had one. That is true — 20 `${_ll##...}` chains, zero
unguarded heads.

What no assertion covers is the arm itself. Measured at 703a7493 in a detached
worktree:

    # delete `[ -z "$_ll" ] || ` from the exemption-set block
    bash .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh
    -> 145 passed, 0 failed, exit 0

The guard is structurally unable to fail, which is the defect this branch spent
14 commits closing one level down. It matters because the arm exists to stop a
`${_ll##*pattern*}` chain reading a *missing* last line as a match: with `$_ll`
empty, `${_ll##*x*}` is empty, so `[ -n "" ]` is false and the block passes by
finding nothing. A run where the script died before printing a summary would
read as a pass on every one of those 20 chains.

WHY IT SURVIVES: no fixture makes `$TMP/err` empty. The script prints something
on stderr on every path the suite exercises, so `last_line` is never "".

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a fixture where the script emits no stderr at all — e.g. a
stub that makes it exit before the first echo — asserted once against a chain
that would otherwise pass vacuously. One assertion covers the shape; the other
19 arms are then protected by argument rather than by 19 fixtures.

Not a live bug: every arm has the guard today. This is about whether their
removal would be noticed.

title: codegen/age: ADR 0028 states a forward universal about AGE versions that do not exist yet
description:
ADR 0028 line ~501 reads: 'no projection of date() will ever parse on this server, whatever carrier AGE later grows'.

This is a forward-looking universal over unreleased Apache AGE versions. Nothing in this repo can witness it — the pinned image is apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8 (PG 18.1, AGE 1.7.0), and a claim quantified over 'whatever carrier AGE later grows' is unfalsifiable by any probe we can run. The repo's standing rule is that a 'cannot / never / every' in prose must be replaced by a stated negative with its limits enumerated.

WITNESS: found by the adversarial review of PR #809 (feat/age-dialect-gap-admission), recorded as nit 3. The reviewer established that the clause governs MESSAGE ORDERING only — it does not gate anything, so this is prose accuracy, not a behavioural defect. That is why it is P3 and not a blocker on #809.

FIX: restate as a measured negative bounded by the pinned image, e.g. what the 1.7.0 probe actually returned for a date() projection, and drop the quantification over future versions. If a forward statement is genuinely wanted, it belongs in the ADR's explicitly-speculative section alongside the 'Suspected and unverified' entries, not stated as fact.

Related: gqlc-kb2c (#794) is the sibling prose-rot bug in the same ADR (six cardinals in one sentence).

title: codegen: the committed golden corpus has no list column past nesting depth two
description:
`TestGoldenBuild` (internal/codegen/conformance) compiles the committed
`test/data/codegen` module, so it is the gate that says the golden tree
itself builds. Its deepest list column is `LIST<LIST<...>>`:
`list_list_int`, `schema_list_any_property` and `schema_list_property_widths`
are all depth two.

Depth two does not reach the element loop's local collision. gqlc-ye6g's
witness: at `origin/master` before the fix, a depth-three column emitted
`innerAcc = append(innerAcc, innerAcc)` and

    valid/probe_depth3/golden/neo4j-go-v5/queries.cypher.go:55:32:
    cannot use innerAcc (variable of type []int64) as int64 value in
    argument to append

while every committed depth-two golden compiled. So a re-broken emitter
whose goldens were regenerated would leave `TestGoldenBuild` green.

After gqlc-ye6g the depth-three coverage lives only in
`internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go`, whose corpus is assembled in a
temp dir. That harness is stronger (it compiles AND runs the emitted
package) but it is one harness, and deleting the query from
`testdata/corpus_queries.cypher` together with its test from
`corpus_test.go.txt` removes the coverage without failing anything —
`declaredTests` reads the pass set from the same template.

Fix: add a `list_list_list_int` fixture under `test/data/codegen/valid/`
mirroring `list_list_int` one level deeper, so the committed tree carries
a depth-three witness that `TestGoldenBuild` compiles.

title: resolver: two resolvedCovers writes are unpinned today and become load-bearing the moment the lane is carried
description:
Mutation testing of `feat/resolver-narrow-plural-endpoints` at 40ce99a7 (28-row
matrix, out-of-tree copy, `go build` green before every run) found two writes to
the `resolvedCovers` lane that SURVIVE deletion with the whole suite green:

- `internal/resolver/scope.go`, the collapse arm of `NarrowPluralEndpoints`:
  deleting `s.resolvedCovers[v] = struct{}{}` while keeping
  `delete(s.nodeCands, v)` changes no test.
- `internal/resolver/resolve.go`, `candidateTypes`' Phase B commit: deleting the
  `else { delete(t.resolvedCovers, n.Variable()) }` arm changes no test.

Both survivals are honest — the comments beside each already say "changes no
answer today and no test can pin it" and enumerate why. The collapse write is
unobservable because `CloseEdges` returns immediately after the pass and the
lane is not carried; the else arm is unobservable because an unlabelled pending
binding is never already in the lane and `newScope` does not seed it from the
carry.

## Why this outlives the branch

Both reasons are stated as properties of the CURRENT call order and the CURRENT
carry, and both are exactly what `gqlc-etj6` proposes to change. Carrying the
lane across a `WITH`, or moving the narrowing relative to the carry check, makes
both lines live — and whoever makes that change gets no red test if they get
either one wrong. The collapse omission would silently mark a correctly-narrowed
singleton as uncovered (lost precision); the else-arm omission would leave a
stale `covered` on a binding a later Phase B iteration demoted (a WRONG type
committed, which is the unsound direction).

So the risk is not that the lines are wrong now. It is that the safety net for
the person who makes them matter does not exist, and the comments that carry the
reasoning are not a gate.

## Fix

Do this as part of `gqlc-etj6` rather than before it — there is nothing to pin
until the lane is observable. When the lane is carried, add one row per write:
a query whose answer differs with and without the write, asserted on the
resolved column type, not on a golden.

## Witness

Mutation ids G16-collapseCovers and G25-phaseB-elsearm, both SURVIVE; the
remaining 20 guards in the same matrix were KILLED by named tests.

title: codegen/age: the witness sweep binds the server answer into the body, not into an assertion
description:
`TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness` (internal/codegen/age/dialect_test.go) renders the named live test's body from the AST and requires every probe text, every recorded server answer and every served control text to appear in it. That is what makes the witness-required property mechanical rather than aspirational, and it kills the mutations that matter (unwitnessed probe added, probe commented out, witness shared between gaps, table emptied, recipe selector broken four ways).

What it does NOT bind is that the witness **uses** the answer. A live test whose body contains the answer string as a dead local, a log line, or an unasserted variable satisfies the sweep exactly as well as one that does `require.Contains(t, err.Error(), p.answer)`.

Measured, not supposed: mutation M18 in the #809 review moved a recorded `answer` out of its assertion and left it as a bare string in the same body. The sweep stayed green.

The branch shipped this disclosed rather than fixed — `dialect_test.go`'s header comment and ADR 0028 both say the binding is textual containment, not assertion reachability. This bead is to close or ratify it, not to re-litigate the disclosure.

**Severity is low and the reason is specific.** The failure requires a human to write a live witness that carries the exact server answer as a string while not asserting on it — which is more work than writing the assertion. The realistic decay path is refactoring: someone rewrites the witness to assert on a sentinel/SQLSTATE instead of the message text, leaves the old message string in a comment-adjacent position or a table row, and the sweep does not notice the coverage left.

Fix shapes:

1. Narrow the render. Instead of the whole body, render only the arguments of assertion calls (`require.*` / `assert.*` / `s.Require().*`) reachable in the body, and require the answer to appear there. Costs a small call-expression walk; kills M18 directly.
2. Or invert it: have the live witness itself iterate `gap.refused` and assert per probe, and have the sweep require that the witness ranges over the table rather than restating it. That makes the binding structural and removes the string-matching entirely — but it is a bigger change to `test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go` and needs a live run to land safely (Docker/CI, per gqlc-0oau).

Option 1 is the cheap one and is checkable without a container.

title: codegen/age: the undefined-function diagnose ships two universals no witness carries
description:
`internal/codegen/age/dialect.go`'s `ErrUndefinedFunction` diagnose text tells the author two universal things:

- "Apache AGE 1.7.0 defines **no temporal constructor at all**"
- "AGE's **whole** temporal surface is timestamp()"

Neither is carried by anything on the branch that shipped them (PR #809, ADR 0028). The live witness `TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine` measures five refusals and two served texts; five "does not exist" answers and one working `timestamp()` do not establish a closed set over AGE's function catalogue.

The provenance is a hand-run spike, recorded at ADR 0028:29 — "of the 348 functions in `ag_catalog` exactly one has a temporal name". That 348 is itself an unwitnessed cardinal: no live test counts `ag_catalog`, so a version bump of the pinned image (`apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8...`) that adds a temporal function silently falsifies the ADR line AND the author-facing message, with nothing red.

**Why this was not a blocker on #809.** It errs toward under-refusing: the claim only affects the remediation advice, never the refusal decision, so no author is refused because of it. The `find` path is driven entirely by `undefinedFunctionProbes`.

**Why it is still worth closing.** It is advice with a universal quantifier in it, in the one place an author actually reads, and the branch's own posture is that the gap table is short on purpose (bd gqlc-osf1). "No temporal constructor at all" reads as the opposite of "short on purpose" — the message asserts closure over exactly the surface the ADR says is unmeasured.

Fix shapes, in the ratified order (a claim not made > a claim a test carries > a number > a hedge):

1. Drop the universals. The message works as "AGE 1.7.0 defines no temporal constructor this project has measured, and `timestamp()` is the one that answered" — same advice, no closure claim.
2. If closure is wanted, make it a live assertion: query `ag_catalog`'s function names from the pinned image inside the existing `ageDialectHarness` and pin the temporal-named set. That would also give the 348 a witness and redden it on an image bump.

Related: gqlc-osf1 (the table is known short), gqlc-kb2c (the ADR's cardinals rot together — the 348 is a seventh of the same family, on the provenance axis rather than the table-size axis).

title: review: a counterfactual comment ('X rather than Y') is two claims; add the fourth prose grep
description:
Round 7 of fix/emitted-decoder-reachability found a false claim that had passed a lead review, including my own.

The sentence: "It is \`!=\` rather than \`>\` so that the other direction - more names than values - binds nothing either."

I graded it TRUE-but-unpinned. Only the first half was true. Truth table, built out of tree with the operator as a parameter (/tmp/probe-05tl-op/main.go):

| shape | != shipped | < | > |
|---|---|---|---|
| more names than values | binds nothing | BINDS | binds nothing |
| fewer names than values | binds nothing | binds nothing | PANIC |

`>` rejects the more-names direction too; it differs from `!=` only by dropping the bounds guard. The operator that breaks the property is `<`. Round 6 named the wrong counterfactual.

Two process consequences worth adopting repo-wide:

1. A fourth prose grep for review briefs: `rather than|instead of|as opposed to`. The existing three (universals / distributive-cardinal / detector-direction) all structurally miss this shape. A counterfactual asserts a property of the road not taken, which nothing runs.

2. A KILLED mutation row is evidence for your claim only if the failure it produces is the one your claim predicts. My own `>` row was recorded KILLED, but its kill was a panic on an unrelated fixture, not a naming change - the disproof was already in my matrix and I misread it. Match the named failure to the mechanism, not just the sign.

Both are already written into agent memory. This bead is for propagating them into CLAUDE.md / the standing reviewer brief if we keep one in-repo.

title: codegen/conformance: the length guard's bounds direction is pinned only by a panic
description:
`boundLiteralNames`'s length guard `len(lhs) != len(rhs)` (internal/codegen/conformance/decoder_reachability_test.go) is pinned in both directions, but asymmetrically.

- more-names-than-values: pinned by a fixture. Mutating to `<` reddens TestSweepMarksEachYieldedFunctionByItsSpelling with a clean list diff (`the function literal at line 15` -> `unpaired`). Landed in 6912d310.
- fewer-names-than-values (the bounds hazard): pinned only because mutating to `>` PANICS with index out of range inside TestSweepReadsAFunctionLiteralAtAnyDepthOfADeclaration/a_value_of_a_declaration_binding_fewer_names_than_values. The run aborts, so `=== RUN` drops from 2311 to 860.

A panic-abort is a real kill but a poor pin: it takes the binary down rather than producing a named assertion about the guard, and the RUN drift makes it noisy in any matrix. The comment above the guard also names only the more-names test, not this one.

Residue from the round-7 review of fix/emitted-decoder-reachability. Not blocking - the direction IS covered. See /tmp/lead/verdict-05tlr7.md.

title: codegen: two gates are called the fence, and the codegen-fence CI context runs the other one
description:
Two different things in this repo are called "the fence", and the CI context
named after one of them runs the other.

- `just test-codegen-fence` is the **nested-module quality gate**: `cd
  test/data/codegen && go build ./... && go vet -tags codegen_live ./...`, `go
  mod tidy -diff`, `golangci-lint run`. `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` §8
  calls it "the compile fence".
- `internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go` is the **spec fence**, added
  by `gqlc-rz0l`. `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` §5.3 says the argument name
  and the binding values "are fenced" and names those tests.

The required CI context `codegen-fence` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:104-113`)
runs the first, not the second. The spec fence runs under `just test` — `go test
-shuffle=on ./...` — and so is PR-blocking via the `test` context.

So the gate is real; the naming is the hazard. A reader who wants to know
whether the spec fence blocks a PR will look at the context whose name matches
and find a recipe that never loads `internal/codegen/conformance`. The reverse
mistake is worse: someone narrowing `just test-codegen-fence` would believe they
were touching the spec fence.

Not a defect in either gate. Both halves of PR-blocking hold for the spec fence:
the check runs (`test`) and it is required.

## Fix, if taken

Rename one of them. `codegen-fence` -> `codegen-goldens` for the nested-module
job and its recipe is the smaller edit and the more accurate name; it touches
`justfile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the branch-protection required-contexts
list and the §8 prose. Renaming a required context needs the protection setting
updated in the same change or merges block.

Alternatively leave the names and add one line to §8 and to the fence file's
header saying which gate runs which, so the collision is at least documented.

## Acceptance

Reading either name leads to the right gate without opening the justfile.

Filed from the pre-merge adversarial review of `docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift`.

title: spec fence: a graded site inside an HTML comment is invisible to the reader but not to the census
description:
The spec fence reads raw markdown bytes, so a `<!-- ... -->` HTML comment is
graded exactly as visible text is. Measured on both sides at `2d1b603e`, in a
detached worktree:

**A commented site reddens the fence.** Appending

    <!--
    func (q *Queries) Ghost(ctx context.Context, id int64) error
    -->

to `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c4.md` fails `TestSpecMethodArgIsGeneratorOwned`
with "documented method argument is not generator-owned". That direction fails
closed — a maintenance annoyance, the same shape as `gqlc-173n`'s second half.

**A commented site also satisfies a census.** A new document
`docs/notes/ghostdoc.md` whose only `ctx context.Context` occurrence sits inside
`<!-- -->` is reported as "the sweep produced an entry specSigDocs does not
declare: docs/notes/ghostdoc.md". So `sweep.sigDocs[file]` is set by an invisible
site, and a listed document can keep its census entry on a signature no reader
of the rendered document ever sees.

That second direction is the one that matters, and it is not the same claim as
`gqlc-0rjn`. `gqlc-0rjn` is a floor of one *graded* site per listed document.
This says a graded site need not be a *printed* site — which is the word the
fence uses for itself throughout (`specSigDocs` are "the documents that print an
emitted query method signature whole"; the census exists to catch "a document
that still prints the surface and no longer contributes to the sweep"). Comment
carriage lets a document stop printing the surface while still contributing.

Not currently exploited: no `<!-- -->` in any swept document contains
`ctx context.Context` or `map[string]any{` (verified by grep at `2d1b603e`).

## Fix, if taken

Strip HTML comments from a document's text before scanning it, in `readDoc` or
in a wrapper around it. Cheap, and it moves both directions the right way at
once. The thing to keep is a witness: a row asserting that a signature inside
`<!-- -->` is neither graded nor exempted, so the stripping cannot quietly stop
happening. Do not strip fenced code blocks or inline code along with it — those
are where nearly every graded site lives.

## Acceptance

A drifted signature inside an HTML comment in a swept document is not graded,
and a document whose only graded site is inside an HTML comment does not satisfy
its census entry.

Filed from the pre-merge adversarial review of `docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift`.

title: codegen/age: ADR 0028's probe cardinals are six numbers in one sentence that rot together
description:
ADR 0028 'What is refused today' states: 'Two gaps carrying eight refused probes and four served texts — twelve query texts, counted off dialectGaps itself: three refused and two served for the alternation, five refused and two served for the undefined function.'

All six cardinals are TRUE as of cc4df90e — verified by counting dialectGaps in internal/codegen/age/dialect.go: gap 1 (ErrRelationshipTypeAlternation) has 3 refused probes and 2 served texts; gap 2 (ErrUndefinedFunction) has 5 (undefinedFunctionProbes) and 2. Totals 2/8/4/12 check out.

The defect is structural, not factual: adding one probe to undefinedFunctionProbes — which the ADR explicitly invites, since that slice is the ONLY source of the refused name set and grows as live measurements land — silently falsifies six cardinals in one sentence, and nothing fails. Same rot-together class as the recipe-count cardinal that gqlc-35yu.12 removed at cc4df90e ("the recipe count is written at the pin and nowhere else"), on a different axis, in the same document.

Disclosed by the 35yu.12 implementer as deliberately out of scope: it stopped at the axis the lead ruled on rather than expanding unasked, and expected the sweep to find live ones. It did not — they are all currently true. Hence P3 rot-risk rather than a defect.

Fix shape, per the ratified ordering (a claim not made > a claim a test carries > a number > a hedge): prefer deleting the cardinals in favour of the length-invariant mechanism they illustrate. If a number is genuinely needed, derive it in a test that reddens when dialectGaps grows and the prose does not follow.

---

**Amendment (2026-08-17, review of PR #809 at 3ce7798a): a seventh cardinal, outside the ADR.**

The site list above is short by one, and the extra site is not in `docs/`. `test/data/codegen/invalid/unrepresentable_temporal_localtime_column/queries.cypher` reads:

> AGE's dialect gate (internal/codegen/age/dialect.go) refuses the **five** constructor names a live session was measured on — date() among them — on the query TEXT

Same mechanism, same trigger: append one probe to `undefinedFunctionProbes` and "five" goes false, silently. It matters slightly more than the ADR copies, because that comment is the fixture's stated reason for existing — it explains why `localtime()` reaches the carrier refusal rather than the dialect gate — so a reader who trusts the "five" will mis-reason about which arm is under test.

Deliberately NOT swept on PR #809. A partial fix would have left this issue's own site list wrong while reading as addressed. The whole set should move together, under the same ratified ordering: prefer deleting the cardinal in favour of the mechanism ("the constructor names a live session was measured on", no number), and if a number is wanted, derive it where `undefinedFunctionProbes` can redden it.

Sites now known: ADR 0028 "What is refused today" (six cardinals in one sentence) and this fixture comment (one).

title: resolver: Phase B's covered=false conjunct is coarser than the evidence requires
description:
Round-4 review of feat/resolver-narrow-plural-endpoints (PASS, /tmp/lead/verdict-0tftr4.md) left this as precision residue.

candidateTypes sets covered=false for any folded edge failing witnessesItsEndpoints. That is sound and was the correct fix for F3 — the edge is not evidence about every returned row, so its far-end enumeration cannot license narrowing. But it is coarser than strictly needed: it discards the edge's contribution to COVERAGE wholesale, where a finer rule could still credit the rows the edge does witness.

Deliberately not skipping the edge entirely: skipping widens the intersection and turns a unique inference into ErrAmbiguousBinding, a refusal master does not make. The reviewer built that alternative and measured 4 rows where it regresses against both master and the fix.

Also here: mutation L05 (the narrowing collapse's resolvedCovers write) SURVIVES and is annotated in-situ as unpinnable. If the conjunct is refined, check whether L05 becomes reachable.

Non-breaking widening under ADR 0006, so this is precision-only.

title: resolver: writtenBindings over-approximates anonymous CREATE bindings, and Phase B now reads it
description:
Round-4 review of feat/resolver-narrow-plural-endpoints (PASS, /tmp/lead/verdict-0tftr4.md) left this as residue.

candidateTypes now takes written map[string]struct{} from scope.writtenBindings() so a folded edge failing witnessesItsEndpoints marks covered=false. writtenBindings over-approximates for ANONYMOUS bindings in a CREATE/MERGE clause. The reviewer confirmed this is observable — naming the CREATE's bindings changes the answer — and that NO test pins any of it.

Both the implementer and the reviewer measured the shapes they could reach as landing on master's answer, i.e. an unrealised widening rather than a regression. That is why it is residue and not a defect in the change.

Wanted: a test row that pins the anonymous case, so a future edit to writtenBindings cannot silently move Phase B's answer.

title: codegen spec fence: prose residue and a listPlaceholderRe widening the fence tolerates
description:
Non-blocking residue from the round-2 adversarial review of docs/c1-bare-arg-spec-drift at 3dd322dc (PASS). None of these falsify a stated claim; they are precision debt.

1. specfence_test.go:54-56 -- loose anaphora. 'that shrinkage' has no unambiguous antecedent in the preceding sentence. Name the thing.

2. docs/c1.md:823 -- 'the rest of every other signature' is vague about what 'the rest' ranges over. Say which components are covered and which are not.

3. listPlaceholderRe tolerates a lowercase-only widening. The reviewer measured this and was explicit that it does NOT falsify the fence's stated claim, because the named risk <bareParam> is pinned and still dies. So this is a note about the regex being broader than strictly needed, not a hole. Worth deciding whether to tighten it or to state the tolerance, rather than leaving a reader to rediscover it.

Context worth keeping: the round-2 reviewer went looking for a fifth false universal in this file on the theory that four is a pattern, and did NOT find one. The sharpest claim in the file (specfence_test.go:1051-1053, that an arm reporting another arm's headline is invisible to the sweeps) is exactly true. So this file is in good shape; the above is polish.

Related: gqlc-0rjn (the per-document census floor, documented not closed).

title: githooks: the bd-gh-sync assertion census cannot notice its own deletion
description:
The bd-gh-sync test suite keeps a census of its own assertions (added ca5e70cb, branch fix/bd-gh-sync-pull-witness). Adversarial review of 0c13ddcb found the census guards MEMBERSHIP but not its own EXISTENCE or the STRENGTH of what it counts.

Three measured holes:

1. Deleting the whole census block -> exit 0, '140 passed, 0 failed'. Truncating the file at the census (test:2164) -> exit 0 with no '--- N passed' summary line at all. The census cannot detect that it was removed.

2. Weakening an assertion in place survives. Replacing test:2158's condition with a comparison against an impossible sentinel, while leaving the assertion NAME and its ok/bad calls untouched, exits 0 at 141/141. The census checks that an assertion by that name ran, not that it still tests anything.

3. Prose at test:2166 says the suite 'still makes every assertion it made yesterday'. That overstates what is enforced: the census pins the SET of assertion names, not their content. State the negative instead.

Reviewer priced the existence half at roughly three lines, external to the suite (something outside the script must assert the summary line appears and the count is >= a floor sourced from outside the run). Holes 2 and 3 may be acceptable-and-documented rather than closed; a census that pins assertion strength is a much larger design.

Note the general shape: this is a gate that cannot observe its own absence, the same class as a conditional check that is skipped silently. A pass count sourced from the run itself cannot detect that the run was empty.

title: resolver: a directed close still collects the right-to-left endpoint reading
description:
endpointContribution (internal/resolver/resolve.go) applies readsRightToLeft to every candidate regardless of e.Directed(). When srcs and tgts overlap, a directed candidate can satisfy both readings, and the pattern's left end then also collects k.Target -- a type the arrow rules out.

Reproduction (test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_chain.gql):

  MATCH (p:Node)-[r:X]->(q:Node) RETURN p
    -> ambiguous label: A&Node, B&Node, C&Node

C&Node has no outgoing X, so the arrow proves p is in {A&Node, B&Node}. The extra C&Node comes from readsRightToLeft firing on the B->C declaration because srcs and tgts overlap.

Precision only, never unsound: the contribution stays a superset of the truth, so this is missed widening in the ADR 0006 non-breaking direction. Filed rather than fixed under gqlc-0tft because the fix changes which queries resolve.

Note readsLeftToRight's doc comment ends 'on a directed close only the left-to-right reading was ever probed', which reads as if the other reading were irrelevant on a directed edge. The code does not act on that. Either act on it or say the code deliberately does not.

title: spec: the spec fence's docRoots can fail to grow, and no census notices
description:
`docRoots` in `internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go` enumerates the trees the spec fence sweeps: `docs`, `README.md`, `CONTEXT.md`.

It cannot shrink quietly. A root that stops existing fails `docFiles` by name (`docRoots entry "docs" does not exist`), and dropping `docs` loses every document `specSigDocs` / `specBindDocs` / `specListRuleDocs` declare, so the census reports each by name.

It can fail to grow, and nothing objects. The censuses name **documents**, not roots, so they are silent about markdown `docRoots` never reaches. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` sit beside the two files named in `docRoots` and are unswept; a new document added at the repository root joins them with no edit to the fence at all.

That is strictly weaker than the floor the fence sets for itself everywhere else. Dropping a declared document is a visible two-part edit that deletes a named document from a list in a test file. Adding an unswept one is a zero-part edit.

Not currently exploited: none of the three prints a query method signature or a `map[string]any` driver-binding literal (verified by grep for `ctx context.Context` and `map[string]any{`).

Filed from gqlc-rz0l, which corrected the two prose claims that overstated the floor — the fence comment said "One thing no check that reads only these documents can reach" and C1 §5.3 said "What is left open is what no check reading only these documents can close". Both now enumerate this second limit and cite this bead.

Options, not decided here:
- A census over the repository-root markdown set, so a new root document is red until declared swept or declared out of scope. Mirrors the existing censuses exactly; costs one line per new root document.
- Sweep every `.md` in the tree with an exclusion list (`test/data/`, `.beads/`, vendored trees) instead of an inclusion list, so the default for a new document is swept.

Acceptance: adding a repository-root markdown document that prints a single-parameter query method signature reddens the fence, or the fence records why that is out of its scope.

title: resolver: plural endpoint narrowing does not reach across a WITH carry
description:
`gqlc-0tft` made a plural node binding narrow from an edge that every returned
row provably has. It does not reach across a `WITH`:

    MATCH (p:Person) WITH p MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN p.id

stays refused. The plural carry is rejected before Part 1's edge gets the chance
to narrow `p`, so the query is refused for a reason that the second part would
have answered.

## Why this is a widening and not a bug

Nothing here is unsound: the refusal is conservative and no wrong column is
emitted. It is a query a user can reasonably write and reasonably expect to
resolve, refused because of the *order* two mechanisms run in rather than
because the schema cannot answer it.

Confirmed by `linus-0tft-r2` during the round-2 review, who separately
established that a plural binding cannot cross a `WITH` at all on master
(`MATCH (p:Person) WITH p RETURN p.id` is `ErrAmbiguousLabel` there), so this is
not a regression introduced by the narrowing — it is the narrowing not yet
reaching a place that was already refused.

## Fix

Work out whether the narrowing can run before the carry check, or whether the
carry check can consult the narrowed set. Ordering changes in the resolver have
been load-bearing on this epic — `gqlc-0tft` itself had to move its narrowing
*below* the deferred-edge close, pinned by
`TestDeferredEdgesCloseBeforeTheNarrowing` — so whatever order is chosen needs a
test that fails when it is reversed.

## Acceptance

The query above resolves, with `p` committed to the single type `WORKS_AT`'s
declared source endpoint names, and a test that reddens if the two mechanisms
are reordered.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-0tft-r2`'s non-blocking findings (NB-4),
who described it as "missed widening, filed-shaped".

title: bd-gh-sync: _run_batch's loop stdin is the allowlist, so a bd that reads stdin truncates the batch
description:
`_run_batch` runs `bd github sync` inside

    while read … done <"$_tmp/allow.txt"

so the loop's stdin is the allowlist file. A `bd` that reads stdin — for a
prompt, a confirmation, or anything else — consumes the remainder of that file,
and the batch silently stops partway through the ids it was given.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

**Pre-existing**, not introduced by `gqlc-nvjz` or `gqlc-b7lt`, and it fails in
the **safe** direction: the ids that get eaten are ids that never reach `bd`,
so they are never pulled, never counted as pulled, and — since `gqlc-b7lt` — 
never exempted from the deletion detector either. The run is short, not wrong.

That is exactly why it is worth a bead rather than a silent fix in an unrelated
branch: today's `bd` does not read stdin, so nothing exercises it, and the day
one subcommand grows a prompt this becomes a truncation nobody can see. The
current safety depends on a property of a *different program*.

## Fix

Redirect the loop's stdin away from the allowlist, or feed the ids by a
mechanism that does not occupy fd 0 — `< /dev/null` on the inner command is the
usual spelling, reading the file on a non-standard descriptor is the other.

## Acceptance

A test in `.githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh` whose `bd` stub reads a line from
stdin on `github sync`, asserting every id in the allowlist still reaches it.
It must fail against the current script for the reason it names.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-ghsync-r5`'s non-blocking findings (F5),
who flagged it as latent and pre-existing so it would not be mistaken for a
regression on this branch.

title: bd-gh-sync: a listing that exits 0 with garbage refuses without naming which listing
description:
`bd-gh-sync` now names the exit status behind a refused pull (`gqlc-nvjz`), but
only when the status is **non-zero**. A listing command that exits **0** and
writes garbage still refuses with a bare

    JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1

and no line naming which of `bd list` or `gh issue list` produced it.

The script's own comment says the two "send the operator to different places".
Only half of that is delivered: the operator learns the input was unparseable
but not whose input it was.

## Scope

Symmetric with the push side, which has the same gap, so this is **not a
regression** introduced by `gqlc-nvjz` — it is the remaining half of the same
claim, on both paths.

## Why it is filed rather than folded in

`gqlc-nvjz` asked for the discarded exit status to be captured and named. It
was, and that fix is sound. This is a different failure mode — a command that
*succeeds* and lies — and the fix is a different one: the parse has to be
attributed to its source rather than the status to its command. Doing it on
one path only would leave the asymmetry the pull-path work exists to remove.

## Fix

Attribute the decode failure to the listing it came from, on both the pull and
the push path. The status-naming lines added by `gqlc-nvjz` are the model for
where the message belongs.

## Acceptance

A test in `.githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh` for each of the four cases —
`bd list` and `gh issue list`, on the pull and the push path — where the
command exits 0 and writes unparseable bytes, asserting the refusal names the
command. Each must fail against the current script for the reason it names.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-ghsync-p4`'s non-blocking findings (NB-4),
who flagged it as symmetric with the push side so it would not be mistaken for
a regression on the pull path alone.

title: spec: C5 prints GetAction with two different parameter types in one document
description:
`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c5.md` prints one method under two different
parameter types:

- `:418` — `GetAction(ctx context.Context, arg GetActionParams)`
- `:996` — `GetAction(ctx context.Context, arg int64)`

One method name, two arities, in one document. At most one of them is what the
emitter produces for that method.

Confirmed present at `77a8cc12`, so it is **pre-existing** and not introduced by
`gqlc-rz0l`.

## Why the fence does not catch it

`gqlc-rz0l`'s spec fence grades the argument **name** position and explicitly
disclaims the type position. The name is `arg` in both lines, which is correct,
so both pass. The divergence is entirely on the axis the fence says it does not
read — this is the fence being honest about its boundary rather than failing.

## Fix

Work out which arity `GetAction` actually has by reading the emitter and the
goldens rather than by picking the line that looks more recent, then correct the
other site. If both are intended — two different examples that happen to share a
method name — rename one, because a reader who greps the document for
`GetAction` currently gets two incompatible answers with nothing to choose
between them.

## Acceptance

The two sites agree, and agree with what the emitter emits.

Worth considering while in there: whether the type position can be graded at all
for these signatures. If it can, this is the fixture for it. If it cannot —
`gqlc-vu7z` records why multi-parameter signatures are hard to grade without a
hand-maintained exclusion list — then say so and close this on the correction
alone rather than leaving an implied promise of a fence that is not coming.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-rz0l-r2`'s non-blocking findings (NB-6),
who flagged it as pre-existing and off-axis so it would not be lost.

title: spec: prose can redefine the argument name under an intact code span the fence grades
description:
The spec fence grades **identifiers** — the argument name a signature, a
`<param-list>` bullet or a binding map literal spells. It does not read the
prose around them, and prose can contradict the code span it sits under.

Reviewer's mutation, green against the fence at `163d1873`:

Leave `` `, arg <T>` `` intact in C1 §5.3 and rewrite the sentence beneath it to

> the argument name is `arg` where the query parameter is named `arg`;
> otherwise it is the parameter field-name mangle

The graded span still says `arg`, so every assertion passes — and the document
now specifies the capture vector `gqlc-rz0l` removed, in the section that is
this repository's statement of the rule.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

Out of the fence's declared scope, and the fence says so rather than
over-claiming. Closing it means grading natural language against an emitter,
which is not a thing a Go test can do honestly. Every cheap approximation —
keyword blacklists, "no sentence near this span may contain 'derive'" — is a
guard that passes over the rewordings nobody predicted and fails over innocent
prose, which is worse than the honest gap.

Noted rather than closed so no reader mistakes the fence for a claim about the
whole document.

## If it is taken

The tractable half is narrowing what prose *can* say by giving the rule one
canonical statement and having every other mention point at it rather than
restate it. A document with one place to change is one a reviewer can watch.
That is an editorial change to `docs/specs/`, not a test.

Do not close this by adding a fence that greps prose for suspicious words. The
repo's recurring defect class is a guard green over nothing, and a
keyword-matcher over English is that shape by construction.

## Related

`gqlc-vu7z` — the fence grades only one-parameter signatures.
`gqlc-173n` — the bind sweep grades every map literal under `docs/` and cannot
see a deref.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-rz0l-r2`'s non-blocking findings (NB-3).

title: codegen/age: the edge-union dispatch is emitted in a query method, so 05tl's gate cannot see it
description:
`gqlc-05tl` gates emitted label guards on reachability: a `switch label { case
"X": ... }` whose case no value can satisfy is dead code the generator emitted
at exit 0, which ADR 0025 already treats as a defect ("it emits a column no
decoder can fill at exit 0").

The gate sweeps `decode<T>` function bodies. AGE's edge-union dispatch is not
in one. `internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go:477` emits the same
`switch label { case ... }` shape **inside a query method**, so the sweep does
not read it and the gate's reachability claim does not cover it.

Same defect class the gate exists to close, one emission site over.

## Check first whether this is already moot

`gqlc-35yu.14` **deletes** AGE's edge-union emission — `writeEdgeUnionDecode`,
`columnName`, `labelName` and `edgeKeyToEntityName` all go — because AGE 1.7.0
rejects relationship-type alternation outright (SQLSTATE 42601), so the decoder
was for a query the backend can never run.

If `.14` has merged, `render_queries.go:477` may no longer exist. **Do not
close this bead on that alone.** The finding is that the sweep is keyed on
`decode*` bodies while emission is not confined to them; if the one site that
demonstrated it is gone, the gate is still keyed the same way and the next
in-method emission is still invisible. Confirm whether any in-method `switch
label` remains on any backend before deciding which of the two this is.

## Fix

Either widen the sweep to every emitted `switch` on a label regardless of the
function it sits in, or state the boundary in the gate's own docstring so no
reader takes it for a whole-tree claim. The first is preferable; the second is
acceptable only if the first is genuinely out of reach, and then the docstring
must say what escapes rather than what is covered.

## Acceptance

A label guard emitted inside a query method, unsatisfiable by any value on its
axis, fails the gate.

The regression must redden when the widening is reverted — a gate that passes
before and after is the exact shape `gqlc-05tl` was filed against, and would be
self-undermining here.

Note the axis rule `gqlc-05tl` round 2 established: a node decoder's guard is
satisfiable by a node label, an edge decoder's by an edge label, and the two
alphabets are **not** unioned. Whatever reads this site must be held to the same
per-axis rule.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-05tl-r1`'s findings.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-16 on fix/emitted-decoder-reachability @85e5749d, answering this bead's own 'check first whether this is already moot'.

AGE's site is GONE. gqlc-35yu.14 merged; internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go emits no 'switch label' at any width, and AGE refuses an edge-union column whole on codegen.ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion, so no AGE emission carries one.

neo4j's site REMAINS, and it is the live instance of this bead. Both walkListElemBody (internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:729, emits at :775) and writeEdgeUnionDispatchBody (:857, emits at :861) write 'switch rel.Type { case "<relationship type>": ... }' into a query METHOD. packageLevelFuncs skips a receiver form, so the sweep does not read it. Confirmed in the golden: test/data/codegen/valid/edge_union_many_two_candidates/golden/neo4j-go-v5/queries.cypher.go.

So this is your second case, not the first: the gate is still keyed the same way and the next in-method emission is still invisible.

The branch takes fix option 2 (state the boundary in the gate's own docstring, naming what escapes) at commit d1542b3a. Option 1 -- widen the sweep to every emitted switch on a label regardless of enclosing function -- is NOT done and this bead stays open for it. Note the branch's docstring previously named AGE's render_queries.go:477 as the escaping site; that citation was stale and is corrected to neo4j's two.

Under 'just test' the only thing beneath an unsatisfiable case label there is a golden byte diff, which go test -update blesses away. The run that would catch it is edgeUnionDispatch in test/data/codegen/live_test.go, behind the codegen_live build tag and outside the default suite.

title: resolver: an OPTIONAL edge in a proven group is a witness NarrowPluralEndpoints throws away
description:
`NarrowPluralEndpoints` skips every edge binding that is nullable, so an
OPTIONAL edge never constrains its endpoints. That is the conservative fix
`gqlc-0tft` shipped, and it is correct: an edge that may not exist on a
surviving row is not evidence about that row's node type.

But it is *more* conservative than the truth. `DemoteNullability` at
`internal/resolver/scope.go:616` walks the identical shape and guards it with

    (e.Nullable() && !demotedGroups[...]) || !qualifiedDemoter(e)

— the extra clause being the point. An OPTIONAL edge **inside a proven group**
genuinely is a witness: the group's demotion is exactly the finding that every
surviving row carries that edge. `NarrowPluralEndpoints` throws that away.

## Why it was not taken with the fix

Ruled by the coordinator during `gqlc-0tft`'s review round. The refinement is a
*further widening* of what narrows, and a widening shipped without coverage is
precisely how the original defect arrived — `NarrowPluralEndpoints` was green
with the bug and green with the fix, which is to say the branch had zero
coverage for the distinction it got wrong. Fixing an unwitnessed widening with a
second unwitnessed widening is not a fix.

So the plain guard shipped, and the precision is filed here to be taken with
its own fixtures.

## Fix

Adopt `DemoteNullability`'s guard verbatim rather than paraphrasing it — the two
sites are answering the same question about the same shape, and a guard that
drifts from its sibling is how the next one of these gets written.

The `demotedGroups` set has to reach `NarrowPluralEndpoints`; check whether the
call order already computes it before the narrow pass runs, and say so
explicitly if it does not, because reordering the two passes is a larger change
than this bead's headline.

## Acceptance

The load-bearing half is the fixtures, not the guard. Required, in both
directions:

- An OPTIONAL edge in a **proven** group narrows its endpoints — the column that
  is now correctly NOT NULL is null-typed without the refinement.
- An OPTIONAL edge in an **unproven** group still does not narrow — this is the
  `gqlc-0tft` case and must not regress.

Each fixture must redden when the corresponding half of the guard is deleted.
A fixture that passes with and without the refinement is not coverage for it,
and this bead exists because that is what happened last time.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-0tft-r1`'s findings.

title: resolver: a Temporal kind declared through an alias or as a bare untyped const escapes the enum sweep
description:
`declaredTemporals` (`internal/codegen/conformance/assembled_input_test.go`)
derives `resolver.Temporal`'s membership by parsing source, because
compilation erases the fact it needs: a constant the block names and
`Temporal.String` has no arm for is, to anything running, identical to a
value nobody declared. Membership is decided syntactically — a const spec
whose written type is the identifier `Temporal`, or which inherits that
type from the `iota` anchor's declaration.

Two shapes satisfy the compiler and escape the sweep. Both were reproduced
live in the `linus-h4ug-r9` round: each compiles, each declares a seventh
kind with no `String()` arm, and `just test` stays green over both. In each,
the kind renders as `Temporal(6)`, `firstUndeclaredTemporal` hands the
`list-elem-temporal` case a value that IS declared, and nothing says so.

## Through a type alias

    type temporalAlias = Temporal
    const TemporalWeek temporalAlias = 6

The written type is `temporalAlias`, so the sweep does not recognise it;
the alias makes it the same type to the compiler, so `case TemporalWeek:`
compiles in a switch over the enum.

## As a bare untyped declaration

    const ( TemporalWeek = 6 )

as its own declaration, not sharing the `iota` anchor's. Untyped integer
constants are assignable to `Temporal`, so `case TemporalWeek:` compiles.
The existing untyped guard refuses an untyped line only WHERE IT SHARES THE
ANCHOR'S DECLARATION — a standalone one has no anchor to inherit from and
no anchor to be refused against.

## Why filed rather than fixed

Coordinator ruling. The third escape the reviewer found — a
`TemporalWeek Temporal = 6` in another file of package `resolver` — WAS
promoted and fixed, because the sibling fence on the same branch
(`scanSources`, `internal/codegen/errors_test.go:789`) already sweeps every
non-test file in its package and its docstring states the reason in terms
that transfer word for word.

These two do not transfer. Resolving an alias syntactically means chasing
alias declarations and getting it wrong in the general case; doing it
properly means type information, which is a different kind of test than a
source sweep. And fencing the bare untyped form in general means refusing
every untyped integer constant in the package, since any of them is
assignable to `Temporal` — unbounded, and it would fire on unrelated code.

The code states both boundaries honestly rather than over-claiming, which
is the reason these are P3 and not blocking: `temporalsOf`'s docstring says
the untyped refusal applies "wherever it shares the anchor's declaration".
A reader is not misled about what is fenced.

## If taken

`go/types` over the loaded package rather than `go/parser` over the files
answers both at once, and would also subsume the file-level widening. Weigh
that against the cost: the sweep currently needs no build, which is part of
why it can run inside the conformance suite.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-h4ug-r9`'s non-blocking finding (a),
escapes 2 and 3.

title: spec: the fence's bind sweep grades every map literal under docs/, and cannot see a deref
description:
Two reach limits in `scanSpecBinds`, `internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go`.
Both were measured in the `linus-rz0l-r1` round; neither is live today.

## `unwrapConversions` strips `*`, so a deref is invisible (his #17)

The sweep reduces a binding expression to the identifier it ultimately
reads, peeling carrier conversions: `float64(arg)` binds `arg`. It also
peels `*` and `&`, so

    map[string]any{"x": float64(*arg)}

reduces to `arg` and passes.

This is DECLARED rather than concealed — C1 §5.3 scopes the fence to the
argument NAME, and `*arg` does carry the right name. But it is worth
recording because of what sits next to it. The `gqlc-rz0l` branch corrected
C3 §5.7 out of scope, precisely because a mechanical rename there would have
produced `float64(*arg)`, which is both wrong (a nullable parameter binds
bare — `paramBindExpr` at `internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:428`
returns before `driverCarrier` is reached) and a nil panic at runtime. So the
one correction on that branch whose whole point was the deref is unfenced
against its own failure mode.

Fix, if taken: grade the binding SHAPE for nullable parameters as well as
the name — a documented `map[string]any` entry whose expression derefs is
drift against `paramBindExpr`'s nullable-first ordering, regardless of what
identifier it names.

## The sweep grades every `map[string]any{` under `docs/` (his #39)

`docRoots` is the whole of `docs/` plus `README.md` and `CONTEXT.md`, and
`mapAnchor` is the bare literal `map[string]any{`. Any such literal in any
markdown file is graded as a documented parameter binding. A future ADR or
design note showing

    opts := map[string]any{"debug": true}

fails `TestSpecParamsMapBindsGeneratorOwnedValue` and is told its
"documented parameter binding is not generator-owned."

This FAILS CLOSED, so it is a maintenance annoyance rather than a hole — the
danger is that whoever hits it responds by narrowing `docRoots`, and the
breadth of `docRoots` is load-bearing (the original drift reached C1, C3, C4
and C5, and an ADR prints the same signatures). Verified as a live mutation:
an unrelated literal planted in a doc reddens the sweep.

Fix, if taken: require the literal to sit in a binding context — adjacent to
a graded signature, or inside a section the spec marks normative — rather
than widening the identifier allowlist, which would weaken the sweep in the
direction that matters.

Filed by the coordinator from `linus-rz0l-r1`'s non-blocking findings #17
and #39.

title: spec: the spec fence grades only one-parameter signatures, so multi-parameter drift is unswept
description:
`internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go` pins the documented method
argument name against `codegen.ParamArg`, closing the capture vector
`gqlc-lhs3` removed from the emitter. It grades a signature only when the
parameter list splits into exactly two:

    params := splitTopLevel(list)
    if len(params) != 2 {
        continue
    }

So a documented signature carrying the query author's parameter names as
separate bare arguments —

    PeopleOverAge(ctx context.Context, minAge int64, locale string)

— is skipped. The emitter renders two-or-more parameters as a single
`arg <MethodName>Params` struct, so that signature is drift, and it is the
naive sqlc-shaped form a reader would plausibly write. Verified as a live
